The lungs are passive: the sticky pleural fluid makes them follow the chest wall outward on inspiration, and the recoil of that wall compresses them on expiration.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.4 Diseases, Disorders and Injuries of the Integumentary System, Melanoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(1) (2027 I.C.6.g(1)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which skin cancer is the most fatal, and which cell does it arise from?
opciones: Melanoma, from the melanocytes that make the pigment of the skin
Melanoma, from the keratinocytes of the layer beneath the surface
Basal cell carcinoma, from the melanocytes that make the pigment
Squamous cell carcinoma, from the stem cells of the deepest layer
preguntas.explicacion: Melanoma is the melanocytes, the cells that make pigment, growing out of control, and it usually starts from a mole; it spreads readily and is hard to catch before it reaches other organs, which makes it the deadliest of the skin cancers. Basal cell carcinoma is the most common one, and squamous cell carcinoma arises from keratinocytes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is put in the specimen refrigerator to await pick-up. Why is that the wrong choice?
opciones: Whole blood for these assays is held at room temperature, not chilled
Whole blood for these assays is held frozen, and chilling is not enough
Refrigeration bursts the red cells and haemolyses the whole specimen
Refrigeration hardens the gel barrier and traps the plasma underneath
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood drawn for clotting tests is kept at room temperature, roughly eighteen to twenty-four degrees, and refrigeration is avoided because cold can activate factor VII. Chilling whole blood also lowers factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, which can imitate a bleeding disorder.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers: Insulin benefit
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6 (2027 III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose insulin pump is covered under Part B picks up a three-month supply. What is the most that supply can cost her?
opciones: $105, because a month's supply of that covered insulin is capped at $35
$315, because a month's supply of that covered insulin is capped at $105
$105, but only after the yearly Part B deductible has been satisfied
$35, because the cap covers the whole supply however long it lasts
preguntas.explicacion: Insulin covered under the Part B durable medical equipment benefit costs the patient no more than $35 for a month's supply, and the yearly Part B deductible is not applied to it. A three-month supply is capped at $35 for each of those months, which generally comes to no more than $105 in all. A Medigap policy that pays the Part B coinsurance should cover that amount.

preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 2(4) and 2(8); StatPearls, "Needlestick", Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: Scale of sharps injuries · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: How many percutaneous injuries, needlesticks among them, did Congress estimate happen each year among U.S. healthcare workers when it passed the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act?
opciones: 6 to 8 million
380,000 in all settings
preguntas.explicacion: Section 2 of the Act cites CDC estimates published in March 2000: over 380,000 percutaneous injuries a year from contaminated sharps in U.S. hospital settings alone, and between 600,000 and 800,000 such injuries, needlesticks among them, once every healthcare setting is counted. The same findings put at 62 to 88 percent the share of sharps injuries that safer devices could prevent. StatPearls lands nearby, about 600,000 a year, and adds that close to half are never reported.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Remote patient monitoring · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is listing what its remote monitoring program will accept. Which group of devices does the guidance name?
opciones: Pacemakers, glucose meters, blood pressure monitors, heart rate monitors, wireless scales, oximeters
Blood pressure monitors, fitness trackers, applications that record exercise, and dose reminders
Glucose meters, oximeters, wireless scales, and applications that store discharge instructions
Pacemakers, oximeters, secure messaging platforms, and applications that store health education
preguntas.explicacion: Remote patient monitoring means patient data and clinical information traveling to the provider, whether from devices kept in the home or keyed in and sent electronically by the patient. Named as examples: pacemakers, glucose meters, blood pressure monitors, heart rate monitors, wireless scales and oximeters. Fitness trackers, exercise applications and medicine reminders belong to mobile health, not here.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", sections Introduction and Other Issues (Human Clinical Studies)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: 'If you don't let me draw this, the doctor is going to be very upset with you.' Which requirement of valid consent does this remark violate?
opciones: Voluntariness: the decision must be made free of coercion
Disclosure: the risks of the procedure were never fully listed
Capacity: the patient's understanding was never assessed
Documentation: the consent form was never signed
preguntas.explicacion: Valid consent requires a patient competent to make a voluntary decision, and clinicians must avoid creating any sense of coercion toward their recommendation; the research-consent list names the voluntary nature of the decision as one of three elements. Pressure through a third party's displeasure attacks that element directly, whatever was disclosed or signed.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 5. Cleaning and Disinfecting Environmental Surfaces in Healthcare Facilities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How often should the mopping solution be replaced during floor cleaning?
opciones: Every three patient rooms, and no less often than every 60 minutes
Every three patient rooms, and no less often than every 30 minutes
Every ten patient rooms, and no less often than every 60 minutes
Once per shift, unless the solution turns visibly cloudy before then
preguntas.explicacion: Leave the water-and-disinfectant mixture unchanged for too long and mopping stops cleaning: it starts spreading heavy contamination through the building. The interval given is about every three patient rooms and never longer than 60 minutes. Mop heads and cleaning cloths are also decontaminated regularly, with laundering and drying at least daily.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Issues of Concern; and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Termination of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(1) · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who cannot pay is in a critical stage of illness. What does the duty to avoid abandonment require?
opciones: Care continues until the patient is stable, whatever the ability to pay
Care continues for 30 days from the notice, then stops at the deadline
Care stops, but the practice must file the records with the state board
Care stops, provided the patient is handed a list of low-cost clinics
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency, or while the patient is critically ill, termination has to wait until she is medically stable. Abandonment cases have consistently affirmed the responsibility to go on caring for someone at a critical stage of illness whatever her ability to pay, and one court held a psychiatrist liable where a foreseeable risk of self-harm was involved.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Accessible formats · CMAA 5 k65, k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) / 2027 II.F.1.d(3) · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with very low vision says she cannot read her Medicare summary notice. What can she be told is available?
opciones: The notice in an accessible format, large print or Braille among them
The notice read out by a Medicare representative over the telephone
The notice in large print, but only for the electronic version of it
The notice in an accessible format, once her provider requests it for her
preguntas.explicacion: The summary notice can be had in an accessible format where the beneficiary needs one, with large print and Braille given as the examples. Electronic delivery is a separate choice, and it brings an e-mail carrying a link to the notice for any month in which a claim has been processed.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.D.2.n
preguntas.pregunta: How does an ultrasonic cleaner remove soil from an instrument?
opciones: Acoustic waves cause cavitation and implosion that break the bonds holding debris on surfaces
Acoustic waves heat the bath to a temperature that dissolves protein and fat residue away
Acoustic waves drive a detergent through lumens under pressure until the channels run clear
Acoustic waves inactivate the bacteria directly, which then wash off with the loosened debris
preguntas.explicacion: Ultrasonic cleaning works mechanically: waves of acoustic energy travel through the solution and the cavitation and implosion they produce break the bonds that hold particles to the surface. The sound alone does not kill bacteria to any useful degree, and used cleaning solutions can themselves carry bacterial contamination, since they make no antibacterial claim.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Oral Antidiabetic Medications", Adverse Effects and Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.4
preguntas.pregunta: Among the oral antidiabetic agents, which one carries the highest hypoglycemia risk because of its long half-life and active metabolites?
opciones: Glyburide
Glipizide
Glimepiride
Repaglinide
preguntas.explicacion: All three sulfonylureas listed can push the glucose down, but glyburide carries the greatest risk: it lingers and leaves active metabolites behind, which is also why it is avoided once the eGFR falls under 30. For that same reason glimepiride or glipizide tends to be chosen ahead of it. Repaglinide is a meglitinide; hypoglycemia is its main adverse effect too, but it is usually milder because the drug acts briefly.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR), What is a prothrombin time test with an INR?
preguntas.subtema: Purpose of the INR · PBT IV.A.3 / IV.C · CCMA 3D k111 · CMA I.C.10.b.(5) INR (2027: b.(8)) · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why are prothrombin time results usually reported as an INR in addition to seconds?
opciones: PT in seconds varies between laboratories and methods, and the ratio makes results comparable
Seconds measure only the intrinsic pathway, and the ratio adds in the extrinsic pathway result
The ratio corrects the raw clotting time for the patient's hematocrit and platelet count
The ratio converts the prothrombin time into the equivalent partial thromboplastin time
preguntas.explicacion: A prothrombin time counts the seconds a sample takes to clot, but that number differs from one laboratory or reagent method to another. Converting it to an international normalized ratio lets providers compare and interpret results from different laboratories and methods, which matters when a warfarin dose is adjusted on the basis of serial tests. The PTT is a separate test that examines different clotting factors.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 5: Fire-Fighting Measures
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 5 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 VI.G.2 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section tells you which extinguishing agent is right for a fire involving that chemical, and which is not?
opciones: Section 5, which also warns about products given off as it burns
Section 6, which also covers containment and cleanup after a spill
Section 9, which also gives the flash point and the boiling range
Section 7, which also covers safe storage and incompatible products
preguntas.explicacion: Section 5 is written for the fire: which extinguishing equipment is suitable and which is not appropriate for a given situation, the specific hazards the chemical develops while burning, such as hazardous combustion products, and any special protection or precautions for the people fighting it. The flash point in section 9 tells you the chemical can burn; section 5 tells you what to do about it, and section 6 begins where the release has not caught fire.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Cane Basics
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65
preguntas.pregunta: A cane is being adjusted to a patient's height. Where should the handle sit?
opciones: Level with the patient's wrist, so that the elbow bends a little on the grip
Level with the patient's hip, so that the elbow stays straight on the grip
Level with the patient's waist, so that the shoulder can be raised slightly
Level with the patient's elbow, so that the forearm rests along the shaft
preguntas.explicacion: Standing straight with the arms down, the handle should reach the crease of the wrist; gripping it then leaves the elbow slightly bent. Hip level is the landmark for the handles of a walker, not a cane. The patient is taught to look ahead rather than down at the feet, and to check the rubber tips daily and replace them once they wear.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Prognosis; Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Go now, not tomorrow · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck at the end of her shift and says she will go to occupational health tomorrow. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Be seen at once, rather than waiting twelve to seventy-two hours for a visit
Be seen within seven days, the deadline that applies to hepatitis B treatment
Be seen at the end of the shift, once the incident report has been written
Be seen within ninety days, while the baseline sample is being preserved
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up with occupational health should be immediate rather than delayed by twelve to seventy-two hours, because the decisions that depend on it are time-sensitive: baseline testing, hepatitis B immune globulin within about a day, and antiretroviral prophylaxis started preferably within hours. The ninety days is how long a baseline sample is preserved when the employee does not consent to HIV testing on the spot, not a period in which to be seen.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Fixed Recessed Needle
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is recommended for a device whose sharp sits recessed inside a fixed housing?
opciones: The housing extends past the sharp and keeps fingers out
The housing retracts on activation and exposes the used sharp
The housing is removed before disposal so the bin fills slowly
The housing is colored orange to match an insulin syringe hub
preguntas.explicacion: For a fixed recessed needle the housing has to reach past the sharp, covering it completely and keeping fingers off. Color is a separate recommendation: it should serve a definite purpose, such as telling models or sizes apart, and follow conventions users already know.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth preparation · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4H k62 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: How early should a patient be told to connect for a video appointment, and why?
opciones: Fifteen minutes early, to leave room for last-minute troubleshooting
Thirty minutes early, so staff can complete the whole intake by telephone
Five minutes early, since the platform will reconnect automatically if it drops
Exactly on time, so the virtual waiting room does not fill with early arrivals
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance for getting set up tells patients to pick a spot with plenty of light and not to sit with a window behind them, to keep the camera steady and at eye level showing head and shoulders, to wear loose clothing where skin has to be shown, to find somewhere quiet, to close other applications, and, for a video appointment, to sign on fifteen minutes ahead so there is room to sort out any last-minute trouble.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: What Information is Protected
preguntas.subtema: Security Rule scope · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which information does the HIPAA Security Rule protect, as distinct from the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Only health information that is kept or transmitted in electronic form
Health information in any form, including paper charts and spoken conversations
Only the demographic fields the practice sends in a standard claim transaction
Only information that has already been encrypted or otherwise rendered unreadable
preguntas.explicacion: National standards for one subset of the health information that identifies an individual are what the Security Rule sets: the electronic PHI a regulated entity creates, receives, keeps or transmits. The Privacy and Breach Notification Rules go wider; this one does not reach PHI held on paper or spoken aloud. Its text sits in 45 CFR Part 160 and in Part 164, Subparts A and C.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Choice of gauge
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge and complications · CPT D3 k56 k55 k68 · PBT II.J II.I · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A 16 G needle is used on a small forearm vein and a large hematoma forms. According to WHO Chapter 3, what is the effect of a needle that is too large, and of one that is too small?
opciones: Too large tears the vein and causes bleeding; too small damages the cells and invalidates whole-cell tests
Too large damages the blood cells and invalidates the tests; too small tears the vein and causes a hematoma
Too large slows the draw so the sample clots in the tube; too small lets air into the tubing of the set
Too large causes haemoconcentration of the sample; too small causes the tube to lose its vacuum early
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says that a needle too large for the vein will tear it and cause bleeding, a hematoma, while a needle too small damages the blood cells as the sample is taken and invalidates tests that need whole cells, hemoglobin or free plasma. It adds that transfusion collection needs a larger gauge than blood drawing, and Table 3.1 reserves 16 to 18 G for blood donation.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient faints in a crowded corridor where there is no room to lie down. What is the alternative position?
opciones: Seated forward, with the head between the knees
Seated upright, with the chin lifted and eyes closed
Standing, leaning back against the corridor wall
Seated backwards, with both legs stretched out flat
preguntas.explicacion: The person is normally kept lying down for at least ten to fifteen minutes, ideally somewhere cool and quiet. Where that cannot be arranged, the alternative given is to sit the person forward with the head between the knees; tight clothing round the neck is loosened either way.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for visual deficits
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient with poor sight is about to be handed the printed fasting instructions. Which check does the guidance put on the person handing them over?
opciones: That she brought her glasses or contact lenses and has them on before she starts to read
That she can read the top line of the sheet aloud before the phlebotomist lets her keep it
That a relative able to read the sheet for her is present in the room while it is explained
That the sheet has been read to her aloud first, because print alone is not enough at her age
preguntas.explicacion: The measures for a visual deficit are practical and go in order. Light the room well, with light on your own face and as little glare as possible; check that the person actually brought the glasses or lenses she needs and is wearing them; make handwriting clear and keep printed type big enough in an easy face. Nothing there asks the patient to prove she can read, or puts a relative in charge of reading for her. Reading everything aloud belongs to low vision, where print has stopped working at any size.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the show-me method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4I evaluate understanding · CMA I.A.6.d · 2027 I.A.6.d · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a blood thinner correctly states the dose and the times. What should still be done?
opciones: Use the show-me method and have him demonstrate the dose with the pills
Accept the correct statement, since saying it right proves he can do it
Repeat the same explanation once more and end the teaching there
Have him write the dose and the times down and file the note in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: Research behind the show-me method found that many patients who state the timing and amount of a new or changed medicine correctly still get the dose wrong when asked to demonstrate it. Having the patient show the dose with the actual pills catches what words alone hide.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Granular Leukocytes and Agranular Leukocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A differential on a patient with a bacterial infection shows 80 percent of one leukocyte type. Which type is normally the most common and rises with bacterial infection?
opciones: Neutrophils, normally 50 to 70 percent of leukocytes
Lymphocytes, normally 20 to 30 percent of leukocytes
Monocytes, normally 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
Eosinophils, normally 2 to 4 percent of leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Neutrophils are the most common leukocyte at 50 to 70 percent of the count; they respond fast to infection, prefer bacteria, and high counts point to bacterial infection or inflammation, as well as burns and stress. Lymphocytes are second at 20 to 30 percent and rise with viral infections; monocytes are 2 to 8 percent and eosinophils 2 to 4 percent, rising with allergies and parasitic worms.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Media Mail
preguntas.subtema: Media Mail · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office is shipping loose-leaf medical reference pages and their binders to a satellite clinic on the cheapest eligible service. What must staff know about it?
opciones: Media Mail takes those pages and binders, and every package may be opened for inspection
Media Mail takes any office paper, and the contents of a package are never examined
Ground Advantage takes those pages, and packages of paper are exempt from inspection
Priority Mail takes those pages, and books are the only content it accepts by weight
preguntas.explicacion: Medical loose-leaf pages and binders are on the short list of what qualifies for Media Mail, along with books, printed music, recordings and manuscripts. The trade for the low price is that every Media Mail package may be opened and inspected, and anything ineligible inside means somebody pays the higher postage.

preguntas.subtema: Correction period · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A violation is due to willful neglect. What period does the regulation give for correcting it before the top penalty tier applies?
opciones: Thirty days from the first date the entity knew, or would have known with reasonable diligence
Sixty days from the first date the entity knew, matching the deadline for breach notification
Ten working days from the first date the entity knew, as with new hire vaccination records
Six years from the first date the entity knew, matching the documentation retention period
preguntas.explicacion: Tier three catches willful neglect that gets put right inside a window of 30 days. The clock starts the day the entity, or the business associate acting for it, first knew of the violation, or would have known of it had reasonable diligence been used. Let that window close without correcting and the case drops into the fourth tier, the costliest one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix A: Check and Record Temperatures; Appendix B; Test!: Resolving Problems
preguntas.subtema: Daily temperature checks · CPT D1 1E · PBT IV.B.2 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.d · RMA III.C.3.e
preguntas.pregunta: A waived site's refrigerator has a digital data logger with an alarm. How often should staff still check and record its temperature?
opciones: Daily, and the testing room's temperature before the room is used
Weekly, since the logger records continuously and alarms on excursions
Only when the alarm sounds or a control result falls out of range
Monthly, when the QC records are reviewed for shifts and trends
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigerator, freezer and storage-room temperatures are checked and recorded daily, and the testing room's temperature before the room is used, regardless of whether the unit has an alarm, a chart recorder, a data logger or a continuous monitoring system. The log is one of the records a site keeps; refrigerator or freezer failure is a problem to document, report to the person overseeing testing, and correct.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part D (Drug Coverage) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who put off joining a Medicare drug plan asks when a late enrollment penalty starts to apply.
opciones: Once she has gone sixty-three days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once she has gone thirty days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once eight months have passed since her job-based health coverage ended
Once her first seven months of Medicare eligibility have run out entirely
preguntas.explicacion: The way to dodge the Part D penalty is to join a drug plan when Part A or Part B first starts, and never to spend sixty-three days or more with no creditable drug coverage, meaning coverage similar in value to Part D. Someone on a limited income and with limited resources who qualifies for Extra Help pays no late enrollment penalty at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: P-wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What does the P wave on a tracing represent?
opciones: Depolarization of the atria, right side first, then left
Repolarization of the atria, left side first, then right
Depolarization of the ventricles, right first, then left
Repolarization of the ventricles, from apex toward base
preguntas.explicacion: The P wave is atrial depolarization. Because the impulse is born in the sinoatrial node, which sits in the right atrium, the first half of the wave belongs to the right atrium and the second half to the left. A P wave of abnormal shape or size can point to enlargement of one of the atria.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Lung Exam", Function: Auscultation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a(1) · RMA III.F.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a loud, high-pitched musical sound heard over the neck on inspiration. What is that?
opciones: Stridor, which points to obstruction of the upper airway
Wheezing, a continuous sound of 400 Hz or more from the airways
Rhonchi, a low-pitched sound from fluid or mucus in the airways
Crackles, brief popping sounds made by air passing secretions
preguntas.explicacion: Stridor is loud, high-pitched and musical, and it comes from obstruction of the upper respiratory tract; heard on inspiration it points above the thoracic inlet. Wheezes are continuous sounds at 400 Hz or above; rhonchi are continuous but around 200 Hz or less; crackles are brief, discontinuous and non-musical. A patient reporting wheeze often has stridor.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4c: Common Metric Conversions in Health Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(1) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7
preguntas.pregunta: A label reads 0.25 g and the order is written in milligrams. Which equivalence applies?
opciones: 1 gram equals 1000 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 1000 micrograms
1 gram equals 100 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 100 micrograms
1 gram equals 1000 micrograms, and 1 milligram equals 1000 grams
1 gram equals 10 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 10 micrograms
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is built on units of ten, so converting is a matter of moving the decimal point. The equivalences to hold in the head are that a gram is 1000 milligrams and a milligram is 1000 micrograms, alongside a liter being 1000 milliliters. Confusing milligrams with micrograms is a thousand-fold error, which is exactly why the microgram symbol is written out as mcg on an order.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.1 The Language of Epidemiologists, Patterns of Incidence
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k42 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Influenza rises every winter in the northern hemisphere. Why is it wrong to call that an epidemic each year?
opciones: The seasonal rise is expected, and an epidemic exceeds what is expected
The seasonal rise is worldwide, and an epidemic is limited to one country
The seasonal rise lasts months, and an epidemic lasts only a few days
The seasonal rise is caused by a virus, and an epidemic requires a bacterium
preguntas.explicacion: An epidemic is a larger than expected number of cases in a short time within a region, so the word rests on what was expected. Influenza climbing every winter is the expected pattern; a winter with an unusually large number of cases in particular regions is what qualifies. Going worldwide would make it a pandemic.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Eating Right for Chronic Kidney Disease — Protein
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with chronic kidney disease heard he should stop eating protein entirely. How should that be corrected?
opciones: Some patients moderate protein, and too little brings malnutrition
Protein is stopped completely once kidney disease has been diagnosed
Protein is raised sharply so the kidneys have material to repair with
Protein is left untouched, since only sodium affects the kidneys
preguntas.explicacion: Protein builds and maintains muscle, bone, skin, organs and blood, and helps wounds heal. As the body uses it, waste is left for the kidneys to clear, so some patients are asked to keep protein moderate. Cutting it too far causes malnutrition, which is why the balance is set with a dietitian rather than by the patient.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting; and Plasma Anticoagulants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74 post-procedural bleeding) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on daily low-dose aspirin keeps bleeding at the puncture site longer than expected. What does aspirin do to hemostasis?
opciones: It is an antiplatelet; it inhibits the aggregation of platelets
It is a thrombolytic; it converts plasminogen into plasmin
It inactivates factor X, in the same way antithrombin does
It blocks vitamin K, so the liver makes fewer clotting factors
preguntas.explicacion: Aspirin is an antiplatelet drug that is very effective at inhibiting platelet aggregation, which is why it is given during heart attacks and strokes and sometimes daily at low dose to people at cardiovascular risk. Thrombolytics such as tissue plasminogen activator work on plasminogen instead, and antithrombin works on factor X and on the conversion of prothrombin.

preguntas.subtema: Dental code set · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice adds a dental service line and asks which code set covers it, and who keeps that set up to date. What is the answer?
opciones: The dental procedure code set, kept by the American Dental Association
The dental procedure code set, kept by the federal health department
The procedure coding system for inpatients, kept by the federal health department
The common procedure coding system, kept by the American Medical Association
preguntas.explicacion: For dental services the regulation names the Code on Dental Procedures and Nomenclature. The American Dental Association is the body that maintains it and distributes it. The federal health department keeps the diagnosis set, the inpatient procedure set, and the level of the common procedure system that covers supplies and equipment.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label: Calories; and The Percent Daily Value
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What calorie level are the % Daily Values on the Nutrition Facts label based on?
opciones: 2,000 calories a day, used as general nutrition advice
2,500 calories a day, used as general nutrition advice
1,800 calories a day, the average for adult women
The calorie level the shopper enters in the MyPlate Plan tool
preguntas.explicacion: The footnote of the panel states that the percentages rest on a 2,000-calorie day, offered as general advice. A given person may need more or fewer calories depending on age, sex, height, weight and activity, which is why the label points readers to a personalized plan for their own estimate.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 7 to 10
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.J · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's order calls for every tube on the chart. Which one is filled ninth?
opciones: The pale yellow tube used for tissue typing and DNA work
The purple top tube used for hematology and cross-match
The light gray top tube used for glucose determinations
The light green tube used for chemistry panels on plasma
preguntas.explicacion: Position 9 belongs to the pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube, whose listed uses are HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies. EDTA is number 8 and the fluoride/oxalate tube number 10, so the ACD tube falls between them; the light green PST comes earlier, at position 7.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, Health Plans
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: Which TRICARE plans are the premium-based ones available worldwide?
opciones: TRICARE Reserve Select, Retired Reserve and Young Adult
TRICARE Prime, Prime Remote and the Family Health Plan
TRICARE Select, Select Overseas and Prime Remote Overseas
TRICARE Prime, the Prime demonstration and TRICARE For Life
preguntas.explicacion: The premium-based group, the one available worldwide, holds TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Young Adult and TRICARE Retired Reserve. The plans listed for the United States are Prime, Prime Remote, the Uniformed Services Family Health Plan option, a Prime demonstration, Select and TRICARE For Life; the overseas group holds Prime Overseas, Prime Remote Overseas and Select Overseas.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Maximum Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does the maximum out-of-pocket limit that the federal government sets each year actually do?
opciones: It caps the cost sharing for covered care given inside the network
It caps the premium a plan may charge one family over the year
It caps what a provider outside the network may bill the patient
It caps the deductible a plan may apply to one single service
preguntas.explicacion: The federal figure is the ceiling on what one individual or family can be made to pay in cost sharing over the plan year for covered care taken in network, and it applies to most kinds of plan. A plan's own out-of-pocket limit may be lower than that ceiling. Premiums and balance-billed charges are never part of it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicare Advantage (Medicare Part C); and Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is a Medicare Advantage Plan?
opciones: A private plan under contract with Medicare that delivers Part A and Part B benefits
A private plan sold by insurers that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare
A federal plan that replaces Part A for patients treated in a network of hospitals
A state plan that covers premiums and deductibles for people with low income
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Advantage, also called Part C, comes from private companies under contract with Medicare to deliver every Part A and Part B benefit, usually with drug coverage on top; the types include health maintenance organizations and preferred provider organizations. Private insurance that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare is Medigap, and help with premiums for people on a low income comes through Medicaid.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Normal and Abnormal Complete Blood Count With Differential", section White Blood Cell Tests; Platelet Tests
preguntas.subtema: WBC reference interval · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.10.b.(4)(b) (2027: b.(5)) · RMA III.C.4.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which total white blood cell count falls within the usual adult reference interval?
opciones: 7,800 cells/µL
3,200 cells/µL
13,500 cells/µL
150,000 cells/µL
preguntas.explicacion: The adult white blood cell count is usually 4,500 to 11,000 cells/µL, so 7,800 is within range. A count of 3,200 would be leukopenia and 13,500 leukocytosis; 150,000 is the lower limit of the platelet reference interval, not a white cell figure. Spurious values occur too: white cell clumping can lower the count, while platelet clumps and fibrin clumps can be counted as white cells and raise it.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services and Effective Communication Provisions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA II.B.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: A relay call comes through 7-1-1 to book a fasting draw. How must the front desk handle it?
opciones: Accept it and treat it exactly like any other telephone call
Ask the caller to attend in person, since relay is not private
Transfer it to the interpreter line before a booking is made
Take the booking only once a hearing relative confirms it
preguntas.explicacion: The telecommunications relay service, free and nationwide, is reached by dialling 7-1-1 and puts communications assistants in the middle for people with hearing or speech disabilities. A covered entity is required to accept calls placed through relay and video relay services, and whoever answers treats them exactly like other calls; the assistant explains how the system works.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.5 Homeostasis, Positive Feedback
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Cervical stretching during labor triggers oxytocin, which strengthens the contractions and stretches the cervix further. What does that loop illustrate?
opciones: Positive feedback, which intensifies a change until a definite end point
Negative feedback, which intensifies a change until a definite end point
Positive feedback, which reverses a change back toward the normal range
Negative feedback, which reverses a change back toward the normal range
preguntas.explicacion: Positive feedback pushes a change further instead of reversing it, and in the body that is normal only where the loop has a definite end point. Labor is one example: stretching, oxytocin and stronger contractions feed each other until the baby is born. The clotting cascade after a wound is the other standard example.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label: Nutrients
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of nutrients does the Nutrition Facts label flag as ones to get less of?
opciones: Saturated fat, sodium and added sugars
Saturated fat, sodium and dietary fiber
Total fat, total sugars and total carbohydrate
Cholesterol, protein and trans fat
preguntas.explicacion: The label separates the nutrients to get less of, which are saturated fat, sodium and added sugars, from the ones to get more of: calcium, dietary fiber, iron, potassium and vitamin D. Fiber belongs to the second list. Total sugars and trans fat carry no percentage at all, so they are not part of either guide.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 8: Conduct Brown Bag Medicine Reviews
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMA I.A.6.d · 2027 I.A.6.d · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to bring everything to a brown bag medicine review. What does that include?
opciones: Prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, supplements and herbals
Prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs, but not vitamins or supplements
Prescriptions only, since the rest are not entered in the medication list
Prescriptions and the pill organizer, but not the original containers
preguntas.explicacion: The review covers every prescription, every over-the-counter product, every vitamin, supplement and herbal medicine, plus topicals, liquids, injections and inhalants, and the pills in both their original bottles and any organizer. Seeing the actual containers is what reveals whether and why medicines are being taken wrong.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Small quantities of capillary blood
preguntas.subtema: Shared glucometers · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k104 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A glucometer and its lancet platform are used for several inpatients during a round. What does best practice require?
opciones: Dedicate it to one patient, or clean and disinfect it between uses
Change the lancet and wipe the platform with a dry gauze pad
Rinse the platform under running water at the end of the round
Keep it in a clean bag between patients, which avoids contact
preguntas.explicacion: For small quantities of capillary blood the equipment is single-use: a lancet, or a retractable one, and a platform or glucometer either dedicated to a single patient for the whole stay or, between patients, wiped free of every visible trace of dirt and then disinfected with alcohol. The reason is on the record: hepatitis has reached patients where a glucometer or its platform was passed from one person to the next without that reprocessing.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the assistant to point out the PR segment on a printed strip. How does it differ from the PR interval?
opciones: The interval takes in the P wave and the segment starts after it
The segment takes in the P wave and the interval starts after it
The interval reaches the T wave and the segment reaches the QRS
The segment lies above the baseline and the interval below it
preguntas.explicacion: A segment is the stretch between two waves; an interval is a segment plus one or more waves. So the PR segment runs from the end of the P wave to the start of the complex, while the PR interval begins with the P wave, which is why it is the useful measurement.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Step 7 and Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection"; and WHO Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010) (NBK138665)
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error: haemolysis · CPT D3 k9 k59 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory rejects a sample as hemolyzed. Which collection practices are recognized causes of hemolysis?
opciones: Pressing the syringe plunger, shaking the tube, and a short draw in the gray tube
Leaving the tourniquet on for more than one minute, and drawing the tubes in the wrong sequence
Using a 21 G needle in an adult, and inverting the citrate tube three to six times
Preparing the skin with povidone iodine, and labeling the tubes away from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Pressing the plunger raises the risk of hemolysis, Table 2.3 warns that a short draw in the fluoride tube may cause hemolysis, and vigorous shaking or overmixing of the tube produces hemolysis. A long tourniquet causes hemoconcentration, the wrong sequence causes additive carry-over, iodine raises potassium, and three to six gentle inversions is the correct handling of the citrate tube.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Food Allergies: Major Food Allergens — label declaration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4)
preguntas.pregunta: A parent of a child with a peanut allergy asks where the allergen appears on a package. Where does the law require it?
opciones: In the ingredient list itself, or in a "contains" statement beside it
In the ingredient list itself, or in the Nutrition Facts panel below it
In a warning box on the front of the package, in bold red type
In the ingredient list only, since "contains" statements are voluntary
preguntas.explicacion: The food source of a major allergen has to be declared at least once, either inside the ingredient list or in a statement right after or next to it, worded like "Contains wheat, milk, and soy". The rule also forces the specific tree nut, fish species or shellfish species to be named.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD asks what those letters mean. Which expansion is correct?
opciones: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a disease of the lungs
Chronic obstructive peptic disorder, a stomach disease
Congenital obstructive pulmonary defect, a lung disease
Chronic occlusive peripheral disease, an artery disease
preguntas.explicacion: COPD is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the long-standing lung condition that makes breathing hard. The look-alike abbreviations belong elsewhere: PUD is peptic ulcer disease, CHD is congenital heart disease and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, the arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Complications and Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Complications: haematoma · CPT D3 3Q 3L k70 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E9 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A hematoma forms at a site where the technique looked correct throughout. Which omission is the likely explanation?
opciones: Pressure was not kept up during and after the needle came out
Pressure was kept up too long after the needle had come out
The tourniquet was released before the needle was withdrawn
The site was cleaned with alcohol rather than povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma can form when too little pressure is kept up during the draw and after it, which is why the gauze is taped down to give continuous pressure. Releasing the band before the needle comes out is the correct order, and alcohol is the preferred antiseptic for a routine draw.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Oxygen Therapy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2B.14 · CCMA 3B4 · CMA I.A.6.d
preguntas.pregunta: A nasal cannula is running at 4 L/min. Roughly what oxygen concentration does that deliver?
opciones: Somewhere in the 24% to 40% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Somewhere in the 40% to 60% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Close to 50%, which is what a face tent reaches at high flow
Between 60% and 80%, the range of a mask with a reservoir bag
preguntas.explicacion: A cannula runs at one to six liters a minute and gives roughly 24% to 40% oxygen; the figure is approximate because how much room air is mixed in depends on the patient's rate and depth of breathing. A simple face mask at 5 to 10 L/min gives about 40% to 60%, a face tent up to 15 L/min about 50%, and a nonrebreather at 10 to 15 L/min more still.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (equipment compatibility and expiration dates)
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality checks · CPT D3 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A box of evacuated tubes is found to be past its expiration date. What two problems do expired tubes present?
opciones: Reduced ability to draw blood in, and additives that may have degraded
Loss of sterility of the stopper, and a gel that no longer separates serum
A higher risk of hemolysis, and colors that no longer match the order of draw
Cracks in the plastic, and an anticoagulant that turns plasma into serum
preguntas.explicacion: Expiration dates matter because expired vacuum tubes have a decreased capacity to aspirate blood and their additives may be degraded, so even small deviations can affect the results. The other options mix real problems from the tube collection review, such as a missing anticoagulant or a lost vacuum after uncapping, with effects the chapter does not attribute to expiry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram" (NBK549803)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches a normal T wave?
opciones: Upright in I, II and V3 through V6, and inverted in aVR
Upright in aVR, and inverted in I, II and V3 through V6
Upright in all twelve leads, without a single exception
Inverted in V1 and V2 always, and upright in every other lead
preguntas.explicacion: Ventricular repolarization normally writes an upward T wave in I, II and V3 to V6, an inverted one in aVR, and something variable in V1 and V2. Height counts too: under 5 mm in the limb leads and under 10 mm in the chest leads.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Electronic notice delivery · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice takes its first new patients through an online intake before any in-person visit. What does the notice rule require?
opciones: An electronic notice sent automatically with the first request, and an attempt at a return receipt
A paper notice mailed within thirty days of the electronic request for service being received
An electronic notice posted on the web site only, since online patients can read it there
A telephone call reading the notice aloud, since electronic delivery cannot be acknowledged
preguntas.explicacion: Where the first delivery of service happens over the Internet, by e-mail or in some other electronic way, the notice goes out electronically, automatically and at the same moment as the patient's first request for service, and the provider has to make a good faith effort to get back a return receipt or another response transmission. Any web site describing the entity's services or benefits must carry the notice prominently as well.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Understanding telehealth technology options
preguntas.subtema: Consent before a video visit · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: When does the telehealth guidance say informed consent for a video visit has to be obtained?
opciones: Before the appointment, alongside a platform that meets the privacy requirements
At the start of the appointment, once the clinician has confirmed who the patient is
Only where the session will be recorded or a third party is to be brought into it
After the appointment, when the visit is documented as having been done by video
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may worry about privacy and about data security, both over what they share during a visit and over home devices that collect their health data. Providers are told to deliver telehealth from private locations, to apply safeguards that are reasonable to the protected health information, to use a platform that meets the privacy requirements, and to obtain informed consent from the patient before the telehealth appointment.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, introduction and Section 9
preguntas.subtema: Nothing left blank · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What must a safety data sheet do when its preparer finds no information for a required element?
opciones: Say that no applicable information was found for that element
Leave that element blank, which is read as not applicable
Copy the entry from a sheet for a similar product in the family
Move the element to section 16 with the other information
preguntas.explicacion: Silence is not allowed. Where the preparer finds no relevant information for a required element, the sheet must say outright that nothing applicable was found, and section 9 repeats the rule for the physical and chemical properties: an item that is not relevant, or not available, carries a note saying so for that property. A blank leaves the reader unable to tell an absent hazard from an unresearched one.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 preparation step 3 and collection step 13
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen procedure · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 witness · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: How is the donor's hand washing handled in a federal workplace drug test collection?
opciones: The donor washes under the collector's direct observation before the void
The donor washes in private, since observing would violate the donor's dignity
The donor washes only after handing over the specimen container
The donor uses gloves instead, because soap can adulterate the specimen
preguntas.explicacion: The collector gives the donor a way to wash their hands and watches while they do it; where the collection area has no sink, a waterless cleanser or a moist towelette stands in. Soap, cleanser and disinfectant are cleared out of the restroom as possible adulterants, which is why the washing happens beforehand and under the collector's eye. Once the specimen has changed hands the donor may usually wash again.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Geriatric Care Special Needs Assessment", Issues of Concern: Functional Status
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA 2B.2 · CMA I.A.4.g
preguntas.pregunta: A geriatric intake separates basic from instrumental activities of daily living. Which pair is right?
opciones: Bathing and dressing are basic; shopping and handling finances are instrumental
Shopping and cooking are basic; bathing and toileting are instrumental activities
Walking and feeding are basic; grooming and bladder control are instrumental
Driving and using the telephone are basic; dressing and feeding are instrumental
preguntas.explicacion: Basic activities are self-care: bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, feeding oneself, and control of bladder and bowel. Instrumental ones are what independent living needs on top of that: taking medicines, shopping, cooking, transport, finances, housework and the telephone. The Katz index measures the first group and the Lawton scale the second.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule
preguntas.subtema: Identity theft protection · CCMA 5F · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4C k63 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many elements must a written identity theft prevention program contain under the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Four: identify, detect, respond and update
Three: identify, detect and report to the police
Five: identify, detect, respond, update and insure
Two: identify the red flags and train the staff on them
preguntas.explicacion: The program must include reasonable policies for identifying the red flags of identity theft in day-to-day operations, procedures designed to detect the flags it identified, the actions to take when one is detected, and a way of keeping the program current against new threats. A red flag is a suspicious pattern, practice or activity signaling possible identity theft, such as an identification document that does not look genuine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: ST-Segment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A tracing shows the ST segment sitting 2 mm above the baseline in two chest leads. How is that graded?
opciones: Abnormal: a shift of 1 mm or more at the J point counts
Normal: a shift counts only past 5 mm at the J point
Normal: the segment is measured at the peak of the T wave
Abnormal only when the segment falls below the baseline
preguntas.explicacion: The ST segment should sit level with the PR interval. The measurement is taken at the J point, the corner between the QRS complex and the segment, and a shift of 1 mm or more in either direction is abnormal. The medical assistant reports the tracing to the provider and does not read it out as a diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note describes a threatened condition that in the end did occur. How is it coded?
opciones: As a confirmed diagnosis, just as if it had been documented outright
As threatened, using the index subentry for that term where it exists
As threatened, since that is the word the provider used in the record
Not at all, because a threatened condition is an uncertain diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: A condition the note calls impending or threatened is coded as a confirmed diagnosis if it did in fact occur. Only when it did not occur does the coder look for a subentry for impending or threatened, and where no such subentry exists the underlying conditions are coded instead of the threatened one.

preguntas.subtema: Medicare Advantage records · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract. For how long must it keep the books and records behind that contract?
opciones: Ten years, so that the accounting and the services can be audited and inspected
Seven years from the date of service, as with orders and certifications in Part B
Five years, as with the medical records a hospital keeps to take part in Medicare
Six years from creation, as with the documentation the privacy standards require
preguntas.explicacion: Every retention period in this area belongs to a different rule, and the trap is borrowing one for another. The Medicare Advantage contract obliges the organization to keep its books, records and other evidence of accounting for ten years, enough for CMS to audit the finances and to inspect the quality and timeliness of the services.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 6.5 Fractures: Bone Repair
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(2) (2027 I.C.6.g(2)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A broken bone is manipulated back into position without surgery. What is that procedure called?
opciones: Closed reduction, as opposed to open reduction
Open reduction, as opposed to closed reduction
Internal fixation, as opposed to closed reduction
Debridement, as opposed to open reduction
preguntas.explicacion: Setting a broken bone into its natural position by hand, with no incision, is a closed reduction; in an open reduction the fracture is exposed surgically and the bone reset that way. The words describe how the bone is put back, not how badly it broke, and both may be followed by immobilization.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Adult BMI Calculator: BMI Category Ranges
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: An adult has a body mass index of 41.2. How is that classified?
opciones: Class 3 obesity, also called severe obesity, from 40.0 upward
Class 2 obesity, the band that runs from 35.0 to 39.9
Class 1 obesity, the band that runs from 30.0 to 39.9
Obesity without a class, since the classes stop at 40.0
preguntas.explicacion: Obesity is divided into three classes: 30.0 to 34.9, 35.0 to 39.9, and 40.0 or greater, the last of which is also called severe obesity. Naming the class matters because risk climbs with it: high cholesterol, diabetes of type 2, blood pressure that runs high. The index is still a screening measure, not a diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, The Golgi Apparatus
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which organelle sorts and packages the products that arrive from the rough endoplasmic reticulum?
opciones: The Golgi apparatus, a stack of flattened membranous discs
The peroxisome, a stack of flattened membranous discs
The nuclear envelope, a stack of flattened membranous discs
The intermediate filament, a stack of flattened membranous discs
preguntas.explicacion: The Golgi apparatus looks like a stack of flattened discs and works like a post office. One side receives vesicles from the rough endoplasmic reticulum, the contents are sorted and modified, and new vesicles leave from the other side, either to another part of the cell, out of the cell, or as new lysosomes.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient adds up what she has spent and asks which of it will never count toward her out-of-pocket limit.
opciones: Her premium, any balance-billed charge, and care the plan does not cover
Her copayments and the deductible she paid earlier in the same plan year
Her in-network coinsurance on services the plan does in fact cover for her
Her deductible and the coinsurance she paid at a preferred provider's office
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit is the most a person could pay in a coverage period for her share of covered services, after which the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount. It never includes the premium, balance-billed charges or care the plan does not cover, and some plans leave out out-of-network payments and certain other expenses as well.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Precautionary Statements
preguntas.subtema: Precautionary statements · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What are the four types of precautionary statements found on a Hazard Communication label?
opciones: Prevention, response, storage and disposal
Physical, health, environmental and unclassified
Identification, composition, handling and transport
Danger, warning, caution and notice
preguntas.explicacion: Precautionary statements describe the measures recommended to minimize or prevent harm from exposure, storage or handling, and they come in four types: prevention, to limit exposure; response, for spills, emergencies and first aid; storage; and disposal. Physical, health and environmental are the three hazard groups of the GHS; identification, composition, handling and transport are SDS section titles; and Danger and Warning are the only two signal words, so caution and notice do not exist in this system.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine collection - infants (003417), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Infant bag collection · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(e) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A mother is sent home to collect urine from her 6-month-old with an adhesive bag. Which instruction is correct?
opciones: Wash the genital area, apply the bag, put a diaper over it, check the baby often and remove the bag once urine collects
Apply the bag over the unwashed skin so the adhesive holds better, and leave it in place until the next diaper change
Wash the genital area, apply the bag without a diaper so it is visible, and leave it on for exactly 24 hours
Wash the genital area with an antiseptic, pass a small catheter into the bladder and drain the urine into the bag
preguntas.explicacion: The area around the urethra is washed with the soap or wipes the provider recommends, the bag is opened and stuck on (the whole penis inside it, or over the labia), a diaper goes on over the bag, and the baby is checked often. Active infants can displace the bag, so extra bags are useful. The urine is emptied into the container without touching its inside and, at home, kept in a plastic bag in the refrigerator. Catheterization is done by a provider.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment; Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A prenatal clinic wants one body measurement to follow nutritional status. Which one is reported as the measurement of choice in pregnancy?
opciones: Mid-upper arm circumference, taken at the marked midpoint of the arm
Waist circumference, taken over each hip bone at the mid-axillary line
Body mass index, worked out again from height and weight at each visit
Triceps skinfold, taken with calipers just above the midpoint of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Mid-upper arm circumference helps grade how severe malnutrition is, and in the pregnant population one study reports it as the anthropometric measurement to choose. It is taken standing, with the arm hanging freely and the muscles unflexed, the tape snug at the marked midpoint of the arm and not pressed into the skin.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Actions for Invalid or Questionable Test Results; Recording Results
preguntas.subtema: Result beyond reportable range · CPT D5 5G · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: A glucose meter displays 'HI' instead of a number for a patient who looks unwell. What is the correct handling of this result?
opciones: Treat it as a value beyond the reportable range and follow the manufacturer's steps for such results; a number is not reported
Record 600 mg/dL, the top of the meter's range, as the patient's result and notify the provider of a critical glucose
Record 'HI' as the final result in the log and file it, since the meter has already interpreted the reading correctly
Treat the display as a meter malfunction, switch to a second meter and report whichever numeric value it produces
preguntas.explicacion: When a quantitative result is above or below the reportable range of the instrument, or the system prevents the display of a result, the test is repeated, which may require a new sample; the manufacturer's instructions describe how to handle values that cannot be measured accurately, and results are reported only after the problem is identified and resolved. A display like 'HI' is not a number to transcribe, and an invalid or unacceptable first result is still recorded before retesting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking a beta blocker has a resting rate of 54 with a normal sinus tracing. Which link does the material draw?
opciones: Beta blockers are on the outside list of causes of a slow sinus rhythm
Beta blockers are on the outside list of causes of a fast sinus rhythm
Beta blockers widen the QRS complex past 120 milliseconds on the strip
Beta blockers lengthen the QT interval past 440 milliseconds on the strip
preguntas.explicacion: The extrinsic causes of sinus bradycardia are largely a drug list: digoxin, clonidine, adenosine, the calcium channel blockers and the beta blockers among others, alongside vagal stimulation. The tracing is recorded and reported, and no medicine is stopped on the patient's own say-so.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Treatment / Management: Epinephrine
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 k82 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which epinephrine dose is described for an adult in anaphylaxis?
opciones: 0.3 to 0.5 mL of the 1:1,000 concentration, by intramuscular injection
0.01 mg/kg, or 0.15 mg, which is the figure quoted for a small child
1 mg of the 1:10,000 concentration, repeated every 3 to 5 minutes
0.1 mg of the 1:10,000 concentration, infused over 5 to 10 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The adult dose is 0.3 to 0.5 mL of 1:1,000 epinephrine given intramuscularly, and it may be repeated every 5 to 10 minutes while symptoms persist. The pediatric figure is 0.01 mg/kg or 0.15 mg. The 1:10,000 concentration belongs to the intravenous route, and 1 mg every 3 to 5 minutes is the dose used during cardiac arrest.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(a)(3), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A swab reaches the laboratory carrying the patient's name and ID number, but nothing on it says where on the body it came from. Under CLIA's specimen labeling policy element, what is missing?
opciones: The specimen source, which must appear on the label when appropriate
The test requested, which must be written on every specimen container
The collector's signature, which is required on all microbiology specimens
The date of birth, which is mandatory on the label for every specimen
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(a)(3) requires the laboratory's labeling procedure to cover the patient's name or unique identifier and, when appropriate, the specimen source; for a swab the site is exactly that appropriate case. The regulation does not put the test name, the collector's signature or the date of birth on the container itself, although the requisition must carry the sex and the age or date of birth.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(2)(ii)(M), Special practices
preguntas.subtema: The biosafety manual · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C2 k109 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: In a laboratory that works with concentrated HIV or HBV, what does the standard require of the biosafety manual?
opciones: It is reviewed and updated at least yearly, and staff must read and follow it
It is written once at start-up and kept for the duration of employment
It is posted at the door with the name and phone of the laboratory director
It takes the place of the exposure control plan for employees in that area
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(ii)(M) asks for a biosafety manual to be prepared or adopted, then reviewed and updated periodically, at least once a year and more often if needed. It also puts a duty on the staff: they are advised of the potential hazards, and they have to read the practices and procedures they are given and then follow them. What goes on the door is the warning sign of (g)(1)(ii)(A). All of this sits on top of the exposure control plan, which paragraph (c) still demands.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, overview
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: How long does a fainting episode usually last, and what is the typical recovery?
opciones: Usually less than a couple of minutes, with quick recovery
Usually 10 to 15 minutes, with gradual recovery over an hour
Usually a few seconds, with confusion for several minutes afterwards
Usually 5 to 10 minutes, with weakness for the rest of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting is a brief loss of consciousness from a drop in blood flow to the brain, most often lasting less than a couple of minutes, with quick recovery; the medical name is syncope. Ten to fifteen minutes is how long the person is kept lying down afterwards, and confusion on waking points to a seizure rather than syncope.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Blood in an arm vein drains toward the heart against gravity. Which feature of the vein keeps it from running back down?
opciones: One-way valves set inside the lumen of the vein
A thicker muscular coat than the artery beside it
The perforating branches that reach the deep veins
The venae comitantes that travel with the artery
preguntas.explicacion: Veins carry one-way valves in the lumen, and their job is to stop the blood draining backwards on its way up to the heart. The wall holds less muscle than an artery, which is why a vein stretches and acts as a reservoir. Perforating veins link the superficial system to the deep one, and the venae comitantes are the paired veins that run with the forearm arteries.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Streptococcal Pharyngitis", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Rapid strep testing · CPT D4 4G · PBT V.C.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.10.d.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b
preguntas.pregunta: A child scores in the intermediate range on a clinical decision rule for sore throat. What testing follows?
opciones: Rapid antigen detection testing, the primary diagnostic tool for group A streptococcus
A sputum culture with Gram stain, the primary diagnostic tool for a pharyngeal infection
No testing at all, since an intermediate score is treated the same as a low-risk score
Blood cultures drawn from two sites, the primary diagnostic tool for streptococcal disease
preguntas.explicacion: History and examination alone cannot diagnose group A streptococcal pharyngitis, so a clinical decision rule goes together with rapid antigen detection, which is highly specific. Patients at intermediate or high risk get the rapid test; those at low risk need nothing further. The rapid test may be skipped under age 3, since both the infection and rheumatic fever are rare that young.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A soft fatty lump under the skin is reported as a lipoma. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning inflammation
A root meaning muscle plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning enlargement
preguntas.explicacion: Lip- and lipo- name fat, and so does adip-; the ending -oma is a tumor. The endings that crowd around it say something else entirely: -itis is inflammation, -megaly is enlargement and -osis is an abnormal condition. Muscle is my- or myo-, so a tumor built on that root would be a myoma.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet · CPT D3 k60 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: What does a tourniquet do that makes venipuncture easier?
opciones: It presses on the limb and blocks the venous return for a while, so the veins show up
It stops arterial inflow so that the veins below it empty and become straighter
It disinfects the skin above the site, so the alcohol contact time can be shortened
It keeps the blood from clotting in the tubing of a winged collection set
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet puts a passing pressure on the limb and blocks the flow artificially, which helps the phlebotomist find the veins, and cites studies showing the veins dilate and gain surface area right after a tightly placed tourniquet. It must not stop arterial flow, it has no antiseptic role, and it has nothing to do with the air in butterfly tubing.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Water in diet — Food Sources
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(g) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(g) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient counts his evening beers toward his daily fluid. How should that be corrected?
opciones: Alcohol is a diuretic, so it makes the body release water rather than add it
Alcohol counts as fluid, but only about half of the volume in the glass
Alcohol counts fully as fluid, the same as soup, milk, tea or juice
Alcohol is a diuretic, so it should be matched with a salt tablet each time
preguntas.explicacion: Soup, milk, tea, coffee, soda, juice and drinking water all add to body water, and some water also arrives in solid food or is made during metabolism. Alcohol is the exception: it acts as a diuretic and drives water out of the body, so it does not add to the day's fluid at all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Surgical Fire Safety", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k80 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.j
preguntas.pregunta: What are the three components of the fire triangle in a procedure room?
opciones: A source of fuel, an oxidizer and a source of ignition
