A fuel source, an oxidizer and a conductive surface
A fuel source, an ignition source and a smoke plume
An oxidizer, an ignition source and a grounding pad
preguntas.explicacion: A surgical fire needs fuel, an oxidizer and a source of ignition together. Fuel means the drapes and towels, the sponges and dressings, the tapes, the gowns, the ointments and the alcohol; oxygen, nitrous oxide and plain room air are the oxidizers; and ignition comes from light sources, lasers, electrocautery, sparks off drills and burrs, defibrillators and glowing charred tissue.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(g)(1), (g)(3) and (g)(5), Personal representatives
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks for the lab results of their 8-year-old child. How does HIPAA treat the parent?
opciones: As the child's personal representative, acting as the individual for that PHI
As a third party who needs the child's own signed authorization first
As a family member entitled only to a verbal summary at the visit
As a personal representative only after a court has appointed the parent as guardian
preguntas.explicacion: Under section 164.502(g) a personal representative is treated as if they were the individual. For an unemancipated minor that representative is the parent, the guardian or a person acting in loco parentis who holds authority under applicable law to make health care decisions, and it covers the PHI relevant to that role, with no court appointment needed. The exceptions are services the minor may lawfully consent to alone, and situations of abuse or endangerment where the entity may refuse to treat the person as representative; state law can widen or narrow parental access.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A report describes one structure as cranial to another. Which directional term is used for that same idea?
opciones: Superior, toward the head end of the body
Inferior, away from the head end of the body
Anterior, toward the front of the body
Posterior, toward the back of the body
preguntas.explicacion: Most directional terms travel in pairs that mean the same thing: superior and cranial point toward the head, inferior and caudal away from it, anterior and ventral name the front, and posterior and dorsal the back. That is why the hand belongs to the superior extremity and the foot to the inferior one.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Germs and Hygiene — How can I protect myself and others from germs?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k169 disease prevention education · CMA I.A.6.c · 2027 I.A.6.c · RMA III.A.1 infection control · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long she should scrub when washing her hands at home. What is the answer, and when does it matter most?
opciones: At least 20 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
At least 20 seconds, but only after using the toilet or changing a diaper
At least 10 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
At least 60 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
preguntas.explicacion: Hands are scrubbed well and often, for at least 20 seconds. The moments that matter most are the ones where germs are picked up or passed on: before, during and after handling food, before eating, around caring for someone sick or treating a wound, after the toilet or diapers, after coughing or sneezing, and after animals or garbage.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k149 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: In lead V6 the ventricular complex writes a deep downward deflection instead of the usual tall upright wave. What is suggested?
opciones: Record from a position further to the left, out at V7
Record from a position further to the right, back at V1
Drop V6 one intercostal space and run the tracing again
Raise the standardization and run the tracing again
preguntas.explicacion: V6 is expected to write a tall upward wave. When a deep S appears there instead, the guidance is to move out to the left and take V7, hunting for a pattern whose main deflection points up. Moving an electrode down a space is not part of that advice.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(a), (b) and (d), Notification to individuals
preguntas.subtema: Breach notification deadline · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: A breach of unsecured PHI has just been discovered. How fast must the covered entity notify the individuals affected?
opciones: No more than 60 calendar days after discovery, and without unreasonable delay
Within 30 days after discovery, matching the right-of-access deadline
Within 90 days after discovery, the period a substitute web notice stays posted
By the end of the calendar year, regardless of the number of individuals
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.404 requires notice to every individual whose unsecured PHI was accessed, acquired, used or disclosed, or is reasonably believed to have been. Two limits apply at once: no unreasonable delay, and 60 calendar days from discovery as the outer edge. A breach counts as discovered the first day it is known, or would have been known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member other than the one who caused it. Written notice travels by first-class mail, or by e-mail if the person agreed to that; where contact details are missing for 10 or more people, a substitute posting on the website or a media notice runs for 90 days.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Conduction System of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: In which order does a normal impulse travel through the conduction system?
opciones: SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV bundle, AV node, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, AV bundle, Purkinje fibers, bundle branches
SA node, AV node, bundle branches, AV bundle, Purkinje fibers
preguntas.explicacion: The impulse starts in the sinoatrial node, spreads across both atria to the atrioventricular node, is held there briefly, then runs down the atrioventricular bundle, splits into the right and left bundle branches, and finishes in the Purkinje fibers that reach the ventricular muscle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dilation and Curettage", Equipment: Dilators
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a)
preguntas.pregunta: Three sets of cervical dilators are on the shelf. Which description fits the Pratt dilator, the one commonly preferred?
opciones: A long tapered tip, so the least mechanical force opens the canal
A cuffed shaft with a sharper taper, the cuff stopping the advance
A short blunt end and sizes that climb fast, so more force is used
A blunt short tip, which suits a long vaginal lumen better than most
preguntas.explicacion: Pratt dilators taper along a long tip, which is why the operator needs the least mechanical force and why they are usually chosen. The cuff belongs to the Hank. The short blunt end and the quick jumps in size belong to the Hegar, which may be too short to cross a long vaginal lumen.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(B) and (C), specimen containers
preguntas.subtema: Specimens that can puncture · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A specimen stiff enough to puncture its primary container is being shipped to a reference laboratory. What does the standard add?
opciones: A secondary container that resists puncture as well as leakage, and is labeled
A secondary container that closes and holds fluids, with no puncture requirement
A red bag around the primary container, which substitutes for the outer label
A label stating which portion of the primary container remains contaminated
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii) builds up in three steps. The specimen goes in a container that will not leak. If the outside of that container becomes contaminated, subparagraph (B) puts it inside a second leakproof container that is labeled or color-coded. And subparagraph (C) adds the extra requirement here: when the specimen itself could puncture the primary container, the secondary one must be puncture-resistant on top of everything else. The label naming the contaminated portion is for equipment being serviced, under (g)(1)(i)(H).

preguntas.subtema: Activity review · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which administrative safeguard makes a practice review, on a regular basis, records of system activity such as the audit logs and the reports on access and on security incidents?
opciones: Information system activity review, part of the security management process
Audit controls, the technical standard that makes the system record the activity
Evaluation, the periodic check of whether the policies still meet the standards
Security reminders, the periodic updates sent to every member of the workforce
preguntas.explicacion: Audit controls make the system capable of recording and examining activity; the duty to actually read what it recorded is a different, required specification of the security management process, called information system activity review. A practice can satisfy one and fail the other.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is counted as nonverbal communication?
opciones: The pace at which the conversation is carried
The words chosen so the receiver understands
The feedback message returned to the sender
The handout given in the patient's own language
preguntas.explicacion: Nonverbal communication covers facial expressions and body language, the tone of voice and the pace of the conversation, and it may carry more weight than the words themselves. Choosing words the receiver understands is the definition of verbal communication; the return message is the feedback step of the cycle; a handout is written communication.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Issues of Concern: Children
preguntas.subtema: Consent for minors · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: When a parent authorizes a procedure for their 9-year-old, what is that authorization called?
opciones: Informed permission, since consent itself belongs to the patient
Implied consent, because the parent brought the child in for care
Proxy consent, given under a durable power of attorney for the child
Waived consent, the category used when a patient cannot sign for themselves
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically those under 18, cannot give informed consent, so the parent or legal guardian permits the treatment and the process is named informed permission instead. Implied consent is inferred from the patient's own situation, such as an emergency. A waiver is when the patient voluntarily gives the consent process up, and a power of attorney is a document an adult signs about their own care.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(8) (2027 I.C.6.g(8)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: An older man reports a weak stream and trouble emptying the bladder, and benign prostatic hyperplasia is suspected. What underlies that growth?
opciones: A loss of balance between prostatic cell proliferation and cell death
A loss of balance between urine production and bladder wall thickness
An infection that ascends from the perineum into the prostate gland
A malignant transformation of the epithelial cells of the prostate
preguntas.explicacion: Benign prostatic hyperplasia arises when the balance between proliferation and apoptosis in the prostate tips toward growth, leaving more periurethral epithelial and stromal cells. Testosterone acting on prostate tissue is part of the picture: men castrated before puberty do not develop it. Benign means it does not invade or spread.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: malpractice
preguntas.subtema: Malpractice · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is malpractice defined as a legal term?
opciones: Professional negligence: breaching the duty to follow accepted professional standards
Any error a professional makes while a patient is under that professional's care
An intentional act by a professional that the client did not agree to beforehand
A breach of the written contract between a professional and the paying client
preguntas.explicacion: Malpractice is professional negligence, the tort that arises where a professional breaks the duty owed to a client, and that duty is generally to keep to the professional standards that are generally accepted. Every other element of a negligence tort still has to be shown too: the duty, the breach, both kinds of causation and the damages. Doctors and lawyers are the commonest defendants.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k157 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: At what speed does the paper run during a standard recording?
opciones: 25 mm per second, so one large square is 0.2 seconds
50 mm per second, so one large square is 0.2 seconds
25 mm per second, so one large square is 0.4 seconds
10 mm per second, so one large square is 0.5 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The paper moves at 25 mm per second, with time on the horizontal axis and voltage on the vertical one. At that speed one second is divided into five large squares, so each large square stands for 0.2 seconds. Any other speed changes what every square on the grid is worth.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Follow up after telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether every one of her follow-ups can now be booked by video. How does the workflow guidance answer that?
opciones: It can bridge between office visits, but some care needs one
It replaces office visits once the patient is set up on it
It is limited to the first visit for any new problem
It is used only when the patient cannot travel to the office
preguntas.explicacion: Virtual care is put forward as a bridge that sits between visits to the office: part of the care still calls for the patient to be in the room, and it is the mixture of the two that supports care management. Nothing in the guidance limits virtual visits to new problems or to patients who cannot travel.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Flash Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Flash (immediate-use) steam sterilization was originally defined with which cycle?
opciones: An unwrapped item at 132 °C for 3 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, gravity displacement
An unwrapped item at 121 °C for 3 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, gravity displacement
A single-wrapped item at 132 °C for 10 minutes at 15-16 pounds of pressure, prevacuum
An unwrapped item at 135 °C for 30 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, prevacuum
preguntas.explicacion: The original definition was an unwrapped object held at 132 °C for three minutes at 27 to 28 pounds of pressure in a gravity displacement machine. The item goes in an open tray or a rigid container designed to let steam in fast. Many facilities now stretch the exposure to four minutes at that temperature so the lethality matches a wrapped load.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Peripheral Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Why do so many organs receive fibers from both the parasympathetic and the sympathetic division?
opciones: One stimulates and the other inhibits, and the balance maintains homeostasis
Both stimulate together, and the doubled signal maintains homeostasis
One carries sensory fibers and the other motor fibers to the same organ
One works during the day and the other only during sleep at night
preguntas.explicacion: Many visceral organs receive fibers from both autonomic divisions, and the two work against each other: where one stimulates, the other inhibits. That antagonistic relationship is not waste but a brake and an accelerator on the same organ, and the balance between them is what holds the internal setting steady.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Which spores are used in the biological indicator for a steam sterilizer, and which for dry heat and ethylene oxide?
opciones: Geobacillus stearothermophilus for steam, and Bacillus atrophaeus for dry heat and ethylene oxide
Bacillus atrophaeus for steam, and Geobacillus stearothermophilus for dry heat and ethylene oxide
Geobacillus stearothermophilus for both, incubated at two different temperatures by method
Bacillus atrophaeus for both, with a longer incubation used for the steam sterilizer strips
preguntas.explicacion: Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores, incubated at 55 to 60 °C, monitor steam, and also gas plasma of hydrogen peroxide and peracetic acid in liquid form; ethylene oxide and dry heat use Bacillus atrophaeus, incubated at 35 to 37 °C. These spores are chosen because they resist the agent more than the bioburden found on the devices themselves.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: assault; and Wex: battery
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(5) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist raises a needle toward a patient who has clearly refused, and the patient recoils. No contact occurs. Which tort fits?
opciones: Assault, since the patient was put in apprehension of imminent contact
Battery, since raising the needle is itself an offensive act toward them
False imprisonment, since the patient was held in the chair by the act
Negligence, since a reasonable phlebotomist would not have done that
preguntas.explicacion: Assault means an intentional act leaving another person in reasonable fear of contact that is imminent and either harmful or offensive. No physical injury has to occur; the actor must have intended the contact and the victim must have been aware it might happen. Battery is the contact itself, so with no contact there is no battery.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 ECG Abnormalities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What is an ectopic focus?
opciones: A site outside the sinus node that fires and gives an early beat
A site inside the sinus node that fires later than it ought to
A block that keeps the impulse from leaving the AV node itself
A pause that follows every second beat written on the tracing
preguntas.explicacion: It is an area other than the sinus node, sometimes part of the conduction system and sometimes ordinary contractile cells, that starts an impulse and produces a premature contraction. Ischemia, caffeine, digitalis and heavy autonomic stimulation can set it off.

preguntas.subtema: Order documentation retention · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders a Part B diagnostic test. How long must documentation of that written order be kept and made available to CMS?
opciones: Seven years from the date of service
Five years from the date of service
Six years from the date of service
Three years from the date of service
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment regulation puts the duty on both sides. Whoever furnishes the Part A or Part B service that was ordered or certified, referred or prescribed, and the physician or eligible professional who ordered it, must each hold the documentation for seven years from the date of service and give CMS or a Medicare contractor access on request. That documentation includes the NPI of the ordering professional.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.3 Wound Assessment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: Drainage covers about half of the dressing at a change. How is the amount documented?
opciones: Moderate, the band that runs from a quarter to three quarters of the dressing
Minimal, the band that runs from a quarter to three quarters of the dressing
Scant, since the wound is moist though no measurable drainage reached the dressing
Copious, since the tissue is filled with fluid and exudate soaked the dressing
preguntas.explicacion: The scale runs by how much of the dressing the exudate covers. Scant means the wound is moist though nothing measurable reaches the dressing; minimal is under a quarter of it; moderate is a quarter to three quarters, with the tissue wet; and large or copious is more than three quarters, with the tissue filled with fluid.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2)(4) / 2027 F.1.d(1)(3) · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient who uses sign language comes for a draw without an interpreter. Under the ADA effective-communication rules, what may the clinic NOT do?
opciones: Require the patient to supply her own interpreter, family or friend
Offer video remote interpreting, if the connection meets the standards
Exchange written notes for a short, simple question at the counter
Let a companion interpret when the patient asks and the companion agrees
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA puts the duty of effective communication, interpreters included, on the covered entity, and the entity may not tell a patient to bring somebody along to interpret. VRI is an allowed choice where it works, notes will do for simple exchanges, and a companion may interpret in two situations only: an emergency with an imminent threat, or where the patient asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Description
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth modalities · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a non-face-to-face exchange with her doctor that took place through the practice's online portal. What is that called?
opciones: An e-visit, one of the ways of communicating with a provider through telehealth
A virtual check-in, a brief real-time exchange lasting ten minutes or less
Remote patient monitoring, which sends clinical data from a device to the provider
Store-and-forward, where an image is uploaded for a specialist to read later
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth means medical services taken from a provider elsewhere in the country over audio and video, and in some cases over audio alone. Two of the named routes are e-visits, exchanges that are not face to face and that usually run through the practice's online portal, and virtual check-ins, short live exchanges that usually last ten minutes or less.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Eating Disorders: What are the types of eating disorders?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 patient education · CMA I.A.6.g(5) · 2027 I.A.6.g(5) · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with normal weight admits to vomiting after large meals. Which disorder does that pattern fit, and what follows?
opciones: Bulimia nervosa; weight is often normal, so the disorder is easy to miss
Bulimia nervosa; weight is always far below normal by the time it is seen
Anorexia nervosa; purging after bingeing is what defines that diagnosis
Binge-eating disorder; purging is one of its listed symptoms as well
preguntas.explicacion: Bulimia nervosa is bingeing followed by purging, whether by vomiting or laxatives, and sometimes by fasting or over-exercising. Someone with it may be overweight, of normal weight, or a little underweight, so appearance rules nothing out. Eating disorders are medical conditions, not a lifestyle choice, and treatment exists.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A documented condition has no code of its own, and the Alphabetic Index shows the abbreviation NEC. What does that point the coder to?
opciones: The other specified code for that condition in the Tabular List
The unspecified code for that condition, which NOS also stands for
The excluded code above the note, which is never reported alongside
The manifestation code, which is bracketed and sequenced second
preguntas.explicacion: NEC stands for not elsewhere classifiable and, in both the Index and the Tabular List, represents the other specified code: it is used when the record has detail for which no specific code exists. NOS stands for not otherwise specified and is the equivalent of unspecified, which is used when the record does not have enough detail to be more precise.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 4: Vaccine Information Statements
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(3)
preguntas.pregunta: A parent declines one of the vaccines due at a visit. What does the record need to show?
opciones: That the statement was provided, and that the vaccine was refused
That the statement was provided, with no note of what was declined
That the vaccine was refused, with no need to note the statement given
No further entry, because a dose not given creates no record at all
preguntas.explicacion: Documenting that the Vaccine Information Statement was provided is required by law before each dose. The statement gives an outline for discussing benefits and risks, and further detail of the discussion should also go in the record, including a refusal to receive a vaccine. That documentation may reduce potential liability if the patient later develops the disease. Copies and translations come from immunization programs.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Body Planes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A radiologist describes a cut made exactly down the middle of the body into equal right and left halves. What is that plane called?
opciones: The midsagittal or median plane
The parasagittal or lateral plane
The frontal or coronal plane
The axial or cross-sectional plane
preguntas.explicacion: Any vertical cut that separates right from left is sagittal. When it runs straight down the midline and leaves equal halves it earns the extra name midsagittal or median; when it leaves unequal sides it is parasagittal. Front from back is the frontal plane, and upper from lower the transverse.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(iii); OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Latex Allergy
preguntas.subtema: Latex allergy and glove alternatives · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist develops hives after wearing the gloves supplied at work. What must the employer provide?
opciones: Glove liners, powderless or hypoallergenic gloves, or a similar alternative, readily accessible
A prescription antihistamine and a return to the same gloves once the hives have settled
A respirator, because latex protein becomes airborne when powdered gloves are removed
A transfer to duties without patient contact until the allergy has been evaluated
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(iii) wants PPE in the right sizes readily accessible, and specifically that a worker allergic to the gloves normally supplied find within reach glove liners, powderless gloves, hypoallergenic gloves or an equivalent alternative. OSHA's latex allergy page warns against assuming those alternatives are latex-free, and among the options it lists gloves that are synthetic, low in protein or free of powder; it also notes that washing the hands once the gloves come off removes powder and latex left on the skin. The glove exception of (d)(3)(ix)(D) belongs to volunteer blood donation centers alone.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the note means by an upper respiratory infection. Which everyday term matches it?
opciones: The common cold
A stomach bug
A urinary infection
A skin infection
preguntas.explicacion: URI stands for upper respiratory infection, which is another name for the common cold. Translating it out loud is part of the job, because the abbreviations the staff use daily are not the words a patient uses. A urinary tract infection is UTI, one letter away and a completely different problem.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrioventricular Block", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: What defines a first-degree atrioventricular block?
opciones: A PR interval over 200 ms, constant, with every P conducted
A PR interval over 200 ms, lengthening, with a dropped beat
A PR interval under 120 ms, constant, with every P conducted
A PR interval over 300 ms, constant, with every third P dropped
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing is actually blocked here: the impulse is only slowed, so each P wave still reaches the ventricles in a one to one relationship and the PR interval stays constant above 200 ms. Past 300 ms it is called marked, and the P wave may be buried in the preceding T wave.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: When may a Schedule II prescription be sent to the pharmacy by facsimile and serve as the original?
opciones: For a compounded parenteral infusion, a long-term care resident, or a hospice patient
For any Schedule II drug, as long as the paper original follows within seven days
For any Schedule II drug, as long as the practitioner signs the facsimile by hand
Never, because a Schedule II prescription is always handed over on paper instead
preguntas.explicacion: Three situations let a facsimile stand as the original written prescription: a Schedule II narcotic compounded for direct parenteral infusion into a vein, a muscle, subcutaneous tissue or the intraspinal space; a Schedule II prescription for a resident of a long-term care facility; and one for a patient in a certified or licensed hospice program, noted as such on it. The facsimile is then kept as the original record.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A wound specimen for culture reaches the laboratory in a non-sterile cup that barely covers the bottom. Which two requirements did the collection miss?
opciones: A sterile leak-proof container, and enough material for the full microbiological and serological work
A sterile leak-proof container, and a fixative to hold the organisms until the plates are poured
A tightly lidded transport container, and enough material for the full biochemical work-up
A sterile leak-proof container, and a site chosen away from where the organism is most likely to be
preguntas.explicacion: Specimens for culture belong in sterile, leak-proof containers, and the quantity has to be enough for the whole microbiological and serological examination, not just the first plate. The site is chosen from the clinical picture and from where the causative organism is most likely to be found. A fixative would defeat the purpose, since the organisms have to stay alive.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Stool ova and parasites exam (003756), How the Test is Performed; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Ova and Parasite Test, What happens during an ova and parasite test?
preguntas.subtema: Stool from a diaper · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) / (2)(e) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A stool specimen for parasites is needed from a child in diapers. How should the parent collect it?
opciones: Line the diaper with plastic wrap placed so urine and stool stay apart, then move the stool to the container
Scrape the stool directly from the absorbent diaper into the container, avoiding the wet areas
Apply an adhesive collection bag over the perianal area, as is done for infant urine samples
Place plastic wrap loosely over the toilet bowl, held by the seat, as for an older child
preguntas.explicacion: For a child in diapers the diaper is lined with plastic wrap positioned to keep urine and stool from mixing, which gives a better sample; the stool is then transferred to the clean container and returned as directed. Plastic wrap over the toilet bowl is the method for patients who use the toilet, and the adhesive bag is a urine device. The container is labeled with name, date and time.

On the outer leg, about 4 to 5 cm above the ankle
On the inner leg, about 10 to 15 cm above the ankle
On the inner thigh, about 4 to 5 cm above the knee

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following is a HIPAA covered entity?
opciones: A health care provider that transmits claims electronically
An outside computer repair company that services the lab's servers
A pharmaceutical sales representative who visits the clinic
An accredited agency that conducts patient satisfaction surveys
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule binds covered entities, which are health plans, health care providers that transmit health information electronically, and clearinghouses, and it binds business associates as regards a covered entity's PHI; a clearinghouse acting as a business associate follows a narrower set of sections. Outside computer repair firms, survey agencies, equipment companies and pharmaceutical representatives are examples of third parties who reach PHI only through business associate arrangements, which require written satisfactory assurances.

preguntas.subtema: How the SDS is arranged · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which sections of a safety data sheet are meant to be read first, for quick general information about a chemical?
opciones: Sections 1 through 8, from identification to exposure controls
Sections 9 through 11 and 16, the technical and scientific ones
Sections 12 through 15, the ones OSHA does not enforce at all
Sections 4 and 5 alone, on first aid and on fighting the fire
preguntas.explicacion: The sheet is built in blocks. Sections 1 through 8 carry the general information: identification, the hazards, what is in the product, how it is handled safely, and the emergency control measures such as fire fighting; they are written for someone who needs the answer fast. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold the technical and scientific detail, and sections 12 through 15 are there for consistency with the international system, their content left to other agencies.

preguntas.pregunta: What did comparison of dedicated phlebotomy teams with staff who have broader duties show?
opciones: The teams reached lower rates of contamination, even with equal training
The teams reached higher rates of contamination, despite equal training
The two groups performed identically once both had the same training
The teams drew more tubes per hour but hemolyzed more specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratory staff and members of phlebotomy teams reach lower contamination rates than staff whose responsibilities are broader, even where the training received is the same. It is one of the arguments for formal training and supervised practice in this procedure.

preguntas.pregunta: A group of clinics ran a scheme, knowingly and willfully, to obtain money from a health benefit program. Which law is aimed at exactly that?
opciones: The criminal health care fraud statute, which reaches any such program
The civil False Claims Act, which asks for no specific intent at all
The Anti-Kickback Statute, which reaches payment made for referrals
The exclusion statute, which keeps offenders out of those programs
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal health care fraud statute covers knowingly and willfully carrying out, or trying to carry out, a scheme to defraud a health care benefit program or to obtain its money by false pretenses, and it is punished with fines, imprisonment or both. The other laws named reach false claims, remuneration for referrals and participation itself.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)

preguntas.pregunta: A nurse inoculates a blood culture bottle straight from the syringe used for the draw, then fills the second bottle with 1 mL. Which two points of technique were missed?
opciones: Changing the needle before inoculating the bottle, and inoculating about 10 % of the medium volume (3 mL into 30 mL)
Cleaning the bottle bung with alcohol only after inoculation, and inoculating about 50 % of the medium volume
Warming the bottle to 37 °C before inoculation, and inoculating at most 1 mL so that the medium is not diluted
Drawing the culture after the first antibiotic dose, and inoculating 10 mL into each bottle regardless of medium volume
preguntas.explicacion: For blood cultures the syringe needle is swapped before the bottle is inoculated, so skin flora do not ride in; the rubber bung is wiped with iodine both before the injection and again afterwards; and the volume drawn runs to roughly 10 % of the medium, 3 mL into a 30 mL bottle for instance. Ask the laboratory which media suit the organism suspected, and take the set before antimicrobials start whenever that is possible.

preguntas.pregunta: Which information must appear on the label of a reagent, control or calibration material under CLIA?
opciones: Identity and strength, storage requirements, and preparation and expiration dates
The CLIA number of the laboratory and the initials of the person who opened it
The manufacturer's lot number and the date of the last calibration verification
The name of the test, the reportable range and the critical values for the analyte
preguntas.explicacion: Reagents, solutions, culture media, control and calibration materials must be labeled with their identity and, when it matters, titer, strength or concentration; their storage requirements; their preparation and expiration dates; and any other information needed for proper use. Materials past their expiration date, deteriorated or of substandard quality must not be used. Writing the date opened on a new vial is the waived-site habit that supports this.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss is being booked for her first video visit. Which planning question does HHS file under meeting patient needs?
opciones: How the practice will support patients with a disability such as hearing or vision loss
How the practice will bill for the extra minutes a supported appointment will take up
How the practice will judge whether the request suits a telehealth appointment at all
How the practice will know that its staff are comfortable using the new technology
preguntas.explicacion: Meeting patient needs takes in how the office will work out what accommodations a patient might need, how and when reminders reach her, how support will be arranged for a patient whose disability is a hearing loss or a loss of vision, and how a caregiver or other helper will be supported through the visit. Judging appropriateness is a scheduling question; comfort with the technology is a staffing one.

preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument gives the most accurate recumbent length in an infant?
opciones: An infantometer, which holds the baby in position while the length is read
A horizontal length scale, the flexible scale laid alongside a small baby
A stadiometer laid on its side, with the head and the feet against it
A nonstretchable tape measure run from the crown of the head to the heel
preguntas.explicacion: Length in a baby who cannot stand is taken lying down, and the instrument matters. The horizontal length scale is a flexible scale for that job; the infantometer does the same with greater accuracy because it holds the infant securely in position. For a child who can stand, the preferred instrument is the stadiometer, upright as it was built to be.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance

preguntas.pregunta: How far does the primary payer go before a claim passes to the secondary payer?
opciones: It pays up to the limits of its own coverage and sends on the rest of the balance
It pays the whole allowed amount and sends on only the patient's own cost sharing
It pays half of the allowed amount and sends on the remaining half of the balance
It pays up to the limits of the secondary plan and sends on the unpaid remainder
preguntas.explicacion: The primary payer covers up to the limit of its own coverage and hands what is left over to the secondary payer. Where the secondary payer does not pick that remainder up, the patient can be left owing it. This ordering of payment is what coordination of benefits means. Where the group health or retiree coverage is the one paying second, it may pay nothing at all until the patient has signed up for Part B.

preguntas.pregunta: A colleague asks where to place the stethoscope for a blood pressure reading. Where is the brachial pulse felt?
opciones: Just medial to the biceps tendon
Just lateral to the biceps tendon
Directly over the median cubital vein
Just medial to the pronator teres muscle
preguntas.explicacion: The brachial artery crosses the fossa medial to the biceps tendon, and that is where the pulse is palpated and where the stethoscope goes when blood pressure is measured. Knowing the line matters at the bedside, because the artery lies under the same small triangle used for venipuncture.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Reservoirs and Carriers
preguntas.subtema: Carriers · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist skips hand hygiene after a patient with an infection and carries the organism to the next patient without becoming infected herself. In epidemiologic terms she is which of these?
opciones: A passive carrier, contaminated but not infected
An active carrier, infected but without symptoms
A biological vector, in which the pathogen reproduces
A nonliving reservoir, like contaminated water
preguntas.explicacion: A carrier is someone who can pass a pathogen on without showing symptoms. A passive carrier is contaminated and can move the pathogen mechanically to another host without being infected, and the microbiology text uses exactly this example: the health worker who does not wash her hands after seeing an infected patient. An active carrier is infected, symptoms or not, and may transmit during incubation or convalescence. Vectors are animals, usually arthropods, and a reservoir is where a pathogen normally lives.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k9 k63 · D1 1K k31 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What can poor infection control during a draw produce, besides risk to the worker?
opciones: Bacterial infection where the needle went in, and contaminated specimens
Bacterial infection where the needle went in, and a lost tube vacuum
Hemolysis of the specimen, and degradation of the tube additive
A prolonged clotting time, and a falsely low platelet count reported
preguntas.explicacion: Weak infection prevention and control practices can lead to bacterial infection at the site where the needle was inserted and to contamination of the specimens themselves. It is one reason the cleaned site is not touched again and single-use devices are never shared between patients.

preguntas.pregunta: What information belongs on the label of each forensic sample container?
opciones: A unique code, the location, the date and time, and the collector's signature
A unique code, the patient's diagnosis, and the ordering provider's signature
The requested analysis, the courier's name, and the receiving clerk's signature
The unique code alone, so that the container carries no identifying detail
preguntas.explicacion: Each container label carries a unique identification code, the place, the date and time it was collected, the collector's name and signature, and a witness's signature where there is one. What analysis is wanted and who receives it belong on the chain of custody form instead, and each evidence bag needs a form of its own.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Quality Control and Lab Safety; StatPearls, "Hemoglobin A1C", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: A1C interferences · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.c.(5) · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with known sickle cell trait has a point-of-care A1C ordered to screen for diabetes. What limitation applies?
opciones: Hemoglobin variants alter the relationship between A1C and average glucose, so plasma glucose criteria should be used for diagnosis
Sickle cell trait shortens the fasting requirement, so the A1C is valid only if the patient has fasted at least 8 hours beforehand
The A1C is unaffected because the assay measures glucose bound to plasma proteins rather than to the hemoglobin itself
The point-of-care A1C should simply be repeated in three months, when a new population of red cells has formed
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions that change hemoglobin concentration or red cell turnover, including hemoglobin variants such as sickle cell trait, hemolytic anemia, recent transfusion, kidney failure and pregnancy, distort the link between A1C and average glycemia. In those patients plasma glucose criteria are used for diagnosis instead, and monitoring may rely on blood glucose meters, continuous monitoring or fructosamine. Iron deficiency can push the A1C falsely high.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System: How We Conduct Case Surveillance
preguntas.subtema: Communicable disease reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.a / 2027 E.5.a · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Who legally requires a positive result for a notifiable condition to be reported, and to whom?
opciones: State law requires it to the health department; notifying the CDC is voluntary
Federal law requires it to the CDC; notifying the health department is voluntary
State law requires it to the CDC, which then informs the health department
Accreditation standards require it to both, on the same reporting form
preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals, providers and laboratories report positive results or diagnosed cases to the appropriate health department under state disease reporting laws, and that case reporting is mandatory. What the state and local health departments then send on to the CDC is de-identified data about confirmed cases, and that notification is voluntary.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Adolescent development, Information
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · CMA F.1.c(7)(b) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: Which cognitive change marks adolescence?
opciones: Understanding abstract ideas, including moral philosophy
Understanding conservation of quantity in a taller glass
Understanding object permanence when a parent walks out
Understanding deferred imitation of an absent person
preguntas.explicacion: Adolescents come to understand abstract ideas, which includes higher mathematics and the development of moral philosophies about rights and privileges. Conservation is a concrete-operations skill, and object permanence and deferred imitation belong to the sensorimotor and preoperational periods.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Using a cane; and Cane Basics
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being fitted for a cane. Which two kinds are the main ones?
opciones: A cane with a single tip and a cane with four prongs at the bottom
A cane with a single tip and a cane with a wheel at the bottom
A cane with two prongs and a cane with four prongs at the bottom
A cane with a padded tip and a cane with a folding shaft and grip
preguntas.explicacion: The two main types are the single-tip cane and the four-pronged one, and the choice turns on how much support the patient needs. Whichever is used, the tip or all four prongs have to be flat on the ground before any weight goes onto the cane. Marked pain, weakness or poor balance points to crutches or a walker instead.

preguntas.fuente: DOL, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical Assistants
preguntas.subtema: Administrative responsibilities · CCMA 1 k2 · CMA II.F.4 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 1 k2 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which duties does the Bureau of Labor Statistics list on the administrative side of a medical assistant's job?
opciones: Answering telephones, scheduling appointments and restocking office supplies
Setting the fee schedule and negotiating the practice's contracts with health plans
Auditing the practice's claims for fraud and reporting findings to the payer
Approving which staff members may open the electronic health record system
preguntas.explicacion: Medical assistants take on both administrative and clinical work, and often specialize in one of the two. On the administrative side the Handbook describes helping patients get to grips with their insurance and obtain coverage: filling out forms, coding the information, ringing the companies about a bill. It also lists keeping medical and office supplies inventoried and restocked, answering the telephone and scheduling appointments.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Osteoporosis in Females", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(2) (2027 I.C.6.g(2)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why is osteoporosis often called a silent disease?
opciones: It is usually not diagnosed until a fracture has already occurred
It is usually not diagnosed until the joints become visibly enlarged
It is usually not diagnosed until the patient reports constant bone pain
It is usually not diagnosed until blood calcium falls below its range
preguntas.explicacion: Osteoporosis means porous bone: low bone mineral density with changes in the microarchitecture that make fractures easy. It produces nothing the patient can feel, so the diagnosis often arrives only after a break of the hip, spine or wrist. Bone mineral density testing is what finds it before that.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Patient instructions · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the scheduler whether she can take her video visit while she drives to work. What does the patient guidance say?
opciones: She should not, since a telehealth visit is not to be taken while driving or on errands
She may, if she switches to audio only and pulls over whenever an examination is required
She may, provided the car has hands-free equipment and the connection is private
She should not, unless the appointment is a brief exchange of ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: The tips for a successful visit tell the patient to stay on track, which means leaving food and drink alone while the visit lasts, and to stay safe, which means not taking a visit at the wheel or in the middle of errands. She is also told to sign on early so she can message or telephone the office if the video refuses to start, and to be patient when the clinician runs late.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Data Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Processing mail · CCMA 5O · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7D · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Incoming mail includes lab reports for several patients. What does the Privacy Rule require of the way it is handled?
opciones: Reasonable safeguards protecting it against uses the rule does not permit
An accounting entry for each report before it is filed in the record
A business associate agreement with the carrier that delivered the mail
A written authorization from each patient whose report arrived that day
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity has to keep safeguards in place, administrative, technical and physical alike, that protect against uses and disclosures the rule does not permit and that hold incidental ones down. What counts as reasonable shifts with the size of the entity and the nature of its business; the examples given are shredding documents that hold PHI before throwing them out, and keeping records under lock and key or behind a pass code.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Adapting collection · CPT D3 3C k55 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I VI.G · CCMA 3E4 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient due for a draw is on several blood thinners. Which team member is suggested as a resource?
opciones: The pharmacist, over the medicines that could complicate the draw
The radiographer, over imaging of the arm before the puncture
The dietitian, over the fasting the patient was asked to observe
The phlebotomy supervisor, over which stopper color to select
preguntas.explicacion: Where a patient is taking blood thinners or other medicines that could bring on unwanted complications, the pharmacist is the person to consult. For difficult venous access the case goes instead to a certified phlebotomist, and everyone involved is expected to know the medical history.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors (Storage and temperature)
preguntas.subtema: Cold activation of factor VII · PBT IV.A.3 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(5) INR (2027: b.(8)) · RMA III.C.3.f
preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time was refrigerated overnight as whole blood before testing. What effect is described for cold storage of whole blood?
opciones: Cold activation of factor VII, which can shorten the measured prothrombin time
Loss of factor VII activity in the cold, which can prolong the measured prothrombin time
No effect on the PT, since whole blood is stable for 7 days when it is kept refrigerated
Hemolysis of the red cells, which affects only the partial thromboplastin time result
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood for prothrombin time should be kept at 18 to 24 °C; refrigeration is avoided because cold can activate factor VII and shorten the clotting time. Cold storage of whole blood also lowers factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, which can mimic hemophilia A or von Willebrand disease. Samples are acceptable for less than 24 hours, and cold may be tolerated for other tests once the plasma has been separated.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: At which point in the life of a needle do sharps injuries most commonly happen?
opciones: Between the use of the device and its disposal
While the needle is being pushed into the vein
While the packaging is being opened at the tray
After the container has been sealed for collection
preguntas.explicacion: Injuries from sharps commonly occur between the use of a needle or similar device and its disposal, which is the window that recapping, disassembly and a distant sharps container all lengthen. Discarding into a puncture-resistant container straight away markedly reduces these injuries.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient receives ABO-incompatible blood. What happens to the transfused red cells, and which organ is at risk of failing?
opciones: Antibodies clump them; hemolysis then overloads the kidneys with hemoglobin
They sickle and lodge in narrow capillaries, starving the brain of oxygen
They are phagocytized by macrophages in the spleen, which fails under the load
Platelets coat them and form thrombi that occlude the coronary arteries
preguntas.explicacion: In a transfusion reaction, antibodies bind the foreign antigens on the donated erythrocytes and clump them together, a process called agglutination; the clumps block small vessels, and as they are degraded (hemolysis) their hemoglobin floods the blood. The kidneys cannot clear that load and the patient can rapidly develop kidney failure. Sickling and thrombi are other disorders entirely.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A hospice patient being cared for at home asks what she may be charged for a medicine given to control her pain.
opciones: A copayment of up to $5 for each drug prescribed for pain or symptom control
A copayment of up to $35, the ceiling that applies to a month of covered insulin
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most services covered by Part B
Five percent of the approved amount, which is the share for inpatient respite care
preguntas.explicacion: Covered hospice services cost the patient nothing under Part A. What she may still owe is up to $5 in copayment on each prescription drug, and on similar products used at home to relieve pain and control symptoms, plus five percent of the amount approved for respite care given as an inpatient. The $35 ceiling belongs to covered insulin under Part B.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 809
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187 · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient disputes a medical debt in writing within the 30-day window. What must the collector do?
opciones: Stop collection until it mails the patient verification of the debt
Stop collection permanently and close the account as uncollectible
Continue collection while it asks the provider for the chart notes
Report the dispute to a consumer reporting agency within five days
preguntas.explicacion: When the consumer disputes the debt in writing inside the 30 days, or asks for the original creditor's name and address, the collector must stop collecting the disputed portion until it has obtained either verification of the debt or a copy of the judgment and mailed that to the consumer. The pause is temporary, not a cancellation, and failing to dispute a debt may not be treated by a court as an admission of liability.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Electrical injury", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found slumped against a floor lamp with a frayed cord and is not moving. What is the first action?
opciones: Turn off the current at the breaker before touching the patient at all
Pull the patient away by an arm and start checking for breathing
Unplug the lamp and then move the patient with a metal walker frame
Start compressions at once and have someone unplug the lamp meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: The current goes off first: unplug the cord, pull the fuse or trip the breaker, since switching an appliance off may not stop the flow. The patient is not touched with bare hands while still in contact with the source; a non-metallic object is used to separate them. Only then are airway, breathing and pulse checked and first aid begun.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", Issues of Concern (EMTALA and the emergency exception)
preguntas.subtema: Consent in emergencies · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: An unaccompanied 10-year-old arrives at a federally funded emergency department and no parent can be reached. What happens first?
opciones: A medical screening exam is done regardless of consent or ability to pay
Care waits until a parent or a guardian is reached and gives permission
A hospital administrator signs the consent form in place of the parent
The child is moved to a pediatric hospital before any examination is done
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law requires a medical screening exam for everyone who comes to a federally funded emergency department, minors included, whatever their consent status or ability to pay. If that exam finds an emergency medical condition, life- or limb-saving treatment proceeds without waiting for a parent. Once no emergency condition is found, that protection ends and consent has to be sorted out.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Collection; Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Short draw in citrate tube · PBT IV.A.3 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(5) INR (2027: b.(8)) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A light-blue-top tube for a PT/INR arrives filled to about half its volume. How does this affect the result?
opciones: Excess citrate relative to plasma prolongs the clotting time, so the result is falsely high
Excess citrate relative to plasma shortens the clotting time, so the result is falsely low
The 9 to 1 ratio corrects itself during centrifugation, so the PT is not affected by the volume
Only the aPTT is affected by underfilling; the PT can be reported exactly as it was measured
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate tubes are pre-filled with 3.2 % sodium citrate for a blood-to-anticoagulant ratio of 9 to 1, and the tube must be filled to at least 90 % of its stated volume, marked by a line. A short draw leaves too much anticoagulant for the plasma present and prolongs clotting times, giving a falsely long PT and high INR. Nothing in centrifugation restores the ratio, and the effect applies to clot-based tests generally.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Active features
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A safety needle requires the user to activate its shield after the draw. How does the FDA say an active feature should be designed to work?
opciones: It can be activated with one hand, with the hands staying behind the exposed sharp
It can be activated with two hands, so that the shield locks firmly over the needle tip
It activates on its own as the needle leaves the vein, with no user action
It is activated after the needle has been placed in the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: For active features, those the user must trigger, FDA Table 1 recommends that activation be possible with a single-handed technique that lets the user's hands remain behind the exposed sharp. A two-handed action brings a hand toward the point. Automatic activation describes a passive feature, and the feature is meant to protect during handling before and through disposal, not after.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Plasma Proteins and Blood Plasma; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Common Pathway
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is essential for clotting and is therefore no longer present in serum?
opciones: Fibrinogen
Albumin
Transferrin
Immunoglobulin
preguntas.explicacion: Fibrinogen is the third major plasma protein group, made by the liver and required for coagulation; in the common pathway thrombin turns it into insoluble fibrin. Because serum is plasma with the clotting factors removed, fibrinogen (factor I) is gone from serum. Albumin and the immunoglobulins are not clotting factors, and transferrin is the plasma carrier of iron.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), MSP Contractor Claims Investigation
preguntas.subtema: Claim follow-up · CMA III.G.3.b(4) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: A claim reaches the Medicare contractor with another insurer's remittance attached but no record of the other coverage. What may come next?
opciones: A questionnaire to the patient or the insurer asking for the other coverage details
A denial issued at once, because the coverage details cannot now be reconstructed
A request that the provider resubmit without the other insurer's remittance attached
A conditional payment issued at once, to be recovered from the other insurer later
preguntas.explicacion: Where the contractor does not hold full information on other insurance that might be primary, it asks the secondary payer contractor for more, and that contractor may send the patient, the employer, the insurer or the attorney a questionnaire for developing the secondary claim. It is used when a claim arrives with another insurer's explanation of benefits or remittance, when payment information appears in the electronic loops, or when the patient or an attorney reports it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Your Responsibilities
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5B k66 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: Registration finds an open workers' compensation record in a Medicare patient's eligibility file. May the hospital turn her away?
opciones: No, because care may not be refused over an open or closed secondary payer record
Yes, because admission may wait until the compensation carrier confirms it will pay
Yes, because admission may be refused unless she signs a responsibility agreement
No, because care may not be refused, but the claim waits until the record is closed
preguntas.explicacion: A provider may not refuse Part A or Part B services, nor refuse admission to a hospital or a skilled nursing facility, on the strength of an open or closed record for a group or non-group health plan, a no-fault or workers' compensation record, or a claim mistakenly denied over one of them. Doing so runs against Medicare law and policy. The claim still goes to the primary payer first, but the care does not wait for that.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.c · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: What separates HCPCS Level I from HCPCS Level II?
opciones: Level I is CPT, kept by the AMA; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by CMS
Level I is CPT, kept by CMS; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by the AMA
Level I codes diagnoses and Level II codes the procedures done to treat them
Level I is used by hospitals for inpatient care and Level II by offices for visits
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS has two subsystems. Level I is Current Procedural Terminology, a numeric system of five digits that the American Medical Association maintains and republishes each year. Level II is a standardized alphanumeric system, a letter followed by four digits, for products, supplies and services outside Level I such as ambulance and durable medical equipment, and CMS maintains it. Diagnoses are coded in ICD-10-CM.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Intimate Partner Violence
preguntas.subtema: Abuse of a partner · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Whom does the term intimate partner cover in intimate partner violence?
opciones: Spouses and dating partners, present ones and former ones
Current spouses and people living at the same address
People in the same household, including relatives and roommates
Married partners only, once the marriage is on public record
preguntas.explicacion: Intimate partner violence is abuse or aggression inside a romantic relationship, and intimate partner takes in spouses and dating partners, present and former alike. It covers stalking, sexual violence, aggression that is psychological, and physical violence, and ranges from a single episode to years of severe abuse.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: What makes an interpreter 'qualified' under the ADA effective-communication rules?
opciones: Interprets accurately, impartially and effectively, receptively and expressively
Holds a state license and is directly employed by the covered entity
Is a family member fluent in sign language and already known to the patient
Is certified only for the specialized vocabulary of the medical setting
preguntas.explicacion: A qualified interpreter is someone who can interpret accurately, impartially and to effect, both receptively, understanding the person, and expressively, carrying the information back, using whatever specialized vocabulary is needed. Family members often lack the impartiality and the vocabulary, and the definition turns on skill rather than on employment or licensing.

preguntas.subtema: Contingency operations · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A burst pipe closes the suite, and the technicians need to get inside the damaged office to bring the data back. Which specification should have planned for that?
opciones: Contingency operations, which arrange facility access in support of the recovery plans
Emergency access procedure, which gets a clinician to the record during an emergency
Applications and data criticality analysis, which ranks what has to come back first
Testing and revision procedures, which put the contingency plan through a rehearsal
preguntas.explicacion: Contingency operations is the physical safeguard: procedures allowing access to the facility so that lost data can be restored under the disaster recovery and emergency mode plans. The emergency access procedure is the technical twin, and it is about reaching the information itself, not the building.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A cuff that is too small for the patient's arm is used. Which way does the reading err?
opciones: Falsely high, while a cuff that is too large produces a falsely low reading
Falsely low, while a cuff that is too large produces a falsely high reading
Falsely high, and a cuff that is too large errs in the same direction
Neither, so long as the bladder still encircles the arm without a gap
preguntas.explicacion: An undersized cuff pushes the value up and an oversized one pulls it down. That asymmetry is why guidance says to take the larger cuff when the choice is not obvious: an artificially low reading is less likely to trigger treatment nobody needs. Cuff size is checked before the arm is even wrapped.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Fire Hazards, 29 CFR 1910.38(b) and 1910.39(b)
preguntas.subtema: Emergency action plan · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan must be in writing. What does OSHA's rule provide?
opciones: With 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
It must be in writing regardless of size and posted at each exit
With fewer than 25 employees it may be oral; above that it must be written
It may be oral only if the clinic also has no fire prevention plan
preguntas.explicacion: Under 29 CFR 1910.38(b), as the eTool summarizes it, an emergency action plan is normally written, kept at the workplace and available to employees; where there are 10 employees or fewer, the employer may simply brief them orally. Section 1910.39(b) sets the same threshold for the fire prevention plan. The two plans stand apart, so having or lacking one changes nothing for the other. With 8 employees this clinic may brief its staff by word of mouth, though the minimum elements of 1910.38(c) still have to be covered.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Conduction System of the Heart; Atrioventricular Bundle, Bundle Branches, and Purkinje Fibers
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A student is asked to put the conduction system in order, from where the impulse starts to where it reaches the ventricular muscle. Which sequence is right?
opciones: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, bundle of His, AV node, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV node, Purkinje fibers, bundle of His, bundle branches
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting components run in order: the sinoatrial node starts the impulse, internodal pathways carry it across the atria to the atrioventricular node, where it pauses about 100 ms; it then runs down the bundle of His in the interventricular septum, splits into the two bundle branches, and reaches the Purkinje fibers, which spread it through the ventricular muscle from the apex up.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.1 The Language of Epidemiologists, Patterns of Incidence
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k42 · CMA I.C.6.h (2027 I.C.6.g) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Malaria is constantly present at a low level in some regions of Brazil but not in the United States. Which pattern of incidence is that?
opciones: Endemic, a disease constantly present within a geographic region
Sporadic, a disease seen only occasionally and without concentration
Epidemic, a disease with more cases than expected in a short time
Pandemic, a disease whose case count has grown on a worldwide scale
preguntas.explicacion: The four patterns run by scale and expectation. Sporadic diseases turn up only now and then and scattered, such as tetanus, rabies and plague. Endemic ones are always there in a region, as malaria is in parts of Brazil. Epidemic means more cases than expected in a short time, and a pandemic is an epidemic gone worldwide.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Clotting Factors Involved in Coagulation and Table 18.1; and MedlinePlus, Coagulation Factor Tests, Why do I need a coagulation factor test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with severe liver disease and a vitamin K deficiency bleeds longer than usual after a draw. Why is coagulation impaired?
opciones: The liver makes most clotting factors and needs vitamin K for many
Vitamin K is factor IV, the calcium needed for the entire cascade
The liver stores the platelets that release ADP and serotonin
Vitamin K activates plasmin, so clots dissolve as fast as they form
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting factors come mostly from the liver and the platelets, and the liver cannot build several of them without vitamin K, which is fat-soluble: factors II, VII, IX and X carry that mark in the table. Serious liver disease and a shortage of vitamin K are both listed causes of bleeding. Calcium is factor IV, and it is the spleen, not the liver, that stores platelets.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Downtime job aid · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which job aid does the contingency guidance suggest an organization hand its staff for use during an outage?
opciones: A small self-contained card or checklist of the resources and actions available
A printed copy of the whole electronic record of every patient booked that day
A telephone list of the software developer's support engineers and their hours
A binder holding the last six months of temperature and equipment inspection logs
preguntas.explicacion: Next to training and drills the guidance names a concrete tool: a job aid, which it describes as a reference card or checklist, small and self-contained, that helps staff locate the resources and the actions open to them while the record system is down. It is meant to work when nothing on the screen can be consulted.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fecal culture (003758), How to Prepare for the Test; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Ova and Parasite Test, What happens during an ova and parasite test?
preguntas.subtema: Multiple stool bottles · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is given several stool collection bottles with different colored caps for a culture and a parasite exam. What should he be told?
opciones: Each bottle may carry different instructions, so read them all before starting and follow each exactly
All bottles take the same sample, so fill them from a single bowel movement in any order
Only the culture bottle matters; the others are spare containers for repeat collections
The bottles should be refrigerated for 24 hours before being returned, as for urine culture
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on which stool tests are ordered, the patient may receive several bottles, and they can come with different instructions; the advice is to read everything ahead of time and follow each set carefully. The specimen goes back to the laboratory as soon as possible, labeled with name, date and time of collection, and the patient washes the hands with soap and water afterward.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(5) (2027 I.C.6.g(5)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which exposure accounts for most cases of COPD in high-income countries, and what does that leave for the rest?
opciones: Cigarette smoking, with up to a quarter or more of patients who never smoked
Cigarette smoking, with essentially no patients who have never smoked at all
Biomass fuel smoke, with cigarette smoking a distant second in those countries
