Use the legal name on the requisition until the record has been formally amended
Ask the partner who accompanies her which pronouns you should use
Avoid using any name or pronoun for the rest of the visit, to be safe
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told to call a patient by the name she gives and the pronouns she has chosen, to follow the patient's lead and ask where there is doubt, and to leave a note in the record so that later visits go the same way, editing the electronic record if that is what it takes. Identifying the specimen is a separate step and uses the identifiers on file.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244)
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2 · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: What separates fraud from abuse in the Medicare program?
opciones: Fraud involves knowing deception; abuse causes needless program cost without it
Fraud is committed by providers only; abuse is committed by patients and staff
Fraud is billed to a federal program; abuse is billed to a commercial insurer
Fraud is punished by the payer; abuse is punished only by the state licensing board
preguntas.explicacion: Fraud typically means knowingly submitting false claims, misrepresenting facts, or paying or taking remuneration for referrals. Abuse is the label for practices that cause unnecessary program costs, directly or indirectly, or that fall short of professionally recognized standards. Which of the two applies depends on the facts, the intent and the knowledge involved, and either can bring administrative, civil and criminal liability.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A smear shows platelets sticking to the white cells rather than to each other. What is that finding called?
opciones: Platelet satellitism
Platelet clumping
Rouleaux formation
Pseudo-polycythaemia
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets adhering to polymorphonuclear cells is known as platelet satellitism, and careful microscopic review of the smear is what picks it up. Clumping of platelets with one another in EDTA is the neighbouring artefact, and rouleaux are stacks of red cells, not platelets.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)-(4), Core elements and requirements
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a valid HIPAA authorization contain?
opciones: An expiration date or event, plus the individual's signature and date
A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements in 164.508(c)(1) are a specific description of the information, the person or class authorized to disclose it, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date, with the authority of any personal representative described. The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. It must be in plain language and the individual receives a copy. Notarization is not required, and a no-revocation clause would contradict the rule.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the cable wires pulled as straight as possible when they are attached?
opciones: Loops in them can cause alternating-current interference
Loops in them can shorten the life of the patient cable
Loops in them can slow the paper as it feeds through
Loops in them can reverse the polarity of that lead
preguntas.explicacion: Each wire is picked out of the cable distribution block, plugged into its connector, and then laid out straight. A loop in a lead wire is one of the recognized invitations to interference from the room current, an artifact that can bury the small waves the provider needs to see.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Clinical Significance: Focused History
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 · CMA I.A.3.a · RMA III.F.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with breast cancer on chemotherapy comes in for a cough. How is the history taken?
opciones: Focused on the cough, with the immunosuppression from the chemotherapy kept in mind
Comprehensive, starting again from childhood illnesses and every past operation
Focused on the cancer treatment plan, which outranks the reason for today's visit
Deferred until the oncology notes from the previous visits have all been reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: A problem-focused visit calls for a focused history: the presenting complaint, plus whatever has changed since the patient was last seen, an admission, a trip to the emergency department, a medication adjusted. The complete history is already on file. What the cancer treatment adds here is immunosuppression, which widens the differential for a cough rather than replacing it.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.17(c)(4); FDA, CLIA Categorizations: Note on test systems not yet categorized
preguntas.subtema: Uncategorized tests default to high complexity · PBT VI.F.4 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A new test system does not appear on any published list of categorized tests. How must a laboratory treat it until HHS reviews it?
opciones: As a high complexity test
As a moderate complexity test
As a waived home-use test
As a PPM procedure
preguntas.explicacion: When a test system, assay or examination is missing from the categorization notices, the rule is to consider it high complexity until the Public Health Service reviews it and notifies the applicant. The same default applies to tests developed in-house or modified from the manufacturer's instructions. Categorization takes effect on the date of the written notification.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(2)(iii)(A) and (B), Containment equipment
preguntas.subtema: Biosafety cabinet certification · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: How often must a certified biological safety cabinet be recertified in a laboratory working with concentrated HIV or HBV?
opciones: When it is installed, whenever it is moved, and at least once a year
Every three years, the period for which training records are kept
Once at installation, and again only after a spill occurs inside it
Every six months, and after each change of the exhaust air filter
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(iii) requires certified biological safety cabinets, or equivalent containment such as special clothing, sealed rotors, safety cups for the centrifuge or respirators, for any activity that could throw droplets, splashes, spills or aerosols of infectious material. Subparagraph (B) sets the certification schedule: at installation, at every move, and at least once a year. That annual cycle is shared with the biosafety manual review in (e)(2)(ii)(M); three years is the retention period for training records.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Reproductive System: Male Reproductive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(8) (2027 I.C.6.f(8)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the male reproductive system?
opciones: Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, prostate and penis
Testes, epididymis, ureters, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, bladder and penis
Testes, Fallopian tubes, vas deferens, accessory glands, prostate, urethra and penis
Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, adrenal glands, seminal vesicles, kidney and penis
preguntas.explicacion: The male system is a pair of testes plus a network of excretory ducts, namely the epididymis, the ductus or vas deferens and the ejaculatory ducts, and to those are added the penis, the bulbourethral glands, the prostate and the seminal vesicles. The ureters and the bladder belong to the urinary system, even though the two share the urethra.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for single-dose vials
preguntas.subtema: Single-dose vials · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A single-dose vial of lidocaine contains far more than one patient needs. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Do not keep the remainder for later or another patient; buy the smallest vial that meets the need
Label it with the date and use it for up to 28 days, as with a multi-dose vial
Pool the leftover contents with other single-dose vials in a clean preparation area
Save the remainder for the same patient's next visit, since it is dedicated to one person
preguntas.explicacion: A single-dose vial is approved for one patient for one case, procedure or injection, typically lacks a preservative, and must never be used for more than one patient. If it holds more than needed, the remainder is not retained for future use even on the same patient, leftover contents are not pooled or stored, and the practical advice is to purchase the smallest vial necessary. The 28-day dating rule applies to opened multi-dose vials, which contain a preservative.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Respiratory Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for an adult?
opciones: 12 to 20 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
20 to 30 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
8 to 12 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
30 to 60 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
preguntas.explicacion: The adult range is 12 to 20 breaths per minute, and the assessment records rate, depth and pattern rather than the number alone. The 30 to 60 band belongs to infants. Respiration is the vital sign most often left out of the chart, and it is also the one that changes earliest when a patient is deteriorating.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Abdominal Regions and Quadrants
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many regions does the detailed regional scheme of the abdomen produce, and how many does the quadrant scheme produce?
opciones: Nine regions and four quadrants
Four regions and nine quadrants
Six regions and three quadrants
Twelve regions and six quadrants
preguntas.explicacion: Providers divide the abdominal cavity either into nine regions or into four quadrants, so that a complaint can be placed precisely. The regional scheme is the more detailed one and comes from two horizontal and two vertical lines; the quadrant scheme is simpler and is the one used more often in medicine.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: A and B Recommendations — Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C screening timelines · CMA I.A.5 · 2027 I.A.5 · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition c
preguntas.pregunta: A 52-year-old patient with obesity and no symptoms asks whether he should be tested for diabetes. What applies?
opciones: Yes; screening covers adults 35 to 70 who have overweight or obesity
Yes; screening covers every adult 35 to 70 regardless of body weight
No; screening starts at 45 for adults who have overweight or obesity
No; screening applies only once symptoms of high blood glucose appear
preguntas.explicacion: Adults from 35 to 70 who are overweight or have obesity and show no symptoms are recommended for screening for prediabetes and for type 2 diabetes, at a B grade. The point of screening is to find the condition before symptoms, and patients found to have prediabetes are offered or referred to preventive interventions.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 4: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · PBT II.F · CCMA 3C4 k100 k101 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Before a routine venipuncture, what does the WHO's Step 4 require for hand hygiene and gloves?
opciones: Soap and water, or 3 ml of alcohol rub if hands are not visibly soiled, then well-fitting non-sterile gloves
Use 3 ml of alcohol rub in every case, even on visibly soiled hands, then put on sterile gloves
Wash with soap and water, dry with a reusable towel, then put on sterile gloves for every patient
Put on well-fitting non-sterile gloves first, then clean the gloved hands with alcohol rub
preguntas.explicacion: Step 4 gives two options: wash the hands with soap and water and dry them with single-use towels, or, if they are not visibly contaminated, rub 3 ml of alcohol rub over palms, fingertips and backs of the hands until dry; only then are well-fitting non-sterile gloves put on. Sterile gloves are reserved for blood cultures. Gloves are never a substitute for hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k59 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with polycythemia has a hematocrit of 60%. What should be considered when collecting a citrate specimen from this patient?
opciones: The high hematocrit raises the citrate effect, so the anticoagulant volume may need adjusting
The high hematocrit lowers the citrate effect, so the tube should be filled only halfway
The tube is collected as usual, since hematocrit affects the EDTA tube and not the citrate tube
A larger 16 to 18 G needle is used so the viscous blood reaches the 9:1 ratio faster
preguntas.explicacion: Inadequate filling or a hematocrit above 55% increases the citrate level in the sample and interferes with the recalcification performed during analysis, and with a high hematocrit the anticoagulant volume may need to be adjusted. Half filling would make the citrate excess worse. The 16 to 18 gauge belongs to blood donation in the WHO needle table, not to coagulation draws, for which 19 to 22 G is suggested.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.D.2.n · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Which order of steps does the guideline require before an instrument can be high-level disinfected or sterilized?
opciones: Clean it thoroughly first, because leftover organic and inorganic matter blocks the process
Soak it in the germicide first, so the softened soil rinses off with less friction afterward
Disinfect at a low level first, so the item is safe for the person who will scrub it later
Rinse it in sterile water first, so tap-water organisms cannot dry onto the working surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Cleaning always comes first. Material left on the surface interferes with the process in two ways: it reacts chemically with the germicide, using it up, and it shields microbes as a physical barrier. Meticulous cleaning also lowers the bioburden, which shortens the exposure needed. Sterile-water rinsing is what follows high-level disinfection, not what precedes it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Social History
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k44 · CMA I.A.4.g
preguntas.pregunta: Which framework does the CDC recommend for taking a sexual history?
opciones: The 5 Ps: partners, practices, protection, previous infections and prevention of pregnancy
The PQRSTU mnemonic, applied to the symptoms of any sexually transmitted infection reported
OLDCARTS, which sets out the onset, location and duration of each reported exposure
Gordon's functional health patterns, whose sexuality category covers the same ground
preguntas.explicacion: The five headings are partners; practices; protection against infections passed on sexually; whether the patient has had one of those infections before; and prevention of pregnancy. The framework matters because sexual histories are often left incomplete in routine practice, and a complete one makes appropriate education, counseling and testing far more likely.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(2)(i), Training Records
preguntas.subtema: Content of training records · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which information must a bloodborne pathogens training record include?
opciones: Dates, a summary of the content, the trainer's name and qualifications, and attendees' names and titles
Dates, the trainer's name, and each attendee's hepatitis B vaccination status and serology
Dates, the content, and the type and brand of any device that caused an injury during the year
Dates, the attendees' names, and a copy of each attendee's signed declination or consent
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(i) lists four items for the training record: the dates of the sessions, the contents or a summary, the names and qualifications of whoever conducted the training, and the names and job titles of everyone who attended. Vaccination status and serology belong to the confidential medical record of (h)(1); the type and brand of a device belong to the sharps injury log of (h)(5); and the signed declination of Appendix A is a separate document required by (f)(2)(iv).

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Coordination of Benefits & Recovery Overview
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5 k75 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: Which entity collects, manages and reports the other insurance coverage a Medicare patient holds?
opciones: The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, working for the secondary payer program
The Medicare Administrative Contractor, working for the secondary payer program
The Commercial Repayment Center, working for the secondary payer program
The clearinghouse, working for the providers that route their claims through it
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare Secondary Payer program keeps Medicare from paying first where it should not, and coordination of benefits rules settle which payer goes first. Collecting, managing and reporting whatever other insurance covers a beneficiary is the job of the Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center. The Commercial Repayment Center does something else entirely: it pursues recovery when a group health plan should have paid first.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Synovial fluid analysis (003629), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Synovial fluid analysis · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a
preguntas.pregunta: Joint fluid has been aspirated from a swollen knee. What does the laboratory look for that is specific to this fluid?
opciones: Crystals, which point to gout, along with cell counts and a culture
Casts, which point to renal disease, along with cell counts and a culture
Ova and parasites, which point to infestation, along with a cell count
Acid-fast bacilli only, since joint fluid is cultured for no other organism
preguntas.explicacion: Normal synovial fluid is thick, straw-colored and there in only small amounts. The skin is cleaned, a sterile needle enters the joint space, and fluid is drawn into a sterile syringe. The laboratory notes color and clarity, counts red and white cells, hunts under the microscope for bacteria or for the crystals of gout, measures uric acid, glucose, protein and LDH, and puts the fluid up for culture.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Semen analysis (003627), How to Prepare for the Test; and StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Semen abstinence · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A man scheduled for a semen analysis asks how long he should abstain from ejaculation beforehand. What is the usual instruction?
opciones: From 2 to 3 days, and in no case longer than 5 days before the test
From 2 to 3 hours, and in no case longer than 5 hours before the test
At least 7 days, and preferably 10 days or more before the test
No abstinence at all, since recent activity does not change the count
preguntas.explicacion: To get an adequate sperm count the patient avoids any sexual activity that ends in ejaculation for 2 to 3 days, and the interval should not stretch past 5 days because quality falls off after that. The StatPearls account of the same test sets the window differently, at a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 7 days, so the figure a candidate quotes depends on which reference the laboratory follows.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Biological Hazards, Requirements under 29 CFR 1910.1030 (Universal Precautions); OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens: Hazard Recognition
preguntas.subtema: Universal vs Standard Precautions · CPT D1 k11 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k99 k100 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, may a facility apply Standard Precautions instead of Universal Precautions?
opciones: Yes, as an alternative, if the facility follows all other provisions of the standard
No; Universal Precautions is the only approach the standard's definitions recognize
Yes, but only in hospitals holding accreditation from a CMS-approved body
Yes, and doing so exempts the facility from the exposure determination requirement
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool explains that Standard Precautions, like Body Substance Isolation before them, treat every body fluid and body substance as infectious, and that OSHA accepts them as alternatives to Universal Precautions so long as the facility keeps to every other provision of the bloodborne pathogens standard. OSHA's hazard page dates Standard Precautions to 1996 and describes them as broadening Universal Precautions with extra infection prevention elements. The exposure determination of (c)(2) still has to be done, and accreditation is a CLIA matter, not a condition here.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.D.2.n
preguntas.pregunta: Instruments are being loaded into a washer-disinfector. Which loading practice does the guideline call for?
opciones: Open hinged instruments fully, take apart what comes apart, and do not stack the pieces
Close hinged instruments fully, keep assemblies together, and stack them to fit one load
Open hinged instruments fully, keep assemblies together, and stack the heavier ones on top
Close hinged instruments fully, take apart what comes apart, and lay them flat in one layer
preguntas.explicacion: The detergent solution has to reach every surface, so hinged instruments are opened all the way, items are disassembled as far as they will go, and stacking is avoided because one piece shields another. The same logic governs the sterilizer later: only surfaces the agent actually reaches get processed.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), What's Medicare Fraud?
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic sends Medicare claims for appointments its patients never kept. How does CMS class that practice?
opciones: As fraud, since it claims payment for care never given
As abuse, since it adds cost the program need not bear
As waste, since the appointment slot could not be reused
As an error, since the schedule was not kept up to date
preguntas.explicacion: Claiming from Medicare for an appointment the patient never kept sits on the CMS list of fraud examples, alongside billing for services never provided and upcoding. Abuse covers practices that push unnecessary cost onto the program without that knowing deception, which is why the two are told apart by intent and knowledge rather than by the amount.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Ending the relationship · CCMA 5 k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · CMAA 4F k60 · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to drop a patient he finds difficult and demanding. What do the ethical guidelines say?
opciones: Being a challenging patient is not on its own a ground for ending the relationship
Any patient may be dismissed at will, since the relationship rests on mutual consent
Dismissal is allowed once the patient has been rude to a member of the office staff
Only the health plan may end the relationship, by removing the patient from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The clinician-patient relationship usually begins by mutual consent and is governed by State law. Ethical guidance holds that a clinician may not terminate it merely because someone is a challenging patient, and that irresponsible health behaviors do not release the professional from the duties of the relationship. The expected route is to try to resolve the conflict and, failing that, seek help from a consultant.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Disorders of Platelets; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 3C bleeding disorders) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is far below normal. What is the term for this, and what is the main risk?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia; excessive bleeding even from minor wounds
Thrombocytosis; the formation of unwanted clots or thrombosis
Leukopenia; an inability to ward off infection and disease
Thrombophilia; an inherited or acquired tendency to form thrombi
preguntas.explicacion: An insufficient number of platelets is thrombocytopenia; blood may then fail to clot properly, so excessive bleeding can follow even minor wounds. The opposite, too many platelets, is thrombocytosis and carries a risk of unwanted clots. Leukopenia is too few white cells, and thrombophilia (hypercoagulation) is a tendency to thrombosis that can be genetic or acquired.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi)
preguntas.subtema: Removing the gown · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What is the correct way to take off a gown after caring for a patient?
opciones: Release the ties, touch only the inside, and turn it inside out
Release the ties, roll it from the sleeves toward the neckline
Pull it over the head without untying, keeping the front outward
Fold it front to front and hang it for the rest of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: The gown is third in the doffing sequence. Ties or straps are released first; then it comes off touched only on the inside, eased away from neck and shoulders and turned inside out so the contaminated face finishes up enclosed, and it goes straight into the proper container. The bloodborne pathogens standard adds the companion rule: a garment that blood has soaked through comes off immediately, in a way that avoids contact with the outer surface, and a gown is never hung up for a second use.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.4 Diseases, Disorders and Injuries of the Integumentary System, Burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(1) (2027 I.C.6.g(1)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A deep burn appears white and the area is oddly not very painful. Why is the lack of pain a bad sign?
opciones: The burn has destroyed the nerve endings along with the dermis
The burn has cooled the nerve endings without harming the dermis
The burn has flooded the nerve endings with the fluid lost from cells
The burn has stretched the nerve endings across the swollen dermis
preguntas.explicacion: A third-degree burn goes through epidermis and dermis, destroying tissue and taking the nerve endings and sensory function with it, and a fourth-degree burn reaches muscle and bone. That is why the deepest burns hurt less than the shallow ones. They also cannot heal on their own and need debridement and grafting.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Electrolyte Panel, What is an electrolyte panel?
preguntas.subtema: Electrolyte roles · CMA I.C.10.c.(6) · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: On an electrolyte panel, which electrolyte is described as maintaining the body's acid-base balance and helping move carbon dioxide through the blood?
opciones: Serum bicarbonate
Serum potassium level
Serum chloride
Serum magnesium
preguntas.explicacion: An electrolyte panel measures sodium, chloride, potassium and bicarbonate, sometimes calcium, magnesium and phosphate too. Bicarbonate helps hold the acid-base balance (pH) steady and has a hand in carrying carbon dioxide around in the blood; sodium and chloride govern how much fluid the body holds, potassium keeps cells, heart and muscles working, and magnesium supports muscles, nerves and heart. Abnormal levels can point to kidney disease, high blood pressure or a dangerous arrhythmia.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(A), Housekeeping
preguntas.subtema: Decontamination of surfaces and spills · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C k97 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b / 2027 I.B.4.b I.B.6.b · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A work surface in the draw room is splashed with blood during a procedure. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Decontaminate it with an appropriate disinfectant immediately or as soon as feasible
Decontaminate it at the end of the work shift, the time the standard sets for possibly contaminated surfaces
Remove and replace the protective covering at the end of the shift, as with plastic wrap over equipment
Flush it with water immediately, as the standard requires for skin and mucous membranes
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(A) names three moments for decontaminating a work surface with a suitable disinfectant: when a procedure is finished; right away, or as soon as feasible, when the surface is visibly contaminated or blood or OPIM has been spilled on it; and at the end of the shift if it may have been contaminated since the last cleaning. A visible spill falls under the second case and does not wait for the shift to end. Protective coverings, in (d)(4)(ii)(B), are likewise replaced as soon as feasible once overtly contaminated. Flushing with water is the rule for eyes and mucous membranes in (d)(2)(vi), not for surfaces.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative, Submitting an Appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A claim is denied by a correct coding edit and the practice wants to appeal. Where does the appeal go?
opciones: To the Medicare contractor that processed the claim
To the contractor that keeps the edit files updated
To the committee that maintains the coding manual
To the Inspector General, who reviews the denials
preguntas.explicacion: Appeals of denials tied to the correct coding edits go to the Medicare administrative contractor or the qualified independent contractor, following the ordinary appeals route. The contractor that maintains the edit files cannot process a claim-specific appeal and does not forward one, so an appeal sent there simply loses time.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Two separate conditions treated at one visit both fall under the very same diagnosis code. How many times is that code reported?
opciones: Once, since a unique code is reported only once for an encounter
Twice, once for each of the two conditions the provider documented
Twice, because the units reported have to match the work done
Once, and only where the two conditions are on the same side
preguntas.explicacion: A unique diagnosis code goes on an encounter a single time. The rule covers bilateral conditions where no distinct codes identify laterality, and it covers two different conditions that are classified to the same code. Units of service belong to procedure reporting, not to the diagnosis list.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: No prescreening as a condition · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic wants to check each new hire's antibody level first and offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to those who are not immune. What does the standard say?
opciones: Screening may not be made a condition of receiving the vaccine that is offered
Screening is required before the first dose, and has to be repeated a year later
Screening replaces the vaccine when the employee signs the declination form
Screening is allowed only within ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Two sentences have to be read together. Paragraph (f)(2)(i) has the vaccine offered after training and within ten working days of initial assignment, unless the employee has already completed the series, unless antibody testing has shown the person to be immune, or unless the vaccine is medically contraindicated. Paragraph (f)(2)(ii) then bars the employer from making a worker join a prescreening program as the price of getting vaccinated. So a result that already exists can remove the need for the offer, while nobody may be told to be screened first in order to qualify.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Closure Techniques", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: A contaminated wound with no major tissue loss is irrigated, debrided and watched for several days before it is closed. Which type of healing is that?
opciones: Tertiary intention, also called delayed primary closure
Secondary intention, in which granulation fills the defect
Primary intention, in which the edges are approximated at once
Maturation, the last of the four phases that every wound goes through
preguntas.explicacion: Tertiary intention, or delayed primary closure, is the route for a grossly contaminated wound that has not lost much tissue: it gets explored and irrigated, debrided, then watched for roughly three to seven days before it is closed or grafted. Primary intention is closure at once with sutures, staples or glue; secondary intention leaves the wound open to granulate and contract.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has fainted in the chair and been eased to the floor. How high should the feet be raised?
opciones: About 12 inches (30 cm) above the level of the heart
About 4 inches (10 cm) above the level of the heart
About 3 feet (90 cm), by resting the legs on the chair seat
Level with the heart, with the head turned to the side
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps after a faint are: check airway and breathing, loosen anything tight at the neck, raise the feet above heart level by about 12 inches or 30 centimeters, turn the person on the side if they have vomited, and keep them lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes. The side position is for vomiting; it does not replace elevating the legs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient recovers from a faint during a draw. Which finding afterwards is a red flag pointing away from a simple vasovagal episode?
opciones: A bitten tongue, which suggests a seizure
Pallor and sweating during the event itself
A slow pulse and low blood pressure during the event
Generalized weakness for a few minutes after waking
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is usually slow of pulse, hypotensive, pale and sweating during the event and should have an entirely normal examination afterwards; findings such as tongue biting, which points to a seizure, or pallor that carries on, which points to symptomatic anemia, call for a fuller evaluation. The syncope chapter notes that generalized weakness on regaining consciousness is typical.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Table 18.1 Clotting Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factors require vitamin K for their production?
opciones: II, VII, IX and X
I, V, XI and XIII
III, IV, VIII and XII
VIII, IX, XI and XII
preguntas.explicacion: Four factors need vitamin K for their synthesis: prothrombin (II), proconvertin (VII), antihemolytic factor B (IX) and the Stuart-Prower factor (X), all made in the liver. The intrinsic-pathway set VIII, IX, XI and XII is a different grouping, and fibrinogen, proaccelerin, factor XI and the fibrin-stabilizing factor are not vitamin K dependent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adverse Drug Reactions", Function: Type A Reactions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: How is a side effect related to an adverse drug reaction?
opciones: It is one category of adverse reaction, predictable and often dose related
It is the opposite of an adverse reaction, since a side effect is never harmful
It is unrelated: side effects come from the disease and not from the medication
It is any reaction the pharmacological properties of the drug fail to predict
preguntas.explicacion: A side effect is an effect other than the main one the drug was given for; it can be foreseen from the pharmacology, it tends to track the dose, and it may be desirable, adverse or of no consequence. Side effects fall inside the Type A adverse reactions along with overdose and drug interactions. Gastritis after an NSAID and diarrhea after an antibiotic are the examples given. What pharmacology fails to predict is a Type B reaction.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders blood cultures, a CBC and a fasting glucose on the same venipuncture. Which sequence follows the WHO table?
opciones: Blood culture bottle, purple EDTA tube, light gray fluoride tube
Purple EDTA tube, blood culture bottle, light gray fluoride tube
Light gray fluoride tube first, blood culture bottle, purple EDTA tube
Blood culture bottle, light gray fluoride tube, purple EDTA tube
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3 the blood culture bottle is drawn first (position 1), EDTA sits at position 8 and the oxalate/fluoride glucose tube closes the list at position 10. Any sequence that places the gray tube before EDTA, or the culture bottle anywhere but first, breaks the table. The footnote also reminds the reader that local color codes can differ, so the laboratory's own chart is checked.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.3 and 1.2
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · CPT D3 k54 · D1 1D k26 · PBT II.K · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which two activities does the word phlebotomy cover in this guidance?
opciones: Sampling for laboratory tests, and collecting blood for donation
Sampling for laboratory tests, and inserting intravenous cannulae
Collecting blood for donation, and transfusing blood to a patient
Sampling for laboratory tests, and collecting non-blood specimens
preguntas.explicacion: For the purposes of the guidance the term covers two things: blood sampling for laboratory tests and blood collection for donation. Cannulation, transfusion and non-blood specimens sit outside that definition, as do central line, arterial line, cord blood and stem cell collections.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 15: Make Action Plans
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient action plan, and who builds it?
opciones: A few easy steps toward a health goal, worked out with the patient
A few easy steps toward a health goal, written by the clinician alone
The full treatment plan for a chronic condition, signed by the patient
A schedule of the follow-up appointments the practice has booked
preguntas.explicacion: An action plan lays out one or more easy steps toward a health goal, such as losing weight or managing a chronic condition better, and patient and health professional create it together. Nurses, clinicians, health coaches, diabetes educators and medical assistants can all do the action planning once trained for it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Storage of PHI Data; Use of Wireless Networks
preguntas.subtema: Portable media and wireless · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep her worklist on a personal flash drive and check it over the clinic's open wireless network. What is the guidance?
opciones: Avoid storing it on portable media, and use only encrypted networks
Store it on the drive but keep the drive locked in the staff room
Use the open network, since the worklist holds no test results
Store it on the drive after deleting the names, keeping the numbers
preguntas.explicacion: Portable media are a documented source of breaches: laptops and flash drives get stolen, so workers are told not to keep patient data on them, and to encrypt it if it must be kept, or better, to view the data without storing it. Where several computers reach records over a wireless network, the network's encryption has to be switched on, and staff must stop using an unencrypted one because of the risk of interception.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Active Listening and Attending Behaviors
preguntas.subtema: Active listening · CCMA 6C k202 · CMAA 2A k21 · CMA F.1.g · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: What separates active listening from passive listening?
opciones: The listener verifies their understanding with the speaker
The listener stays quiet and never interrupts the speaker
The listener concentrates on presenting their own viewpoint
The listener assumes the message was understood correctly
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of listening get named: competitive, where you are busy with your own point of view; passive, where you assume you understood without checking; and active. In active listening you show interest and then verify, often by restating what was said. That verification is the dividing line.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Membrane Potentials in Cardiac Contractile Cells
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What holds a working heart muscle cell depolarized for so long after the rapid upstroke?
opciones: A plateau of about 175 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
A plateau of about 75 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
A plateau of about 250 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
A plateau of about 5 ms, held open by slow calcium channels
preguntas.explicacion: The rapid depolarization of a contractile cell lasts only 3 to 5 ms. Then the membrane potential falls very slowly for roughly 175 ms while calcium enters and little potassium leaves; repolarization takes about 75 ms more, and the whole event runs 250 to 300 ms.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Strep A Test, What is a strep A test?; What do the results mean?; StatPearls, "Streptococcal Pharyngitis", section Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Culture after negative RADT · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA I.C.10.d.(2) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: An 8-year-old with fever and exudative tonsils has a negative rapid strep test. What does current guidance recommend?
opciones: Send a throat swab for culture, because a negative rapid test in a child or adolescent is backed up by culture
Accept the negative result as final, because the rapid antigen test is highly specific for group A streptococcus
Repeat the rapid test at once with a second swab, and treat only if the second cassette also turns positive
Order a throat culture only if the rapid test had been positive, to identify which streptococcal group is present
preguntas.explicacion: A rapid strep test detects group A streptococcal antigen in 10 to 20 minutes, but a throat culture, which takes 24 to 48 hours, sometimes finds infections the rapid test misses. Culture after a negative rapid test is therefore important in children and teens, who can develop rheumatic fever from untreated strep. High specificity means a positive is trustworthy; it says nothing about the negatives the antigen test misses.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · D2 2E k41 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Once the sample has been taken, what does the quality framework say is essential?
opciones: A system of identification and tracking that ties sample, result and patient
A system of storage that keeps every tube upright at four degrees
A system of billing that records which tests each patient received
A system of duplicates that keeps a second tube for every request
preguntas.explicacion: Identification starts by matching the patient to the laboratory request form, and once the samples are taken, a way of identifying and tracking them is essential so that the specimen is matched correctly to the result and to the patient. For donors the match is to the screening results.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Notice of privacy practices · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient is registering at the front desk. When must the notice of privacy practices be given to her?
opciones: By the date of the first service at the latest, with a good faith effort at written acknowledgment
Within thirty days of the first visit, matching the deadline for responding to an access request
At the second visit, once the office knows the patient intends to keep using the practice
Only if the patient asks for it, since the notice is posted in the reception area anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Where the treatment relationship is a direct one, the provider hands the notice over by the date of the first service at the latest and tries, in good faith, to obtain written acknowledgment of receipt. Where no acknowledgment can be got, the provider documents what was tried and why it did not work. The notice also has to be posted prominently at the site and kept available for people to take away.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Handwashing Technique
preguntas.subtema: Handwashing technique · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: While washing hands at a sink for routine hand hygiene, which technique detail is correct?
opciones: Keep the hands below the elbows and turn off the faucet with a towel
Keep the hands above the elbows, as in the surgical scrub, and rinse toward the fingertips
Turn off the faucet with clean hands so the towel stays dry for drying
Dry the hands on a shared cloth towel and apply lotion before gloving
preguntas.explicacion: Routine handwashing is done with the hands kept below the elbows so water runs from less to more contaminated areas, 3 to 5 mL of soap, at least 15 to 20 seconds of friction over palms, backs, wrists, finger webs, fingertips, thumbs and nails using WHO's six-step pattern, a thorough rinse, drying with a clean or disposable towel, and using a towel to turn off the water so the clean hands are not recontaminated. Hands above the elbows is the surgical scrub position, where the hands are the cleanest area.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(6)(i) and (f)(6)(ii), Workplace labeling
preguntas.subtema: Labeling a secondary container · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A stock bottle of disinfectant is decanted into a smaller labeled bottle kept at the draw station for the week. What must that bottle show?
opciones: The product identifier and words or symbols giving the general hazards
The full sixteen-section data sheet printed and taped to the bottle
The date it was filled and the initials of the employee who filled it
Only the biohazard symbol, since the area also handles specimens
preguntas.explicacion: A container of a hazardous chemical kept in the workplace has to be labeled, tagged or marked either with everything a shipped container carries, or, more simply, with the product identifier plus words, pictures or symbols that give at least general information about the hazards, working together with the rest of the hazard communication program. The data sheet stays in its binder or on the computer; the biohazard label belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard and marks a different hazard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Recognition and Initial Management of Cardiac Arrest
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant finds an adult unresponsive, not breathing, and with no pulse. In what order are the steps of CPR performed?
opciones: Chest compressions first, then the airway, then rescue breathing
The airway first, then rescue breathing, then chest compressions
Rescue breathing first, then the airway, then chest compressions
The airway and two breaths, then a pulse check, then compressions
preguntas.explicacion: Circulation is handled first: compressions are started before the airway is opened and before any breath is delivered. The older airway-first order was set aside in 2010 after research showed that beginning compressions early gave better results than managing the airway first. A lone rescuer compresses and leaves ventilation for a second responder.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Equipment: Manual Auscultation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Sounds are heard, fade to silence, and then come back as the cuff keeps deflating. What has happened?
opciones: An auscultatory gap: listening continues, and the diastolic is the final silence
A false start: the cuff was underinflated, and the first sounds heard were artifact
A normal phase II, in which the swishing quality always drops below hearing
A leaking valve: the pressure fell too quickly and the sounds were skipped over
preguntas.explicacion: In some patients, particularly those with a wide pulse pressure, the sounds vanish between phase II and phase III and then return. Stopping at that silence underestimates the systolic value or records the diastolic too early. Auscultation carries on, and the diastolic is taken at the last disappearance of sound.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Body Cavities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.d (2027 I.C.6.c) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which organs lie in the pelvic portion of the ventral cavity. Which answer is right?
opciones: Most of the urogenital system, together with the rectum
Most of the gastrointestinal tract, with the kidneys
The heart and the lungs, with the large blood vessels
The brain in the upper part and the spinal cord below
preguntas.explicacion: The ventral cavity is divided by the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity above, which holds the heart, lungs, trachea, esophagus, large vessels and nerves, and the abdominopelvic cavity below. That lower one splits again: the abdominal portion holds most of the gastrointestinal tract with the kidneys and adrenal glands, the pelvic portion most of the urogenital system and the rectum.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for multi-dose vials
preguntas.subtema: Multi-dose vials in patient areas · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial is carried into a patient's room for an injection. What does the CDC say about that vial afterwards?
opciones: Dedicate it to that single patient; it may not go back into use for others
Return it to the clean medication room and keep using it for up to 28 days
Discard it immediately, since any vial entering a patient area is contaminated
Wipe the septum with alcohol and continue using it for other patients
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC would rather each multi-dose vial served a single patient. Where one has to cover several, it is kept and drawn from in a clean space set aside for preparing medication, apart from where patients are actually being treated. Taking it into a treatment space instead ends the shared use: an operating or procedure room, an anesthesia or procedure cart, a patient room or bay all count, and from that point the vial belongs to that one patient. Nothing requires binning it on the spot, but it may not go back to anyone else, and the 28-day clock that started at the first puncture keeps running.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Lifecycle of Erythrocytes; 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements, opening paragraph; and 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets; and MedlinePlus, Blood (health topic), Summary
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A blood donor asks how long the red cells she just gave would have lived. What is the lifespan of an erythrocyte, and what removes it?
opciones: About 120 days; macrophages in spleen, liver and marrow remove them
About 10 days, after which macrophages phagocytize them in the spleen
About 4 to 6 weeks, the time the body needs to replace donated cells
A few hours to a few days, like most of the granular leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: A red cell lasts as long as 120 days in the bloodstream, and the worn-out cells are then taken up by macrophages that sit mostly in the marrow, the liver and the spleen. Ten days is far too short: nothing here puts a red cell's life in days. Four to six weeks is what the body needs to rebuild the cells given in a donation, and hours to days covers most of the white cells.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.c / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: A family moving to another state asks whether their child's Medicaid lab work will still be covered. Which service must every state Medicaid program cover?
opciones: Laboratory and X-ray services, which federal law lists as mandatory
Eyeglasses and dentures, which federal law lists as mandatory benefits
Physical therapy, which federal law lists as mandatory for adult patients
Prescription drugs, which federal law lists as mandatory for every state
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law splits Medicaid benefits into mandatory and optional. Mandatory benefits, which every state must provide, include inpatient and outpatient hospital care, laboratory and X-ray services, physician services, nursing facility care, home health, family planning and the screening program for children. Prescription drugs, eyeglasses, dentures and physical therapy are on the optional list, which is why coverage differs from state to state.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Instruments Used in Diagnosing Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How is an infrared temporal artery thermometer used?
opciones: It is drawn slowly from the middle of the forehead across to the lateral hairline
It is held just off the frontal bone, never touching the skin at all
It is pressed on the forehead and held still until the display stops changing
It is drawn from the lateral hairline down the neck over the carotid pulse point
preguntas.explicacion: This device is moved slowly from mid-forehead across to the hairline at the side, reading infrared radiation from the skin above the superficial temporal artery and reporting the highest of the many values it samples. The instrument that is held away from the skin without contact is the infrared forehead thermometer.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Hematocrit Test, What do the results mean?; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D4 4G hematocrit) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hematocrit result comes back as 42. What does that number mean?
opciones: That 42% of the blood volume is made up of red blood cells
That 42% of the blood volume is plasma, the liquid portion
That the red blood cell count is 4.2 million per microliter
That 42% of the formed elements are white cells and platelets
preguntas.explicacion: A hematocrit is reported as the percentage of the blood that consists of red cells; the rest of the sample is white cells, platelets and plasma. The usual figure is about 45 percent, with women at 37 to 47 (mean 41) and men at 42 to 52 (mean 47). White cells and platelets together form under 1 percent of a sample, so they are not counted in the hematocrit, and 4.2 million per microliter would be a cell count, not a percentage.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services
preguntas.subtema: Ground shipping · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which service does the Postal Service describe as the affordable ground option for packages, with insurance included?

Priority Mail Express, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
First-Class Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
Certified Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is presented as the affordable, reliable route for parcels weighing as much as 70 pounds inside the country, expected to arrive in two to five days, with a hundred dollars of insurance built in and extra coverage available up to five thousand. It is also the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot travel by air.

preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k22 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's voice breaks while she describes her diagnosis. The assistant names the emotion and reflects it back. Which technique is that?
opciones: Exploring feeling tones
Providing the rationale
Summarizing the visit
Clarifying the account
preguntas.explicacion: Exploring feeling tones is listed as identifying and empathizing with the patient's emotional state and reflecting it back to them. Providing rationale explains why information is needed, summarizing restates the content in the provider's own words and can close the interview, and clarifying draws out detail from a statement that was not clear.

preguntas.subtema: Privacy options before a visit · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.3.g · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booking a visit about a sensitive matter says she may not be able to speak freely at home. Besides helping her find a private spot, what does the guidance offer?
opciones: Other channels such as e-mail, text or the platform's chat, which matter where safety is a concern
A recording of the visit she can watch later, held on the platform under her own account
An office appointment instead, since a sensitive matter cannot be handled over a video link
A code word agreed with the clinician that will end the video call without alarming anybody
preguntas.explicacion: When sensitive topics are going to come up at an appointment, the office is asked to talk through why privacy matters and when, and to offer tips on finding somewhere private at home, in the car or at a friend's house. Other channels are named alongside that, e-mail, text, or the platform's chat feature, especially where personal safety could be an issue.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Otitis Media", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which event most often opens the door to acute otitis media in a child?
opciones: A viral upper respiratory infection that disturbs Eustachian tube function
A viral upper respiratory infection that perforates the tympanic membrane
A build-up of cerumen that blocks the external auditory canal completely
A rise in middle ear pressure caused by hearing loss in the affected ear
preguntas.explicacion: Acute otitis media appears where pathogens, a susceptible host and the environment meet, and the usual trigger is a viral upper respiratory infection that upsets the working of the Eustachian tube. Once drainage fails, the middle ear inflames and microbes multiply. Immunocompromise and genetic predisposition raise the risk further.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conjunctivitis", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Among the infectious causes of conjunctivitis, which comes first and which pathogen leads it?
opciones: Viral conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Bacterial conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Allergic conjunctivitis, led by adenovirus
Viral conjunctivitis, led by Staphylococcus aureus
preguntas.explicacion: Infection is only one branch of the causes of red eye with discharge, and within it the viral form comes first and the bacterial one next; adenoviruses alone account for 65 to 90 percent of viral cases. The noninfectious branch is headed by allergens and toxins, and allergic conjunctivitis is reported to affect 15 to 40 percent of the population, which is why the question asks only about the infectious causes: across every cause, allergy would come out ahead. Staphylococcus aureus leads the bacterial causes in adults.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Where open access works · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A fee-for-service practice is told that open access only suits capitated managed care. Is that right?
opciones: No: it is reported to work in fee-for-service settings as well as in managed care
Yes: the model rests on capitation, since a same-day slot is not separately billable
Yes: the model was designed inside managed care and has not been tried outside it
No, but it holds up only where the practice also carries a large managed care panel
preguntas.explicacion: Experts in designing and implementing the model report that it works in fee-for-service settings as much as in managed care. Its logic has nothing to do with how a visit gets paid for: it brings queuing theory and industrial engineering to bear on matching the demand for visits against the supply of clinician time, on the supposition that the trouble is not a shortage of capacity but an imbalance between the two.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccine protection and anti-HBs testing; CDC, Exposure to Blood (2003), Treatment: HBV
preguntas.subtema: Post-vaccination testing · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: When should anti-HBs be tested to document a healthcare worker's response to the hepatitis B vaccine series?
opciones: 1 to 2 months after the final dose
6 months after the final dose
Within 10 working days of the final dose
Every year, at the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Postvaccination serologic testing for anti-HBs is done 1 to 2 months after the third dose, so that the worker's response status is on record for any future exposure; a level of 10 mIU/mL or more after a documented series is the correlate of protection. For workers who also received HBIG, testing may have to wait until the HBIG antibody has cleared, about 6 months after it was given. Ten working days is the OSHA deadline for offering the vaccine, and annual testing is not recommended for immunocompetent responders.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Denied item on the notice · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.5.b / 2027 III.G.3.b / 2027 III.G.3.b · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient brings in her Medicare summary notice showing one service as denied. What does the guidance tell her to do first?
opciones: Ring the provider's office to check that what it submitted was correct
Ring Medicare to open an appeal against the decision on that service
Ring her supplemental insurer to see whether it will pay the balance
Ring the provider's office to ask for the charge to be written off
preguntas.explicacion: For a denied item or service the first step is a call to the office of the doctor or supplier to make sure the information sent in was right; if it was not, the office may resubmit. Only if the patient disagrees with the decision itself does she appeal, and the last page of the notice sets out step by step when and how to do that.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Conducting telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Pre-visit paperwork · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A first video visit is being booked for a new patient. Which paperwork step does the workflow guidance place before the appointment?
opciones: Asking her to complete forms online covering the reason, insurance, symptoms and history
Asking her to bring printed forms to the nearest office on the morning of the appointment
Asking her to complete the forms with the clinician during the first minutes of the visit
Asking her to post the completed forms so the record is updated before the day arrives
preguntas.explicacion: Among the things done before a video visit, the guidance has the office ask the patient to complete forms online covering why she is coming, her insurance details, her symptoms and her medical history. Where she is not comfortable entering that electronically, a staff member gathers the same information before the visit begins.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pregnancy Test, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; What do the results mean?; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: HCG in urine (003619)
preguntas.subtema: False-negative urine hCG · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.d.(4) · RMA III.C.4.b.iv · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose period is two days late drank several glasses of water before giving a random urine sample, and the office pregnancy test is negative. How should this result be handled?
opciones: It may be a false negative from dilute urine or early testing; a repeat on first morning urine in about a week is advised
It is reliable, because office cassettes detect hCG from 10 days after conception regardless of urine concentration
It should be repeated immediately with a second cassette from the same kit, since a single negative can never be reported
It confirms that the patient is not pregnant, because urine tests are 97 to 99 % accurate at any point after a missed period
preguntas.explicacion: Drinking large amounts of fluid before collecting the sample can dilute the hCG so that it does not show on the test, and testing too soon after conception may precede detectable hormone levels; both produce false negatives. First morning urine is the most concentrated. Because hCG rises daily in early pregnancy, a negative test is repeated about a week later, and a still-suspected pregnancy is referred to the provider. The 97 to 99 % accuracy figure applies to tests done a week or two after a missed period.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38
preguntas.pregunta: What does an automated external defibrillator do once its pads are on the chest?
opciones: It reads the heart rhythm and shocks only when the rhythm calls for a shock
It delivers a shock as soon as the pads are attached to an unresponsive patient
It paces the heart at 100 to 120 beats a minute while compressions go on
It confirms the pulse and holds compressions until a pulse can be felt
preguntas.explicacion: The device analyzes the rhythm on its own and delivers a shock if, and only if, a shock is what that rhythm needs; the rescuer follows its spoken instructions exactly. When a shock is advised, compressions pause and everyone stands clear; the moment the shock is delivered, or if none is advised, CPR resumes without delay.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k147 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: A conventional 12-lead ECG is being set up. How many wires are attached to the patient?
opciones: Ten: four on the limbs and six across the chest
Twelve: four on the limbs and eight across the chest
Six: two on the limbs and four across the chest
Fourteen: six on the limbs and eight across the chest
preguntas.explicacion: Twelve leads are produced from ten wires. Four limb electrodes generate the six limb leads, and each of the six chest positions has its own wire. The limb leads look at the heart in the vertical plane and the chest leads record it in the horizontal plane, which is why both groups are needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Facial Laceration Repair", Special Considerations for Suture Choice
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A superficial laceration is closed with cyanoacrylate skin glue. What should the patient be told to expect?
opciones: It gives a water-tight seal and tends to come away on its own after about 7 to 10 days
It gives a water-tight seal and has to be dissolved off with acetone at the follow-up visit
It gives a water-tight seal and is removed with a staple extractor once the wound is closed
It gives a water-tight seal and stays on until the scar has finished maturing at 12 months
preguntas.explicacion: Skin glue seals the wound against water and lends it tensile strength while it lasts, and it generally falls off after roughly seven to ten days. It is quick and comparatively painless, which suits pediatric and percutaneous wounds, but it is only good for superficial lacerations: anything deeper needs a layered suture closure underneath.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Healing Phases", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: How much of its original strength does a healed incision regain, and when does maximal tensile strength arrive?
opciones: About 80 percent, reached at roughly 11 to 14 weeks after the injury
About 80 percent, reached at roughly 4 to 6 weeks after the injury
About 100 percent, reached at roughly 11 to 14 weeks after the injury
About 50 percent, reached at roughly 9 to 12 months after the injury
preguntas.explicacion: The remodeling phase starts around week three and can run up to twelve months; excess collagen degrades and contraction peaks around week three. Maximal tensile strength of an incision wound comes at roughly 11 to 14 weeks, and the scar never regains full strength, settling at about 80 percent of the original.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Specimen Collection (Fecal Samples)
preguntas.subtema: Representative stool portions · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.2 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: When a stool specimen is collected for the laboratory, which portions should be included?
opciones: Any visible pus, mucus or blood, plus material from the first, middle and last parts of the stool
Only the formed central portion, and never any mucus or blood, which would contaminate the culture badly
The last part of the stool only, since it has been in contact with the rectal mucosa longest
About 1 mL mixed with 9 mL of saline, the preparation used for every stool culture
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen is passed into a clean, dry container with a tight lid and moved on into a labeled transport container. It should deliberately take in anything abnormal the eye can see, blood, mucus or pus, and stand for the first, middle and last parts of the stool. Mixing about 1 mL with 9 mL of buffered saline and freezing the supernatant is the preparation for a suspected viral infection, not a general rule.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), note on eye contact
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 k16 · CCMA 6 k197 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: For which patients is the advice to sit near and hold eye contact given with caution?
opciones: Patients with psychotic disorders or paranoia, whom it may destabilise
Patients with hearing loss, who need to watch the speaker's lips move
Patients with dementia, who need one idea presented at a time
Patients who use sign language and watch the interpreter instead
preguntas.explicacion: The note under the table of techniques warns that eye contact, and sitting close to the patient, may destabilise some people, among them patients with paranoia or a psychotic disorder, and should be used with caution; where the provider's safety is uncertain, sit at a safe distance without leaving the patient feeling isolated. Hearing loss and dementia call for other adjustments.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.g · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: What is done to the work surface itself before any sterile supply is placed on it?
opciones: It is disinfected and then allowed to dry completely
It is disinfected and covered while still visibly wet
It is wiped with sterile water and dried with a towel
It is covered with a second drape without being wiped
preguntas.explicacion: The surface is disinfected and left to dry all the way through before anything sterile goes down on it. A surface still wet with disinfectant lets moisture wick through the drape, and moisture wicked from an unsterile area contaminates the field within an inch of where it appears. Only sterile supplies are allowed onto the field once it is established.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 12: Use Health Education Material Effectively
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant hands a patient a pamphlet about her new diagnosis and moves on. Why is that not enough?
opciones: Material works only inside a teaching plan: review it and check understanding
Material works only if it is written at or below the fourth grade level
Material works only when it is mailed home instead of handed over in person
Material works only when the patient signs that she received the pamphlet
preguntas.explicacion: Handing over a pamphlet or pointing at a website does not by itself produce understanding or a change in behavior. When the information matters, someone in the practice goes through it with the patient and the caregiver, circling or highlighting key points, personalizing it, and confirming with teach-back.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Facilitated virtual visit · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: In a facilitated virtual visit, what is the role of the medical assistant at the patient's site?
opciones: Collecting objective data with equipment and transmitting it to the remote clinician
Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit
Recording the encounter so the clinician can review the video after the appointment
Waiting outside the room, since a facilitated visit requires the patient to be alone
preguntas.explicacion: This is a synchronous model: the patient travels to a nearby site stocked with diagnostic equipment, usually a clinic, while the clinician joins from somewhere else. On site a telehealth facilitator, described as a medical assistant or a nurse, works the tools (digital stethoscope, thermometer, pulse oximeter), gathers the objective findings and sends them across for the clinician to evaluate.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: What shapes the workflow · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Two practices adopting telehealth find their workflows end up looking very different. Which factors does the guidance say the changes depend on?
opciones: The vendor chosen, the size and setting of the practice, the patient population and the services given
The vendor chosen, the age of the record system, the state licensing board and the payer mix
The size and setting of the practice, the services given, and the number of exam rooms it keeps
The patient population, the services given, and whether the practice owns its own building
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth reshapes several processes at once: check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and the structure of the appointment. How far each one shifts depends on which telehealth vendor was chosen, on the size and the setting of the practice, on its patient population and on the services it provides. The record system is expected to merge easily into whatever workflow comes out.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Timeliness
preguntas.subtema: Right of access · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient submits a written request for a copy of her chart on March 3. By when must the office act on it?
