opciones: Retract the foreskin first, then wipe the glans with a sterile wipe
Wipe the glans with a sterile wipe, leaving the foreskin where it is
Wash the tip of the penis downward with soap and water, as for an infant
Wipe the urethral opening twice, front to back, with two separate wipes
preguntas.explicacion: For a man the instruction is to wipe the glans with a sterile wipe, and if he is not circumcised the foreskin comes back first so the wipe reaches it. Leaving the foreskin in place defeats the cleaning. Washing with soap and water from the tip downward is the infant routine, and the two front-to-back wipes are the female instruction. He then voids a little into the toilet, stops, and collects until the cup is half full.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Safe and Effective Administration of Vaccines and Epinephrine Autoinjection", Anaphylaxis and Epinephrine Autoinjector
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collapses with wheezing and hives after an injection. What comes first?
opciones: Give the epinephrine, then call for help and arrange transport
Call for help, then wait for the team before giving epinephrine
Take a full set of vital signs, then decide whether epinephrine fits
Draw blood for a serum histamine level before giving any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: In anaphylaxis the drug goes in first and the call for help comes after. Providers have repeatedly been shown to delay epinephrine, and the speed of its benefit far outweighs the risk of holding it back. The patient is asked whether they can inject themselves or need help. Emergency services are called next, and the patient goes to hospital in case a second, biphasic crisis follows. Laboratory testing is of little use.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 160.404(b)(1)-(2); 45 CFR 102.3, penalty adjustment table
preguntas.subtema: Penalty cap · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What sets the top civil money penalty for all violations of one identical HIPAA provision in a calendar year?
opciones: A statutory ceiling, whose dollar figure is republished every year adjusted for inflation
A fixed ceiling of fifty thousand dollars, which is the same in all four culpability tiers
A ceiling of twenty-five thousand dollars, carried over from the rule as it stood before HITECH
A ceiling that binds only the top tier, willful neglect that was never corrected in time
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH set four culpability tiers and one ceiling covering every violation of an identical provision inside a calendar year. The enforcement rule still prints $1,500,000 there, and $50,000 per violation, but HHS republishes both adjusted for inflation at 45 CFR 102.3, where the calendar-year cap already stands above two million. The $25,000 cap belongs to violations occurring before February 18, 2009.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Clean catch urine sample (007487), How the Test is Performed; and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Midstream portion · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: During a clean-catch collection, at what point should the patient start filling the cup?
opciones: After voiding a small amount into the toilet and stopping, then collecting until the cup is about half full
As soon as the stream begins, collecting the first portion until the cup is about half full
After voiding a small amount into the toilet, then collecting every drop until the bladder is empty
After the stream has ended, collecting the last portion that remains and filling the cup to the top
preguntas.explicacion: The patient voids a small amount into the toilet, stops the flow, holds the cup a few inches from the urethra and fills it to about half, then finishes voiding into the toilet. The first portion carries the most contaminating cells and bacteria, which is why it is discarded; collecting every drop is the rule for a timed collection and for semen, not for a midstream sample. About 15 to 30 mL is enough for analysis, so the cup is never filled to the top.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Four tubes are needed: a serum separator tube, a light green PST, a purple EDTA tube and a light blue citrate tube. In the WHO order, which sequence is correct?
opciones: Light blue, serum separator, light green PST, purple EDTA
Serum separator first, light blue, purple EDTA, light green PST
Light blue, light green PST, serum separator, purple EDTA
Purple EDTA, light blue, serum separator, light green PST
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 assigns position 3 to the citrate tube, 5 to the serum separator tube, 7 to the light green plasma separator tube with lithium heparin and gel, and 8 to EDTA. So the sequence runs light blue, SST, PST, EDTA. Footnote d adds that the PST, when used, is drawn in the position shown, that is, after the serum tubes and before EDTA.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Red Reflex", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.2.b · CCMA 3B4 k62 · CMA I.C.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's red reflex is being checked with an ophthalmoscope. How is the room and the instrument set?
opciones: A dark or dimly lit room, the scope set at zero, held one to two feet away
A brightly lit room, the scope set at zero, held one to two feet away
A dark or dimly lit room, the scope set at plus ten, held six inches away
A brightly lit room, the scope set at plus ten, held about four feet away
preguntas.explicacion: The pupils have to be wide enough for light to get in, so the room is darkened; a bright room can leave the reflex absent for that reason alone. The direct ophthalmoscope is set at zero and light is shone on both eyes at once from one to two feet away, then the examiner moves in to look at each eye separately.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Septal Q-Wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of measurements makes a Q wave pathological rather than the small septal one?
opciones: Over 40 ms wide, over 1 mm deep, or over 25% of the QRS
Over 40 ms wide, over 5 mm deep, or over 50% of the QRS
Over 120 ms wide, over 1 mm deep, or over 10% of the QRS
Over 200 ms wide, over 2 mm deep, or over 25% of the QRS
preguntas.explicacion: The ordinary septal Q wave is a tiny negative dip in leads I, aVL, V5 and V6, and its amplitude does not pass 0.1 mV, so it is not always visible. A Q wave wider than one small square, deeper than 1 mm, or larger than a quarter of the QRS complex is pathological and can mark an old infarct.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Complications · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I III.B · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which two problems are attributed specifically to improper venipuncture technique?
opciones: More pain than expected, and possible injury to a nerve
More pain than expected, and clotting inside the citrate tube
A mislabelled specimen, and possible injury to a nerve nearby
A short draw in the gray tube, and bruising around the site
preguntas.explicacion: Increased pain and potential nerve injury are the two complications tied to improper technique, and both can be avoided with correct technique and equipment. Identifying the wrong patient and labeling a tube badly are reported separately as the errors most likely to happen.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection step 16 and Chapter 8 Section C
preguntas.subtema: Insufficient specimen · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: A donor hands over a container with about 30 mL of urine. What does the collector do?
opciones: Discard it and begin a second collection with a new container and the same form
Pour the 30 mL into bottle A and leave bottle B empty for a later collection
Send it as an insufficient specimen and let the laboratory decide what to do
Keep it and ask the donor to add to the same container after drinking water
preguntas.explicacion: Below 45 mL the specimen is discarded and a second collection begins immediately, using a new collection container and the same chain of custody form; temperature and physical characteristics are checked again on the second one. If the donor still cannot produce 45 mL after three hours, the collection stops, the reason is recorded and the agency's representative is notified about an alternate specimen.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5: Description of Procedure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(2) · RMA III.G.2.a(ii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A subcutaneous heparin injection has just been delivered. What happens as the needle comes out?
opciones: Keep pinching until just before withdrawal, press gently, and do not massage
Release the pinch before injecting, then massage the site to spread the dose
Keep pinching until just before withdrawal, then massage to avoid a hematoma
Release the pinch before injecting, then hold firm pressure for five minutes
preguntas.explicacion: With heparin, and with an insulin pen, the skinfold stays pinched through the whole injection and is let go just before the needle leaves. The needle comes out fast at the angle it went in, and gentle pressure follows with sterile gauze. Rubbing the spot is avoided: after a heparin dose it can help a hematoma form. The needle is never recapped.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Laboratory: Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders, Recognized Controls and Work Practices
preguntas.subtema: Ergonomic controls · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.9 / 2027 I.B.8 · NCMA 2A.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which control does OSHA suggest for a phlebotomist who sorts specimens at a bench for hours at a stretch?
opciones: Rotate tasks; provide an adjustable bench with knee room and a chair with a footrest
Provide a back belt and require two-person lifts for every full specimen rack
Limit sorting to 20 minutes per shift and assign the rest to housekeeping
Install anti-fatigue mats and require standing for the whole shift
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized controls for laboratory musculoskeletal hazards include automated specimen delivery systems to cut reaching and repetition, supportive chairs with footrests, adjustable workstations with enough knee clearance so the knees do not hit the bench, rotating tasks or limiting time on them, ergonomic computer stations for sitting and standing, anti-fatigue mats for standing stations, and handling devices for heavy carboys. Mats help where standing is unavoidable but do not justify standing all shift, and back belts are not among the listed controls.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which accessory allows a winged needle to be used with an evacuated tube system?
opciones: A luer-lock connector
A rubber sleeve adapter
A screw-thread reducer
A one-hand scoop guard
preguntas.explicacion: A vacuum system can also take a winged butterfly needle joined to it by luer-lock connectors, and winged butterfly needles come with safety-engineered features as well. The one-hand scoop is not a connector at all: it is the maneuver used to re-sheath a used needle.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative, NCCI Implementation
preguntas.subtema: Coding applications · CMA III.G.1.a(3) (2027 III.G.1.a(1)) · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184
preguntas.pregunta: A claim reports many more units of one service than a patient could receive in a day. Which set of correct coding edits catches that?
opciones: The medically unlikely edits, which look at units of service
The procedure to procedure edits, which look at code pairs
The add-on code edits, which look at the base code billed
The correct coding manual, which explains why edits exist
preguntas.explicacion: Within the national correct coding initiative, the medically unlikely edits exist to prevent improper payment where a service is reported with the wrong number of units. The procedure to procedure edits are the other half of the program and deal with pairs of codes that should not be reported together. The policy manual explains the reasoning behind both.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 k70 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous cannula has just been threaded and blood samples are wanted through it. What happens to the tourniquet?
opciones: It is loosened after threading and put back briefly to get adequate flow
It stays tight from the first puncture until the last tube has been filled
It is removed for good once the flashback appears in the chamber
It is moved down the forearm below the cannula before the tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: During cannulation the band is loosened or removed once the cannula is in and the needle is being withdrawn. If samples are to be taken at that point with a syringe or a phlebotomy adaptor, the band is put back for a moment to give enough flow, and then taken off again.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), section 3.5 Inhibitors: Endogenous and exogenous
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT V.B · CCMA 3D1 k113 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is about to give a saliva specimen for a molecular test and has just finished a coffee and brushed his teeth. Why does the collection instruction usually ask for a waiting period?
opciones: Food, non-water drinks, oral hygiene products and tobacco introduce substances that inhibit the molecular assay
Food and drink dilute the saliva so that its volume no longer reaches the minimum the collection device needs
Toothpaste raises the pH of saliva, which the assay reads as a positive result for most respiratory viruses
Coffee stains the collection swab, which blocks the optical reading of the amplification curve on the instrument
preguntas.explicacion: Saliva and buccal samples are normally taken only after a set interval with no food, no drink other than water, no oral hygiene products and no tobacco: what has been swallowed carries substances that interfere with molecular techniques, mainly polysaccharides and glycogen, enzymes like the plasmin of milk products, and minerals, calcium among them. One study of children found interference from food minimal when saliva was collected 20 minutes after a meal; the interval that applies is the manufacturer's.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Protein in diet — Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(c) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(c) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: About how much protein does one ounce of most protein-rich foods supply?
opciones: About 7 grams of protein
About 4 grams of protein
About 14 grams of protein
About 21 grams of protein
preguntas.explicacion: One ounce, roughly 30 grams, of most protein-rich food carries about 7 grams of protein. An ounce of meat, fish or poultry, one large egg, or a quarter cup of tofu each land in that range. The number 4 is a different one: it is the calories that a single gram of protein supplies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k59 k51 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for a PT/INR comes back only about half full. What is the fill requirement for this tube, and why is a half-filled tube a problem?
opciones: Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 9:1 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to at least 50% of the tube volume, so that the 9:1 ratio is still within range
Filling to at least 90% of the tube volume, to keep the 1:9 blood-to-citrate ratio
Filling to the line only when the patient's hematocrit is above 55 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The tube has to be filled to within 90% of its full volume so that blood and sodium citrate stay in a 9 to 1 ratio; a half-filled tube breaks that ratio. The coagulopathies review adds that underfilling, like a hematocrit above 55%, raises the relative citrate level and disturbs the recalcification step of the assay. The ratio is nine parts blood to one of citrate, not the reverse.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Self re-sheathing needles
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: How does a self re-sheathing needle and syringe protect the worker?
opciones: A sleeve is pushed forward over the used needle to guard it
A spring pulls the used needle back inside the syringe barrel
A hinged cap is snapped shut over the bevel with both hands
A blunt inner cannula slides out ahead of the sharpened tip
preguntas.explicacion: In this design a sleeve is moved forward over the needle, forming a guard around the used tip and preventing the device being used again. Retraction into the syringe body is the mechanism of the manually retractable device, which is a different row of the same table.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hearing Loss Assessment in Children", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which two methods are used to screen the hearing of a newborn?
opciones: Otoacoustic emissions and automated auditory brainstem response testing
Pure-tone audiometry and the word recognition score obtained at bedside
Tympanometry and the whispered voice test done at arm's length behind
Conditioned play audiometry and visual reinforcement audiometry
preguntas.explicacion: Newborn screening rests on emissions from the cochlear outer hair cells and on the automated brainstem response. A present emission counts as a pass; an absent one means a referral and usually reflects middle ear disease or a sensorineural loss of at least 40 decibels. Reinforcement audiometry starts around six months and play audiometry between ages two and five.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory offers a practice free rent in exchange for sending it specimens. Which law does that implicate?
opciones: The Anti-Kickback Statute, which covers remuneration of any kind
The False Claims Act, which covers false statements on a claim form
The Exclusion Statute, which covers convictions for patient neglect
The Civil Monetary Penalties Law, which covers late claim filing
preguntas.explicacion: The Anti-Kickback Statute makes it a crime to offer, pay, solicit or receive remuneration knowingly and willfully so as to induce or reward a referral for items or services that federal health care programs pay for; remuneration covers anything of value, with free rent among the examples given. Penalties run to fines, imprisonment and exclusion, and under the penalties law up to three times the amount of the kickback.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's forearm shows no vein joining the cephalic and basilic veins at the elbow. Which pattern of the cubital fossa is that?
opciones: Type IV, in which no communicating branch links the two veins
Type II, in which the median cubital vein links the two veins
Type I, in which the median antebrachial vein links both veins
Type III, in which the median cubital vein is unusually large
preguntas.explicacion: The superficial veins here fall into four patterns. Type IV is the one with no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic; type II, where the median cubital vein joins them, is the commonest, followed by type I with a dominant median antebrachial vein. Type III has a poorly developed vein.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method, Action
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: During teach-back the patient says she will have coffee with sugar before the fasting draw. What is the next step?
opciones: Explain again using a different approach, then ask her to teach it back once more
Repeat the same words more slowly and then move on to the next topic
Have her read the instruction sheet aloud back to you, word for word
Record that she did not pass the teach-back and reschedule the test
preguntas.explicacion: When teach-back uncovers a misunderstanding, the clinician explains with a different approach and asks for teach-back again, repeating the cycle until the patient can describe the information correctly in their own words; parroting the words back, or reading the handout verbatim, does not show understanding. Teach-back is not a test that a patient fails.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 7: Handling and Storage
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 7 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Where does a safety data sheet say how a chemical should be stored and which products it must be kept away from?
opciones: Section 7, which also gives the hygiene practices for handling it
Section 2, which also gives the classification and the signal word
Section 14, which also gives the shipping name and the UN number
Section 11, which also gives the toxicity figures and the symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7 is the day-to-day section: precautions for safe handling, including how to deal with incompatible chemicals, how to keep the product from being released, and general hygiene advice such as the ban on eating, drinking and smoking in work areas; and then the conditions for safe storage, incompatibilities and any specific requirement such as ventilation. Section 14, on transport, is one of the four sections OSHA does not enforce.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine collection - infants (003417), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Infant bag placement, male · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(e) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A urine collection bag is being applied to a male infant. Where does the bag go?
opciones: The whole penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the skin around it
Only the tip of the penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the diaper
The bag is taped across the two skin folds flanking the opening where urine flows out
The bag is laid loose inside the diaper, without adhesive, so that the voided urine drains into it
preguntas.explicacion: For a boy the whole penis goes inside the plastic bag and the sticky strip fixes to the skin; for a girl the bag covers the two skin folds that flank the vaginal opening. Before it goes on, the area round the urethra is washed thoroughly with the soap or wipes the provider supplied. A bag not sealed to the skin, or one holding only the tip, will leak.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k84 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.g · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: A pharmacist dispenses a Schedule II drug on an oral authorization in an emergency. What must the prescriber do next?
opciones: Deliver a written prescription within 7 days, marked Authorization for Emergency Dispensing
Deliver a written prescription within 48 hours, marked Authorization for Emergency Dispensing
Deliver a written prescription within 30 days, together with a copy of the DEA order form
No further step: the pharmacist's written note of the oral order is the only record
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency the quantity is held to what treats the patient through the emergency period, and the pharmacist immediately puts the oral order in writing with everything the regulation demands except the prescriber's signature. Within 7 days a written prescription for that quantity has to reach the pharmacist, carrying the date of the oral order and the legend Authorization for Emergency Dispensing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position)
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical factors · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E1 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives at the office laboratory out of breath after climbing several flights of stairs. What is recommended before the draw, and why?
opciones: Have the patient sit for at least 15 minutes, since posture changes alter biochemistry results
Draw immediately, because exertion raises the venous pressure and makes the veins easier to find
Have the patient lie down for two to three minutes and then draw with a butterfly set
Postpone the draw for 24 hours, the interval the chapter sets after physical activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients in an office setting should stay seated for at least 15 minutes before the procedure, because statistically significant changes in several biochemistry parameters follow a change in position, and any unavoidable change should be recorded. The 24-hour rule in the same chapter concerns avoiding excessive physical activity before the collection, not a postponement.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · CMA F.5.b / 2027 F.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: At the start of an interview the clinician says how much time there is. How does that help?
opciones: It lets the patient rank concerns and feel in control of them
It shortens the history so that the examination can begin
It keeps the patient from raising more than one problem
It replaces the prompting question about other concerns
preguntas.explicacion: Expressing the time allocation at the beginning helps the patient prioritize their concerns and empowers them to feel in control of the discussion. It does not replace the prompting question about anything else, which often has to be asked more than once because the main concern is rarely the first one mentioned.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Intoxicated Patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who smells strongly of alcohol refuses his draw and the nurse is unsure how impaired he is. What is directed?
opciones: Carry out the usual capacity assessment, since intoxication varies in degree
Draw anyway, because intoxication always removes the right to refuse care
Accept the refusal with no assessment, since the refusal is his to make
Wait for a court order before any decision about the draw is taken
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol or drugs on board may leave a patient without capacity, and where the level of intoxication is uncertain the usual capacity assessment is carried out. That impairment is often temporary: sober again, the same patient may decide soundly. Formal guardianship through a court belongs to long-term situations.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Body Fluid Samples
preguntas.subtema: Body fluid transport · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.1 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: Pleural, peritoneal and synovial fluids have been aspirated for culture. How should they travel to the laboratory?
opciones: Promptly and at room temperature, which keeps the organisms viable
Promptly and refrigerated, which keeps the organisms viable in transit
Promptly and frozen, since the cell count is read from the thawed fluid
Whenever convenient, provided each container has been sealed and labeled
preguntas.explicacion: Aspiration is aseptic and the container sterile, and what gets recorded is the appearance, the color, the turbidity, the viscosity and any clot. Portions go out for cell count and differential, for protein and glucose, for culture and for cytology. The microbiology portion depends on prompt transport at room temperature to keep the organisms alive, the same principle that governs cerebrospinal fluid.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Other Issues, Human Clinical Studies; and StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Under which measure was the Institutional Review Board established in the United States?
opciones: The National Research Act, in 1974
The National Research Act, in 1984
The Belmont Report, issued in 1976
The Declaration of Helsinki revisions
preguntas.explicacion: The National Research Act created the board in 1974, bringing regulation to human research after unethical practices such as the Tuskegee syphilis experiments. The Belmont Report names beneficence, justice and respect for persons as its guiding principles, and the Declaration of Helsinki is an ethical statement; neither created the board.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hemoglobin A1C", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure; Diagnostic Tests; StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Quality Control and Lab Safety
preguntas.subtema: POC A1C confirmation · CPT D5 k90 · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 k114 · CMA I.C.10.c.(5) · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A fingerstick A1C on a clinic's point-of-care analyzer reads 6.6 % in a patient without a diabetes diagnosis. What should happen next?
opciones: The result is confirmed with a venous sample before any diagnosis, because capillary point-of-care A1C values are variable
Diabetes is diagnosed on the spot, because 6.5 % or higher on any A1C method is diagnostic without a second test
The fingerstick is repeated the same day and the two capillary results are averaged to reach the diagnostic value
The patient is scheduled for a repeat fingerstick A1C in three months, and diabetes is diagnosed if it is still 6.5 % or more
preguntas.explicacion: Capillary point-of-care A1C is variable, so an A1C taken from a capillary sample gets confirmed on a venous one before any diagnosis is made; point-of-care devices also tend to read about 0.5 % below laboratory assays. For screening and diagnosis, point-of-care A1C is limited to FDA-approved devices run in CLIA-certified laboratories doing moderate complexity testing or higher, with certified methods.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: Forearm crutches are being fitted. Where does the cuff sit and how far out do the tips go?
opciones: The cuff 1.5 inches below the elbow and the tips 4 inches outside the feet
The cuff 1.5 inches above the elbow and the tips 6 inches outside the feet
The cuff 2 inches below the elbow and the tips 6 inches outside the feet
The cuff 4 inches below the elbow and the tips 1.5 inches outside the feet
preguntas.explicacion: For forearm crutches the cuff is set an inch and a half below the elbow and the crutch stands about four inches to the outside of the foot, with the hand grip giving 30 degrees of elbow flexion. The two-inch clearance and the six-inch offset belong to the axilla crutch, which is fitted differently.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which superficial vein connects the cephalic and basilic veins in the cubital fossa?
opciones: The median cubital vein
The median antebrachial vein
The brachial vein
The dorsal venous arch
preguntas.explicacion: As the cephalic and basilic veins approach the cubital fossa they become joined by the median cubital vein, which has a median cephalic and a median basilic connection. The dorsal venous arch is where both veins begin on the back of the hand, the median antebrachial vein is the dominant vessel only in the type I fossa, and the brachial vein is deep.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Barrier removal · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: An older office building has two steps at its entrance. What does the law ask of the practice inside it?
opciones: Remove the barrier where doing so is readily achievable, and otherwise serve by other means
Remove the barrier only when the building is next altered or the lease comes up for renewal
Remove the barrier only if a patient files a written complaint about the entrance first
Leave the entrance as it stands, since buildings raised before the law are not reached by it
preguntas.explicacion: Every building is subject to the requirements for existing facilities, whatever its age. Under Title III architectural barriers are removed where removal is readily achievable, that is, easily accomplishable without much difficulty or expense; where it is not, the services still have to be made available by alternative methods that are readily achievable.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: First morning specimen · PBT V.B.1 / V.A · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the first void of the morning considered the best representative urine specimen for testing?
opciones: It is the most concentrated, so it shows concentrating ability and reveals substances present in traces
It is the most dilute, so cells, casts and crystals stay intact in it until they can be examined
It has spent the least time in the bladder, so bacteria have had no chance to grow in it overnight
It is collected before meals, so it averages out the effect of food and of physical activity
preguntas.explicacion: Urine that has accumulated in the bladder through the night is the most concentrated of the day. That is what makes it the best representative sample: it shows how well the kidneys concentrate and it lets small amounts of a substance be detected that a diluted specimen would hide. Random, two-hour postprandial and 24-hour collections are ordered instead when the purpose calls for them.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Low blood sugar", Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.f · 2027 I.B.8.f · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: At which blood glucose level is a patient considered to be hypoglycemic?
opciones: Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), which can already do harm
Below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L), the lower end of the fasting range
Below 55 mg/dL (3.1 mmol/L), and never above that figure
Below 40 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L), when the patient loses consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: A blood sugar under 70 mg/dL, or 3.9 mmol/L, counts as low and can be harmful at or below that level. Symptoms may not appear until the glucose falls below 55 mg/dL, which is why the number matters and not only how the patient looks. Severe low blood sugar that ends in unconsciousness is what is called insulin shock.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Handoff Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: How is a handoff report defined?
opciones: A transfer and acceptance of responsibility for a patient's care
A written summary filed at the close of every nursing shift
A standing set of orders that follows the patient between units
A review of the record made before the next provider walks in
preguntas.explicacion: The definition used is a transfer and acceptance of responsibility for patient care achieved through effective communication: patient-specific information passed in real time from one caregiver, or one team, to the next, so that care stays continuous and safe. A filed summary or a set of orders is not that exchange.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Blood pressure measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.d · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: How is a blood pressure of 120 over 80 correctly recorded?
opciones: 120/80 mm Hg, systolic first and the units written after the pair
80/120 mm Hg, diastolic first because it is the resting value of the two
120/80 mm, since the unit of the gauge is millimeters of the column
120 over 80 kPa, the pressure unit used on automated office devices
preguntas.explicacion: The systolic value goes first, then a slash, then the diastolic, and the unit is millimeters of mercury: 120/80 mm Hg. The gauge on the cuff reads in that unit, and the arm used and the patient's position belong in the record beside the numbers, since both change the value.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: USPS Ground Advantage
preguntas.subtema: Hazardous shipments · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An item classed as hazardous material cannot travel by air. Which domestic service is named as the primary option for it?
opciones: USPS Ground Advantage, the ground service that reaches most places in two to five days
Priority Mail Express, whose network is built around the fastest possible movement
First-Class Mail, whose light pieces travel with ordinary letters and small envelopes
Media Mail, whose slower schedule already allows for surface transport of the contents
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is described as the low-rate ground service with expected delivery in two to five days and as the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot go by air. Its handling fee for such items is also the only one of the three parcel services set at nothing extra.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields; and StatPearls, "Sterile Technique" (NBK459175)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.g · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: A sterile drape has been opened over a treatment table. Which part of it counts as contaminated from the start?
opciones: The one-inch border running around the edge of the drape
The one-inch border running around the edge, plus the center
The half of the drape furthest from the person who opened it
The four corners where the flaps were folded before opening
preguntas.explicacion: An imaginary border one inch wide along the edges is treated as unsterile, so supplies are never tossed or slid into it. The same one-inch rule applies around any hole, tear or patch of moisture wicked in from an unsterile area. Peel-pack wrappers carry the same border, which is why items are not slid out near the edge of the pouch.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Light Blue; and "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: What concentration of sodium citrate does the light blue coagulation tube contain?
preguntas.explicacion: Both the tube collection review and the prothrombin time chapter give 3.2% sodium citrate as the anticoagulant of the light blue tube. The figure 9 comes from a different rule in the same chapter, the 9 to 1 ratio of blood to citrate that the tube must keep, and the other two numbers are misplacements of the decimal point. The citrate works by chelating calcium.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: A and B Recommendations — Folic Acid Supplementation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C preventive medicine · CMA I.A.5 · 2027 I.A.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient planning a pregnancy asks about folic acid. What is recommended, and to whom?
opciones: 0.4 to 0.8 mg daily for everyone planning or able to become pregnant
0.4 to 0.8 mg daily, but only once the pregnancy has been confirmed
4 to 8 mg daily for everyone planning or able to become pregnant
0.4 to 0.8 mg daily, but only for those with a previous affected pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation carries an A grade and covers everyone who plans to become pregnant or could: a daily supplement holding 0.4 to 0.8 mg, that is 400 to 800 micrograms, of folic acid, to prevent neural tube defects. Waiting for a confirmed pregnancy misses the window in which the tube closes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?
preguntas.subtema: Where consults happen · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a telephone consult about a named patient from the phone in the hospital cafeteria. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The talk is allowed, but it has to happen away from the public
The talk is barred, since consults require written authorization
The talk is allowed only if the patient is on the line as well
The talk is barred, because phone lines are never encrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Consulting another provider is a permitted conversation; where it happens is what matters. Such talk belongs in a private room, out of earshot of the public, and a telephone consult taken from a cafeteria line, where anyone nearby can hear, is the example given of how not to do it. Staff may still coordinate verbally at a nurses' station, and providers may discuss a patient's status by telephone.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications
preguntas.subtema: Soap and water vs alcohol rub · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: When does the CDC say soap and water must be used rather than alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
opciones: When hands look soiled, after using the restroom, or during a C. difficile outbreak
Before every aseptic task and after any contact with the patient's immediate surroundings
Whenever the sanitizer on hand contains less than 60 percent alcohol by volume
Whenever gloves have been worn for longer than the 20 seconds a hand rub takes
preguntas.explicacion: In most clinical moments the CDC prefers an alcohol-based hand rub, and it sends staff to soap and water in a short list of situations: hands that look soiled, before eating, after a restroom visit, and while caring for patients with known or suspected C. difficile or norovirus during an outbreak. The reason is chemical, since spore formers and non-enveloped organisms survive alcohol and have to be removed mechanically by washing. Aseptic tasks and contact with the patient's surroundings are moments for hand hygiene by either method, not reasons to reach for soap.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: How is a spot tested to decide whether it is non-blanching?
opciones: Brief pressure is applied, and the spot does not disappear
Brief pressure is applied, and the spot fades then returns
The skin is stretched, and the spot spreads sideways with it
The skin is cooled, and the spot pales under the cold pack
preguntas.explicacion: A non-blanching spot is one that stays visible after brief pressure is put on the area. That single maneuver separates bleeding into the skin, which does not pale, from simple redness of the skin, which does. Both petechiae and purpura are defined as non-blanching.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: Under the civil False Claims Act, what does the government have to prove about intent?
opciones: No specific intent to defraud is needed; reckless disregard is enough
A specific intent to defraud the program has to be shown for each claim
Only that the claim was denied by the payer after it had been reviewed
Only that the provider failed to refund an overpayment within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: The civil False Claims Act catches anybody who knowingly presents a false or fraudulent claim, or causes one to be presented, and knowingly there takes in actual knowledge, deliberate ignorance and reckless disregard of the truth. No specific intent to defraud is required. A denial proves nothing on its own, and the 60-day overpayment rule is a separate duty whose breach can then create liability.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification; Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen from a neurology ICU arrives in a urine cup instead of a sterile CSF tube. How does the emergency laboratory handle it?
opciones: A laboratory medicine specialist decides whether this precious specimen is rejected or accepted
The accessioning clerk rejects it automatically, as with any specimen in an improper container
It is accepted without review, because CSF can never be recollected from the same patient
It is transferred by the clerk into a sterile tube and processed as an ordinary specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Improper container is a standing rejection criterion, and sending CSF in a urine cup is described as a common mistake in the neurology ICU; but for precious specimens such as CSF, bone marrow or aspirates received in unsuitable tubes or under wrong transport conditions, the decision to reject or accept is reserved to the laboratory medicine specialists rather than made automatically at the desk.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: During the Visit, Needle Length
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(2) · RMA III.G.2.b · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: An adult woman weighing about 250 lb is to receive an intramuscular vaccine in the deltoid. Which needle is chosen?
opciones: A 1.5-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, because she weighs more than 200 lb
A 1-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, which is the choice below 130 lb
A 5/8-inch needle, 23 to 25 gauge, which is the subcutaneous choice
A 1-inch needle, 18 to 22 gauge, chosen for a thicker vaccine product
preguntas.explicacion: Needle length for an intramuscular vaccine in an adult follows weight. Below 130 lb, and from 130 to 152 lb, an inch is used; men from 153 to 260 lb and women from 153 to 200 lb take 1 to 1.5 inches; men over 260 lb and women over 200 lb take 1.5 inches. The gauge stays 22 to 25 throughout. Five eighths of an inch with 23 to 25 gauge is the row for the subcutaneous route at any age.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tonometry", Introduction
preguntas.pregunta: What is the accepted normal range of intraocular pressure?
opciones: 10 to 21 mmHg, above which ocular hypertension is described
10 to 21 mmHg, above which glaucoma is definitively diagnosed
20 to 31 mmHg, above which ocular hypertension is described
5 to 15 mmHg, above which ocular hypertension is described
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure inside the eye normally sits between 10 and 21 millimeters of mercury, a range taken from average levels in healthy people. Pressure above 21 is called ocular hypertension and is the single greatest risk factor for glaucoma, but the raised pressure alone is not the diagnosis: glaucoma is a progressive optic neuropathy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A child with Down syndrome is plotted below the usual curves. What does the technique call for?
opciones: A specialized chart for that condition is used in place of the standard one
The standard chart is kept, and the values below the curve are simply noted
The chart is dropped, and only the measurements themselves are recorded
The chart for a younger age group is used, since growth runs behind schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions that change the pattern of growth need their own plots to give a meaningful result, and specialized charts exist for achondroplasia, for cerebral palsy, and for the syndromes of Down, Turner, Williams, Prader-Willi and Rett. Whatever chart is used, it contributes to the picture rather than making a diagnosis by itself.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Hypodermic single-use needle and syringe
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which disadvantage does the WHO device table attach to collecting blood with a hypodermic needle and syringe?
opciones: The blood has to be transferred, adding needle-stick and splash risk
It cannot be used for blood drawing in the pediatric population
It cannot be heparinized, so it is unsuitable for arterial blood samples
It requires more training than an evacuated tube system
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 lists as disadvantages of the syringe that the blood has to be transferred, which adds a risk of needle-stick injuries or blood splashing, that large or multiple samples are difficult, and that a smaller syringe and pediatric tube are needed for children. Its advantages include use in children, heparinization for arterial draws, low cost and no special training.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: When is compression-only CPR accepted instead of compressions with rescue breaths?
opciones: When the rescuer is untrained, or has no barrier device such as a rescue mask
When the patient is a child, whose arrest usually starts as a heart problem
When two rescuers are present and the compressor is being rotated often
When an advanced airway is already in place and the breaths are given separately
preguntas.explicacion: Compression-only CPR is an acceptable alternative for the untrained layperson, and also for a trained rescuer outside the hospital who has no barrier device such as a rescue mask. Once an advanced airway is in place the opposite happens: compressions run without interruption and breaths are given at 10 a minute, which is not compression-only CPR.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E
preguntas.pregunta: What does the Medicare eligibility system send a provider every month, and what is the provider expected to do with it?
opciones: A report of the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be reviewed
A report of the claims paid under its identifier, to be matched against postings
A list of the patients whose coverage lapsed, to be corrected before the next visit
A bill for the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be paid monthly
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are told to check the monthly reports detailing the eligibility transactions associated with their National Provider Identifier, and to take anything that looks wrong up with their vendor or clearinghouse directly. That is also why the enrollment has to keep a current email address: the monthly reports and the recertification contacts are sent there, and vendors are told to make sure their customers keep valid addresses.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position and fasting)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the only thing taken that morning before a fasting draw was a cup of black coffee, no sugar. Under the guidance on fasting samples, is the specimen acceptable?
opciones: No: during the fasting period water is acceptable, but coffee and other drinks such as energy drinks are not allowed
Yes: black coffee without sugar adds no calories and is treated the same way as plain water during a fast
Yes, provided the coffee was taken more than 2 hours before the draw and the patient then drank plain water
No: coffee is allowed only together with the morning medicines, which this patient did not take
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended set-up is a morning draw after at least 12 hours without solid food. Water during the fast is fine; coffee, energy drinks and any other beverage are off the table that morning, and alcohol is dropped for the preceding 24 hours. A non-fasting sample is accepted only for patients who cannot manage the fast, in emergencies, and for analytes that fasting does not move. Fasting status is confirmed a second time once identity has been verified.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B: Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: Refrigerator, freezer and room ranges · CPT D1 1E · PBT IV.B.2 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.d · RMA III.C.3.e
preguntas.pregunta: A refrigerator that stores patient samples and control materials is typically kept in which temperature range?
preguntas.explicacion: The usual sample refrigerator runs between 2 and 8 °C, a sample freezer between −25 and −15 °C, and rooms used for testing and storage between 15 and 30 °C. The correct range for any unit is ultimately set by the acceptable storage range in the manufacturer's instructions for what is kept in it. Temperatures are checked and recorded daily, and the testing room before it is used, whatever monitoring device is installed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications; and StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Technique
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 k49 · PBT II.D II.I · CCMA 3E1 k128 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's history shows a right radical mastectomy. Which precaution applies when choosing where to draw?
opciones: Avoid drawing from the arm on the side of the mastectomy
Draw from the right arm but use a smaller-gauge needle
Draw from the right hand only, never from the antecubital fossa
Draw from either arm, as long as the tourniquet stays under one minute
preguntas.explicacion: A history of radical mastectomy on the same side is listed among the site contraindications, along with scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or an abscess, fibrosis of the vein, a hematoma, a vascular graft, and any venous access device such as a port, a central catheter or an IV. Capillary testing repeats the rule: keep off the side of a recent mastectomy or of an ongoing infusion.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Copayment; and Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Copayment vs coinsurance · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.6.e, III.G.9.c / 2027 III.G.6.c · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a copayment and coinsurance?
opciones: A copayment is a set dollar figure per service and coinsurance is a percentage of it
A copayment is a percentage of the service and coinsurance is a set dollar figure
A copayment is owed before the deductible and coinsurance replaces the deductible
A copayment is owed monthly for coverage and coinsurance is owed at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: A copayment is a fixed amount, $20 for instance, that the patient pays for a covered service. Coinsurance is a share expressed as a percentage of the allowed amount, 20% for instance, so the dollars change with the price of the service. Both are usually owed after the deductible is satisfied. The monthly amount owed for the coverage itself, used or not, is the premium.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with new angina is booked for a Holter as the first test. Why is that the wrong step?
opciones: Because a monitor that holds up urgent care is contraindicated
Because palpitations once a week are too rare for a monitor
Because a patient with a pacemaker cannot wear a monitor
Because strong fields at work would spoil the recording
preguntas.explicacion: It is contraindicated when it delays urgent care: it should not open the workup of angina, where a stress test fits better, and a patient with syncope and high-risk features belongs in hospital. Screening people who have no symptoms is also ruled out.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(D), Gloves in volunteer blood donation centers
preguntas.subtema: Donation center gloving policy · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A volunteer blood donation center decides gloves are not routinely needed for every draw. What must the employer still do?
opciones: Reevaluate the policy periodically, keep gloves available, and never discourage their use
Record every draw done without gloves in the sharps injury log kept for the year
Obtain a signed declination from each employee who draws without wearing gloves
Report the policy to the Assistant Secretary before the first donation session
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(D) lets a volunteer blood donation center judge that routine gloving for every phlebotomy is unnecessary, but it attaches four duties: reevaluate that judgment periodically, make gloves available to anyone who wants them, do nothing to discourage their use, and require them when the employee has cuts or breaks in the skin, when hand contamination looks likely, and while the employee is being trained. The declination statement is for the hepatitis B vaccine, and the sharps log records percutaneous injuries, not gloving decisions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Other Issues: Disposing of PHI
preguntas.subtema: Disposal of PHI · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How should paper records and prescription labels that contain PHI be disposed of?
opciones: Shredded or incinerated so that nobody can piece them back together
Placed in a red biohazard bag and treated as regulated waste
Handed to the person in charge of shredding to take home and destroy later
Kept in a locked cabinet indefinitely, since PHI may never be destroyed
preguntas.explicacion: Documents with PHI are shredded or incinerated so that no reconstruction is possible, computers, CDs and drives are completely erased before disposal, and the people assigned to destruction are chosen so that records are in fact destroyed rather than taken home; letting the shredding staff carry records home is exactly what that selection is meant to prevent. A red bag is the container for regulated waste under the bloodborne pathogens standard, which is about infection, not confidentiality, and HIPAA sets a retention period for its own documentation rather than a ban on destroying records.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Language Barriers; and ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2F k16 k43 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 k127 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who is deaf and uses sign language needs the informed-consent discussion for a therapeutic phlebotomy. What should be arranged?
opciones: An American Sign Language medical interpreter for the discussion
A written summary handed to the patient in place of the discussion
The patient's hearing spouse to relay the discussion in sign language
A shorter discussion, since the procedure is routine and low risk
preguntas.explicacion: Language barriers and interpreters used badly complicate informed consent, so interpreter services go to patients whose command of the spoken language is limited, and medical interpreters in American Sign Language should be available for patients who are hearing-impaired. Under the ADA a companion may interpret only in narrow circumstances, and a doctor's office discussing a procedure generally needs an interpreter.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A paternity test is requested. Which tube does the WHO order-of-draw table assign to that use?
opciones: The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The light blue tube with sodium citrate
The purple tube with EDTA anticoagulant
The yellow-black striped blood culture bottle
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies as the uses of the pale yellow tube containing acid-citrate-dextrose (ACD, ACDA or ACDB), whose mode of action is described as complement inactivation. The light blue tube is for coagulation, the purple tube for hematology and cross-match, and the yellow-black bottle for aerobic and anaerobic cultures and fungi.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Non-invasive Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: Volume and labeling · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D4 k113 · CMA I.C.8.a · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: How much urine is needed for an accurate routine urinalysis, and where should the label go?
opciones: About 15 to 30 mL, with the label placed on the container itself and not on the lid
About 15 to 30 mL, with the label placed on the lid so the container stays see-through
The container filled to capacity, with the label placed on the container and not the lid
About 100 to 120 mL, with the label placed across the lid and the container together
preguntas.explicacion: Roughly 15 to 30 mL is enough for an accurate analysis, so patients are told not to fill the cup to the top. The lid and rim are closed carefully to avoid contaminating them, and the specimen is labeled before or immediately after collection, on the container and never on the lid, because a lid can end up on a different cup.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples
preguntas.subtema: CSF numbered tubes · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.8.a · RMA III.C.4.a.vi
preguntas.pregunta: Cerebrospinal fluid from a lumbar puncture is distributed into three sterile tubes. Which tube goes to microbiology?
opciones: Tube 2, while tube 1 goes for chemistry and serology and tube 3 for cytology
Tube 1, while tube 2 goes for chemistry and serology and tube 3 for the cytology
Tube 3, while tube 1 goes for chemistry and serology and tube 2 for cytology
Any tube, as long as each one is labeled with the test it is meant for
preguntas.explicacion: The fluid is split into three sterile tubes with fixed assignments: the first for chemistry and serology, the second for culture and sensitivity, and the third for cytology. The fluid is taken under strict aseptic precautions, usually at the L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace. Processing has to be immediate, since delay degrades the cells and shifts the results, glucose above all.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), If an Exposure Occurs; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Step 1
preguntas.subtema: Needlestick first aid · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the CDC say about squeezing the wound or applying bleach to it?
opciones: Neither has evidence behind it, and caustic agents like bleach are not advised
Squeezing is recommended to expel contaminated blood; bleach is not advised
Bleach at a 1:10 dilution is recommended on the wound; squeezing is not
Both are recommended right away, before the wound is washed with soap and water
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing in the evidence says an antiseptic, or squeezing the wound, lowers the chance of passing on a bloodborne pathogen, and bleach and other caustics are not advised at all. What is recommended is washing the needlestick with soap and water. The WHO annex on occupational exposure says the same: soap and water, no alcohol and no strong disinfectant, let the wound bleed freely, and leave it undressed. The 1:10 bleach dilution belongs to surfaces after a spill, never to skin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Introduction: Burden of Proof
preguntas.subtema: Civil and criminal acts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4 · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What does the jury have to be convinced of in a civil medical negligence case?
opciones: That the plaintiff's account is more plausible than the defendant's
That the plaintiff's account is proven beyond any reasonable doubt
That the plaintiff's account is supported by two expert witnesses
That the plaintiff's account is admitted by the treating clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Civil cases use a lower bar than criminal ones. The plaintiff has to convince the jury by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning at least 51 percent: the argument and the evidence must look likelier as the proximate cause of the injury alleged than whatever the defense puts up. Proof beyond a reasonable doubt belongs to criminal prosecutions.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(a)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the collection agency that her employer forbids calls of that kind at work. What does the statute then require?
opciones: The collector must stop telephoning her at her place of employment altogether
The collector may go on calling provided it leaves no message with a colleague
The collector may go on calling until she puts the objection down in writing
The collector must contact her only through the attorney representing her instead
preguntas.explicacion: Contacting a consumer at her place of employment is barred where the collector knows, or has reason to know, that her employer forbids her to receive such communication. A separate provision blocks contact with a consumer the collector knows is represented by an attorney whose name and address it has or can readily find, unless that attorney fails to respond or consents.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Daily Value on the Nutrition and Supplement Facts Labels: Which nutrients are required
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4)
preguntas.pregunta: Which vitamins and minerals must appear on the Nutrition Facts label with both an amount and a %DV?
opciones: Vitamin D, calcium, iron and potassium
Vitamin D, calcium, iron and magnesium
Vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium and iron
Vitamin D, folate, iron and potassium
preguntas.explicacion: Those four are the mandatory micronutrients, listed with the actual quantity and the percentage. Others may be added voluntarily, and must be listed when the manufacturer fortifies the food or makes a claim about them on the package. They are also the four the label groups as nutrients to get more of, along with fiber.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Underpayment Recoveries
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMA III.G.6.a (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: How much of net patient revenue do providers fail to collect, and what is blamed for it?
opciones: Two to five percent, partly from weak billing and the effort of disputing claims
Five to ten percent, partly from weak billing and the effort of disputing claims
Ten to fifteen percent, mostly because patients never pay the balances they owe
Under one percent, mostly because contractual write-offs get posted incorrectly
preguntas.explicacion: Underpayment recoveries measure what never comes in: between two and five percent of net patient revenue, blamed in part on inefficient revenue-cycle work and in part on the sheer effort of disputing claims, with certain insurers so notorious for wearing claimants down that practices have stopped accepting them. Five to ten percent is a different benchmark in the same material, the claim denial rate.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities
preguntas.subtema: Employer disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: An employer asks the practice for information about an employee's work-related injury. When may that be released without authorization?
opciones: When the employer needs it to comply with an occupational safety requirement
Whenever the employer is the one paying the premium for the employee's plan
Whenever the employee has already told the employer that the injury happened
Only when a court has ordered the practice to produce the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Among the public health activities, a covered entity may disclose to an employer, at the employer's request and about its own employee, information on an illness or injury that is work- related or on medical surveillance of the workplace, because the employer needs it to satisfy the requirements of OSHA, or those of the Mine Safety and Health Administration, or of a State law that does the same job. Workers' compensation disclosures are a separate national priority purpose.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging, Positron Emission Tomography
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which imaging technique shows physiologic activity such as blood flow and nutrient metabolism rather than a static picture?
opciones: PET, which uses short-lived radiopharmaceuticals given before the scan
CT, which uses short-lived radiopharmaceuticals given before the scan
MRI, which uses short-lived radiopharmaceuticals given before the scan
Ultrasound, which uses short-lived radiopharmaceuticals given before the scan
preguntas.explicacion: Positron emission tomography relies on radiopharmaceuticals whose radiation dies away quickly, which is what makes them reasonably safe to give. Its advantage over CT and MRI, which produce static images, is that it shows the organ at work, which is why it is used for heart disease, spread of cancer, and brain and thyroid problems.

preguntas.fuente: DEA, Drug Scheduling
preguntas.subtema: Laws and regulations · CCMA 7A k214 (Controlled Substances Act) · CMA E.5.b · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: On what basis are controlled substances placed into their schedules?
opciones: On accepted medical use and the potential for abuse or dependency
On the strength of the dose and the route by which it is given
On the cost to the health plan and the risk of diversion in transit
On the length of time the drug has been approved for sale in the country
preguntas.explicacion: Drugs and substances, and certain chemicals employed in making them, are sorted into five schedules by their accepted medical use and their potential for abuse or dependency, with the abuse rate as the determining factor. Schedule I has a high potential for abuse and no medical use currently accepted; Schedule V has the lowest potential of all and holds limited quantities of certain narcotics.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: R-Wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k149 k153 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: A tracing shows no build-up of the R wave across the chest leads. Which technical cause does the assistant check?
opciones: An electrode that was not put where its landmark falls
A paper speed that was set below 25 mm per second
A calibration mark that printed at half its usual height
A lead wire that was left looped across the patient's arm
preguntas.explicacion: The R wave should grow steadily from V1, the smallest, to V5, the largest. When that build-up is missing, the listed causes are an old anteroseptal infarct, hypertrophy of the left ventricle and an electrode that was placed inaccurately, which is the fixable one.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 9.5 Types of Body Movements, Supination and Pronation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to turn the forearm so the palm faces forward. Which movement is being tested, and what happens to the two forearm bones?
opciones: Supination, and the radius and ulna end up parallel to each other
Pronation, and the radius and ulna end up parallel to each other
Supination, and the radius crosses over the ulna in an X shape
Dorsiflexion, and the radius and ulna end up parallel to each other
preguntas.explicacion: Supination is the palm-forward position of the forearm, the one used in anatomical position, and in it the radius and ulna lie parallel. Pronation turns the palm backward and the radius crosses over the ulna into an X. Dorsiflexion belongs to the ankle, not the forearm.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Peripheral Nervous System; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception (CC BY 4.0)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which division of the nervous system controls the heart, the stomach and the intestines without conscious effort?
opciones: The autonomic division of the peripheral nervous system
The somatic division of the peripheral nervous system
The sensory division of the central nervous system
The reflex division of the central nervous system
preguntas.explicacion: The peripheral system splits in two. The somatic part serves the skin and skeletal muscles and handles conscious activity. The autonomic part connects the center to the visceral organs and works continuously without conscious effort, minding heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure and body temperature.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 21.1 Anatomy of the Lymphatic and Immune Systems, Primary Lymphoid Organs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027 I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where do B cells mature and where do T cells mature?
opciones: B cells in the red bone marrow; T cells in the thymus gland
T cells in the red bone marrow; B cells in the thymus gland
B cells in the spleen; T cells in the lymph nodes of the neck
B cells in the lymph nodes; T cells in the red bone marrow
preguntas.explicacion: Both kinds of lymphocyte start in bone marrow. The B cell does nearly all of its development there, whereas the T cell leaves while still immature, as a thymocyte, and matures largely in the thymus, which sits between the sternum and the aorta. Marrow and thymus are the primary lymphoid organs; the spleen and the lymph nodes are secondary ones.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Interface inventory · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which list does the contingency guidance tell an organization to keep and review as part of its downtime planning?
opciones: Its system-to-system connections, marking those that must be told of an outage
Its staff members trained on paper charting, marked by the date of their training
Its patients seen during the last outage, marked by the unit that attended them
Its equipment serviced in the past year, marked by the date of the next service
preguntas.explicacion: Interfaces are the part that fails quietly. The organization keeps a comprehensive list of its system-to-system interfaces and reviews it regularly, every six months or yearly, noting which of them raise legal or regulatory duties to warn the other side, such as a state immunization registry or a prescription drug monitoring program.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Capillaries; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Classification & Structure of Blood Vessels, Capillaries
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3 k71) · PBT I.A.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is the wall of a capillary made of, and what is the capillary's job?
opciones: One endothelial layer on a basement membrane; exchange with tissue fluid
Three tunics with a thin muscular media; regulation of blood pressure
Endothelium with a few muscle cells; collecting blood as it leaves the bed
Rings of smooth muscle called sphincters; control of flow into the bed
preguntas.explicacion: A capillary is an endothelial layer wrapped in a basement membrane, and in the narrowest ones a single cell curls round to touch itself; its job is perfusion, the exchange of gases and other substances between blood and interstitial fluid. The three tunics belong to the arteriole, the sphincters to the metarteriole, and endothelium with a few muscle cells and elastic fibers describes the venule that gathers blood leaving the bed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Directing to a Third Party
preguntas.subtema: Directing PHI to a third party · CCMA 5 k176 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants her records sent straight to a research app she uses. What does the Privacy Rule require of her request?
opciones: It must be in writing, signed by her, and name the recipient and where to send the copy
It must be approved by the privacy official, who decides whether the recipient is suitable
It must come with an authorization from the app developer accepting business associate duties
It must be limited to a summary, since only summaries may be directed outside the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond taking copies herself, an individual may direct the covered entity to send her PHI on to another person or entity of her choosing.
