The request has to be in writing, has to be signed, and has to say plainly who that designated recipient is and the address the information should go to; an electronic copy of a signed request, or one executed electronically through a secure portal, is acceptable. The same fee limits and the same form-and-format rules apply.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature; and StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever" (NBK562334)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's oral temperature is 36.6 °C at 7 am and 37.1 °C at 5 pm on the same day. What accounts for the difference?
opciones: Normal daily variation: the value is lowest early in the morning and peaks late in the afternoon
A change of site: an axillary reading runs about one full degree above an oral one in the same patient
The second half of the menstrual cycle, which lowers the recorded value by about one degree
An early low-grade fever, which is graded from a reading of 37.3 °C upward at any hour
preguntas.explicacion: Body temperature swings by roughly half a degree Celsius over 24 hours: lowest in the early morning, highest late in the day. Both readings sit inside the 36.5 to 37.5 °C band, so neither is a fever. Low-grade fever starts at 37.3 °C, the axilla reads lower than the mouth, and the luteal phase raises the value, it does not lower it.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.6: Current and Past Medical History
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.3.c · CCMA 3A3 · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas.pregunta: During an intake interview, when is a closed or direct question the better tool?
opciones: When one specific detail has to be pinned down, such as whether medicines are taken as prescribed
When the patient is first invited to say, in their own words, exactly what brought them in today
When the patient's cultural background and what matters about it is being explored
When the patient is asked to put into words what the dizziness actually feels like
preguntas.explicacion: Closed questions collect a fact: taken as prescribed or not, allergic or not, pregnant or not. Open-ended ones invite the patient to elaborate and are what the interview opens with, what cultural background and beliefs are explored with, and how a symptom gets described. A closed answer of no or sometimes is then followed up with an open-ended request to tell more.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urea Breath Test", Procedures (14C-UBT and 13C-UBT)
preguntas.subtema: UBT oral contamination · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.3 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the labeled-urea capsule for a 14C urea breath test swallowed whole rather than opened or chewed?
opciones: Because oral flora can carry urease, which would break the urea down in the mouth
Because the capsule shell is what delays gastric emptying long enough for the test
Because the radioactive dose is only safe if the isotope never touches the mucosa
Because chewing releases citric acid, which lowers the pH and slows the stomach
preguntas.explicacion: The test rests on urease, an enzyme absent from human cells, splitting urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide that is then breathed out. Bacteria in the mouth also carry urease, so the capsule goes down whole with lukewarm water to keep the reaction where it belongs. In the 13C version the mixture is drunk through a straw for the same reason, and citric acid is the test meal that slows gastric emptying.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes come back faulty from the same phlebotomist: one is hemolyzed and one holds small clots. What separates the two errors?
opciones: Too much mixing haemolyses the sample; too little leaves small clots
Too little mixing haemolyses the sample; too much leaves small clots
Too much mixing leaves clots; a short draw is what haemolyses a sample
Both faults come from mixing too little, at different points in the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant are inverted in a figure-of-8 until the blood and additive are properly combined. Push it too far and hemolysis appears; stop too soon and small clots form. Both faults make the specimen unusable, and both are decided at the bedside, not in the laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, Considerations and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Bleeding control · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a / 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's venipuncture site keeps bleeding through the gauze after the draw. What is the most important first step?
opciones: Apply direct pressure over the site and keep it until the bleeding stops
Apply a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the site and note the time
Remove the soaked gauze, clean the wound, and apply fresh gauze
Raise the arm above the heart and peek every minute to check
preguntas.explicacion: For bleeding on the outside, nothing matters more than direct pressure, and it stops most of it: press on the wound with a sterile bandage, a clean cloth or, failing those, a hand, and hold the pressure until the bleeding stops, without peeking. Raising the bleeding part can be added where possible, but lifting the dressing every minute disturbs the clot. A soaked dressing stays where it is with another laid on top, and a tourniquet is kept for severe, life-threatening limb bleeding that continuous pressure has not controlled.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why are veins preferred over arteries for a routine blood draw?
opciones: Veins run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and more nerves, so puncturing them hurts more
Veins carry oxygenated blood, which is what most chemistry analysers are calibrated to measure
Arteries collapse under the vacuum of the tube, while veins tolerate the negative pressure
Arterial blood clots too quickly in a citrate tube to allow coagulation testing
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for efficiency and patient comfort because they run superficially, whereas arteries tend to have thicker walls and more associated nerves, making a puncture more painful; arterial sampling is reserved for arterial blood gases. The chapter says nothing about arteries collapsing or clotting faster, and thick walls are a property it credits to the median cubital vein.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What exactly is a platelet?
opciones: A fragment of megakaryocyte cytoplasm wrapped in plasma membrane
A small complete cell with a two-lobed nucleus, 8 to 10 µm wide
An immature erythrocyte that still contains remnants of organelles
A leukocyte that has left the circulation to phagocytize debris
preguntas.explicacion: A platelet is not a cell: it is a piece of the cytoplasm of a large marrow cell, the megakaryocyte, enclosed by a bit of plasma membrane, which is why the older name thrombocyte is misleading. Each megakaryocyte releases 2000 to 3000 platelets. The small two-lobed cell is the basophil, the immature red cell is the reticulocyte, and the emigrated phagocyte is the macrophage.

preguntas.subtema: Media accountability · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A practice writes down which staff member took which laptop out of the building and when it came back. Which specification does that log satisfy?
opciones: Accountability, a record of hardware movements and of the person answering for them
Maintenance records, a record of repairs made to doors, walls and locks in the office
Workstation use, which fixes what may be done at a given class of workstation
Facility security plan, which guards the premises and its equipment against theft
preguntas.explicacion: Accountability sits under device and media controls, and it is the addressable specification calling for a log of where hardware and electronic media go and of who answers for them. Maintenance records look at the building itself, not at equipment that travels.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and tube labeling)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: To save time, a phlebotomist prints and sticks labels on all the tubes at the nursing station before entering the patient's room. What is wrong with this practice?
opciones: Tube identification and labeling must be done in the presence of the patient to avoid misidentification
Labels printed in advance lose their adhesive and can peel off during centrifugation or refrigeration
Tubes must be labeled only after the draw is complete, and the label must be applied later at the accessioning desk
Pre-printed labels are acceptable only when the requisition is placed outside the transport bag
preguntas.explicacion: Both identifying the tube and applying its label are done with the patient present, so that the tube cannot be matched to the wrong person; before the draw the patient's identification data and the tube labels are double-checked against each other. Labeling away from the patient, whether before at the station or later at the accessioning desk, breaks that link. The transport bag pocket is a separate rule about the requisition, not about when to label.

preguntas.subtema: Conditioning an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.b · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses to sign an authorization sending her records to her employer. May the practice make her appointment conditional on signing it?
opciones: No, treatment may not be conditioned on an authorization outside narrow exceptions
No, unless the practice notes the refusal in the record and offers a later date
Yes, a practice may set the terms on which it accepts a patient for treatment
Yes, where the employer is the source of the coverage that pays for the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment in a plan or eligibility for benefits on the individual signing an authorization is forbidden to a covered entity. The exceptions are narrow: research-related treatment, a plan's own enrollment or underwriting determinations, and care provided solely in order to create information for a third party. The form itself has to state which case applies.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Seizures", When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.i · 2027 I.B.8.i · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these makes a seizure in the office an emergency call rather than something to watch?
opciones: It is the first seizure that this patient has ever had
The patient bit the side of the tongue during the event
The patient wears a medical bracelet with seizure instructions
The patient is sleepy and confused for a few minutes afterward
preguntas.explicacion: The emergency number is called for a first seizure, for one lasting more than 2 to 5 minutes, when a second begins soon after the first, when the patient does not wake or behave normally afterward, in water, in a patient who is pregnant, injured or diabetic, or with no medical bracelet. Postictal sleepiness and tongue biting are usual findings.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the PASS rule
preguntas.subtema: PASS · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: What does the first S in PASS stand for when operating a portable fire extinguisher?
opciones: Squeeze the trigger, holding the extinguisher upright
Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the flames
Stand back 75 feet, the maximum travel distance
Shut the door behind you before discharging
preguntas.explicacion: PASS sums up how an extinguisher is worked: pull the pin, aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, then, with the extinguisher held upright, squeeze the trigger, and sweep from side to side so the spray covers the fire. Sweeping is the second S. Seventy-five feet is the maximum travel distance to a Class A extinguisher under 29 CFR 1910.157, not a stand-off distance, and shutting the door is the confine step of RACE, done before anyone tries to put the fire out.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients; and StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2D k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist greets an 80-year-old with 'Hi sweetie, I'm here for your blood.' What should change in that greeting?
opciones: Use a formal form of address such as Mr. or Ms., and give your own name and role
Use the patient's first name to build rapport, then state your job title
Speak louder and more slowly, because most older adults have hearing loss
Address the accompanying family member first, to save the patient effort
preguntas.explicacion: Formal terms of address are the default with older patients, and familiar words like 'dear' can be read as disrespect; staff may also ask how the patient prefers to be addressed. The technique table pairs that with introducing oneself by first and last name. Raising the voice distorts language sounds and can sound like anger, and remarks should not be aimed only at the companion.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Topical, Local, and Regional Anesthesia and Anesthetics", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.D.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Into which two chemical families are local anesthetics divided, and which family does lidocaine belong to?
opciones: Amino amides and amino esters, and lidocaine is an amino amide
Amino amides and amino esters, and lidocaine is an amino ester
Amino amides and amino ketones, and lidocaine is an amino ketone
Amino esters and amino alcohols, and lidocaine is an amino alcohol
preguntas.explicacion: The two families are amino amides and amino esters, and they differ in how the body handles them: amides go through hepatic biotransformation. Lidocaine is an amide, and so are etidocaine, ropivacaine, levobupivacaine, bupivacaine and mepivacaine; procaine, chloroprocaine, tetracaine, benzocaine and cocaine are the esters.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(3)(ii)(A) and (C), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Source individual testing · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the standard say about testing the source patient's blood?
opciones: Test it as soon as feasible for HBV and HIV once consent is obtained, unless consent is not legally required
Test it only if the exposed employee first agrees to have his or her own baseline blood drawn
Test it without asking, because a patient's blood already drawn belongs to the laboratory
Do not test it; the standard bases follow-up on the employee's serology and vaccination status alone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(ii) makes identification and documentation of the source individual part of the follow-up unless it is infeasible or barred by state or local law. Under (f)(3)(ii)(A) the source's blood is tested for HBV and HIV infectivity as soon as feasible after consent; if consent is refused, the employer documents that legally required consent could not be obtained, and where the law does not require consent, available blood is tested and the results recorded. Results go to the exposed employee together with the rules on disclosing the source's identity and status.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Warm-site backup · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A large organization that treats patients around the clock keeps a warm-site backup that can run the whole record system. What does the guidance expect of it?
opciones: Current patient data, running within eight hours, and a test at least every quarter
Current patient data, running within eight hours, and a test at least every year
Current patient data, running within one hour, and a test at least every quarter
A weekly copy of patient data, running within eight hours, and a yearly test
preguntas.explicacion: The example given is a remote backup facility, more than fifty miles away and more than twenty miles from the coast, holding current patient data and able to be brought up in less than eight hours, with the backup computer system tested at least quarterly. A single point of failure is what the practice exists to remove.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A light blue sodium citrate tube has just been filled for a PT/INR. How should it be mixed?
opciones: Inverted gently 3 to 6 times immediately after the draw
Inverted gently 8 to 10 times immediately after the draw
Shaken vigorously for a few seconds so the anticoagulant mixes
Left upright for 10 to 15 minutes before any mixing
preguntas.explicacion: Gentle mixing means inverting the citrate tube 3 to 6 times right after the sample enters the tube; vigorous shaking can froth or hemolyse the sample and distort coagulation results. Eight to ten inversions is the figure for blood culture bottles, and the 10 to 15 minute rest is the clotting time for plain red tubes before centrifugation.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, benign
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report calls a growth benign. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: It may keep growing, but it does not spread to other parts of the body
It has stopped growing, and it does not spread to other parts of the body
It is growing slowly, and it spreads only through the lymph system
It is not growing at all, and it will disappear without any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Benign means not cancer. A benign tumor can still get larger, and its size may cause trouble by itself, but it does not invade nearby tissue or travel elsewhere. The opposite term is malignant: those cells grow in an uncontrolled way, invade nearby tissue and spread through the blood and lymph system.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - infant", First Aid; and StatPearls, "Breast Examination Techniques" (NBK459179)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: An infant is found unresponsive and not breathing. How are chest compressions delivered?
opciones: With the two thumbs side by side over the sternum, below the nipple line
With the heel of one hand over the lower half of the sternum, as in a child
With two fingers over the upper third of the sternum, above the nipples
With both hands wrapped around the chest, squeezing from front and back
preguntas.explicacion: The rescuer's hands encircle the infant's chest and both thumbs press together on the sternum below the nipple line, to a depth of about 1½ inches (4 cm) at 100 to 120 per minute. Two fingers on the sternum just under the nipple line is the other accepted hand position. The heel of one hand is what a child of 1 year to puberty gets.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Nursing Rights of Medication Administration", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5
preguntas.pregunta: An order says a dose is due at a set hour. How far from that hour should the dose be given?
opciones: Within about half an hour, since a wider gap can alter the drug's bioavailability
Within about six hours, the widest interval an around-the-clock order would use
Within about four hours, the window written into a typical order given as needed
At any point in the shift, as long as the true time is charted in the record
preguntas.explicacion: The right time means administering the medication as close as possible to the hour the prescriber intended, and the guiding principle is not to stray from it by more than about half an hour, because a longer gap can shift bioavailability and other mechanisms. Drugs given by infusion must also run at the ordered rate. Four to six hours is the window inside an as-needed order, not a tolerance for timing.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Mean Arterial Pressure
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: If the mean arterial pressure stays below 60 mm Hg for an extended time, what is the result?
opciones: Ischemia, too little blood flow, usually with hypoxia
Hypervolemia, too much fluid retained by the kidneys
Hypertension, from an excess of endothelin release
Polycythemia, from a rise in the output of EPO
preguntas.explicacion: When MAP falls below 60 mm Hg for long, pressure is no longer enough to push blood through the tissues; the result is ischemia, insufficient blood flow, commonly accompanied by hypoxia, inadequate tissue oxygenation, to which neurons are especially sensitive. Hypervolemia and hypertension are excesses of volume and pressure, and polycythemia is an overproduction of red cells, a different condition.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", sections Structure and Function and Common Pathway
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins of the arm drain the skin and the fascia beneath it, while the deep veins drain the muscles and the bones. Which vessels carry blood from one system into the other?
opciones: The perforating veins, which drain into the deep veins
The venae comitantes, which drain into the dorsal arch
The median cubital vein, which drains into the palmar arch
The cephalic and basilic, which drain into the radial veins
preguntas.explicacion: The two systems are joined by perforating veins, and those run into the deep veins all along the limb. The venae comitantes are the paired veins that accompany the ulnar and radial arteries; the median cubital joins the cephalic to the basilic at the elbow; and those two channels themselves end up higher in the arm, in the axillary or the subclavian.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Post-visit summary · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient worries she will forget what was said during a video visit. Which step does the patient guidance suggest to her?
opciones: Asking the clinician afterwards to send her a summary or notes of the appointment
Recording the appointment on her own telephone so she can play it back later
Asking the clinician for a direct mobile number she can use with any question later
Asking for the same appointment to be repeated in the office later that week
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling confident in a telehealth visit includes learning how it works, taking her time, choosing a clinician who listens, asking for anything unclear to be explained, and getting a summary: she is told to ask the clinician to send a summary or notes after the visit, which can include answers to the questions she raised. Writing a list beforehand is suggested for the same reason.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule, What Information is Protected
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.1.b HIPAA Security · CMA II.E.1.e security of electronic transmission
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic keeps its old paper charts in a locked room and its current records in an electronic system. Which of the two does the HIPAA Security Rule govern?
opciones: Only the electronic records, since the Security Rule reaches electronic information alone
Both, since the Security Rule reaches every form in which the information is being held
Only the paper charts, since physical safeguards are what the Security Rule is about
Neither, since the Security Rule binds business associates rather than covered entities
preguntas.explicacion: The Security Rule protects one slice of protected health information: the part created, received, maintained or transmitted electronically. Where the Privacy Rule and the Breach Notification Rule reach paper and the spoken word, this one does not. It binds covered entities and business associates alike, and its physical safeguards protect the systems and the media holding electronic information.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Fire triangle · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which three components must be present for a fire to ignite?
opciones: A fuel, an oxidizer like oxygen, and an ignition source
A fuel, a flammable liquid, and a compressed gas
Heat, smoke, and an electrical current from a wall outlet
Oxygen, nitrous oxide, and an electrocautery device
preguntas.explicacion: Three components are needed: a fuel source such as linens, flammable liquids or tissue; an oxidizer such as oxygen or nitrous oxide, which greatly increases combustibility; and an ignition source such as an open flame, electrostatic discharge, electrocautery, lasers or any energized device. The operating room is a high-risk setting because all three are usually present at once. Oxygen and nitrous oxide are both oxidizers and electrocautery is an ignition source, so that combination lacks a fuel; smoke is a product of fire, not a component.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note mentions a condition treated years ago that no longer exists but still shapes today's treatment. How is it handled?
opciones: It is not coded as current, and a history code may be added as secondary
It is coded as current, because the note for this visit still mentions it
It is coded first, since it explains the treatment chosen for her today
It is left out entirely, since a condition that has resolved is never coded
preguntas.explicacion: Coders report the conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect care. Conditions previously treated that no longer exist are not coded as current. Personal and family history categories may still be used as secondary codes where that history bears on the care given today or steers the treatment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dietary Approaches to Obesity Treatment", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with obesity is discouraged because she has lost only 6 percent of her weight. How should that be framed?
opciones: Reaching 5 percent already counts as a successful response to treatment
Reaching 5 percent is a starting point but no benefit appears before 15
Reaching a healthy BMI is the only result that counts as a success
Reaching 25 percent is the target set for every patient with obesity
preguntas.explicacion: At least 5 percent weight loss is the recommended initial goal in obesity management, and hitting it counts as a success when the response to treatment is judged. Losing 5 to 10 percent already lowers the risk of diabetes and coronary artery disease. Realistic goals are advised precisely because slow progress makes people quit.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime paper forms · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: How much paper capacity does the SAFER contingency practice expect each patient care area to hold for a downtime?
opciones: Enough forms to care for its patients for at least eight hours
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least three days
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least thirty days
Enough forms to care for one shift of scheduled visits only
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended practice is to keep paper forms on hand that can stand in for the EHR's key functions while it is down, since clinical and administrative operations have to carry on. The implementation guidance fixes the stock: enough in each patient care area to cover its patients for eight hours at least, forms for entering orders and for documenting medications, laboratory and radiology tests included.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method, Action
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which question is a proper teach-back after explaining a 12-hour fast?
opciones: 'So I know I explained it well, what will you do the night before the test?'
'Does that make sense to you, or should I go over it once more?'
'Do you have any questions about the fasting instructions I gave?'
'You'll remember all of this tomorrow morning, won't you?'
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back is framed as a non-shaming check on how well the clinician explained, with examples such as asking what the patient will tell a partner about the visit. The question must require the patient to restate the plan in their own words. 'Does that make sense' and any yes-or-no form are excluded, and inviting questions is a separate step in Tool 4.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k51 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient using a home oximeter reads 87%. What is the instruction?
opciones: Seek immediate medical attention: 88% or lower calls for emergency care
Call the provider during office hours, as 92% or lower is the reporting level
Repeat the reading in the morning, since a single value is not acted upon
Change the sensor to the other hand and act only if the value stays under 80%
preguntas.explicacion: Two thresholds are given for home monitoring: at 92% or lower the provider is contacted, and at 88% or lower the patient seeks immediate attention. A reading of 87% is in the second group. Bluish lips or nails, trouble breathing, chest tightness and a fast heart rate are the signs that go with a low value.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old is crying and squirming while you try to count the pulse. Which approach suits the arteries of a child that age?
opciones: Use the pads of two fingers with gentle pressure, and settle the child first
Press until the beat disappears and then ease off slowly to pick it up again
Press hard with a single fingertip, since small arteries sit deep in the tissue
Count during the crying, since crying steadies the rate and makes it easier
preguntas.explicacion: A young child's arteries are smaller and closer to the surface than an adult's, so they compress easily and are harder to find. The pads of the index and middle fingers keep the examiner's own pulse out of the count and apply pressure gentle enough not to close the vessel. Crying and movement change the rate, so a calm child comes before the count.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (gloves and tourniquet)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is it suggested to put on gloves BEFORE applying the tourniquet?
opciones: To avoid prolonging the time the tourniquet stays on
To keep the tourniquet free of MRSA from the phlebotomist's hands
To ensure the site is not touched after disinfection
To make the veins dilate before the tourniquet is placed
preguntas.explicacion: Wearing gloves before the tourniquet goes on may be advised so that the band is not left on too long; gloving afterwards adds seconds while the band is already constricting the arm. MRSA on tourniquets is a separate concern the WHO raises, and not touching the cleaned site is the WHO's Step 5 rule; neither is the reason given for the sequence.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Appointment types · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5B k173 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Implementing open access includes simplifying the appointment types. Which three does the improvement guide recommend a practice keep?
opciones: Personal with her own physician, team with another clinician, and unestablished
Routine, urgent and follow-up, each one holding its own block of the morning
New patient, established patient and annual wellness, each of a different length
Short, long and double, where the long one is worth about two of the short ones
preguntas.explicacion: One recommended tactic is to strip out complexity by holding the practice to three types: personal, where the patient sees her own physician; team, where she is seen by another clinician on the team; and unestablished, for patients who do not yet have a physician. Appointment length is handled apart from that, as short or long, a long visit counting for roughly two short ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.c · 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A small fire starts in a clinic storeroom. Which order do the letters of RACE set out?
opciones: Rescue those at risk, pull the alarm, confine the fire, then extinguish
Pull the alarm, rescue those at risk, extinguish the fire, then confine
Rescue those at risk, confine the fire, extinguish it, then pull the alarm
Confine the fire, pull the alarm, rescue those at risk, then extinguish
preguntas.explicacion: Rescue comes first, above all where patients cannot move on their own; then the alarm is pulled to warn the rest of the building, the fire is confined to one place, and last it is put out. The extinguisher itself is worked by pulling the pin, aiming at the base of the flames, squeezing the handle and sweeping side to side.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a large bruise with swelling over the median cubital vein from a draw two days ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Choose another site; a hematoma contraindicates venipuncture there
Draw through the bruise, since the vein beneath it has already been located
Draw just above the bruise after applying ice for 15 minutes
Draw below the bruise with a 23 G butterfly to reduce trauma
preguntas.explicacion: The presence of a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin, is among the local reasons not to puncture a site, together with residual scar tissue and venous fibrosis felt on palpation. Ice for up to 15 minutes each hour is first aid for a bruise, not a preparation for drawing through it, and the chapter gives no 'above or below' exception.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A physician has opted out of Medicare and asks the patient to sign a private contract. What follows for her?
opciones: Medicare pays nothing for his services except in emergencies, and he stays out two years
Medicare pays its share as usual once she files her own claim for those services
Medicare pays the approved amount less the fifteen percent limiting charge for him
Medicare pays none of it for one year, after which the physician returns automatically
preguntas.explicacion: Providers who do not want to work with the program may opt out, and Medicare will not pay for what they furnish except in an emergency. Opting out lasts a minimum of two years, and at each two-year point the provider may stay out, become non-participating, or accept assignment. The patient may have to pay up front or agree a payment plan under the private contract.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Care Coordination in primary care
preguntas.subtema: Procedures to coordinate care · CCMA 4E k163 · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient sees three specialists and none of them seems to know what the others did. Which activity is care coordination?
opciones: Organizing care activities on purpose and sharing information among participants
Reviewing each claim before it is sent so that the payer will not deny it
Assigning the patient to a plan network that limits which providers she sees
Recording the visit in the record so that the note gets signed the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Care coordination means organizing a patient's care activities deliberately and sharing information among everyone concerned with that care, so that care becomes safer and more effective. What the patient needs and prefers is known in advance and passed to the right people at the right moment, across units or sites of care. It is a key element of quality primary care.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time · CPT D3 3E k60 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A PT and PTT are being collected. What is the guidance on tourniquet time for these tests?
opciones: Keep it as short as possible, to avoid artifacts such as hemolysis
Leave it on until the citrate tube is full, so the 9:1 ratio is reached
Apply it for at least one minute, so the vein is engorged before the puncture
Release it before the needle enters, since stasis activates clotting factors
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation sampling calls for an atraumatic venipuncture performed as soon as possible, with tourniquet time minimized during collection, to avoid artifacts in coagulation results such as hemolysis. The 9:1 ratio depends on the fill volume, not on the tourniquet; no minimum time is prescribed; and releasing it before the needle enters is not what any of the sources describe.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.3 Functions of the Integumentary System, Vitamin D Synthesis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(1) (2027 I.C.6.f(1)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Besides acting as a barrier, which vitamin does the skin synthesize when it is exposed to ultraviolet light?
opciones: Vitamin D, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin C, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin K, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin A, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
preguntas.explicacion: The epidermis makes vitamin D under ultraviolet light, and the liver and kidneys then convert it to its active form. Without it calcium and phosphorus are poorly absorbed, and bones suffer: rickets in children and osteomalacia, a softening of bone, in older adults. The lack of vitamin C causes scurvy instead.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Diversion Control Division, Definition of Controlled Substance Schedules: Schedule IV
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k15 · CMA 2027 I.D.1 · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which group of substances is given as examples of Schedule IV?
opciones: Alprazolam, diazepam, lorazepam and temazepam
Ketamine, benzphetamine and the anabolic steroids
Methylphenidate, amphetamine and methamphetamine
Hydromorphone, methadone, meperidine and fentanyl
preguntas.explicacion: Schedule IV holds substances whose abuse potential is low compared with Schedule III; among the listed examples are alprazolam, clonazepam and clorazepate, then diazepam, lorazepam and midazolam, and also temazepam, triazolam and carisoprodol. Ketamine, benzphetamine, phendimetrazine and the anabolic steroids belong to Schedule IIIN, the stimulants named are Schedule IIN, and the narcotics named are Schedule II.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Red
preguntas.subtema: Specimen preparation, serum · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A plain red top tube has just been filled. How long is the blood usually allowed to clot before it is centrifuged?
opciones: About 10 to 15 minutes, though some specimens take up to 60 minutes
About 3 to 6 minutes, the same interval used to invert the citrate tube
About 30 seconds, the time the alcohol needs to dry on the skin
At least two to three hours, so the clot separates from the serum
preguntas.explicacion: A red tube contains no additive; contact with the tube surface activates the coagulation cascade, and the blood is left to clot for 10 to 15 minutes before centrifugation; clotting time varies and can reach almost an hour. Three to six is the number of citrate inversions, 30 seconds is the alcohol drying time, and hours are not mentioned.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Adverse Drug Reactions", Function: Drug Interactions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what counts as a drug interaction. What is the answer?
opciones: A reaction between a drug and another drug, a food, a supplement or a disease
A reaction between a drug and another drug taken at the very same hour only
A reaction between a drug and a food, which no prescription drug can produce
A reaction between two drugs that share the same active ingredient exactly
preguntas.explicacion: An interaction is a reaction set off when a drug meets another drug, a food or beverage, a supplement or a disease, and it counts among the Type A adverse reactions. The examples given include theophylline exposure rising once a macrolide antibiotic is added, warfarin losing anticoagulant effect as vitamin K intake goes up, and respiratory depression when a benzodiazepine and an opioid are taken together.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Planes of the Body
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: An imaging study is cut along a plane that separates the body into right and left portions. Which plane is it?
opciones: The sagittal plane, cut vertically from the front through to the back
The coronal plane, cut vertically from one side across to the other
The transverse plane, cut horizontally straight through the body
The oblique plane, cut at an angle across the other three
preguntas.explicacion: There are three planes in common use. Sagittal is vertical and splits right from left; coronal, also called frontal, is vertical and splits front from back; transverse, also called axial, is horizontal and splits upper from lower. The oblique plane crosses the body at an angle to all three.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Risk of Infection After a Needlestick Injury: HBV and Summary
preguntas.subtema: HBV prophylaxis works · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker exposed to hepatitis B, how well does immune globulin plus starting the vaccine work?
opciones: More than 90% effective at preventing infection
About 50% effective at preventing the infection
About 60% effective, like a booster dose alone
Around 30% effective, as the vaccine alone is
preguntas.explicacion: Hepatitis B is the most transmissible of the three: for a susceptible worker the reported range is 6 to 30 percent after a single needlestick from an infected patient. It is also the one with the best answer: hepatitis B immune globulin together with the start of the vaccine series is more than 90 percent effective at preventing infection. Workers with antibodies from vaccination or past infection are not at risk in the first place. Neither HCV nor HIV has anything comparable.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pap and HPV Testing", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.5.a · CCMA 3A3 k45 · RMA III.F.4.b.ii
preguntas.pregunta: How often does a 25-year-old with no risk factors need cervical cancer screening?
opciones: Cytology alone every three years, which is the schedule from 21 to 29
Cytology alone every year, which is the schedule from 21 to 29 years
Cytology with HPV co-testing every five years, starting at age 21
High-risk HPV testing alone every five years, starting at age 21
preguntas.explicacion: From 21 to 29 the recommendation is cervical cytology alone every three years. From 30 to 65 there are three acceptable options: cytology every three years, high-risk HPV testing alone every five years, or the two together every five years. Below 21 there is no screening at all. Under 30 the usual practice is cytology with reflex HPV testing.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?; and Medicare costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signed up for Part B three years after she was first eligible. How long will the late enrollment penalty last?
opciones: For as long as she holds Part B, and the longer the wait the larger it grows
For three years, one year of penalty for each year that she delayed signing up
Until the eight-month special enrollment period that follows her retirement
Until she buys a Medigap policy, which takes the penalty amount over from her
preguntas.explicacion: Someone who does not sign up for Part B when first eligible has to wait to enroll and goes months without coverage, and may pay a monthly penalty for as long as she has Part B, with the penalty rising the longer the delay ran. A similar penalty exists for Part A when it has to be bought and is not taken at the first opportunity.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Limited English Proficiency (LEP), Your Right to Language Assistance Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic tells a patient that a telephone interpreter costs $30 unless she brings a relative. Per HHS OCR?
opciones: Not allowed: language access services must be provided free of charge
Allowed, if the fee is listed in the posted notice of nondiscrimination
Allowed, because interpreters are required only in emergency departments
Allowed, if the relative is an adult who agrees to interpret for her
preguntas.explicacion: A program funded by HHS, or covered by the civil rights laws it enforces, has to provide language access services free of charge, and a visit to a doctor is among the examples listed. What Section 1557 requires is a notice saying that language assistance can be had, not a fee schedule, and AHRQ Tool 9 adds that a relative is no acceptable substitute for a qualified interpreter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: haematoma and bruise · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Bruises are described in three types. Which is the most severe and painful?
opciones: The periosteal bruise, which involves the bone
The subcutaneous bruise, which is under the skin
The intramuscular bruise, in the belly of a muscle
The dermal bruise, which sits in the skin itself
preguntas.explicacion: Bruises are grouped as subcutaneous, under the skin; intramuscular, in the belly of the muscle underneath; and periosteal, a bone bruise. The bone bruise is the most severe and the most painful of the three, and bruises in general can last from days to months.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has just finished a draw. At which two moments is the label checked against the request form?
opciones: Right after the draw, and again before the tubes are dispatched
Right after the draw, and again when the results are reported back
Before the needle goes in, and again when the patient has left the room
Only once, when the tubes are put into the transport bag with the form
preguntas.explicacion: The closing steps ask the worker to check the label and the form for accuracy once the sharp has been discarded, and then to look over the labels on the tubes and the forms once more before dispatch. Labeling itself is done with the patient present, so that a tube is never matched to the wrong name.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Electrical Safety, 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(5)(i) and 1910.304(g)(6)
preguntas.subtema: Electrical work practices · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.d III.C.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice does 29 CFR 1910.334 prohibit when using portable electric equipment?
opciones: Plugging or unplugging equipment with wet hands
Using extension cords longer than 6 feet
Operating equipment near a sink even when it is grounded
Using cord-and-plug equipment without a GFCI in dry areas
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph 1910.334(a)(5)(i) puts it on the employer: nobody handles the plug of portable electric equipment with wet hands, in or out. The eTool lists wet hands, and pulling equipment along by its cord, among the unsafe practices that end in a shock. Equipment used near water has to be properly grounded under 1910.304(g)(6), which allows its use rather than banning it, and GFCIs are a recognized control for the receptacles the rule specifies, not a prohibition on equipment elsewhere. Neither provision sets a limit on cord length.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth privacy · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: An upcoming telehealth visit will cover a sensitive topic. What extra step does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Helping the patient find a private spot and agreeing what a companion may hear
Moving the appointment to the office, since sensitive topics rule telehealth out
Recording the visit so that the discussion can be reviewed by a second clinician
Asking the patient to bring a relative, who can confirm what was discussed later
preguntas.explicacion: For appointments touching sensitive subjects the guidance suggests discussing whether the patient can find a private place, and offering tips for one at home, in a car or at a friend's house. It also covers other communication options such as e-mail, text or the platform's chat feature where personal safety may be an issue, and says to establish with an interpreter or caregiver present what the patient is comfortable letting them hear, and whether a release is needed.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Fecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT), Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: NSAIDs and FOBT · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Why are aspirin and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen listed among the medicines that can interfere with a fecal occult blood test?
opciones: They can irritate the stomach and cause bleeding, giving a positive result not due to a tumor
They reduce the oxidation of the guaiac reagent, giving a false-negative result
They contain plant peroxidases that react with the developer, like horseradish
They color the stool black, which hides the blue reaction on the card
preguntas.explicacion: Aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, corticosteroids and some other drugs irritate the gastric lining and cause real blood loss, so the card turns positive for a reason unrelated to a colorectal lesion. A patient who takes aspirin for the heart should not stop it without talking to the provider; acetaminophen may be permitted instead. Blocking the oxidation is the vitamin C effect, and plant peroxidases come from raw vegetables.

preguntas.subtema: Media re-use · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: The office wants to hand a set of flash drives that once held claim files to another department. Which Security Rule specification governs that?
opciones: Media re-use, which has the information taken off the drive before it is handed on
Disposal, which governs the final disposition of the hardware once it leaves service
Accountability, which keeps a record of who moved the hardware and where it went
Data backup and storage, which copies the information before equipment is moved
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls carry four specifications. Disposal deals with hardware at the end of its life; the one that fits a drive still in service and about to be passed to someone else is media re-use, and like disposal it is required, not addressable. Both aim at the same risk: information left behind on hardware that changes hands.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Exercise stress test
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: What happens once the exercise part of the test is over?
opciones: Monitoring goes on 10 to 15 minutes or until the rate settles
Monitoring stops as soon as the treadmill has been switched off
Monitoring goes on for a full 60 minutes in every single case
Monitoring goes on only until the blood pressure is taken
preguntas.explicacion: Watching continues for 10 to 15 minutes after exercise, or until the rate is back to where it started, because arrhythmias and tracing changes can appear during recovery. The whole appointment runs about an hour.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1L 1M k37 k38 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which check comes first when someone has just fainted in the drawing room?
opciones: The airway and the breathing
The pulse in the punctured arm
The puncture site for bleeding
The label on the tube just filled
preguntas.explicacion: The first of the immediate steps is to check the person's airway and breathing, calling emergency help and starting rescue breathing and resuscitation if they are needed. Loosening tight clothing, raising the feet and keeping the person down come after that.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities, Part 2
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance · CMA II.F.1.c(4) ADAAA
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair arrives with a friend who pushed the chair into the drawing room. How should the phlebotomist handle the conversation?
opciones: Speak to the patient directly, and ask her whether the friend should stay in the room
Speak to the friend, who can relay the answers if the patient tires during the draw
Ask the friend to step out at once, because privacy rules bar all visitors from the room
Ask the patient to sign a release before the friend may hear any of the questions
preguntas.explicacion: The rule for a patient with a disability is the rule for every patient: address her, not the companion, because a disability says nothing about her ability to speak for herself or follow the answers. Whether the companion stays is her decision, and it should be asked before the discussion starts rather than assumed either way.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k87 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.d
preguntas.pregunta: A small laboratory without an ultracentrifuge keeps receiving milky sera and cannot send them out. Which alternative does the published evidence support?
opciones: High-speed spinning in a micro-centrifuge, validated for the analytes involved
Diluting the serum with saline before running the affected chemistry analytes
Redrawing after a twelve-hour fast, since lipemia always comes from the meal
Reporting the lipemic figures with a comment, since the bias stays within limits
preguntas.explicacion: Ultracentrifugation clears lipemic interference, but the instrument sits only in highly specialized laboratories. A comparison of high-speed centrifugation in a micro-centrifuge against an ultracentrifuge found the cheaper route suitable, on the analyser tested, for creatinine, sodium, lactate dehydrogenase, urate, total protein, magnesium, cholesterol and triglyceride.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Sinoatrial (SA) Node; Atrioventricular (AV) Node; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structure is the heart's pacemaker, where is it, and how often does it fire on its own?
opciones: The SA node, in the upper posterior wall of the right atrium; 70 to 80 per minute
The AV node, in the lower right atrium within the septum; 70 to 80 per minute
The SA node, in the upper wall of the left atrium; about 100 per minute
The bundle of His, in the interventricular septum; up to 220 per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The sinoatrial node lies high and toward the back in the wall of the right atrium, close to where the superior vena cava opens, and it is the pacemaker because nothing else depolarizes as fast; left to itself it fires 70 to 80 times a minute. The atrioventricular node sits lower in the right atrium and passes at most about 220 impulses a minute, which fixes the usual ceiling for heart rate.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: On a Medicare secondary claim, why does the biller have to pick the right claim adjustment reason code?
opciones: Because Medicare may deny the claim when the code for the adjustment is wrong
Because Medicare pays interest on the claim only when the code is entered right
Because the primary payer may reopen the claim when the code for it is wrong
Because Medicare asks for it only on paper claims, where remittances are attached
preguntas.explicacion: A secondary claim has to explain why the other payer denied it, decided the benefits were exhausted, paid less than the full amount, or did not pay at all. That information sits in the claim adjustment segment of the 835 remittance advice or the 837 professional claim, and the correct claim adjustment reason code has to be identified there; if it is not, Medicare may deny the claim outright.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Decontamination, Sterilize
preguntas.subtema: Decontamination vs sterilization · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b / 2027 I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Under the standard, the term decontamination means which of the following?
opciones: Using physical or chemical means to make a surface safe to handle, use or dispose of
Killing every form of microbial life, endospores of bacteria included
Treating all blood and certain body fluids as if known to be infectious
Altering the way a task is performed so that exposure becomes less likely
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines decontamination as treating a surface or an item, physically or chemically, so that the bloodborne pathogens on it are removed, inactivated or destroyed to the point of no longer transmitting infection, leaving the item safe to handle, use or throw away. Killing every form of microbial life, endospores included, is the neighbouring definition of sterilize; handling all blood as infectious is Universal Precautions; and altering the way a task is done is a work practice control.

preguntas.subtema: Signature by a representative · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's son signs the release form as her personal representative. What must the form carry in addition to his signature and the date?
opciones: A description of the authority under which he acts for her
A copy of the identification he presented at the front desk
A statement that she was unable to sign the form for herself
A second signature from a member of the practice's workforce
preguntas.explicacion: The core element covering the signature says that where a personal representative signs, the form must also describe that person's authority to act for the individual. The other core elements do not change: the information, who discloses it, who receives it, the purpose and an expiration date or event all remain.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A blood bank cross-match is ordered. Which two tubes in the WHO table list cross-match among their uses?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the purple EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green PST
The light blue citrate tube and the light gray fluoride tube
The pale yellow ACD tube and the blood culture bottle
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3, blood bank (cross-match) appears in the uses column of two rows: the red top with clot activator, alongside chemistries, immunology and serology, and the purple EDTA tube, alongside hematology. The serum separator and PST tubes are listed for chemistries, the citrate and fluoride tubes for coagulation and glucose, and the ACD tube for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ventricular Fibrillation", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: How are coarse and fine ventricular fibrillation told apart?
opciones: By height: mostly 3 mm or more is coarse, mostly under 3 mm is fine
By height: mostly 5 mm or more is coarse, mostly under 5 mm is fine
By rate: faster than 300 a minute is coarse, slower than that is fine
By width: wider than 120 ms is coarse, narrower than that is fine
preguntas.explicacion: The split is made on the amplitude of the waveforms: at or above 3 mm for most of them is coarse, predominantly below 3 mm is fine. Coarse is generally held to answer defibrillation better, though the resuscitation guidelines do not change what is done.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Introduction; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What is claimed for double gloving in relation to a sharps injury?
opciones: It lowers the volume of blood transferred, but the puncture risk remains
It lowers the puncture risk, but the volume of blood transferred remains
It removes both the puncture risk and the volume of blood transferred
It changes neither, and is recommended only for surgical procedures
preguntas.explicacion: Wearing two pairs of gloves may reduce the amount of blood passed on during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin. Gloves are credited with the same limited benefit in a needle-stick: less blood transmitted, not an injury prevented.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Skin preparation
preguntas.subtema: Cotton and alcohol · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague keeps a jar of cotton balls soaking in alcohol and tears the cotton by hand as she goes. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Cotton pre-torn by bare hands is already contaminated, and bacteria grow in it
Alcohol evaporates from an open jar and is too weak to prepare the skin
Cotton fibers stick to the puncture site and cause the wound to keep oozing
Alcohol stored in an open jar has to be discarded at the end of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: Skin preparation calls for 70 percent alcohol applied with a single-use swab or a clean cotton-wool ball. Cotton torn ahead of time with bare fingers is already contaminated, and bacteria multiply in it as the hours pass, so jars of cotton left soaking in alcohol are not to be kept; the cotton is moistened right at the moment of use, and the main container must not be contaminated while doing it. For a blood donation the recommended preparation is a single step of 2 percent chlorhexidine in 70 percent isopropyl alcohol, left to air dry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Orthostatic Hypotension", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A drop in pressure appears only 6 minutes after the patient has stood up. How is it classified?
opciones: Delayed orthostatic hypotension, which by definition appears after 3 minutes
Classic orthostatic hypotension, which appears within 3 minutes of standing
Initial orthostatic hypotension, which lasts under 15 seconds after standing
Postprandial hypotension, which appears within 2 hours of a large meal
preguntas.explicacion: The types are separated by timing: initial lasts less than 15 seconds after the change of posture, classic appears within three minutes, and delayed appears after three minutes. Postprandial hypotension is a different entity, a systolic fall of at least 20 mm Hg within two hours of eating.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Whose Medicaid income is worked out by the SSI methodologies rather than by the MAGI rules?
opciones: An applicant who is sixty-five or older, or who is blind or has a disability
An applicant who is pregnant and is applying for coverage for the first time
An applicant who is the parent of a child already enrolled in the program
An applicant who is an adult in a state that widened coverage to low earners
preguntas.explicacion: The Affordable Care Act put Modified Adjusted Gross Income at the center of financial eligibility for Medicaid, for CHIP and for Marketplace help, and it governs most adults, most parents, most pregnant women and most children. Certain people are exempt: eligibility resting on being sixty-five or over, on blindness or on disability is generally decided with the income methods of the SSI program.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xi), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Minimizing splashes · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does the standard say every procedure involving blood must be carried out?
opciones: In a way that keeps splashes, sprays, spatter and droplets to a minimum
Inside a certified biological safety cabinet, never on the open bench
With a mask and face shield worn for every procedure regardless of splash risk
Behind a protective covering that is replaced at the end of every shift
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xi) requires every procedure with blood or OPIM to be carried out so that splashing, spraying, spatter and the making of droplets are kept to a minimum. Biological safety cabinets become mandatory under (e)(2)(ii)(E) only where HIV or HBV research, or production work with those viruses, is going on. A mask with eye protection is required by (d)(3)(x) when splashes may be generated and facial contamination is anticipated, not for every task, and the protective coverings of (d)(4)(ii)(B) are an option for surfaces, not a way of performing a procedure.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A blood type is reported as A positive. What does the 'positive' refer to, and what share of Americans share that status?
opciones: The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 85 percent
The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 50 percent
Anti-D antibodies are in the plasma; about 85 percent
The A antigen is on the red cells; about 15 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The Rh group is separate from ABO, and only one Rh antigen, D, matters clinically; those who carry it, about 85 percent of Americans, are Rh positive, and the word positive or negative is added to the ABO letter. Anti-D antibodies are not preformed; they appear only in Rh negative people after sensitization. The lab reports the result simply as Rh+ or Rh−.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Cuts and puncture wounds", When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k79 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: Which sign in a healing wound points to infection?
opciones: A red streak spreading from the wound, with pus-like drainage and fever
A thin scab that itches and edges that have pulled slightly together
Bruising around the wound that is turning from purple to yellow
Clear fluid on the dressing during the first day, with no odor at all
preguntas.explicacion: Warmth and redness in the area, throbbing pain, swelling, fever, a red streak running away from the wound, or drainage that looks like pus are the signs that send the patient back to the provider. They are what the assistant looks for at a dressing change, along with a wound that is large or deep even when it is no longer bleeding much.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stocking the tray for the morning. How should the laboratory sample tubes be kept before use?
opciones: Dry and standing upright in a rack
Damp and lying flat inside the tray
Chilled and upright in a small cooler
Dry and lying flat under the request forms
preguntas.explicacion: The list of equipment assembled before a draw asks for a supply of sample tubes stored dry and upright in a rack. The rack itself stays near the worker and out of the patient's reach, so that it is not knocked over during the procedure.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care · CPT D3 3Q k70 k74 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E9 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: The needle has just been withdrawn. What does the WHO ask the patient to do, and what must the patient avoid?
opciones: Hold the gauze in place with the arm extended and raised, and not bend the arm
Bend the arm firmly over the gauze and keep it tightly bent for at least five minutes
Lower the arm below the heart so the puncture seals under gravity
Rub the site through the gauze for 30 seconds to disperse any pooled blood
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to withdraw the needle gently, apply gentle pressure with clean gauze or cotton wool, and ask the patient to hold it in place with the arm extended and raised; the patient is told not to bend the arm, since bending it brings on a hematoma. Lowering the arm and rubbing the site are not described anywhere in the guideline.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, surgical antisepsis; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: Surgical hand antisepsis · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.b.i · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A surgical hand scrub with an antimicrobial agent usually lasts how long?
opciones: About 2 to 6 minutes
About 15 to 20 seconds
About 10 to 15 minutes
About 30 to 60 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Surgical antisepsis is a scrub that usually lasts 2 to 6 minutes; the clinical literature adds that scrubs of 10 minutes or more give no extra benefit and irritate the skin. The scrub is done with hands above the elbows, jewelry removed, nails cleaned under running water and a sterile brush or sponge, followed by drying with a sterile towel before sterile gloves. Fifteen to twenty seconds is routine handwashing, not surgical antisepsis.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 1: Immunity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(1)
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between active and passive immunity?
opciones: Active is made by the person's own immune system and usually lasts for years
Active is transferred antibody, so protection is immediate but wears off fast
Active comes only from surviving the disease, never from being vaccinated
Active is the antibody an infant receives across the placenta before birth
preguntas.explicacion: Active immunity is protection produced by the person's own immune system after an antigen stimulates antibody-mediated and cell-mediated responses, and it usually lasts for years or for life; surviving the infection and being vaccinated are the two ways to acquire it. Passive immunity is antibody produced elsewhere and transferred in, as from mother to infant or in a blood product: immediate, and temporary.

preguntas.fuente: MyPlate, USDA: Fruits — what counts as a cup
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which amount counts as one cup from the Fruit Group?
opciones: Half a cup of dried fruit
Half a cup of canned fruit
Two cups of 100% fruit juice
Half a cup of frozen fruit
preguntas.explicacion: A cup-equivalent of fruit is one cup of fresh, frozen or canned fruit, one cup of 100% juice, or half a cup of dried fruit, which is concentrated and therefore counts double. The guidance adds that at least half of the fruit eaten should be whole fruit rather than juice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Dehiscence", Interprofessional Team Interventions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these raises a surgical patient's risk of wound dehiscence?
opciones: Hypoalbuminemia, wound infection, steroid use, cancer and emergency surgery
Hypoalbuminemia, early ambulation, regular exercise and elective daytime surgery
Youth, a low body mass index, a high protein diet and an absorbable suture material
A monofilament suture, a running closure, a facial incision and an outpatient setting
preguntas.explicacion: The patient-related risk factors named for dehiscence are advancing age, an infected wound, a low serum albumin, surgery done as an emergency, cancer, and treatment with steroids, and the risk climbs as they accumulate. Diabetes, obesity and smoking also impair healing. The suture material or closure technique chosen weighs less than these patient factors do.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Besides treatment and surgery, for which of these is informed consent listed as required?
opciones: Blood and medication infusions, and anesthesia
Routine vital signs and a height measurement
Transport of specimens to a reference laboratory
Storage of leftover serum for one further week
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is required for treatment, for dissemination of patient information, for the discussion of the HIPAA rules, for specific procedures, for surgery, for blood and medication infusions, and for anesthesia. It is a communication process between clinician and patient, not merely a signature on a document.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Breach exceptions · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse opens the wrong chart by accident, in good faith and within her duties, and closes it without using anything. What is this?
opciones: One of the three exceptions to the definition of a breach
A breach that still requires notice to the patient within sixty days
A reportable security incident that must go to the Secretary each year
A disclosure that must go on the accounting of disclosures
preguntas.explicacion: Three situations sit outside the definition. First: an unintentional acquisition, access or use by a member of the workforce who was acting in good faith and inside the authority given to her. Second: an inadvertent disclosure between two people who are both authorized to reach PHI at the same entity or organized arrangement. In both, the information may not then be used or disclosed improperly. Third: a good faith belief that whoever received it would not have been able to retain it.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Pictograms (Figure 1 note)
preguntas.subtema: Required pictograms · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: The GHS uses nine hazard pictograms. How many does OSHA enforce, and which one is optional?
opciones: Eight; only the environmental pictogram is optional
Nine; none is optional under the 2012 revision
Seven; the environmental and the health hazard ones are optional
Eight; the flame pictogram is optional for laboratory reagents
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA adopted the GHS pictograms but enforces eight of the nine: the one for the environment is not required, since environmental hazards fall to other agencies, though a label preparer may add it as supplementary information, so workers may still see it.
