preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (communication and anxiety)
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E1 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient admits to a history of panic attacks during blood draws. Which two simple measures are described to lower anxiety and prepare for a possible reaction?
opciones: Counting down before the puncture, and having the patient lie down when the history is severe
Drawing without warning so the patient has no time to react, and using a smaller needle
Applying the tourniquet early so the draw is quicker, and keeping the patient standing
Postponing the draw until a family member is present, and skipping the identification questions
preguntas.explicacion: Simple steps such as counting down can significantly reduce anxiety and improve the conditions for the venipuncture, and a patient who reports bad panic attacks during the draw may be asked to lie down; identifying patients afraid of blood tests or with a history of vasovagal attacks in advance lets the team prepare for a possible faint. Drawing without warning contradicts the emphasis on transparent communication and consent.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(A), (B) and (C), Gloves
preguntas.subtema: Torn gloves · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: During a venipuncture the phlebotomist notices a tear in one glove. What does the standard require?
opciones: Replace it as soon as feasible; a single-use glove is never washed for reuse
Finish the draw, then wash the glove with soap and water so it can be reused
Cover the tear with tape until the procedure ends, then discard the glove
Replace it only if blood reached the skin; otherwise finish the draw and discard it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(A) has a disposable glove changed as soon as it is practical once contaminated, and as soon as feasible if it is torn, punctured or otherwise no longer a barrier. Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(B) adds that single-use gloves are never washed or decontaminated to be used again; only utility gloves may be reused, and only while they are intact, under (d)(3)(ix)(C). What triggers the change is the loss of the barrier, not whether blood has already touched skin.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Food Safety — Summary
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k169 disease prevention education · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What are the four basic steps of food safety taught for the home kitchen?
opciones: Clean, separate, cook and chill
Clean, sanitize, cook and freeze
Wash, marinate, cook and reheat
Clean, separate, season and store
preguntas.explicacion: Handling, cooking and storing food safely is what keeps foodborne illness away, and the steps are four: clean hands, produce, counters and utensils; separate raw foods so germs do not travel between them; cook food hot and keep it hot, because heat kills germs; and chill fresh food in the refrigerator right away.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Adapting Your Communication
preguntas.subtema: Speech impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6)
preguntas.pregunta: After a stroke a patient follows what is said but answers in short, effortful phrases such as "Bathroom, go." Which pattern is this?
opciones: Broca's aphasia, the most common type of aphasia
Global aphasia, from damage across the language areas
A stress response that blocks the incoming message
A psychological barrier from the sender's own hurry
preguntas.explicacion: In Broca's aphasia the person usually follows speech and knows what she wants to say, yet produces short phrases with great effort, so she is often aware of the trouble and gets frustrated. Global aphasia comes from injury across several language areas and leaves both speaking and understanding severely limited.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 5 k74 · CCMA 5E k182 · CMA III.G.4.d / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: An active-duty service member with both TRICARE and Medicare is treated. Which pays first?
opciones: TRICARE pays first and Medicare pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first and TRICARE pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first for inpatient care and TRICARE for outpatient care
The patient pays first and both programs reimburse him afterward
preguntas.explicacion: In the table of common Medicare Secondary Payer situations, a service member on active-duty status has TRICARE paying first and Medicare second. The order flips for inactive-status members seen by civilian providers, where Medicare pays first; should that inactive member be seen at a military hospital, or by another federal provider, TRICARE pays first again. The split turns on status and setting, not on the type of service.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, row 3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.G · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A prothrombin time and a partial thromboplastin time are ordered together. What does that mean for the order of draw?
opciones: Both are citrate tubes, so both are filled in the coagulation-tube position
The prothrombin tube keeps its usual place and the thromboplastin tube is filled last of all
Both are citrate tubes, but they are filled after the serum separator tube
The thromboplastin tube is filled ahead of the prothrombin tube
preguntas.explicacion: Both assays are run on citrated plasma, so both use the light blue tube, and the table puts that tube ahead of the clot activator, separator, heparin and EDTA tubes. Nothing separates two tubes of the same kind, so neither goes ahead of the other, and the position filled last belongs to the fluoride tube for glucose.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.11 Checklist for Staple Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: How far should Steri-Strips extend past a staple line, and what is the patient told about them?
opciones: About 1.5 to 2 cm on each side, and to let them fall off on their own over one to three weeks
About 1.5 to 2 cm on each side, and to peel them off gently at the first follow-up visit
About 5 to 6 cm on each side, and to let them fall off on their own over one to three weeks
Only as far as the staple holes, and to soak them off in the bath after three or four days
preguntas.explicacion: The strips are cut so that they reach about 1.5 to 2 cm beyond the incision on either side, which lets them carry the tension across the line and support healing by primary intention. Patients are told not to pull them off but to let them come away gradually, usually over one to three weeks, and to shower rather than soak in a tub.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Repetitive or Continuous Non-covered Care
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is midway through a repeated non-covered treatment and nothing about it has changed. Does each session need its own advance written notice?
opciones: No, the first notice holds while the care, her health and the rules stay put
Yes, a fresh notice has to be signed before every session of the course
Yes, but only where the patient asks for another one to be issued
No, and that first notice holds for the rest of her life as a patient
preguntas.explicacion: A notice stays effective after delivery as long as three things hold: the care described on it, the patient's health status, and the coverage rules for those items or services. If any of them changes during treatment, a new notice goes out. For repetitive or continuous care the provider may issue another notice after a year, though nothing requires it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", section Other Issues; and Table (Common Pitfalls), Negative body language
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient is refusing to sit for the draw. Which de-escalation techniques are described?
opciones: A moderate distance, calm body language, and awareness of the exits
Standing over the patient, speaking firmly, and blocking the doorway
Leaving without a word and returning with two more staff members
Sitting close and holding eye contact so he feels fully attended to
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation borrows from the same set of therapeutic communication techniques and balances the provider's safety against the patient's comfort: hold a moderate distance without looking defensive, keep body language and tone calm and open, stand at a right angle to the person, know where the exits are, and let them leave easily. Standing over a patient is a pitfall.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: QRS Complex
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A QRS complex on a strip measures two small squares. Which range is the normal one?
opciones: Under 120 ms, and usually between 60 and 100 ms
Under 200 ms, and usually between 120 and 160 ms
Under 80 ms, and usually between 40 and 60 ms
Under 440 ms, and usually between 300 and 400 ms
preguntas.explicacion: The QRS complex is ventricular depolarization and normally takes less than three small squares, that is under 120 ms, most often 60 to 100 ms. A wide complex points to a bundle branch block, to high potassium, or to a beat that started in the ventricles instead of above them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Intestinal Stoma", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.4.d (solo outline vigente) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: Which complications of an intestinal stoma are described as late rather than early?
opciones: Stoma prolapse and parastomal hernia, which may be managed conservatively or surgically
Cutaneous irritation and hematoma, which are generally managed conservatively
Twisting of the bowel loop and kinking of its mesentery, both seen at the operation
Tension from a short mesentery and carcinomatosis, both judged before the operation
preguntas.explicacion: Stoma complications sort into early and late. The early ones, irritation of the skin or a hematoma among them, usually call for conservative management; the late ones, prolapse of the stoma and parastomal hernia, may be handled either conservatively or with surgery. Somewhere between a tenth and seven tenths of patients develop some complication.

preguntas.subtema: Access to the Exposure Control Plan · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist asks to see the facility's Exposure Control Plan. What does the standard say?
opciones: A copy must be accessible to employees, and training must explain how to obtain it
It goes only to the Director and the Assistant Secretary, when they ask for it
It may be seen only with the employee's written consent filed in the medical record
It is a management document; employees receive only a summary in the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iii) requires each employer to make a copy of the plan accessible to employees, following 29 CFR 1910.20(e), and (g)(2)(vii)(D) makes an explanation of the plan, and of how to get hold of a copy, a mandatory element of the training program. The access granted to the Director and the Assistant Secretary by (c)(1)(vi) comes on top of employee access, not instead of it. Written consent is the condition for releasing an employee's medical record to others under (h)(1)(iii), not for reading the plan.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1283(a)(4), Standard: Test records
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: During an inspection the surveyor picks a result from three months ago and asks who ran that test. Which CLIA record has to supply the answer?
opciones: The record of specimen testing, which carries dates and who tested
The test report itself, which carries the person who released it
The requisition, which carries the orderer and the collector
The competency file kept for each member of the testing staff
preguntas.explicacion: The test records standard asks for an information or record system holding four things: positive identification of the specimen, the date and time it reached the laboratory, the condition and disposition of any specimen that failed the acceptability criteria, and the records and dates of all testing together with the identity of whoever performed it. That last item is what the surveyor wants.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.6: Description of Procedure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B6 k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(1) · RMA III.G.2.a(i) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: How does the technique of an intramuscular injection differ from a subcutaneous one?
opciones: The skin is stabilized instead of pinched, and the needle enters at 90 degrees
The skin is pinched instead of stabilized, and the needle enters at 45 degrees
The skin is held taut and flat, and the needle enters at 5 to 15 degrees
The skin is stabilized instead of pinched, and the needle enters at 45 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The two procedures run alike until the skin is handled: for an intramuscular injection the non-dominant hand stabilizes the skin around the site rather than pinching it, and the syringe, held like a dart, goes in quickly at 90 degrees with a steady, smooth motion. The needle is 18 to 25 gauge and half an inch to an inch and a half, chosen for the medication, the site and the patient's age and body mass.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k22 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes a hard week at home and the assistant begins telling her what to do. Why is unsolicited advice a pitfall?
opciones: The patient may feel it as intrusive and lacking in empathy
It commits the office to a plan no provider has ordered
It counts as practicing outside the assistant's own scope
It shortens the visit and leaves the history incomplete
preguntas.explicacion: Advice the patient never asked for is listed among the approaches with negative therapeutic value: unless she specifically asked, she may feel it as intrusive and lacking in empathy. It sits in the same table as value judgments, negative body language and false reassurance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, How to Prepare for a Lab Test, section What types of lab tests require special preparation; StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D V.B · CCMA 3D1 k113 k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collecting a 24-hour urine for 5-HIAA asks which foods to avoid. Which list is correct?
opciones: Bananas, avocados, walnuts, pineapples and eggplants
Cooked meats, herbal tea and alcoholic beverages
Douching, tampons and sex in the 24 to 48 hours before
Coffee, energy drinks and lemon-flavoured water
preguntas.explicacion: For a 5-HIAA test the patient may be asked to steer clear of various foods, the examples given being bananas, avocados, walnuts, pineapples and eggplants. Other tests carry other restrictions: creatinine may call for fasting or for avoiding cooked meats, cortisol for resting before the draw and for eating, drinking and tooth-brushing to stop for a period, and a fecal occult blood test for certain foods and medicines to be dropped. The douching, tampon and intercourse restriction belongs to the Pap smear, not to a urine collection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k148 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What should not be put on the chest before a Holter is fitted?
opciones: Lotion or moisturizer, which stops the leads from sticking
Powder or deodorant, which stops the leads from sticking
Alcohol or gel, which stops the leads from sticking
Sunscreen or perfume, which stains the adhesive patches
preguntas.explicacion: Lotion and moisturizer are singled out because they interfere with how the leads attach, and the electrodes have to stay firmly stuck for the recording to be accurate. Alcohol and conductive gel are the opposite: they are part of preparing the skin and the electrode.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · CPT Core k4 (applied D3)
preguntas.pregunta: How many oxygen molecules can a single hemoglobin molecule carry, and what binds them?
opciones: Four, one on the iron ion of each of its four heme groups
Two, one on each alpha-beta pair of globin chains
Four, one bound directly to each of the four globin proteins
About 300 million, one for every hemoglobin in the cell
preguntas.explicacion: Hemoglobin consists of four folded globin chains, two alpha and two beta, each holding a heme group with an iron ion. Oxygen binds to the iron, not to the globin protein, so each hemoglobin carries up to four oxygen molecules. A single red cell holds about 300 million hemoglobin molecules, which is why one cell can carry about 1.2 billion oxygen molecules.

preguntas.subtema: Event notifications · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital's electronic system sends an event notification when a patient is admitted. Which three items must the message carry at a minimum?
opciones: The patient's name, the treating practitioner's name and the sending institution
The patient's name, the admitting diagnosis and the expected date of discharge
The patient's record number, the insurance plan and the treating practitioner
The patient's name, the reason for the visit and the telephone of the unit
preguntas.explicacion: Where a hospital runs a system meeting the adopted content exchange standard, its notification capacity has to be switched on, and every message has to carry at least three items: who the patient is, which practitioner is treating him, and which institution is sending it. Diagnosis and coverage are outside that minimum.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Assess language preferences
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c · 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which question does the toolkit tell staff to ask about language, and why that one?
opciones: What language the patient wants to be spoken to in, since illness erodes English
How well the patient speaks English, since that decides if an interpreter is needed
Whether the patient has a relative who can interpret at the next appointment
What country the patient was born in, since that identifies the language needed
preguntas.explicacion: Every patient is asked what language they want spoken and what language they want written material in, and the answers go in the medical record. Asking preference rather than proficiency matters because people who normally handle English well can lose it when sick, tired or frightened, and because admitting limited English is embarrassing.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heart attack first aid", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Under what condition is chewable aspirin given to a patient with chest pain?
opciones: Only if a physician or the emergency operator has told the patient to take it
Only if the patient's blood pressure is above 140 over 90 at that moment
Always, since the dose is small and the benefit outweighs any risk at all
Never, since every oral medicine is withheld in a heart emergency
preguntas.explicacion: A full 325 mg dose or a low-dose 81 mg tablet is chewed and swallowed only when a physician or the emergency operator has advised it, when the patient is not allergic and has no condition that makes aspirin dangerous. The call for help is never delayed to find the aspirin: help is called first.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Bleeding", When to use a tourniquet
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: Where is a tourniquet placed once direct pressure has failed on a bleeding arm?
opciones: Two to three inches (5 to 7.7 cm) above the wound, clear of the joint
Directly over the wound itself, on top of the soaked dressing
As close as possible to the armpit, no matter where the wound is
Below the wound, between the bleeding point and the fingertips
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet goes on the limb 2 to 3 inches above the wound and away from a joint; if the joint is in the way, it moves higher, toward the trunk. Padding or clothing under it keeps the skin from being pinched. The time it was applied is written down and passed to the responders, because a tourniquet left on too long injures nerves and tissue.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.1 Baseline Drift
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: The patient cable is hanging off the side of the table and the baseline will not settle. What is the mechanism?
opciones: The pull on the wires unsettles the contact at the electrode
The pull on the wires lowers the voltage the unit records
The pull on the wires draws room current into the tracing
The pull on the wires slows the paper leaving the writer
preguntas.explicacion: Tension on the lead wires is one of the six listed reasons for unstable electrode contact, and unstable contact is the prime suspect behind drift. The weight of a hanging wire tugs at the tab, which is why a towel is laid across the wires to take the pull off.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction; Issues of Concern: Medical Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Distributive justice · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k212 · CMA II.E.4 · RMA I.C.4 · NCMA 4.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which ethical principle is at work when a limited supply of a treatment is spread fairly across the patients who need it?
opciones: Distributing resources equitably across the patients
Preserving the patient's life and their autonomy
Avoiding acts known to expose a patient to harm
Placing a high value on the dignity of the person
preguntas.explicacion: Four principles underpin patient rights: the dignity of the person is held high; the clinician works in good will toward the patient, above all to preserve life and autonomy; anything known to place the patient in harm's way, done or left undone, is avoided; and what there is gets shared out fairly among those who need it. That last one is what governs a scarce supply. A right to receive treatment is usually traced back to good will, the sanctity of life and that same distributive fairness.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Nasopharyngeal/Nasal Aspirate and Nasopharyngeal/Nasal Wash
preguntas.subtema: Nasal wash versus aspirate · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: How does a nasopharyngeal wash differ from a nasopharyngeal aspirate?
opciones: Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril first, and only then is suction applied
Several drops of sterile saline go into each nostril afterward, to rinse the suction catheter out
The catheter is passed to a shallower depth, stopping short of the turbinates on either side
The specimen is placed on slides and air dried, rather than into a viral transport medium tube
preguntas.explicacion: Both use a catheter on suction with the head tilted back 70 degrees, and both go in to a depth matching the distance from nostril to the outer opening of the ear. The wash differs in that sterile normal saline, several drops of it, goes into each nostril first. Gentle suction follows, the catheter turns as it comes out, and the specimen goes into viral transport medium.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: physician-patient privilege
preguntas.subtema: Confidentiality · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: How does physician-patient privilege differ from doctor-patient confidentiality?
opciones: The privilege applies inside legal proceedings; confidentiality applies outside them
The privilege applies to written records; confidentiality applies to spoken exchanges
The privilege applies to federal cases; confidentiality applies to state-level cases
The privilege applies while treatment continues; confidentiality applies afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: The privilege protects communications between a clinician and a patient inside legal proceedings: it stops the professional testifying about her medical information unless she waives that protection, and either side may assert it. Confidentiality protects records and information outside litigation, under state and federal statutes. The privilege comes from state statutes and varies.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Third Party Liability
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicaid patient also holds coverage through her husband's employer. Which plan does the practice bill first?
opciones: The employer plan, since Medicaid pays only the portion no third party owes
Medicaid, since a state program always pays ahead of a commercial plan
Whichever plan the patient names, since she may choose the order of payers
Both together, since the two share the bill in proportion to their benefits
preguntas.explicacion: Third party liability means a third party has a legal obligation to pay part or all of the cost of services given to a Medicaid beneficiary, and the examples named are other programs such as Medicare and any other health insurance the person holds. Where such an obligation exists Medicaid pays only its own portion, which is why the other coverage is billed first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Irrigation", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B9 k76 · CMA I.C.2.b · NCMA 2B.17
preguntas.pregunta: Which finding rules out ear irrigation for a cerumen impaction?
opciones: A history of tympanic membrane perforation or of previous ear surgery
A history of using cotton-tipped applicators to clean the ear canal
A cerumenolytic such as mineral oil having been instilled beforehand
Aural fullness and decreased hearing on the side to be irrigated
preguntas.explicacion: Otoscopy comes first, to confirm an intact eardrum and no ventilation tubes. Known perforation, tubes, previous surgery such as tympanomastoidectomy, discharge suggesting infection, or prior radiation to the area all rule it out, and those patients go to an otolaryngologist. Cotton swabs are a cause of impaction, and fullness is a reason to treat it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Primary care provider
preguntas.subtema: Health care roles and settings · CCMA 1A k2 · CMA II.F.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: According to HealthCare.gov, who can serve as a patient's primary care provider?
opciones: An M.D. or D.O., a nurse practitioner, a clinical nurse specialist or a physician assistant, where state law allows
Only a physician holding a medical doctor (M.D.) degree, and never a doctor of osteopathic medicine (D.O.)
A physician or nurse practitioner only; physician assistants and clinical nurse specialists are excluded
Any of the four professionals, but only a physician may coordinate the patient's access to other services
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov's definition names four kinds of professional who can be a primary care provider: a physician, whether M.D. or D.O.; a nurse practitioner; a clinical nurse specialist; and a physician assistant, in each case as state law allows. All four share the same role in the definition: to provide, coordinate or help the patient reach a range of health care services. The D.O. is named alongside the M.D., no one of the four is excluded, and coordination is not reserved to the physician.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies and Hospital Patients; and StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section Etiology
preguntas.subtema: Bandaging and allergies · CPT D3 k73 · D2 k48 · PBT II.I II.J · CCMA 3E9 k137 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.13
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a latex allergy. Which items on a routine phlebotomy tray are likely to contain latex?
opciones: Gloves, tourniquets and elastic bandages or wraps
Gloves and alcohol swabs, but not the elastic band
Evacuated tubes and their stoppers, and the labels
Sharps containers and the plastic transport bags
preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up throughout health care, most commonly in gloves, and the medical items listed alongside them include tourniquets and elastic bandages and wraps. A patient with this allergy needs latex-free substitutes for those items, and the whole team has to be told about the allergy.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1283(a), Standard: Test records
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D5 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.3.b · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A clotted EDTA tube is rejected. Under the CLIA test records standard, what must the laboratory's record system contain about that specimen?
opciones: Its condition and what was done with it, since it did not meet the acceptability criteria
Only the date of receipt, because no test was performed on the specimen
The name and title of the person who collected it and the reason the collection attempt failed
Only its positive identification, because the condition of a rejected specimen is not a record element
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1283(a)(3) puts on the record system what became of specimens that fail the laboratory's acceptability criteria, their state and where they ended up, together with positive identification of every specimen, the date and time it was received, and the dates each test was run and by whom. Who collected it is not on that list, and rejected specimens are named in, not out.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.5 Wound Dressings
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.k · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: A stage 3 pressure injury drains heavily and needs packing. Which dressing fits, and what must be avoided?
opciones: An alginate, which is highly absorptive and must not be put into a dry wound
A transparent film, which retains moisture and must not be put on fragile skin
A hydrogel, which adds moisture and must not be spread onto the surrounding skin
A dry gauze, which costs the least of these and must not be left in place beyond a day
preguntas.explicacion: Alginates and hydrofibers are nonadherent and highly absorptive, which suits heavily exuding wounds and packing of full-thickness injuries at stage 3 or 4. They are usually changed every 24 to 48 hours depending on how saturated they are, and they are kept out of dry wounds because there they can injure the wound bed.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.4
preguntas.subtema: Ransomware prevention · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An e-mail marked urgent asks a receptionist to open an attachment and confirm her log-in. Which trained response does the guidance describe?
opciones: Hover over the link to read where it goes and check the sender by another route
Open the attachment only if the sender's address matches the practice's domain
Forward it to the whole staff so that everyone recognizes the message on sight
Reply to the same message asking the sender to confirm that it is legitimate
preguntas.explicacion: Malicious attachments and callers asking for log-in details are the usual first step of a ransomware attack. Users are trained to hover first and read the destination address, to weigh the sender, the urgency and the spelling, and, when in doubt, to confirm through a separate channel. Replying in the same thread confirms nothing, since the sender may be the attacker.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which position is used for a routine office blood pressure?
opciones: Seated with the back supported, both feet flat on the floor and the legs uncrossed
Seated on the end of the table with the feet hanging and the back left unsupported
Lying supine with the arm at the side, which removes the effect of gravity entirely
Seated with the legs crossed at the ankle, which steadies the patient during inflation
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits with the back against the chair, feet flat and legs uncrossed, and stays that way for at least five minutes before the cuff is inflated. Each departure has a price: an unsupported back and feet add about 6 mm Hg and crossed legs add 2 to 4 mm Hg to the systolic value.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b); StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary in practice · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k36
preguntas.pregunta: A billing clerk asks a phlebotomist for a patient's full medical history to process a claim. Which HIPAA standard is at stake?
opciones: Minimum necessary: limit the PHI to what the payment purpose requires
Right of access: the clerk may see all records that the patient could see herself
Treatment exception: payment staff are exempt from all limits
De-identification: the clerk must receive only coded data
preguntas.explicacion: Payment is a permitted purpose, yet it is not among the exceptions to the minimum necessary standard, so the entity has to make a reasonable effort to hold what the clerk receives down to what processing the claim requires. The treatment exception covers providers treating the patient, not billing. De-identified data would not serve payment, and the right of access belongs to the individual rather than to workforce members. The same principle turns up in guidance that access should match the employee's role, so a laboratory technologist sees laboratory records and not the whole history.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Lack of Patient Comprehension
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2M k43 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which tools are recommended for checking whether a patient really understood the risks, benefits and alternatives?
opciones: The teach-back or test/feedback method
A signed consent form and a staff witness
A formal psychiatric competency evaluation
A reading-level check of the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back or the test/feedback method can be used to assess understanding, and open-ended questions and encouraging questions make the dialogue interactive. It also notes that the emphasis on a signature as proof of understanding is being questioned, and that a psychiatrist is consulted only when capacity is in doubt.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Anatomical Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A scar is documented as being in the anterior carpal region. Which surface of the wrist does that describe?
opciones: The palm side, because anterior is defined from anatomical position
The back side, because anterior is defined from the resting hand
The thumb side, because anterior is defined from the midline
The little finger side, because anterior follows the ulnar edge
preguntas.explicacion: Every directional term is read as if the body were in anatomical position: standing upright, feet forward, arms out to the sides and palms facing forward. In that position the palm faces front, so an anterior carpal scar is on the palm side, and it keeps that name even when the hand is lying palm down on a table.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient lies tense on the table and the tracing is fuzzy. Besides reassurance, which step is suggested?
opciones: Tuck the hands under the buttocks and raise the knees
Fold the arms across the chest and cross the ankles
Have the patient sit up until the shivering has passed
Hold the arms down against the table during the run
preguntas.explicacion: Laying the hands on the stomach helps, and tucking them under the buttocks usually helps more; a pillow under the knees to raise the legs slightly is part of the same list. Crossing the legs is the opposite of what the position calls for, since the arms rest at the sides and the legs stay uncrossed.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Sputum Gram stain (003765), How to Prepare for the Test; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Routine sputum culture (003723), How the Test will Feel; and MedlinePlus, Sputum Culture, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Sputum timing and hydration · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A sputum culture is scheduled. Which two instructions help the patient produce a usable specimen?
opciones: Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect first thing in the morning
Drink plenty of fluids the night before, and collect right after the evening meal
Fast completely for 12 hours, and then collect first thing in the morning
Take an over-the-counter cough suppressant, and collect first thing in the morning
preguntas.explicacion: Fluids the night before make the airways produce more phlegm and the sputum easier to raise, and the test is more accurate done first thing in the morning, before eating or drinking. A 12-hour fast is the preparation for bronchoscopy, not for a coughed specimen, and suppressing the cough would defeat the collection. The provider may tap the chest or offer a salty mist to help.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(iii), (h)(3)(ii) and (h)(3)(iii), Recordkeeping
preguntas.subtema: Access to the medical record · CPT D1 1C 1N k39 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k110 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA I.C.5 III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Who may obtain a copy of an employee's bloodborne pathogens medical record?
opciones: The employee, anyone with the employee's written consent, and OSHA or NIOSH
Any supervisor in the department where the exposure incident took place
The source patient, who is entitled to the results of the exposed worker
The employee's union representative, in the same way as training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iii) keeps these records confidential and bars disclosing them, inside the workplace or outside it, unless the employee has given express written consent, or the standard or another law demands it. Paragraph (h)(3)(iii) then names who does get them: the employee, anyone holding that written consent, the Director of NIOSH and the Assistant Secretary of Labor. Employee representatives appear one paragraph earlier, in (h)(3)(ii), and only for training records.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which three are the augmented unipolar limb leads?
opciones: aVR, aVL and aVF, taken from the four limb electrodes
I, II and III, taken from the four limb electrodes
V1, V2 and V3, taken from the four limb electrodes
II, III and aVF, taken from the four limb electrodes
preguntas.explicacion: The six limb leads split into two families that share the same four electrodes: the standard bipolar leads I, II and III, and the augmented unipolar leads aVR, aVL and aVF. V1 through V6 are the precordial leads and come from the six electrodes stuck on the chest wall.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance; and CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Paid Promptly
preguntas.subtema: Claim follow-up · CMA III.G.3.b(5) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: An insurer that should pay before Medicare has sat on a claim for four months. What may happen next?
opciones: The provider may bill Medicare, which can pay conditionally and recover it later
The provider may bill the patient, who then goes after the insurer for the money
The provider may bill Medicare, which pays and closes the matter with the insurer
The provider may bill the insurer again and wait a second 120 days for an answer
preguntas.explicacion: Where the insurance company does not pay promptly, which usually means inside 120 days, the bill may go to Medicare from the doctor or other provider. A conditional payment can then be made so the bill is settled, and Medicare recovers afterwards whatever the primary payer should have paid. For no-fault and workers' compensation claims with no ongoing responsibility, promptness is measured as 120 days from the day that insurer received the claim.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient points to the breastbone and asks for its medical name. Which root names that bone?
opciones: Stern-, for the sternum
Cost-, for the ribs
Spondyl-, for a vertebra
Phalang-, for a finger bone
preguntas.explicacion: Stern- names the sternum, the bone people call the breastbone. Several roots in this vocabulary come with their plain-language gloss attached, which is what makes them useful at the bedside: cost- is a rib, spondyl- a vertebra of the spine and phalang- any bone in the fingers or toes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Parenteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(1) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the ventrogluteal site preferred over the dorsogluteal one for an intramuscular injection?
opciones: The dorsogluteal site risks injuring the sciatic nerve and the superior gluteal artery
The dorsogluteal site holds so little muscle that it cannot take a full milliliter
The ventrogluteal site lies over a very vascular area, so the drug is absorbed faster
The ventrogluteal site is the only one that can be reached with the patient seated
preguntas.explicacion: An intramuscular dose may go into the deltoid, the vastus lateralis, the rectus femoris, the dorsogluteal or the ventrogluteal site. The dorsogluteal one, in the upper outer quadrant of the buttock, was the traditional pick, yet a needle there can strike the sciatic nerve or the superior gluteal artery. The ventrogluteal site aims at the gluteus medius and clears both, which is why it is recommended.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.4 Diseases, Disorders and Injuries of the Integumentary System, Basal Cell Carcinoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(1) (2027 I.C.6.g(1)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A lesion on the scalp of a patient with years of sun exposure is diagnosed as basal cell carcinoma. Which statement about that diagnosis is right?
opciones: It is the most common cancer in the country and responds best when caught early
It is the rarest of the skin cancers and responds best when caught early
It is the most aggressive skin cancer and rarely responds to any treatment
It is a benign growth of melanocytes that is treated only if it enlarges
preguntas.explicacion: Basal cell carcinoma affects the dividing stem cells of the deepest epidermal layer and is the most common of all cancers in the United States, turning up on the head, neck, arms and back, the areas with the most long-term sun exposure. Like most cancers it responds best to early treatment, whether surgery, cryosurgery or a topical ointment.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Requests for Access
preguntas.subtema: Access requests · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for his records and refuses to say what he wants them for. How should the office respond?
opciones: Process the request, because a covered entity may not require a reason for wanting access
Hold the request until he states a purpose the office can record on its own access form
Deny the request, since a stated purpose is one of the elements of a valid access request
Refer him to the privacy official, who alone may waive the requirement to state a purpose
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may require that access requests be in writing and may use its own form, but only if that does not become a barrier or an unreasonable delay. OCR states plainly that the entity may not require the individual to give a reason, and that a rationale volunteered or already known is not a permitted ground for denying access.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Which sampling container is preferable?
preguntas.subtema: Purpose of clean-catch · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the midstream clean-catch technique used instead of simply voiding into a cup?
opciones: To keep germs from the penis or vagina out of the sample, so contaminants and formed particles are minimized
To obtain the most concentrated urine of the day, which shows the kidneys' ability to concentrate
To bypass the urethra entirely, which is the only way to get a sample free of periurethral flora
To capture the first portion of the stream, where epithelial cells and leukocytes are most numerous
preguntas.explicacion: The clean-catch method exists to keep organisms from the vagina or the penis out of the urine. A multicentre comparison found first-voided samples carrying more epithelial cells, red cells and leukocytes than midstream ones, which is what confirmed midstream as the sample of choice. Concentration is the reason for a first-morning specimen, and bypassing the urethra describes suprapubic aspiration, not a voided sample.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Finding a telehealth vendor
preguntas.subtema: Choosing a platform · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is comparing telehealth platforms and wants the scheduling desk's questions on the list. Which questions belong to that desk's concerns?
opciones: Whether there is a waiting room feature and whether staff or patients can book visits on the platform
Whether there is a waiting room feature and whether the vendor will train the practice's clinicians
Whether the product is compliant with privacy law and whether a written contract is required
Whether patients must download an application and whether the vendor stores the recordings
preguntas.explicacion: The questions suggested for researching a platform include whether it is compliant with privacy law, whether a contract is required, whether it integrates with the record system, whether it will be easy for patients, whether there is a waiting room feature, whether staff or patients can schedule visits through the platform itself, and whether patients can give consent on it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b)
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient in her seventies is being roomed for the first time. How should the assistant introduce themselves and address her?
opciones: By first and last name, addressing the patient formally
By first name only, addressing the patient by first name
By role only, addressing the patient by the room number
By last name only, addressing the patient as dear or honey
preguntas.explicacion: Introducing yourself with first and last names and addressing the patient by a title and last name shows respect for their dignity and autonomy; gender-neutral wording and chosen pronouns belong here too. Older patients in particular may expect formal address, and terms such as dear can land as disrespect.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(2)(i) and (c)(2)(ii), Exposure Determination
preguntas.subtema: Exposure determination · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: When the employer decides which jobs involve occupational exposure, how must protective equipment be treated?
opciones: Ignored: the determination is made as if no protective equipment were worn
Counted: a job is exposed only if PPE cannot fully block the anticipated contact
Counted: the determination lists the PPE provided and excludes tasks it covers
Deferred: PPE is assessed later, in the annual review of safer medical devices
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) has the exposure determination drawn up as though no protective equipment existed. What is being asked is whether contact with blood or OPIM is reasonably anticipated in that job, not whether gloves or a gown would stop it. That is why the lists in (c)(2)(i) are built from job classifications and tasks. The annual review in (c)(1)(iv) looks at technology and safer devices; it is no substitute for the determination.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Issues of Concern: Ethical Principles Involved; and StatPearls, "Medical Ethics" (NBK535361)
preguntas.subtema: Unbiased care · CCMA 7G · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: An uninsured patient and an insured patient need the same limited resource. What does the ethical framework require?
opciones: Fair distribution regardless of insurance status or social standing
Priority for the insured patient, because the cost is already covered
Priority for the uninsured patient, to correct the existing imbalance
A decision by the business manager, who is accountable for the budget
preguntas.explicacion: The principle of justice tells the practitioner to distribute medical resources fairly and equitably, whatever the patient's demographics, insurance, socioeconomic position or mental disability. At the bedside that means rationing the good that can be done evenly and equitably among the patients involved, rather than sorting them by who pays.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Hematoma · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: As the needle is advanced, a swelling rises quickly at the site. What has most likely happened?
opciones: The needle went beyond the lumen of the vein and blood is pooling under the skin
The vein has collapsed under the vacuum of the tube and blood is backing up into it
The tourniquet has occluded the artery and the limb is becoming congested
The alcohol was not dry, and the irritated skin is swelling around the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Inserting the needle beyond the lumen of the vein causes a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin. A hematoma can also form when too little pressure is kept up during the draw and after it. A collapsed vein is not described in these sources, and wet alcohol raises contamination risk, not swelling.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access, the two meanings · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A manager reads that her group is moving to open access and assumes patients will now be able to go straight to a specialist. Why is she mistaken?
opciones: In the scheduling literature the phrase means same-day appointments, not direct specialist access
In the scheduling literature the phrase means direct specialist access, not same-day appointments
In the scheduling literature the phrase means dropping referrals for established patients only
In the scheduling literature the phrase means open enrollment, so any patient may join the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The phrase carries two meanings. In managed care it is sometimes used for removing the gatekeeper so that patients reach specialists directly. In the appointment literature, where it is also called advanced access or same-day scheduling, it means only that every patient can be given a slot on the day she calls, almost always with her own physician.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Documentation for billing · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Where should the search for a diagnosis code always begin?
opciones: In the alphabetic index, before the entry is verified in the tabular list
In the tabular list, before the entry is checked against the alphabetic index
In the payer's coverage policy for the service that was performed that day
In the previous claim for the patient, so the coding stays consistent over time
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines call it the most critical rule: begin the search for the correct code in the alphabetic index and never start in the tabular list, because starting there leads to coding errors. Coverage policies decide payment, not code selection, and copying a code from an earlier claim skips the documentation of this encounter.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Rights of Medication Administration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the extra rights added to the traditional five rights of medication administration?
opciones: The right of the patient to refuse the medication that has been prescribed
The right of the patient to a generic substitution chosen by the pharmacist
The right of the patient to a second opinion before any injection is given
The right of the patient to a written copy of the prescriber's own signature
preguntas.explicacion: The five traditional rights are patient, drug, dose, route and time. Documentation is usually added as a sixth, and the literature stretches the list as far as ten: the right to refuse, the right history and assessment, the right education and information, and the right drug interactions. Others have proposed the right indication, the right patient response and legible orders. Adding rights on its own does not stop errors.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Medicare Advantage Plan (Part C) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage Plan asks whether joining it ends her monthly Part B bill.
opciones: No, she must keep Part B and go on paying that premium to stay in the plan
Yes, the plan takes the place of Part B and of the premium that goes with it
Yes, provided the plan she joined also includes prescription drug coverage
No, but the Part B premium is refunded to her each year by the plan itself
preguntas.explicacion: Premiums, deductibles, copayments and coinsurance under a Medicare Advantage Plan vary by plan and can change every year, and the condition Medicare states plainly is that the enrollee must have Part B and keep paying the Part B premium in order to stay in the plan. Some plans do help pay that premium, but the requirement to hold Part B does not disappear.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: When several tubes are collected in one venipuncture, which tube is filled first?
opciones: The blood culture bottle
The light blue citrate tube
The non-additive tube
The gray fluoride tube
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes are filled in a fixed sequence so that the additive of one tube is not carried into the next. In the order the WHO reproduces from the United States laboratory standards consensus, the blood culture bottle is number 1 and the fluoride/oxalate tube is number 10, the last one used. Summarized in four groups, the same sequence runs sterile containers first, coagulation tubes next, plain and gel tubes after them, and the remaining additive tubes last. Color codes can differ between manufacturers, so the WHO tells you to check with the local laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Burn Classification", Full-Thickness Burns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which finding tells you a burn has reached full thickness?
opciones: The area is leathery and dry and does not blanch or hurt
The area is pink, dry and moderately painful to the touch
The area is red, blisters over, and blanches under pressure
The area is mottled and blanches slowly under firm pressure
preguntas.explicacion: A full-thickness burn takes in the epidermis, the dermis and the tissue underneath, so it looks leathery, stiff and dry, does not blanch because the blood supply is gone, and gives no sensation because the nerves are destroyed. It needs more than 8 weeks and surgery to heal, while a superficial burn heals in 5 to 10 days without scarring.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Confidential Communications Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Confidential communications · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.4 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 4 k62 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that appointment calls go to her work number rather than her home. What must the office do?
opciones: Accommodate her reasonable request that confidential communications go to another number
Refuse, because the number in the demographic record is the only one the office may dial
Require a signed authorization naming the workplace as a permitted disclosure location
Send the reminder by postcard instead, since written notice avoids the problem entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers have to let individuals ask that communications reach them by some other means or at some other location. The rule's example is a patient asking to be telephoned at her office instead of her home, and a provider must accommodate such a request where it is reasonable. The parallel example for written mail is asking for a closed envelope in place of a postcard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii III.F.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's palpitations are there all the time, day and night. Which test is enough to catch them?
opciones: A routine 12-lead tracing, taken while the symptom is present
A 24-hour monitor, worn at home while the symptom is present
An implantable recorder, placed under the skin of the chest
A two-week adhesive patch, worn while the symptom is present
preguntas.explicacion: The choice follows how often the symptoms come. Continuous symptoms are caught by an ordinary 12-lead recording, intermittent ones are what the Holter is usually used for, and symptoms that come rarely call for an event recorder or an implantable device.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Assess language preferences
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA I.A.3 / 2027 A.3.c · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: How should a practice assess each patient's language needs?
opciones: Ask every patient which language they prefer to speak and to read, and record it
Ask patients how well they speak English, and note the answer in the record
Note the preferred language only for patients who visibly struggle to speak English
Infer the language from the patient's surname or country of birth on the form
preguntas.explicacion: Every patient is asked which language they prefer for speaking and which for reading, the answer goes into the medical record, and an 'I Speak' card is used where the patient cannot answer. The reason preference is asked rather than proficiency is spelled out: people lose their English when sick or frightened, and may be too embarrassed to admit that it is limited.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Electronic delivery of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the desk to e-mail her the notice of privacy practices rather than take a paper copy home. May the office do that?
opciones: Yes, once she has said she will take the notice electronically rather than on paper
Yes, once the message has been encrypted and a read receipt has been returned
No, a direct treatment provider always hands the notice over on paper at the first visit
No, unless her first contact with the practice was made over the internet or by e-mail
preguntas.explicacion: The rule lets a covered entity e-mail the notice to an individual who has agreed to that form of delivery. That is a separate matter from the online-intake rule, under which a provider whose first service arrives electronically sends the notice automatically with the first request for service and tries for a return receipt.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 14: Nutrition Therapy — thickened liquids
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3 assisting with patient care · CMA I.C procedures · RMA XIV therapeutic modalities
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dysphagia is prescribed honey-thick liquids. How does that consistency differ from the others?
opciones: It drizzles from a cup and is less pourable than nectar-thick liquid
It holds its own shape and has to be taken with a spoon like pudding
It pours as easily as apricot nectar or a thick cream soup
It is the thinnest of the three and pours the same as plain water
preguntas.explicacion: Thickened liquids are ordered for patients who have trouble swallowing, and three consistencies are used. Nectar-thick pours easily, like apricot nectar or thick cream soup; honey-thick is slightly thicker and drizzles rather than pours; pudding-thick keeps its own shape and needs a spoon. Staff thicken liquids with a commercial product.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.2
preguntas.subtema: Backup power · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does the contingency guidance expect of the power arrangements behind the record system?
opciones: An uninterrupted supply for at least ten minutes and a generator with fuel for two days
An uninterrupted supply for at least one hour and a generator with fuel for one day
A generator alone, tested each year, since the record system restarts by itself after a cut
A second electricity contract with another company, switched over by the building's staff
preguntas.explicacion: Two layers are described. A battery or flywheel supply carries the record system instantly for at least ten minutes, and it is tested regularly, optimally monthly. Behind it sits an on-site generator able to keep the functions critical to operations running, with two days of fuel held on site, tested monthly and kept where flooding is unlikely.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(ii) and (g)(2)(iv), Information and Training
preguntas.subtema: Training frequency · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: When must bloodborne pathogens training be given to an employee with occupational exposure?
opciones: At initial assignment to exposure tasks and at least once a year afterward
At initial assignment only, with a refresher when an exposure incident occurs
Within 10 working days of hire and again whenever the sharps log is updated
Once every three years, matching the retention period for the training records
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(ii) puts training at the moment the employee is first assigned to tasks that may bring exposure, and at least once a year after that; (g)(2)(iv) adds that each annual session must fall inside a year of the last one. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a training cycle. Ten working days is the vaccine deadline of (f)(2)(i), and three years is how long the training records are kept, not how often training happens.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Invasive Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: Suprapubic aspiration · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: Why can a suprapubic bladder aspiration give false-positive protein, red cell and white cell results?
opciones: Blood from the needle puncture can contaminate the specimen
Periurethral flora enter the specimen as the needle passes the urethra
The antiseptic used on the abdominal skin reacts with the strip pads
The urine has usually been held in the bladder for less than 1 hour
preguntas.explicacion: Suprapubic aspiration is the most invasive and uncomfortable way to obtain urine, and blood introduced by the needle can produce false-positive protein, red cells and white cells. Its advantage is precisely that it bypasses the urethra, so periurethral flora are not a problem. It is reserved for cases where other methods fail or keep producing contaminated samples, which usually means small children.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Pulse Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse d · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Beyond the rate, which characteristics does a complete pulse assessment describe?
opciones: Symmetry between the two sides, rhythm, volume, amplitude and rate of rise
Rhythm, skin color at the site, capillary refill time and the limb temperature
Rhythm, the pressure needed to obliterate the beat and the width of the vessel
Rhythm, volume and the oxygen saturation read at the same finger during the count
preguntas.explicacion: Counting beats is only part of it. A full assessment covers rhythm, volume, amplitude, how fast the wave rises and whether the two sides match. Symmetry earns its place because unequal pulses can point to major vascular disease such as aortic dissection or coarctation of the aorta.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Appointment setup instructions · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: The clinician will need to look at a rash on the patient's shoulder by video. Which instruction does the setup guidance give her beforehand?
opciones: To wear loose clothing, so that she can show the part of the body in question
To sit with the window behind her, so that the strongest light falls on the camera
To hold the device in her hand and move it about as the clinician asks her to
To sit far enough back that her whole body stays inside the picture throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The advice on getting set up is to choose a spot with plenty of light and avoid sitting with the back towards a window, since that makes the face harder to see; to keep the camera steady and at eye level with head and shoulders in view; to wear loose clothing where the clinician needs to see skin or a particular part of the body; and to cut background noise and distractions.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Aging changes in vital signs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient on a diuretic gets dizzy when standing up quickly. What connects the two?
opciones: Blood pressure medicines, diuretics among them, are a common cause of the drop
Diuretics raise the pressure on standing, and the dizziness comes from that rise
Diuretics have no effect on posture, so another cause must explain the dizziness
Diuretics slow the pulse, and it is the slow rate that produces the dizziness
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling dizzy on standing up too quickly is the drop in pressure called orthostatic hypotension, and medicines are often behind it, above all the drugs used for blood pressure. Diuretics can lower pressure, most often when the patient changes position too fast. Digoxin and beta blockers are the ones that slow the pulse.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Dislocation", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.o · 2027 I.B.8.o · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's shoulder looks out of position after a fall. What should the assistant not do?
opciones: Move the joint to put the bone back into its socket
Apply a sling to the joint in the position it was found
Press the skin below the joint to check the circulation
Place ice wrapped in a clean cloth over the painful area
preguntas.explicacion: A dislocated joint is splinted or slung in the position in which it was found, and only a bone specialist puts it back. The joint is not moved and a misshapen bone is never straightened or tested for loss of function. Circulation below the injury is checked by pressing the skin, unless the skin is broken, and nothing is given by mouth.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5: Anatomic Sites
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(2) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which description of the subcutaneous injection sites is correct?
opciones: Outer upper arm, front of the thighs, upper back, upper gluteal area, abdomen
Ventrogluteal area, vastus lateralis and deltoid, chosen by age and body mass
Upper third of the forearm, outer upper arms, and the area between the scapulae
Deltoid alone, located three finger widths below the acromion process of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Subcutaneous doses go into the outer side of the upper arm, the front of the thighs, the upper back, the upper ventral gluteal area, and the abdomen between the costal margin and the iliac crest, staying more than two inches from the umbilicus. Each area is wide enough to rotate within it. Skin that is bruised, broken, scarred, over bone or poorly perfused is passed over.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: When is a competing style the appropriate way to handle a conflict?
opciones: In a real emergency, or to stop behavior that is unethical
When feelings need to cool or the stakes are trivial anyway
When the working relationship matters more than the issue
When two parties of equal power are short of time to decide
preguntas.explicacion: Competing is high on assertiveness and low on cooperativeness, and it fits genuine emergencies, decisions that are unpopular but necessary, and standing against unethical behavior. Making a habit of it damages psychological safety. The other three options are the situations that suit avoiding, accommodating and compromising.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Pulse Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's radial pulse is full on the right and barely detectable on the left. Why does the difference between sides matter by itself?
opciones: An uneven pulse can mark major vascular disease such as an aortic dissection
An uneven pulse is a normal variant found in roughly a tenth of all people
An uneven pulse only reflects which arm the patient uses for daily work
An uneven pulse appears whenever the rhythm is irregularly irregular
preguntas.explicacion: A full pulse assessment goes beyond the rate to the rhythm, the volume and the amplitude, how fast the wave rises, and whether the two sides match. Symmetry earns its place because an uneven pulse may point to a coarctation of the aorta, to occlusive disease of a large vessel, or to a dissection of the aorta. That is why both sides are compared rather than one side measured and charted.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Where can I get help; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Who Monitors; 45 CFR 164.530(d) and (g)
preguntas.subtema: Privacy complaints · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Where can a patient file a complaint about a violation of their health information privacy rights?
opciones: With the HHS Office for Civil Rights
With the state insurance oversight agency
With the hospital's patient advocate only
With the long-term care ombudsman office
preguntas.explicacion: The Office for Civil Rights, at the federal Department of Health and Human Services, takes complaints from people who believe their health information privacy rights were violated, or who were discriminated against in their medical care; it investigates, audits, and may pass criminal matters to the Department of Justice. Patient advocates, state health departments, insurance oversight agencies and long-term care ombudsman offices handle other kinds of problem. A covered entity must also run its own complaint process and may not retaliate against anyone who files.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Reporting by Other Persons; and Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect - State Statutes
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: A receptionist with no clinical role suspects a child in the waiting room is being abused. May she report it?
opciones: Yes: every jurisdiction permits any person to report a suspicion
Yes, but only in the 17 states where all persons must report
No: reports from staff outside clinical roles are not accepted
No: the report has to come from the child's treating clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Every state, every territory and the District of Columbia permits any person to report where there is reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected; such voluntary reporters are called permissive reporters. Roughly 17 states and Puerto Rico go further and require any person to report, and four of them list no professions at all.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, comorbidity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.A.2.b · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: One patient's chart lists hypertension, chronic kidney disease and diabetes at once. Which term names that situation?
opciones: Comorbidity, when two or more diseases run at once
Etiology, the set of causes behind two or more diseases
Prevalence, the count of people who have several diseases
Remission, the fading of the signs of several diseases
preguntas.explicacion: Comorbidity means carrying more than one disease at the same time, and it changes both the risk and the plan of care. A risk factor is something else again: anything that raises the chance of developing a disease, such as age, family history, tobacco use or exposure to radiation or certain chemicals.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.4 Electrodes Falling Off
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k152 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: An electrode will not stay on a patient with a very hairy chest. What is the recommended fix?
opciones: Part the hair before applying it, and tape it down if needed
Shave the whole chest and apply a second electrode on top
Move the electrode one space lower where there is less hair
Use extra gel so that the electrode floats above the hair
preguntas.explicacion: Parting the hair first gives the adhesive a surface to grip, and on extremely hairy chests the electrodes may have to be taped down. Moving an electrode off its landmark is never the answer: even a small displacement of a chest electrode can change the pattern considerably.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Irrigation", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B9 k76 · CMA I.C.2.b · NCMA 2B.17
preguntas.pregunta: How is the stream of water directed during an ear irrigation?
opciones: Superiorly and posteriorly in the canal, at low pressure, toward the eardrum
Inferiorly and anteriorly in the canal, at low pressure, away from the eardrum
Superiorly and posteriorly in the canal, at high pressure, to break the plug up
Straight along the axis of the canal, at high pressure, until the plug floats out
preguntas.explicacion: The catheter points up and back so the stream runs behind the wax and lifts it off the tympanic membrane, and it is aimed at the membrane rather than into the canal wall. Low pressure is what keeps it safe: force causes trauma, bleeding and pain. Lacerations, perforation and ossicular injury are the complications, rare as they are.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, sections First Aid and DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether the swollen bruise on the arm can be drained with a needle at home. What is the advice?
opciones: Do not drain it, and rest the bruised part rather than using it
Drain it only with a sterile lancet after cleaning the skin first
Drain it once the color has turned bluish, but not before that
Do not drain it, but keep exercising the arm to disperse the blood
preguntas.explicacion: The instructions are explicit: a bruise is not drained with a needle, the painful part is rested rather than worked, and pain and swelling are not ignored. What does help is ice wrapped in a clean towel and keeping the bruised area raised above heart level where that is possible.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.4
preguntas.subtema: Backup practice · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What backup arrangement does the contingency guidance describe for patient data?
opciones: A daily, complete, encrypted copy held off site and restored as a test regularly
A weekly complete copy kept on a second drive inside the same server cabinet
A monthly copy of the day's new entries stored with the software developer
A copy made each time the system is upgraded and kept until the next upgrade
