An uncooperative patient is the example the standard uses in (d)(3)(ix)(D)(4)(ii) for when a blood donation center must require gloves; splashes to the face trigger masks and eye protection under (d)(3)(x); and Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves under the CDC recommendations, not for head or shoe covering.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8: Draw samples in the correct order
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why the tubes cannot simply be filled in whatever order is convenient. What reason does the WHO give in Step 8 for a fixed order of draw?
opciones: It prevents the additive in one tube from being carried over into the next tube
It ensures the tubes that need a full draw are filled while the tourniquet is still on
It gives the serum tubes 10 to 15 minutes to clot before the last tube is filled
It minimizes platelet clumping, which is the reason given for the capillary sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 states the purpose in one line: draw the tubes in the right order so that additives are not carried across from one tube to the next. The clotting time of 10 to 15 minutes is a processing detail for red tubes, not a reason for the order; and platelet clumping is the reason Chapter 7 gives for the reversed skin-puncture order, not for venipuncture.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Federal plain language guidelines
preguntas.subtema: Plain language · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which federal statute requires that content written for the public be written for its specific audience?
opciones: The Plain Writing Act of 2010
The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016
The HITECH Act of 2009, part of ARRA
The Privacy Rule, published in 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Plain language means content that is clear and easy to grasp; the guidance presents it as more efficient and more effective, and as a legal duty besides. It was the Plain Writing Act of 2010 that laid down the requirement: whatever is written for the public has to be written for the particular audience it addresses. That is why pinning down the audience comes before drafting the letter or the handout.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrial Fibrillation", Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which strip is described as irregularly irregular?
opciones: One where the spacing between beats follows no pattern
One where the spacing changes in a repeating pattern
One where the spacing is even but the rate is above 100
One where the spacing is even but the QRS is over 120 ms
preguntas.explicacion: Sorting a strip into regular or irregular comes before naming anything. Even spacing is a regular rhythm whatever the rate or the width of the complexes; spacing that repeats a pattern is called regularly irregular, as in flutter; and spacing with no pattern at all is irregularly irregular, as in fibrillation.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(ii) and (h)(1)(iv), Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Employee medical record retention · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer keep the medical record it maintains for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus 30 years
For 3 years from the date of the last entry
For 6 years from the date of the last entry
For the duration of employment plus 5 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iv) requires the records of paragraph (h) to be kept at least for the length of employment plus 30 years, following 29 CFR 1910.1020. The record itself holds the employee's name, hepatitis B vaccination status and dates, results of examinations and follow-up, the employer's copy of the written opinion and the information sent to the healthcare professional. Three years is the retention of training records in (h)(2)(ii); six years is the HIPAA documentation period in 45 CFR 164.530(j), a different regulation.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: An excluded provider's period of exclusion has now run its course. What happens to her standing with the federal programs?
opciones: Reinstatement is not automatic; she has to apply for it once the period ends
Reinstatement is automatic on the day the stated period of exclusion runs out
Reinstatement follows as soon as a state Medicaid agency enrolls her once more
Reinstatement follows as soon as a practice checks the list and cannot find her
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusions program is explicit that an excluded individual or entity does not get reinstated automatically when the specified period runs out; an application has to be made. That is why the list gets checked month by month rather than counted forward: a period that has expired does not by itself put anyone back into the federal programs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Box Warning", Definition/Introduction and Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: What does a boxed warning on a prescription drug label mean?
opciones: It is the highest safety warning the FDA assigns, and it is not an absolute ban
It is the highest safety warning the FDA assigns, so the drug may never be used
It is a recall notice, added when a product may cause severe harm or even death
It is a summary of the adverse reactions reported most often after approval
preguntas.explicacion: A boxed warning, once called a black box warning, is the highest safety-related warning the FDA assigns, and it exists to put the drug's major risks in front of whoever reads the label. It usually covers a whole class, because the risk follows the mechanism of action. It is not an absolute contraindication: the prescriber weighs it case by case. More than 400 medicines carry one, and warnings are added, updated or withdrawn.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation (peripheral smear and pseudothrombocytopenia)
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k57 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC drawn in EDTA reports a very low platelet count, but the smear shows the platelets stuck together in clumps. What is this called, and what causes it?
opciones: Pseudothrombocytopenia, from in vitro platelet clumping caused by EDTA-dependent agglutinins
True thrombocytopenia, from platelet destruction that had already begun before the blood was drawn
Hemoconcentration, from a tourniquet left in place for more than one minute
Platelet satellitism, from the sodium fluoride in a gray tube drawn before the EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: Platelet clumping can occur when EDTA is the anticoagulant, producing pseudothrombocytopenia, a falsely low count due to in vitro aggregation from EDTA-dependent agglutinins. It is an artifact of the tube, not a disease of the patient. Platelet satellitism is a different smear finding, and hemoconcentration is the tourniquet effect described in the phlebotomy chapter.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypothyroidism", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(9) (2027 I.C.6.g(9)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which cause of hypothyroidism leads worldwide, and which leads in the United States?
opciones: Iodine deficiency worldwide; autoimmune thyroid disease in the US
Autoimmune thyroid disease worldwide; iodine deficiency in the US
Autoimmune thyroid disease worldwide; pituitary failure in the US
Pituitary failure worldwide; autoimmune thyroid disease in the US
preguntas.explicacion: In iodine-sufficient countries the leading cause is autoimmune thyroid disease, that is, Hashimoto thyroiditis, while in iodine-deficient regions it is a diet short of iodine. Both are primary hypothyroidism, where the gland itself fails. Secondary or central hypothyroidism, from the pituitary or hypothalamus, is much less common.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244); and CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.a(3), III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: A practice bills separately for services that belong in a single comprehensive code. What is that called?
opciones: Unbundling, which the correct coding edits are designed to detect and prevent
Upcoding, which reports a level of complexity higher than the care delivered
Balance billing, which charges the patient the amount above the allowed rate
Downgrading, which reports a level of service lower than the one documented
preguntas.explicacion: Splitting a service into its parts to bill them separately is unbundling, and the procedure-to-procedure edits exist to catch code pairs reported that way. Upcoding is the related abuse of billing a higher level of complexity than was provided or documented. Balance billing is charging the patient the difference between a charge and the allowed amount, which concerns the patient's bill rather than the codes chosen.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Breast self-exam — Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: When in the month should a menstruating patient do a breast self-exam?
opciones: About three to five days after her period starts, at the same time each month
About three to five days before her period starts, at the same time each month
On the first day of her period, when the tissue is at its most tender
Halfway between two periods, which is when the tissue is most nodular
preguntas.explicacion: Three to five days after the period begins the breasts are least tender and least lumpy, which makes changes easier to notice; the point is to repeat it on the same schedule every month. After menopause, the same day of each month is used instead. Experts do not agree on whether the practice finds cancers or saves lives.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Communication and Language Assistance
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A woman with limited English brings her teenage son to interpret for her visit. What should the assistant do?
opciones: Bring in a trained medical interpreter for the encounter
Let the son interpret, since the patient chose him herself
Have the son interpret the history but not the consent
Reschedule the visit until an adult relative can come along
preguntas.explicacion: Organizations are asked to ensure the competence of anyone providing language assistance and to avoid untrained people and minors as interpreters. A relative may edit or soften what is said, and a patient may hold back sensitive details in front of family. Interpreters may be on site, by video or by telephone.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote d
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is worried that tissue fluid from a difficult puncture could contaminate a coagulation specimen. What does the WHO table allow in that situation?
opciones: Collecting a non-additive tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the light blue tube first and then a second one for the test
Collecting a purple EDTA tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the citrate tube last, after all the additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 addresses this exact worry: if tissue fluid or thromboplastin could contaminate the specimen, a tube without additive can be drawn ahead of the additive tube. That keeps the sequence of the table intact, because the plain tube is position 2 and citrate is position 3. EDTA is far down the list at position 8, and citrate never moves to the end.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Table 20.2 Comparison of Arteries and Veins; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 k7 (applied D3 k61 palpation, k62) · PBT I.A.2 I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: While palpating for a venipuncture site you feel a vessel that pulses. Which set of features identifies an artery rather than a vein?
opciones: Thick wall, small rounded lumen, high pressure, no valves
Thin wall, large flattened lumen, low pressure, valves in the limbs
Thin wall, large lumen, high pressure, valves present in the limbs
Thick wall, small lumen, low pressure, valves present in the limbs
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries have thick walls, a rounded appearance, high pressure and no valves; veins have thin walls, irregular often collapsed lumens, low pressure and valves, mostly in the limbs and below the heart. The pulse itself is the expansion and recoil of an artery as blood is ejected from the heart, so a pulsing vessel is an artery.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Examples of Safety Device Designs
preguntas.subtema: Self-blunting needles · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does a self-blunting phlebotomy needle protect the person drawing the blood?
opciones: A blunt cannula inside it is pushed past the tip before the needle leaves the vein
A spring pulls the needle back into the tube holder once the vein has been entered
A hinged shield snaps over the tip as the tube is pushed onto the holder
A blunt cap is screwed onto the tip once the needle has left the vein
preguntas.explicacion: In a self-blunting phlebotomy or winged-steel needle, a blunt cannula sits inside the needle and is pushed past the tip while the needle is still in the vein, so what finally leaves the patient is no longer sharp. Retracting needles and hinged or sliding shields are separate designs on the same list, and each works at a different moment; the blunting one is the only one that acts while the needle is still in the vein.

preguntas.subtema: Security incident · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The firewall blocks a log-in attempt from outside the practice that never reached any record. Does the Security Rule count that as a security incident?
opciones: Yes, the definition takes in attempted as well as successful unauthorized access
No, an incident starts only once information has actually been reached or altered
No, unless the attempt is later shown to have exposed unsecured information
Yes, but only where the attempt interferes with how the information system runs
preguntas.explicacion: The wording is deliberately wide. It reaches unauthorized access, use, modification, disclosure or destruction of information whether the attempt succeeded or not, and it reaches interference with the way the system operates as well. Interference is one branch of the definition, not the whole of it, and the practice has to identify these events, respond to them, mitigate them and write them down.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?; Issues of Concern: Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: How much to tell a colleague · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a phlebotomist to place an IV line for a patient's chemotherapy. How much of the history should the request carry?
opciones: Only what the task needs; the reason for the therapy is not required
The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer
No history at all, since treatment details may not be shared
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are not restricted from talking to one another about treatment, and a patient's care would stall if they were. The caution is about how much: asking someone to place a line does not require telling them why the therapy was prescribed. That is the same minimum necessary thinking behind selective access to records, where a laboratory worker needs the laboratory record and not the whole medical history.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the light blue coagulation tube fall in relation to the serum tubes and the other additive tubes?
opciones: Ahead of all of them: before the clot activator, separator, heparin and EDTA tubes
After the serum tubes, but still ahead of the heparin and EDTA tubes
Last of all, because it is one of the tubes that requires a full draw
Immediately before the fluoride tube, since both of them require a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The numbered table gives the citrate tube position 3, the clot activator 4, the serum separator 5, the heparin tubes 6 and 7, EDTA 8, ACD 9 and the fluoride/oxalate tube 10. The four-group summary used in the coagulopathy review says the same thing in fewer words: sterile containers first, coagulation tubes next, plain and gel tubes after them, and the remaining additive tubes last. Both put the coagulation tube ahead of every serum and additive tube, and the full-draw requirement, which the citrate, EDTA and fluoride tubes share, says nothing about position.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Time Pressures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to sign for a procedure while already medicated in the holding area. Why is that criticised?
opciones: Consent should be a two-way talk with time to ask questions and reflect
Consent signed outside a clinic has to be witnessed by a second nurse
Consent is not valid unless the same clinician performs the procedure
Consent in writing takes the place of discussing risks and benefits
preguntas.explicacion: The improper methods singled out are these: discussing the procedure shortly before it happens; taking consent in the holding area just before surgery; and taking it while the patient is medicated or on the point of falling asleep. What is called for instead is a structured two-way dialogue in a clinic or an office, leaving the patient time to ask questions and to think.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications: Five Moments for Hand Hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Moments for hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has greeted the patient and is about to clean the skin for the puncture. Which moment for hand hygiene is that?
opciones: Before a clean or aseptic procedure
After contact with the patient nearby
After exposure to any body fluid
After leaving the patient's own room
preguntas.explicacion: There are five moments, two of them before and three of them after. The two before are touching a patient and beginning a clean or aseptic procedure; the three after cover body fluid exposure or glove removal, patient contact, and contact with the patient's immediate surroundings. Cleaning the skin for a puncture is the aseptic procedure itself, so hands are done again right before it and not only on arrival.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", sections Introduction and History (1973)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA E.1.d (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which organization created the first patient bill of rights, in 1973?
opciones: The American Hospital Association (AHA)
The American Medical Association (AMA)
The American Cancer Society (ACS)
The Joint Commission (TJC)
preguntas.explicacion: The American Hospital Association produced the first patient bill of rights in 1973, a document about relationships between patients, professionals and organizations that carried little enforceability. The American Cancer Society also produced one in the same decade, and the AMA did not publish a list of patient rights until 2017. Such bills remain non-enforceable.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Why would a 12-lead Holter be chosen over the usual two or three leads?
opciones: To establish where premature beats or a tachycardia are starting
To keep the recording running for a longer stretch of days
To let the patient shower while the device is still in place
To cut down the number of electrodes stuck on the chest wall
preguntas.explicacion: Two or three leads are enough when the goal is only to follow rate and rhythm. When the question is where premature beats, a dysrhythmia or a tachycardia originate, the 12-lead version is preferred, and it can name a long list of rhythms immediately.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 809
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187 · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027)
preguntas.pregunta: A collection agency contacts a patient about a medical debt. What must it send within five days of that first contact?
opciones: A written notice with the amount, the creditor, and the right to dispute
A written notice with the itemized services and the dates of each visit
A copy of the remittance advice showing what the health plan paid on it
A payment plan proposal that spreads the balance over the coming months
preguntas.explicacion: Within five days of the initial communication the debt collector must send written notice of the amount of the debt, the name of the creditor, and a statement that the debt will be assumed valid unless the consumer disputes it within 30 days, along with what happens if the consumer does dispute it or asks who the original creditor was. Itemized bills, remittance advices and payment plans are not part of that notice.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: false imprisonment
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: When is a person falsely imprisoned?
opciones: When they are confined in an area bounded in every direction, without consent
When they are asked to remain in a room until the paperwork has been finished
When they are told they may face a lawsuit if they leave the building early
When they are kept waiting far longer than the appointment time they were given
preguntas.explicacion: False imprisonment is intentionally restraining someone inside a bounded area without their consent or legal authority, and an area counts as bounded only if movement is blocked in every direction; a reasonable and safe way out means it is not. Restraint can come from a locked door, force, failure to release or misuse of authority. A threat of future legal trouble is not enough.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports extreme pressure and severe pain in a large bruised area of the forearm. Why does that need urgent care?
opciones: It may be compartment syndrome, which can threaten the limb and life
It may be a periosteal bruise, which heals only after several months
It may be thrombophlebitis, which resolves once the arm is elevated
It may be simple swelling, which settles with ice applied every hour
preguntas.explicacion: A feeling of extreme pressure in a bruised part, especially when the area is large or very painful, can mean compartment syndrome, in which rising pressure cuts the blood and oxygen supply to the tissues. It is described as life-threatening and needing emergency care, sometimes surgery.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ambulatory Electrocardiogram Monitoring", Equipment; and StatPearls, "Ambulatory ECG Monitoring" (NBK597374)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What does an external loop recorder do that a plain event recorder does not?
opciones: It records all the time, holding 30 days in a loop memory
It records all the time, holding 24 hours in a loop memory
It is implanted under the skin of the chest wall
It transmits every event to the office as it happens
preguntas.explicacion: The loop recorder monitors continuously and keeps a rolling 30 days in memory, so when the patient activates it the device stores a fixed stretch from before and after the press. It suits infrequent symptoms that do not involve fainting, since an unconscious patient cannot activate anything.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Preauthorization; and CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 3 (documentación, enmiendas y correcciones del registro)
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67, 6E · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: The plan approved the preauthorization for a scheduled procedure. What has the office actually obtained?
opciones: A decision that the service is medically necessary, with payment still not promised
A decision that the service is medically necessary, and a guarantee it will be paid
A decision that the patient has met the deductible for the plan year in question
A decision that the provider may bill the patient if the plan denies the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the plan's finding that a service, a treatment plan, a drug or an item of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary. The glossary is explicit that it is no promise the plan will cover the cost, since eligibility, benefits and coding still come into play when the claim is adjudicated. It says nothing about the deductible, and shifting liability to the patient is what an advance written notice of non-coverage does in Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Test!: Recording Results
preguntas.subtema: Recording qualitative results · CPT D5 k94 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D3 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant records a rapid strep result in the log as '+'. What does the record-keeping guidance say?
opciones: Qualitative results are recorded in words or abbreviations, such as 'Positive' or 'Pos', not as symbols
A '+' is acceptable as long as the cover page of the log has a key that explains what each symbol means
Symbols are preferred for qualitative results because they save space and they cannot be misspelled
Only the final result is recorded; a first result that was invalid is omitted so that the log stays clean
preguntas.explicacion: Results are recorded accurately and kept as a permanent record with enough detail to be retrieved. Quantitative results carry the units of measurement given in the manufacturer's instructions, and qualitative results are written as words or abbreviations rather than symbols: 'Positive' or 'Pos', 'Negative' or 'Neg', 'Reactive' or 'R', 'Non-reactive' or 'NR'. Invalid or unacceptable results are recorded too; the test is repeated and only the final acceptable result is reported.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP); MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Creatinine Test, What is it used for?; MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen)
preguntas.subtema: Kidney function tests · CMA I.C.10.c.(2) · RMA III.C.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which two results on a metabolic panel are the waste products used to assess kidney function?
opciones: BUN and creatinine
Albumin and total protein
ALT and AST enzymes
Sodium and potassium
preguntas.explicacion: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine are waste products that the kidneys filter from the blood and remove in urine, so higher-than-normal levels can mean the kidneys are not working well; both appear on the BMP and CMP and are often compared with each other to sort out the cause of a kidney problem. Creatinine is also used to calculate the estimated glomerular filtration rate. ALT, AST, albumin and total protein belong to the liver side of the panel.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), What is a comprehensive metabolic panel?; and Lab Tests: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP), What is a basic metabolic panel?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: An order is changed from a basic metabolic panel to a comprehensive one. Which measurements does the comprehensive panel add to the eight of the basic?
opciones: Albumin, total protein, ALP, ALT, AST and bilirubin
Phosphate, uric acid, lactate and blood ammonia
Cholesterol, triglycerides and the calcitonin level
Hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets and the white count
preguntas.explicacion: The basic panel reports eight substances: glucose, calcium, the four electrolytes, and the two waste products BUN and creatinine. The comprehensive panel reports fourteen, adding albumin and total protein, the enzymes ALP, ALT and AST, and bilirubin, which is what lets it speak for the liver as well as the kidneys. Lipids and blood counts are ordered as separate tests.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Hyperventilation", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.q · 2027 I.B.8.q · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who is overbreathing from anxiety is coached to breathe out slowly through pursed lips. What is the point?
opciones: To raise the carbon dioxide level in the blood, which ends the symptoms
To raise the oxygen level in the blood, which slows the pulse rate down
To lower the carbon dioxide level, which is what causes the tingling
To lower the oxygen demand of the muscles used in breathing hard
preguntas.explicacion: Overbreathing blows off carbon dioxide, and the low blood level of it produces most of the symptoms; the goal of treatment is therefore to raise that level again. Pursed-lip breathing, puckering the lips as if blowing out a candle and breathing out slowly, does it, and calm reassurance from someone nearby helps as much.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Audition and Equilibrium
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures of the inner ear are responsible for hearing and which for balance?
opciones: The cochlea for hearing and the vestibule for equilibrium
The vestibule for hearing and the cochlea for equilibrium
The ossicles for hearing and the tympanic membrane for equilibrium
The ear canal for hearing and the Eustachian tube for equilibrium
preguntas.explicacion: The external ear holds the auricle, the ear canal and the tympanic membrane; the middle ear holds the ossicles and connects to the pharynx through the Eustachian tube; the inner ear holds the cochlea, for audition, and the vestibule, for equilibrium. Head position is read by the utricle and saccule, and head movement by the semicircular canals.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.5
preguntas.subtema: Downtime registration · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient walks in while the record system is down. What does the contingency guidance expect the practice to have arranged?
opciones: Temporary record numbers to assign now and reconcile once the system returns
A paper chart opened under the patient's name and filed as a permanent record
A wait until the system returns, since a record cannot be opened without it
Registration in the read-only backup system, which accepts new patients too
preguntas.explicacion: Patient identification is one of the required practices for downtimes. There has to be a way to register a new patient while the system is unavailable, including assigning unique temporary record numbers, plus a process for reconciling those identifiers once the record system comes back. A read-only system, by definition, cannot take a new registration.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Endocervical culture (003754), How to Prepare for the Test and How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Endocervical culture preparation · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(e) 2027
preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient told in the 2 days before an endocervical culture?
opciones: No vaginal creams or medicines, no douching and no intercourse, and empty the bladder and bowel
No vaginal creams or medicines, no douching and no intercourse, and drink water to fill the bladder
No tub baths and no tampons, and take a dose of an antifungal cream the night before
No solid food after midnight, and empty the bladder and bowel just before the examination
preguntas.explicacion: For the 2 days ahead the patient avoids creams or medicines in the vagina, douching and intercourse, and she empties bladder and bowel before the examination. The provider then uses a speculum to see the cervix and swabs mucus and cells from the endocervix, the part at the opening of the uterus. Douching is discouraged in general because it can cause infection.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Chapter 1: introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g
preguntas.pregunta: How often does federal law require that the Dietary Guidelines for Americans be published?
opciones: At least every 5 years, jointly by USDA and HHS
At least every 5 years, by the FDA acting alone
At least every 10 years, jointly by USDA and HHS
At least every 2 years, jointly by CDC with USDA
preguntas.explicacion: The 1990 National Nutrition Monitoring and Related Research Act obliges the Departments of Agriculture and of Health and Human Services to publish the guidelines together no less than every five years, based on the weight of current scientific and medical evidence. The first edition came out in 1980.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(A), (F), (G) and (I), Labels
preguntas.subtema: Labeling exemptions · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which container is exempt from the biohazard labeling requirement of the standard?
opciones: A unit of blood labeled as to contents and released for transfusion
A refrigerator that stores specimens of blood awaiting testing
A sharps container that is only one-quarter full
A bag of regulated waste that is going to an off-site incinerator
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(F) lets a unit go unlabeled when its container already states what is inside and it has been released for transfusion, or for another clinical use; (g)(1)(i)(G) does the same for individual containers placed inside a labeled one, and (g)(1)(i)(I) for waste that has been decontaminated. Refrigerators holding blood and containers of regulated waste are named in (g)(1)(i)(A) as needing the label, and a sharps container carries a label or color coding from the moment it goes into service under (d)(4)(iii)(A)(1)(iv), whatever its fill level.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.5
preguntas.subtema: Corrections and late entries · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant realizes she charted a blood pressure in the wrong patient's record. How is the correction made?
opciones: The change is clearly and permanently marked, with its date and author identifiable
The wrong reading is erased or covered so that the record shows only accurate data
The entry is deleted from the system and re-entered under the correct patient name
The entry stays as it is, and a note about it goes into the practice incident log
preguntas.explicacion: CMS expects services to be documented when they are rendered, and accepts that entries sometimes have to be amended, corrected or added late. The date and the author of any amendment, correction or delayed entry must be identifiable, and the change or addendum must be clearly and permanently denoted. Reviewers examine such entries against the signature requirements of the same chapter.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Definition of Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why can the same chemical be listed both as a chemical sterilant and as a high-level disinfectant?
opciones: Because a long exposure lets it kill spores, while a short one leaves those spores behind
Because a stronger dilution kills spores, while the ready-to-use dilution never touches them
Because it is a sterilant on metal items and a high-level disinfectant on plastic ones
Because it is a sterilant when heated in a reprocessor and inert at ordinary room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Contact time is what moves the same germicide between the two labels. Left on an item for hours, a handful of disinfectants do kill spores, and at that point the label is chemical sterilant; keep the concentration but cut the exposure, twenty minutes for a two percent glutaraldehyde, and the same product kills everything except large numbers of spores.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Nasopharyngeal culture (003747), Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: NP culture targets · PBT V.C.2 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: Which organism is a nasopharyngeal culture specifically used to look for?
opciones: Bordetella pertussis, the cause of whooping cough
Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the cause of tuberculosis
Escherichia coli, the commonest cause of urinary infection
Streptococcus agalactiae, the group B strep of pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: The nasopharyngeal culture samples the secretions of the throat at its very top, behind the nose, and serves for Bordetella pertussis, Neisseria meningitidis, Staphylococcus aureus including the methicillin-resistant strain, and for viruses: SARS-CoV-2, now the commonest reason for the test, plus respiratory syncytial virus and influenza. Tuberculosis is looked for in sputum, group B strep in a vaginal-rectal swab.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Holter Monitor", Complications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what can go wrong while wearing the monitor for the next two days. What is the answer?
opciones: Irritation of the skin under the electrodes, and sores if they stay on
Bruising under the electrodes, and sores if the device is a heavy one
Burns under the electrodes, from the current the device sends inward
A faster heart rate, from the weight of the device against the chest
preguntas.explicacion: The recorder itself sits outside the body, in a sling or a pocket, so in theory there is nothing to go wrong. What does happen is at the skin: the surface electrodes irritate it and can ulcerate it if left in place, which is rare because they come off with the device.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guides
preguntas.subtema: Downtime resources · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The EHR will be down for a planned upgrade. Which resource is written specifically for that situation?
opciones: The Contingency Planning guide, on planned and unplanned EHR unavailability
The Patient Identification guide, on identifying patients reliably in the record
The Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up guide, on managing results electronically
The Clinician Communication guide, on messaging between care teams and patients
preguntas.explicacion: The 2025 SAFER guides come in eight titles across three groups, and each one names its own subject. Contingency Planning covers the safety practices tied to planned or unplanned EHR unavailability, meaning any time clinicians or other users cannot reach all or part of the system. The other three guides listed cover patient identification, test result follow-up and communication among clinicians and patients.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Desirable Characteristics of Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Activating the safety feature · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: When a safety feature has to be activated by the user rather than working on its own, how should that be done?
opciones: With one hand, and with the worker's hands staying behind the exposed tip
With both hands, so the shield is seated squarely over the used needle
After the needle is in the container, where the tip can hurt no one
By the coworker who receives the device, before the tube is removed
preguntas.explicacion: A passive feature, one that needs nothing from the user, is preferred. Where the user does have to activate it, the recommendation is a single-handed technique that keeps both hands behind the exposed sharp, and a feature the user can plainly see has engaged. Waiting until the device is inside the container defeats the purpose, since injuries also happen during disposal, and passing an unprotected device to another worker adds a second person to the risk.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 3F k62 k9 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices placed for venous access rule out a site for a routine draw?
opciones: A venous port, a central catheter or an intravenous catheter
A venous port only, since catheters can be drawn through safely
An intravenous catheter only, when fluids are actually running
A central catheter only, when the line was placed within a week
preguntas.explicacion: The contraindication is written broadly: any device used for venous access, and the three examples given are a venous port, a central catheter and an intravenous catheter. Blood taken from an existing peripheral access can be hemolyzed, contaminated, or diluted by fluid and medication.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part A covers; and Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether Medicare Part A will pay for her care at the small critical access hospital in her county. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: It pays for an inpatient stay there, as it does in any hospital
It pays for an outpatient visit there, but not for an admission
It pays for neither, since those hospitals bill only under Part B
It pays for both, since those hospitals bill only under Part A
preguntas.explicacion: Part A helps pay for inpatient care in hospitals, in critical access hospitals and in skilled nursing facilities, and it also helps with hospice care, some home health services, nursing home care and inpatient behavioral and mental health care. Outpatient care, office visits with providers and the equipment ordered at them sit under Part B instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cognitive Assessment", Cognitive Assessment Screens
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k46 · CMA I.A.5.h / 2027 I.A.5.f
preguntas.pregunta: Which cognitive screen pairs a three-item recall with a clock-drawing test?
opciones: The Mini-Cog, one of the quickest of the screens in common use
The MoCA, the most widely used and validated of the screens today
The MMSE, which has been studied since it appeared back in 1975
The SLUMS, first developed for use in the veteran population
preguntas.explicacion: The Mini-Cog is built from two short tasks: recalling three items, which tests memory, and drawing a clock, which draws on language, on visuospatial skill and on executive function. The MoCA takes about ten minutes and covers more domains than the MMSE with better sensitivity. None of these replaces a full diagnostic evaluation, and none is recommended for people without symptoms.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: respondeat superior (Exceptions: Independent Contractors)
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(3) · RMA I.C.3 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A practice uses an independent contractor for weekend coverage. Does respondeat superior reach the practice for that person's acts?
opciones: No: the doctrine covers employees and agents, not independent contractors
No: the doctrine covers only acts committed inside the employer's premises
Yes: the doctrine covers every clinician the practice pays to see patients
Yes: the doctrine covers any clinician working under the practice's name
preguntas.explicacion: The doctrine makes an employer or principal answer for whatever wrongful acts an employee or an agent commits inside the scope of that employment or agency, and the plaintiff usually sues both. It does not extend to independent contractors, and courts weigh factors such as how much control was agreed, who supplies the tools, how the person is paid and whether the work forms part of the regular business the principal runs.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A blood count report uses the word leukopenia. What does the ending of that term indicate?
opciones: A deficiency or lack of the cells named by the root
A blood condition involving the cells named by the root
An enlargement of the structure named by the root
An abnormal softening of the tissue named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -penia means a deficiency or lack, so leukopenia is too few white cells. The endings around it name other things: -emia is a blood condition, -megaly an enlargement, and -malacia a softening. Leukocytosis, with -osis for an abnormal condition, points the other way.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Clinical Note: Capillary versus Venous Glucose Measurements
preguntas.subtema: Capillary vs venous glucose · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii
preguntas.pregunta: One hour after lunch, a patient's fingerstick meter reads 205 mg/dL while a venous sample drawn at the same time gives 186 mg/dL in the laboratory. What does this pattern reflect?
opciones: Capillary values run slightly higher than venous ones after meals; discrepant results are confirmed by the laboratory venous test
The meter is out of calibration and must be taken out of service until two levels of liquid control material have been run and passed
The venous sample was falsely low because it was drawn from an arm that was receiving an intravenous glucose infusion at the time
Capillary values run lower than venous ones after meals, so the laboratory value should be reported instead of the meter
preguntas.explicacion: Capillary blood glucose and venous or arterial plasma differ by a clinically relevant margin: the capillary reading runs slightly higher after a meal. What comes off a capillary point-of-care test should not be casually mixed with laboratory venous values, and a discrepant capillary result is confirmed by venous testing in the laboratory, in hospital above all. A postprandial gap of that kind does not by itself mean the meter has failed.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Characteristics of Leukocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC report lists white cells at 7,000 per microliter. How do leukocytes differ from the other formed elements?
opciones: They are complete cells with a nucleus, some 5,000 to 10,000 per µL
They are anucleate biconcave discs, numbering about 5 million per µL
They are cell fragments only 2 to 4 µm across, made in the marrow
They are complete cells that never leave the vessels, unlike erythrocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Among the formed elements only the white cells are complete cells, with a nucleus and organelles, and there are far fewer of them than red cells, about 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter, so 7,000 is in range. Red cells stay inside the vessels, while white cells cross the wall to work in the tissues. The anucleate discs are the red cells, and the fragments 2 to 4 micrometers across are the platelets.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient waiting on a biopsy result says she is frightened, and the assistant answers “I am sure it will be fine.” What is the risk?
opciones: A severe rupture in the relationship if that outcome does not arrive
The patient reads it as a value judgment placed on her situation
The patient hears it as a piece of advice that she never asked for
The subject moves on abruptly and she is left feeling dismissed
preguntas.explicacion: False reassurance is listed among the pitfalls precisely because of what happens when the promised outcome does not come: the relationship can be severely and significantly damaged. The other three options are also named pitfalls, but they describe value judgments, unsolicited advice and an abrupt change of subject, not a promise about the future.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Audio-only telehealth · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a video visit has no working camera and asks whether the appointment is off. What do the categories of telehealth allow?
opciones: An audio-only call still counts as synchronous care when a video visit is not an option
An audio-only call counts as asynchronous care, since no picture is shared between them
The visit must be rebooked in person, because synchronous care requires live video
The visit must become a secure message exchange, which is the audio-only equivalent
preguntas.explicacion: Synchronous care means provider and patient interacting live, with a caregiver joining where that makes sense. The video call is the familiar shape of it, but audio-only calls are listed as synchronous as well, for occasions when a video visit is not possible, and so is secure text messaging used to answer a patient's questions.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Collecting Patient Payment
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77, 6D · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A patient paid after signing an advance written notice, appealed, and the appeal went her way. How soon does the refund have to reach her?
opciones: Within fifteen days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
Within thirty days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
Within sixty days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
Within ninety days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
preguntas.explicacion: Once the notice has been issued and signed, the provider may seek payment from the patient. If Medicare then pays all or part of the claim and the patient has also paid, the money goes back to her promptly: within thirty days of the remittance advice, or within fifteen days of an appeal determination where an appeal was filed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Apgar Score", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.c · RMA III.F.4.a.i · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: Which five components make up the Apgar score?
opciones: Heart rate, respiration, muscle tone, reflexes and color
Heart rate, temperature, muscle tone, reflexes and color
Blood pressure, respiration, muscle tone, reflexes and color
Heart rate, respiratory effort, weight, muscle tone and color
preguntas.explicacion: Each of the five is scored 0, 1 or 2 and the five are weighted evenly, so the total runs from 0 to 10. The score is meant to pick up signs of hemodynamic compromise: cyanosis, poor perfusion, bradycardia, low tone, depressed breathing or apnea. Temperature, weight and blood pressure are not part of it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.D.2.n
preguntas.pregunta: An enzymatic detergent has been used on a set of instruments. What has to happen next, and why?
opciones: The enzymes must be rinsed off, because residue left behind can provoke adverse reactions
The enzymes must be left to dry on, because their action continues while the item waits
The enzymes must be neutralized with a germicide, which finishes off any protein they missed
The enzymes must be reused on the next set, since the proteases stay active between loads
preguntas.explicacion: Enzymatic cleaners are not disinfectants. The proteases in them attack the protein that makes up much of common soil such as blood and pus, but like any chemical they have to be rinsed from the equipment or reactions such as fever and proteinaceous residue can follow. Germicides can inactivate the enzymes, so the two are not combined in one step.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Plasma Proteins
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is the most abundant and contributes most to the osmotic pressure of blood?
opciones: Albumin, about 54 percent of plasma protein
Fibrinogen, about 7 percent of plasma protein
Gamma globulin, the antibody fraction
Alpha globulin, which carries iron and lipids
preguntas.explicacion: There are three groups of plasma proteins. Albumin, made by the liver, is the largest share at about 54 percent (3.5 to 5.0 g/dL); it binds fatty acids and steroid hormones and is the main protein holding water inside the vessels, which helps keep blood volume and pressure. Globulins are second at about 38 percent, and the gamma fraction is the antibodies. Fibrinogen is about 7 percent and is needed for clotting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2B k16 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says angrily that the office lost her paperwork. Why should the reply not be defensive?
opciones: It leaves her room to voice the frustration and find a fix with you
It keeps the exchange from moving to another subject too abruptly
It stops her from reading approval or disapproval into the answer
It avoids handing her a piece of advice that she has not asked for
preguntas.explicacion: Responding defensively is named as a pitfall and is admitted to be a hard one to avoid. Holding back the defense gives the patient room to express the frustration and to work out a solution together with the provider rather than against them. Abrupt subject changes, approving responses and unsolicited advice are separate pitfalls with separate reasons.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, in situ
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A biopsy report reads carcinoma in situ. What do those last two words add?
opciones: The abnormal cells are still only where they first formed
The abnormal cells have reached one nearby lymph node only
The abnormal cells have already settled in a second organ
The abnormal cells are not cancer and will not spread at all
preguntas.explicacion: In situ means in its original place, so in a carcinoma in situ the abnormal cells are found only where they first formed and have not spread. That is a different statement from benign, which means the growth is not cancer, and from metastasis, where cells break away and start a new tumor somewhere else.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Recordkeeping: Sharps Injury Log; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i) and (h)(5)(iii)
preguntas.subtema: Keeping the sharps log · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA II.B.5.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How long is the sharps injury log kept, and what happens when someone asks for a copy of it?
opciones: At least five years after the end of the year it covers, with identifiers removed
Three years after the training it documents, with the trainer's name removed
Thirty years after the employee leaves, with the device brand taken out
Five years, and copies go only to the Assistant Secretary who asks for them
preguntas.explicacion: The standard sends the log's retention to 29 CFR 1904.33, and the model plan spells out what that comes to: five years at minimum, counted from the close of the calendar year the log covers. The model adds that any copy handed out has the personal identifiers stripped, which matches the demand in (h)(5)(i) that the record keep the injured worker's identity confidential. Three years is the training record; employment plus thirty years is the medical record.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Challenges of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Limits of the model · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic receives far more appointment requests every single day than its clinicians could ever see. What can open access do for it?
opciones: Nothing lasting, because no scheduling system works if demand always exceeds capacity
Solve it, because the model assumes the trouble is never a real shortage of capacity
Solve it, once the backlog has been worked down over six to eight weeks of longer days
Solve it, by going back to triaging the callers whose problems sound the most urgent
preguntas.explicacion: The model rests on the supposition that the problem is usually an imbalance between supply and demand rather than a shortage of capacity, and it can absorb excess demand on a given day. But the guide states the limit plainly: where demand is permanently greater than capacity, no scheduling system works. Clearing a backlog does not change that.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Immunization Information Systems (IIS): About
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(2)
preguntas.pregunta: What is an immunization information system?
opciones: A confidential computerized database of doses given in a geographic area
A confidential paper file of doses given, held by each individual provider
A national registry of adverse events reported after a vaccine was given
A federal list of the vaccines each state requires before a child enrolls
preguntas.explicacion: An immunization information system is a confidential, population-based computerized database holding every dose that participating providers give to people who live in a given geopolitical area. At the point of care it shows a consolidated history so the provider sees what is due; at the population level it feeds aggregate data to surveillance. Each system must have a written privacy policy.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Blood Plasma and Plasma Proteins
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What proportion of blood plasma is water?
opciones: About 92 percent
About 55 percent
About 45 percent
About 7 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma is about 92 percent water. Nearly all the rest, about 7 percent, is protein, and the electrolytes, gases, nutrients and wastes together add up to roughly 1 percent. The other figures belong to different measures: about 45 percent of whole blood is red cells (the hematocrit), and plasma is a little over half of whole blood, which is where a 55 percent figure comes from.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Physical Facilities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What relative humidity is set for the working areas of a central processing department and for the sterile storage area?
opciones: 30 to 60 percent in the work areas, and not above 70 percent in sterile storage
30 to 60 percent in the work areas, and not above 45 percent in sterile storage
50 to 75 percent in the work areas, and not above 60 percent in sterile storage
20 to 40 percent in the work areas, and not above 70 percent in sterile storage
preguntas.explicacion: Central processing is laid out in at least three zones: one for decontamination, one for packaging, and one where sterilization and storage happen. The environment is controlled: relative humidity of 30 to 60 percent in every work area, with sterile storage allowed to run higher but never above 70 percent, and a storage temperature that may go as high as 75 °F.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure; Limitations of Vital Sign Measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: An office has used the same automated blood pressure monitor daily for three years and has never had it serviced. What does accurate measurement require of the device?
opciones: That it be validated for use and calibrated again at intervals
That it be retired for a mercury column, the only exact gauge
That it be checked only when a reading looks wrong to the operator
That it be calibrated once, on the day it is first put into service
preguntas.explicacion: Accuracy is not technique alone; it is equipment too. An oscillometric monitor has to be validated as appropriate for use, and it has to be recalibrated from time to time, with the organization keeping up routine maintenance alongside standardized protocols and competency assessment. A device left to drift adds a systematic error that careful positioning cannot undo.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Arrhythmia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is sinus arrhythmia?
opciones: Variation in rate, with the R-R interval changing over 0.12 s
Variation in rate, with the R-R interval changing under 0.04 s
A run of early beats from a focus outside the sinus node
A rate that climbs above 100 and then falls back below 60
preguntas.explicacion: It is a variation of ordinary sinus rhythm: the spacing between beats shifts by more than 0.12 seconds while the P waves keep one shape and the pattern of activation from the sinus node. Vagus nerve activity during breathing produces it, and its presence usually points to good cardiovascular health.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section Causes
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 3C k69 k74 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which medicines make a patient more likely to bruise at a puncture site?
opciones: Aspirin, warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran or clopidogrel
Aspirin, insulin, metformin, levothyroxine, warfarin or amoxicillin
Warfarin only, since the other blood thinners act on platelets alone
Clopidogrel only, since aspirin is taken at too low a dose to matter
preguntas.explicacion: Patients taking a blood thinner are described as likely to bruise more easily, and the drugs listed are aspirin, warfarin, dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and clopidogrel. It is a fair thing to ask about before a draw, since firm pressure afterwards matters more in those patients.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 5. Cleaning and Disinfecting Environmental Surfaces in Healthcare Facilities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A chlorine solution is not made up fresh each day. How long may it be kept, and what happens to it?
opciones: Up to 30 days in a capped opaque bottle, losing about half its chlorine over that month
Up to 30 days in a capped clear bottle, losing about a tenth of its chlorine over that month
Up to 7 days in a capped opaque bottle, after which the free chlorine is entirely gone
Up to 90 days at room temperature, because the hypochlorite ion is stable once diluted
preguntas.explicacion: Diluted chlorine can be held at room temperature for as long as 30 days in a capped, opaque plastic bottle, but the concentration falls by about half over that time: a solution at roughly 1,000 ppm on day zero is down near 500 ppm by day 30. That decay is why the guideline treats daily fresh preparation as the reference practice.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.14
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A subcategory is titled tuberculosis of bones and joints. How does the coder read the word and in that title?
opciones: As either and or or, so bones alone, joints alone or both all belong there
As and alone, so both sites have to be documented before the code may be used
As or alone, so the code may not be used when both sites are documented
As a nonessential modifier, so the whole phrase may be present or absent
preguntas.explicacion: The word and in a title is read as meaning either and or or. The guidelines use this very subcategory as their example: tuberculosis of the bones alone, of the joints alone, and of bones and joints together all classify to it. Nonessential modifiers are a different convention, the terms sitting inside parentheses.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which move belongs to the list for quieting muscle tremor?
opciones: Moving or taking away the pillow under the patient's head
Raising the head of the table until the patient half sits up
Adding a second pillow so the neck is bent further forward
Turning the patient onto the left side until the tremor stops
preguntas.explicacion: The list starts with reassuring and relaxing the patient and goes on with repositioning or removing the pillow under the head, laying the hands on the stomach or tucking them under the buttocks, raising the knees on a pillow, and moving the limb electrodes up.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.1
preguntas.subtema: Monitoring response time · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The guidance asks a practice to monitor how quickly the record system answers on important clinical tasks. What figure does it give as the optimum?
opciones: Under two seconds
Under five seconds
Under ten seconds
Under thirty seconds
preguntas.explicacion: A monitoring and auditing strategy is expected to cover downtime events, access to patient information and system response time for tasks such as reviewing results, entering orders and looking a patient up, with under two seconds named as the optimum. A log of all downtime testing is kept, and leadership watches the unplanned outages.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Safely Using Sharps (Needles and Syringes) at Home, at Work and on Travel; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Exposure response · CPT D1 1H k33 · D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A worker is stuck by another person's used needle. What are the first two actions?
opciones: Wash the area with soap and water or antiseptic, then seek medical care
Squeeze the wound to bleed it, then report the incident at end of shift
Cover the wound with a dressing, then wait for the source result to arrive
Apply an alcohol swab for thirty seconds, then finish the current draw
preguntas.explicacion: The exposed area is washed straight away with water and soap, or cleaned with a skin antiseptic, rubbing alcohol or hand sanitizer, and medical attention is sought at once. The same instructions apply to blood reaching the eyes, nose, mouth or skin, and prophylaxis is not delayed.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient waiting for the ambulance with signs of shock asks for a glass of water. What is the correct answer?
opciones: Nothing is given by mouth, not food and not fluids, while shock is suspected
Small sips of water are allowed as long as the patient can sit up alone
Water is allowed but food is not, since the stomach must stay empty
A sugary drink is offered, which raises the pressure while help is coming
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing is given by mouth to a patient in shock, neither food nor drink. The assistant calls for emergency help, checks airway, breathing and circulation, rechecks the breathing rate at least every 5 minutes, and keeps the patient warm. If the patient vomits or drools, the head is turned to one side to prevent choking.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (Pink Book), ch. 4: Vaccine Information Statements
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(3)
preguntas.pregunta: When must a Vaccine Information Statement be given to the patient or parent?
opciones: Before each dose of the vaccine, and the fact that it was given is documented
Before the first dose of a series only, with the fact of it documented once
After each dose, together with the personal immunization record card given out
Only when the patient or parent asks for the benefits and risks in writing
preguntas.explicacion: The National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act requires the vaccine provider to hand the appropriate statement to the patient, or to the parent, guardian or legal representative, before every dose, and to document having done it. The CDC produces the statements to explain a vaccine's benefits and risks, and translations into other languages exist. Any refusal of a vaccine is documented too.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 5.2 Review, Observations, and Replication
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k149 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: On an acceptable tracing, what does an upright P wave and QRS complex in lead I tell the technician?
opciones: That the limb electrodes were applied the way they should be
That the chest electrodes were applied the way they should be
That the paper speed was set the way the standard asks for
That the calibration mark came out the height it should be
preguntas.explicacion: The standards ask that both the P wave and, except in rare cases, the QRS complex point upward in lead I, and that is read as a sign that the limb electrodes went on correctly. The opposite picture, everything inverted in lead I, points to swapped arm wires.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k199 k202 · CMA F.1.g / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Staff say there is no time to answer a frightened patient's worry. What did an observational study find?
opciones: Empathic responses lengthened the consultation by about 21 seconds
Empathic responses lengthened the consultation by about 21 minutes
Empathic responses shortened the consultation by roughly one third
Empathic responses made no measurable difference to the anxiety
preguntas.explicacion: The worry that there is no time to address emotional concerns is not what the literature shows. Studies of physicians found only a marginal change in the length of a consultation when an empathic response was given, and better communication skills were not associated with longer consultations. One observational study put the average increase at 21 seconds.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practices for Domain 2
preguntas.subtema: Downtime communication · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Why must the communication strategy for an EHR downtime not run on the EHR's own computing infrastructure?
opciones: Because it has to keep working when that infrastructure is the thing that has failed
Because messages about a downtime are protected health information under the rule
Because staff are trained on ransomware prevention through a separate channel entirely
Because the vendor rather than the practice owns the messaging tools inside the system
preguntas.explicacion: Among the recommended practices for using health IT safely, the guide wants the strategy for communicating during downtime and recovery to run on something other than the computing infrastructure that keeps the EHR up. Related practices cover training and testing staff on downtime and recovery procedures, written policies that keep patient care and critical business operations going, and an orderly restart of data exchange across the interfaces.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", HIPAA and Communication With Patients, Contents and Authorizations; StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Relative disclosure
preguntas.subtema: Family and caregivers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: May a phlebotomist tell a patient's spouse, who is present and involved in the patient's care, about the draw and the follow-up?
opciones: Yes, if the patient is informed and does not object; ask when others are present
No; disclosure to any family member requires a signed written authorization
Yes, and the same applies to any relative who telephones the clinic asking about results
No, unless the spouse holds a medical power of attorney on file at the clinic
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets information reach a spouse, a parent, a guardian or another caregiver who takes part in looking after the patient, and no formal agreement is needed for it. The practical move is to ask the patient whether they mind before discussing something specific with others in the room. Patients may also put limits on that sharing, for instance asking that no relative collect medications or be told about their condition. A relative on the telephone is a different case: a hospital may not disclose over the phone to a caller who says they are family.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Closed systems
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the WHO recommend closed vacuum-tube systems over open needle-and-syringe collection?
opciones: They reduce direct exposure to blood and ease multiple samples from one puncture
They are the cheapest devices and need no special training to use
They give better precision on small or difficult veins than any other collection device
They can be heparinized and used for arterial as well as venous sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 3 says closed systems have proven safer than open systems, and that vacuum extraction systems reduce the risk of direct exposure to blood and make several samples from one venepuncture easier to take, though they require training and skill. The other three statements are advantages that Table C.1 gives to the hypodermic syringe (cheap, no special training, heparinized for arterial blood) and to the winged needle (precision on small veins).

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Defects
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.1 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn is cyanotic, a 'blue baby'. Which congenital defect is the most common cause of cyanosis after birth?
opciones: Tetralogy of Fallot
Patent foramen ovale
Aortic coarctation
Patent ductus arteriosus
preguntas.explicacion: Tetralogy of Fallot pairs an opening in the interventricular septum with a blocked pulmonary trunk, so blood low in oxygen crosses from the right ventricle and mixes on the left; of the heart defects it is the one that most often turns a newborn blue. A patent foramen ovale is an opening between the atria, coarctation a narrowed aorta, and a patent ductus arteriosus a fetal vessel left open.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa", section Structure and Function (venous types)
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Four patterns are described for the superficial veins at the elbow. Which of them is the most common?
opciones: Type II, in which the median cubital vein joins the cephalic and basilic veins (the M pattern)
Type I, in which a dominant median antebrachial vein joins both veins (the N pattern)
Type III, in which the brachial cephalic vein is poorly developed or missing
Type IV, in which there is no communicating branch between cephalic and basilic
preguntas.explicacion: Type II, with the cephalic and the basilic joined by the median cubital vein, also called type M, is the most common pattern, followed by type I, the N type with a dominant median antebrachial vein. It adds that because of this variation, bruising, hematoma and sensory changes from mispuncture have been reported across health systems.
