opciones: About 642 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 9,000 kcal
About 642 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 4,500 kcal
About 320 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 4,500 kcal
About 1,280 kcal a day, since a kilogram of fat holds 9,000 kcal
preguntas.explicacion: A kilogram of fat stores 9,000 kcal, so half a kilogram means a net deficit of 4,500 kcal over the week, about 642 kcal a day. That deficit is built by eating less and moving more. For someone eating 2,600 kcal it means cutting a quarter of the day's intake if activity does not rise.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease", Introduction and Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(6) (2027 I.C.6.g(6)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports heartburn and regurgitation after meals. Which structure normally prevents that, and what is the diagnosis?
opciones: The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is peptic ulcer disease
The pyloric sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The upper esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: The usual complaints in gastroesophageal reflux disease are heartburn, regurgitation, and chest pain that is not cardiac; with symptoms as typical as those the diagnosis can be made presumptively. What normally holds the contents down is the lower esophageal sphincter, a physiological sphincter three to five centimeters long whose high resting tone keeps stomach contents out of the esophagus.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Specimen preparation · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A test must be run on plasma. Which tubes will supply it?
opciones: The heparin tubes, the EDTA tube and the citrate tube
The clot activator tube and the serum separator tube alone
The clot activator tube, the citrate tube and the EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma comes from tubes whose additive stops the blood from clotting: heparin in the green tubes, EDTA in the purple tube and citrate in the light blue tube, which is why coagulation testing uses plasma. The red clot activator tube and the gold separator tube are the ones that yield serum.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Never use unacceptable language access services; and Finance language access services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A bilingual receptionist offers to interpret the pre-draw questions. Why are staff untrained as healthcare interpreters ruled out?
opciones: Research shows untrained people make more clinically significant mistakes
Their interpreting time cannot be reimbursed by any state Medicaid program
They cannot be listed in the practice directory of bilingual clinicians
They are barred from signing the practice's interpreter ethics statement
preguntas.explicacion: The unacceptable services include a clinician or a staff member whose command of both languages falls short, and anyone not trained or certified as a healthcare interpreter, because research shows that people untrained in interpreting make more clinically significant mistakes. Medicaid reimbursement for interpreters is in fact available in a number of states.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 9.5 Types of Body Movements, Dorsiflexion and Plantar Flexion
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A therapist asks the patient to lift the top of the foot toward the leg. Which movement is that, and at which joint?
opciones: Dorsiflexion, at the ankle joint
Plantar flexion, at the ankle joint
Inversion, at the intertarsal joints
Eversion, at the intertarsal joints
preguntas.explicacion: Lifting the front of the foot so the top comes toward the leg is dorsiflexion; lifting the heel and pointing the toes is plantar flexion. Those two are the only movements the ankle joint allows. Turning the sole toward the midline is inversion and away from it is eversion, and both happen between the tarsal bones instead.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient's inpatient stay runs to sixty-eight days. What does she pay for days sixty-one to sixty-eight in 2026?
opciones: $434 for each of those days, on top of the deductible she has already paid
$868 for each of those days, which is the rate that starts at day ninety-one
$217 for each of those days, which is the rate for a skilled nursing stay
No charge for those days, because the deductible already covers the whole stay
preguntas.explicacion: Under Part A in 2026 an inpatient stay costs nothing for days one to sixty once the deductible is paid, then $434 a day for days sixty-one to ninety, then $868 a day for days ninety-one to a hundred and fifty while the sixty lifetime reserve days last. After day a hundred and fifty the patient pays everything.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Termination notice · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: How is a written termination notice sent, and what does the practice keep afterwards?
opciones: By certified mail, return receipt requested, keeping the receipt and a copy in the chart
By First-Class Mail, keeping a note of the date the envelope went to the post office
By a portal message, which is now the preferred way of sending these notices
By telephone, with the caller writing the date care ends into the progress note
preguntas.explicacion: Termination notices always go out in writing, and many states demand certified mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the latest address the file holds; the receipt and a copy of the letter then live in the medical record. At least one state now blesses HIPAA-compliant portal messages that report back whether the message has been viewed, and that route may take over, but for now the preferred means is still certified mail.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.3, Table 18.2, and ch. 18.6
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.c(1) · RMA III.G.2.e · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: How much medication may be given in a single intramuscular injection?
opciones: 0.5 to 1 mL in infants and children, and 2 to 5 mL in adults
Up to 1 mL in adults, and up to 0.5 mL in infants and children
0.1 mL at any age, the same volume used for a tuberculin test
Up to 3 mL at any age, at any of the recommended muscle sites
preguntas.explicacion: The volume for an intramuscular injection is 0.5 to 1 mL in infants and children and 2 to 5 mL in adults. Within that range the site still matters: the maximum for one injection at the vastus lateralis in an adult is 3 mL, and the deltoid generally takes about 1 mL. Up to 1 mL for adults with 0.5 mL for children is the subcutaneous rule, and 0.1 mL is the intradermal one.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014); and StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Specific Gravity)
preguntas.subtema: Refrigeration and crystals · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c.(1)
preguntas.pregunta: Which urine examination is disturbed when the specimen is refrigerated before it is examined?
opciones: Crystal identification, because cold precipitates phosphates and urates in the sediment
Leukocyte esterase, because cold destroys the enzyme within 1 hour of refrigeration
Bacterial culture, because cold stops growth so the colony count becomes falsely low
Specific gravity, because cold urine reads falsely high on the refractometer
preguntas.explicacion: Refrigeration is the preferred way to hold urine, but it makes phosphates and urates precipitate, which can confuse the analysis of those analytes; when crystal differentiation is requested a separate aliquot is kept unrefrigerated. Refrigeration preserves, rather than lowers, the colony count for culture, and the documented false elevations of specific gravity are from dextran, intravenous contrast and proteinuria, not cold.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 9: Physical and Chemical Properties
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 9 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which information belongs to section 9 of a safety data sheet, Physical and Chemical Properties?
opciones: Appearance, odor, pH, flash point, boiling range and vapor pressure
Signal word, pictograms, hazard statements and the classification
Permissible exposure limits, ventilation advice and glove material
Symptoms of exposure, the LD50 figure and any carcinogen listing
preguntas.explicacion: Section 9 is the list of measurable properties: appearance and physical state, odor and odor threshold, pH, melting and freezing point, initial boiling point and range, flash point, evaporation rate, flammability, upper and lower flammability limits, vapor pressure and density, relative density, solubility, partition coefficient, auto-ignition and decomposition temperatures, and viscosity. When an item is not relevant or not available, the sheet has to say so rather than leave a blank.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)
preguntas.pregunta: A telephone interpreter was used for a visit. What has to be entered in the progress note?
opciones: The name of the medical interpreter who took part in the visit
The account number of the language line that handled the call
The consent the patient gave before the interpreter was called
The reason a family member was not used to interpret instead
preguntas.explicacion: One of the guidelines for medical interpreters is that the interpreter's name goes into the progress note. Interpreters may be on site or reached by video or telephone. Nothing in the guidance calls for recording an account number, a separate consent or a justification for not using a relative.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(7) (2027 I.C.6.g(7)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A woman reports urinary frequency, urgency, burning on urination and suprapubic discomfort. Which organism most often causes this?
opciones: Escherichia coli, responsible for the majority of these infections
Klebsiella species, responsible for the majority of these infections
Staphylococcus aureus, responsible for the majority of these infections
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, responsible for the majority of these infections
preguntas.explicacion: Dysuria, urgency, frequency and discomfort above the pubic bone are the typical symptoms of an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, and Escherichia coli causes most of them, with Klebsiella next and Proteus, Enterobacter and Enterococcus behind. Bacteria without symptoms are not a urinary tract infection.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Rights & protections under the health care law
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.a (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a costly chronic illness fears her plan will stop paying once she reaches a yearly ceiling. What does the health care law say?
opciones: Yearly and lifetime dollar caps on essential benefits are over
Yearly caps are over, and each state sets the lifetime ones
Caps are allowed once she goes outside her plan's own network
Caps stay in force until her plan renews at the end of the year
preguntas.explicacion: Among the protections of the health care law is the end of lifetime and yearly dollar limits on the coverage of essential health benefits. The same law bars insurers from refusing to cover a pre-existing condition or charging more for it, and gives the member the right to appeal a plan decision. Grandfathered plans may fall outside some of this.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, duration; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique
preguntas.subtema: Duration of hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How long should an alcohol hand rub take, and how long should hands be rubbed with soap and water, according to the CDC?
opciones: About 20 seconds for the rub; at least 15 seconds of rubbing for the wash
About 2 to 6 minutes for the rub; at least 20 seconds for the wash
About 10 seconds for the rub; at least 60 seconds for the wash
About 30 seconds for the rub; at least 30 seconds for the wash
preguntas.explicacion: Rubbing sanitizer over every surface of the hands until they dry takes around 20 seconds; with soap and water the hands are scrubbed briskly against each other for 15 seconds at the least. Either duration is acceptable. StatPearls gives the same numbers: 3 to 5 mL of rub for some 20 seconds, and a wash of at least 15 to 20 seconds covering palms, backs, wrists, between the fingers, the thumbs and under the nails. Two to six minutes is a surgical scrub, not routine hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: negligence (Proximate Cause); and Wex: proximate cause
preguntas.subtema: Negligence · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(1) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What separates proximate cause from cause-in-fact in a negligence claim?
opciones: Proximate cause asks whether the harm was a foreseeable consequence
Proximate cause asks whether the defendant intended the harm to happen
Proximate cause asks whether the plaintiff suffered any monetary loss
Proximate cause asks whether a statute was broken before the harm began
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence needs both a factual link and a legal one. Proximate cause is the test the law adds on top: it usually turns on foreseeability, so throwing a rock off a balcony without looking is the proximate cause of the injury below because the harm was foreseeable. Conduct by the plaintiff or an intervening third party can break that link.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Interest and Benefit Activities
preguntas.subtema: Public interest disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Public interest and benefit activities let a covered entity release information without authorization. How many such purposes does the rule list?
opciones: Twelve national priority purposes, each with its own conditions and limitations
Six national priority purposes, all of them limited to law enforcement requests
Four national priority purposes, all of them requiring a court order beforehand
Eighteen national priority purposes, one for each identifier the rule names
preguntas.explicacion: OCR groups the disclosures that need no authorization or permission into twelve national priority purposes, each with specific conditions: required by law, public health activities, victims of abuse or neglect, health oversight, judicial and administrative proceedings, law enforcement, decedents, organ donation, research, serious threat to health or safety, essential government functions, and workers' compensation. The six-circumstance list belongs to law enforcement alone.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(e), Standard: Restraint or seclusion, paragraphs (e)(2)-(e)(9) and (e)(12)
preguntas.subtema: Restraint orders · CPT D1 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about restraint or seclusion orders is correct under the CMS patient-rights condition?
opciones: They may never be written as standing or as-needed (PRN) orders
They may be written PRN for patients with a history of falls
They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to secure the patient's immediate physical safety, or that of staff or of others, never as coercion, as discipline, for the convenience of staff or as payback, and only once less restrictive measures have failed, on the order of a physician or another licensed practitioner responsible for that patient. Such an order is never written as a standing order, nor on a PRN basis. For violent behavior each order runs at most 4 hours for adults, 2 hours from ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, to a total of 24 hours, with a face-to-face evaluation inside 1 hour, and the intervention stops as soon as it can.

preguntas.fuente: 21 CFR 878.4800(a); and 21 CFR 886.4350, manual ophthalmic surgical instrument
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.a · CMA I.C.5.a (2027 I.C.5.a)
preguntas.pregunta: An ophthalmic forceps and a plain surgical forceps are both nonpowered hand instruments, yet the FDA lists them under different regulations. Why?
opciones: An instrument whose use belongs to one specialty is listed with that specialty
Only an instrument that enters sterile tissue gets a listing of its very own
An instrument used on the eye carries a higher class, so it is listed apart
Reusable instruments are listed by specialty and single-use ones by general use
preguntas.explicacion: The general listing covers nonpowered hand instruments meant for various general surgical procedures, and it states that any instrument with a specialized use in one medical specialty goes instead into that specialty's own regulation. Eye instruments have their own section for that reason. The split does not turn on class, on sterile tissue, or on whether the item is thrown away after one use.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Worker's compensation
preguntas.subtema: Workers' compensation · CMAA 5 k72 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.f / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is workers' compensation insurance?
opciones: Coverage employers must carry for workers who get sick or hurt on the job
Coverage employers may buy to replace the group health plan for their workers
Coverage the state buys for workers whose employer offers no health plan
Coverage that pays the deductible of the group plan after a workplace injury
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation is the insurance an employer is obliged to carry for employees who fall ill or are injured because of their work. It does not stand in for the group health plan, is not bought by the state for uninsured workers, and does not merely pay a deductible: for care related to the job injury it is the payer, which is why those claims go to it first.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Deductible; and Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has met $400 of her $1,000 deductible. Today's visit is allowed at $250 and her coinsurance is 20%. What does she owe today?
opciones: $250, since the whole allowed amount still goes to the deductible
$50, which is twenty percent of the amount the plan allows
$350, which is what is left on the deductible after today
$300, the amount of the visit plus her twenty percent share
preguntas.explicacion: A plan begins to pay only after the deductible has been met, so with $600 still outstanding the whole $250 allowed for the visit is applied to the deductible and the patient pays it. Coinsurance is her percentage share of the allowed amount, and it starts to apply on the services that come after the deductible is satisfied.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L 2N k48 k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 k128 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports that he fainted during his last two blood draws. What is the correct preparation?
opciones: Have him lie down if possible, reassure him, and be ready for a syncope
Draw quickly while he stands, so that he can walk the dizziness off afterwards
Ask him to watch the needle closely so that he stays alert throughout
Postpone the draw until he returns with a signed consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Patients who fear blood tests or have a history of vasovagal attacks during earlier draws are identified specifically so the team is prepared to act on a syncope; with a severe history of panic the patient may be asked to lie down, and the WHO step 2 asks about previous fainting and tells the phlebotomist to reassure an anxious patient. Supine positioning is the WHO default where possible.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Bacterial Pneumonia", Introduction and Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(5) (2027 I.C.6.g(5)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: How is bacterial pneumonia most widely classified?
opciones: As community-acquired, hospital-acquired or atypical, then by severity
As viral, bacterial or fungal, then by the lobe of the lung involved
As acute or chronic, then by whether the patient has ever smoked
As upper or lower tract disease, then by the age of the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Pneumonia is most often sorted by where it was acquired, in the community or in hospital, with atypical pneumonia as the third box, and each is then stratified by severity. Typical pneumonia is the one whose organisms are Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus and Haemophilus influenzae. Where the infection was picked up shapes which organism is likely and what is given for it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Variability of Vital Signs in Older Adults
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An 80-year-old with a serious infection has a pulse of 76 beats per minute. Why does that not rule out the infection?
opciones: The rise in rate is blunted in older adults, so tachycardia may never appear
The rate in older adults is read against a resting band that starts at 50 per minute
The rate falls rather than rises during infection once a patient passes 75 years
The rate is unreliable at the wrist in older adults and only counts at the carotid
preguntas.explicacion: Older adults often show a blunted rise in heart rate under stress because the response to adrenergic drive is reduced, and drugs such as beta blockers and some calcium channel blockers flatten it further. Tachycardia can therefore be missing in serious infection or blood loss, so a normal-looking rate is not reassurance on its own.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.4 Electrodes Falling Off
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: The electrodes on a patient with loose skin keep pulling off. Why is a towel laid over the wires?
opciones: So their weight does not tug at the electrodes
So the patient stays warm and does not shiver
So the wires do not pick up current from the room
So the chest marks are not rubbed off the skin
preguntas.explicacion: Loose skin and hairy chests make electrodes hard to keep on, and the hanging weight of the wire pulls at the tab. A towel over the wires takes that pull away; a twisted wire does the same thing, so the electrode may have to be reset with its tab angled toward the cable box.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet depth · PBT II.J lancets · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.5 equipment by age · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: What is the maximum puncture depth for a heel-prick?
opciones: 2.4 mm
1.5 mm
3.3 mm
preguntas.explicacion: A heel-prick goes no deeper than 2.4 mm, and a 0.85 mm lancet exists for premature neonates. The 1.5 mm figure is the recommended finger-prick depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years, and 3.32 mm is the skin-to-bone distance at the medial and lateral heel of a 3 kg baby, not a puncture depth.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens); PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.A.2 III.D.1 · CCMA 3E10 3E14 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood for serological testing is drawn at a rural clinic in midsummer and sent by car to the laboratory. Which two handling points apply to that specimen?
opciones: Let the blood clot before processing, and protect the sample from extreme temperatures during transport
Centrifuge the tube immediately after the draw, and keep the sample frozen at −20 °C during transport
Mix the tube by five inversions to prevent clotting, and keep the sample at 37 °C during transport
Let the blood clot before processing, and keep the sample on wet ice during the whole transport
preguntas.explicacion: For serological testing the blood is allowed to clot before it is processed, the specimen goes into properly labeled containers, and during transport it is protected from extreme temperatures; serum for prompt serology is then stored at 2 to 8 °C, and only long-term storage or delayed transport calls for freezing at −20 °C or lower. Spinning before the clot has formed is what produces fibrin in the serum, and wet ice is the transport rule for other specimen types.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Infection Control in Healthcare Personnel (2019), section 7, Reporting HCP exposures and illnesses; OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Recordkeeping
preguntas.subtema: Reporting device problems · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k96 · CMA I.B.11.c / 2027 I.B.10.c · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: A safety needle's shield failed to activate and caused a needlestick. Besides the internal report, where can the device problem be reported, according to the CDC?
opciones: To the FDA MedWatch database, voluntarily, so device hazards can be identified
To the state health department, which requires reports of all device failures
To the Ryan White notification system for emergency response personnel
To OSHA within 24 hours, as with work-related hospitalizations
preguntas.explicacion: Adverse events involving medical devices can expose personnel to infection, and devices involved because of a quality problem can be reported to the FDA MedWatch database; the reporting is voluntary but helps identify device hazards that may warrant review. State reporting requirements concern notifiable infections in persons, not device failures. The Ryan White Act covers notification of emergency responders exposed to selected diseases, and the 24-hour OSHA report is for inpatient hospitalizations, amputations and eye loss.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Coding & Billing Dates of Service
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A walker was ordered in March, delivered to the patient in April and paid for in May. Which is the date of service?
opciones: April, when the patient received the item
March, when the provider ordered the item
May, when the payment for it was made
March, since the order opens the benefit
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare counts the expense from the day the patient actually received the item or the service, whatever the day it was ordered on or paid for. Services that run across two calendar dates start on one day and finish the next, and either day may be used, but no claim goes out until the service is complete.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: After the Visit, Vaccine and Supply Disposal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k74 · CMA I.D.3.a(5)
preguntas.pregunta: How are empty and expired vaccine vials discarded?
opciones: As medical waste, following the regulations of the state
In the ordinary office trash, once the label is removed
In the sharps container, together with the used needles
Returned to the manufacturer with the shipping documents
preguntas.explicacion: Empty or expired vaccine vials count as medical waste, and each state's regulations say how they are discarded; further guidance comes from the state or local immunization program or the state environmental agency. That is a separate path from the used needle and syringe, which go into a sharps container immediately after the injection and are never recapped.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 5, 6 and 10
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A gold serum separator tube, a dark green heparin tube and a light gray fluoride tube are all ordered. In which sequence are they filled?
opciones: Gold separator tube, then dark green heparin, then light gray fluoride
Dark green heparin, then gold separator tube, then light gray fluoride
Light gray fluoride, then gold separator tube, then dark green heparin
Gold separator tube, then light gray fluoride, then dark green heparin
preguntas.explicacion: The gold or tiger top separator tube holds position 5, the dark green heparin tube position 6 and the fluoride/oxalate tube position 10, the last one used. The sequence therefore runs separator tube, heparin tube, fluoride tube, and the fluoride tube is always the one left for the end.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Of the ten tube types listed in the WHO order of draw, which one is drawn last when it is needed?
opciones: The light gray oxalate/fluoride tube
The purple EDTA hematology tube
The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The light green plasma separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Position 10 of Table 2.3 belongs to the light gray tube with sodium fluoride and potassium oxalate, used for glucose. The purple EDTA tube is number 8, the pale yellow ACD tube for HLA typing and DNA studies is number 9, and the light green PST with lithium heparin and gel is number 7. Footnote a explains that 1 means draw first and 10 means draw last, if that tube is used at all.

preguntas.subtema: Flexibility of approach · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A two-physician office and a large group implement the same security standard in very different ways. Which factors does the rule let them weigh?
opciones: Their size and capabilities, their technical infrastructure, cost, and the risks
The number of patients seen each year and the volume of claims they send out
Whether the state they work in has passed security legislation of its own
How many staff members hold a formal certification in privacy and security
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility of approach lets a covered entity pick whatever security measures implement the standards reasonably and appropriately, weighing how big it is, how complex and how capable, what its technical infrastructure amounts to and what the security capabilities of its hardware and software amount to, what the measures cost, and how probable and how critical the risks are.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Semen analysis (003627), How the Test is Performed; and StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Semen transport · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collects a semen sample at home. What should he be told about getting it to the laboratory?
opciones: Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature
Bring it within 30 minutes, carried in an insulated bag with a cold pack so that it stays chilled
Bring it within 6 hours, carried in an inside coat pocket so it stays at body temperature
Bring it whenever convenient, since the laboratory warms every specimen to 37 degrees anyway
preguntas.explicacion: A home-collected specimen should reach the laboratory inside 30 minutes, kept warm in an inside coat pocket at body temperature, and a specialist has to examine it within 2 hours of collection; the sooner it is read, the more reliable the result. Chilling is the wrong direction, since the container is meant to stay between 20 and 37 degrees Celsius so that dehydration and temperature swings do not damage the sperm.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Required Disclosures
preguntas.subtema: Required disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations does the Privacy Rule REQUIRE a covered entity to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual asking for access or an accounting, and to HHS for a compliance review
To the individual asking for access, and to any provider who requests records for treatment
To HHS for a compliance review, and to the health plan whenever it asks to audit a claim
To a law enforcement official with a badge, and to the patient's closest living relative
preguntas.explicacion: Almost everything in the rule is permissive: the entity may use or disclose PHI in the situations listed but is not obliged to. Only two disclosures are compulsory, namely to the individual herself, or to her personal representative, when access or an accounting of disclosures is requested, and to HHS when it is conducting an investigation, a compliance review or an enforcement action.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.3.c · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: What decides whether a procedure calls for sterile gloves rather than clean exam gloves?
opciones: Whether a sterile site, a sterile tissue or a body cavity will be touched during it
Whether the patient is on transmission-based precautions during the visit that day
Whether the procedure will last long enough for the practitioner's hands to perspire
Whether any blood or body fluid is likely to reach the practitioner's hands at all
preguntas.explicacion: Clean gloves cover the risk of touching body fluids or contaminated surfaces, as when an intravenous line is started or a catheter bag emptied. Sterile gloves meet FDA sterilization requirements and are used for invasive procedures and whenever a sterile site, tissue or cavity will be touched, so that neither transient nor resident flora is carried in.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 ECG Abnormalities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: Why does a tracing that looks normal not prove the heart is pumping?
opciones: Electrical activity can carry on with no pumping behind it
The tracing follows the atria only, and never the ventricles
The speed of the paper hides the pumping part of each beat
The tracing follows the pumping in the chest leads only
preguntas.explicacion: The recording measures electrical events, and one of its stated limits is that it does not show how well the heart is pumping; electrical activity can appear on the strip with no pumping action to match. Judging the pump takes another test, such as an ultrasound.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an open workers' compensation record is treated for something unrelated, and the contractor denies the claim anyway. What should the office do?
opciones: Appeal with evidence that the care had nothing to do with the injury, and keep treating
Stop treating the patient until the workers' compensation record has been closed
Rebill the compensation carrier, since the open record makes it the primary payer
Write the balance off, since a claim denied on an open record cannot be reopened
preguntas.explicacion: Contractors sometimes deny claims because the diagnosis codes fall within the family of codes attached to a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation record in the patient's eligibility file, even when the care had nothing to do with the accident. Those denials can be appealed with information proving the services were unrelated, and care must go on during the appeal period while the record stays open.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Original Medicare, Level 5; and Medicare.gov, Filing an appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to take her Medicare appeal all the way to federal district court in 2026. What has to be true of the amount in dispute?
opciones: It has to reach $1,960, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $1,960, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
It has to reach $1,000, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $5,000, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
preguntas.explicacion: Judicial review in federal district court is the last of the five levels of Medicare appeal, and it is the only one with a minimum amount in controversy: $1,960 for 2026. Claims may be combined to reach that figure, and the decision letter from the fourth level carries the directions for filing, as every level's letter carries the directions for the next.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, How to Understand Your Lab Results, What is a reference range?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2M k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 4 k160 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her cholesterol figure cannot be set beside the one another laboratory gave her last year. Why not?
opciones: Laboratories use different methods, so their reference ranges differ
Laboratories report in different units, and only the units differ
Laboratories keep results on file for a single calendar year only
Laboratories round the figures differently when they issue reports
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratories often work with different testing methods, and so they describe a normal result against different reference ranges. A figure therefore has to be read against the range printed on its own report, and results from two laboratories cannot be set side by side. Anyone looking for a trend over time is told to try to use the same laboratory each time.

preguntas.fuente: eCFR, 21 CFR 862.1675, Blood specimen collection device, paragraphs (a) and (b)
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under 21 CFR 862.1675, how does the FDA define and classify a blood specimen collection device?
opciones: A device to collect and handle blood specimens and separate serum from cellular components; Class II
A device to collect and handle blood specimens and separate serum from cellular components; Class I device
A device carrying a feature that retracts or shields the needle after use; Class III
A device to transfer blood between tubes without additive carry-over; Class II
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation identifies a blood specimen collection device as one meant to collect and handle blood specimens, and to part the serum from the cellular components before testing, and says the type takes in tubes, vials, whole systems, serum separators, collection trays and vacuum sample tubes. Paragraph (b) assigns it to Class II. Sharps injury prevention features are covered by a separate FDA guidance.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Personnel
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A resting strip is regular at 118 per minute with upright P waves in I and II. What does the assistant do?
opciones: Record it and report the tracing to the provider for reading
Record it and tell the patient it shows sinus tachycardia
Repeat it at half the paper speed to slow the tracing down
Repeat it with the limb electrodes moved up to the thighs
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing is obtained by the technician and interpreted by the clinician, so the finding goes to the provider rather than to the patient. Changing the paper speed would make the recording unreadable against the standard grid, and moving the limb electrodes is a remedy for tremor, not for a fast rate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sputum Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Sputum mouth rinse · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(4) · RMA III.C.4.a.v · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: What should a patient do just before coughing a sputum specimen into the container?
opciones: Rinse the mouth with plain water for 10 to 15 seconds and spit the saliva out
Rinse the mouth with an antiseptic mouthwash and spit the rinse out completely
Eat a light breakfast so the cough reflex is stronger and the sputum comes up
Hold the breath for 10 to 15 seconds, which loosens secretions from the airway
preguntas.explicacion: Rinsing with clear water for 10 to 15 seconds clears contaminants out of the mouth, and the saliva is spat out before the patient takes three deep breaths and coughs at roughly two-minute intervals until sputum arrives. The best time for a deep-cough sample is first thing in the morning, before anything is eaten or drunk. Antiseptic mouthwash is what is specifically avoided before a throat swab.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.5
preguntas.subtema: Stopping system interfaces · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The record system's link to the laboratory has to be stopped for maintenance. What does the contingency guidance want checked before it is halted or restarted?
opciones: That the buffers holding data on the interface have been emptied first
That the laboratory has agreed the window and confirmed it in writing
That the read-only backup system has been switched on for the interval
That the last day of results has been printed and filed in the charts
preguntas.explicacion: Stopping or restarting an interface badly can lose or corrupt data in transit with no warning to anyone. The guidance therefore asks that all interface buffers be empty before the system is stopped or restarted, that buffers be large enough where the sending system keeps producing data, and that users be told when an interface is not working.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E14 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: Serum for hepatitis serology will not reach the reference laboratory for another six days. How should it be stored in the meantime?
opciones: Frozen at −20 °C or lower, the rule for long-term storage or delayed transport
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 °C, the rule for serum awaiting prompt serological testing
At room temperature away from extremes, the rule for specimens while in transit
Frozen at −70 °C, the rule for specimens that must keep the virus intact for culture
preguntas.explicacion: Serum meant for prompt serological testing waits at 2 to 8 °C, but when transport is delayed or storage will be long the specimen is frozen at −20 °C or lower. Protection from temperature extremes applies while the sample travels, and −70 °C is the transport temperature for viral culture specimens, so each distractor is a real instruction attached to the wrong situation. The blood must also have clotted before the serum is processed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors (preservatives)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A ward sends a preserved 24-hour urine and asks for a dipstick from the same jug. Which pairing of preservative and false result is correct?
opciones: Thymol reads as albumin; mercury salts read as no leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as glucose; mercury salts read as no urobilinogen present
Thymol reads as no albumin; mercury salts read as leukocyte esterase
Thymol reads as nitrite; mercury salts read as no bilirubin present
preguntas.explicacion: A preservative keeps the collection usable and distorts the strip at the same time. Thymol fakes a positive albumin and mercury salts push leukocyte esterase falsely negative. Formaldehyde is the broad offender, faking positives for glucose, urobilinogen, the peroxidase reaction and leukocyte esterase alike; hydrochloric acid moves the pH, and boric acid blunts the leukocyte pad.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: During the resuscitation of an infant, which pulse is evaluated?
opciones: The brachial, felt just above the antecubital fossa on the inner arm
The radial, felt at the wrist just above the base of the infant's thumb
The carotid, felt beside the airway as it is in an adult resuscitation
The dorsalis pedis, felt on the top of the foot beside the tendon there
preguntas.explicacion: In infant resuscitation the brachial artery is the site used: the finger goes just above the antecubital fossa, in the groove between the biceps tendon and the medial epicondyle. The carotid is the site preferred during adult resuscitation. The dorsalis pedis is absent in about one person in ten from anatomical variation alone.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Availability of appropriate supplies
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3A k54 k66 · D1 1A k24 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomy service is choosing safety-engineered devices for the first time. What is asked of it before the purchase?
opciones: Investigate their use, fit with current practice and protective value
Buy whichever device the largest hospital in the region already uses
Buy the cheapest device available, since all are cleared for the task
Trial each device on staff volunteers before any patient is drawn
preguntas.explicacion: Safety-engineered devices cut exposure to blood and injuries, but not every one of them suits phlebotomy. Users are asked to investigate the devices available thoroughly, looking at how they are meant to be used, how they fit current practice and how well they protect staff and patients.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A condition is documented on both sides and the classification offers no bilateral code for it. What is assigned?
opciones: Separate codes for the left side and for the right side
The code for the unspecified side, just for this encounter
One code, for the side that was treated at this encounter
The same code reported twice, once for each side treated
preguntas.explicacion: Some codes specify left, right or bilateral. Where the condition is bilateral and no bilateral code exists, separate codes are assigned for the left and the right side. Reporting one code twice is not an option, since a given code goes on an encounter a single time, and the unspecified side is kept for records that never say which side.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 4.1 Types of Tissues, The Four Types of Tissues
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which four tissue types make up every organ in the body?
opciones: Epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue
Epithelial, glandular, cartilage and nervous tissue
Connective, muscle, adipose and vascular tissue
Epithelial, connective, muscle and lymphoid tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Four tissue types cover every job. Epithelium sheets the outer surfaces, lines cavities and passageways and forms glands; connective tissue binds and supports; muscle is excitable and shortens to give movement; nervous tissue is excitable and carries signals. Adipose, cartilage and blood are specialized kinds of connective tissue.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's account of when the pain started keeps contradicting itself. Which technique fits?
opciones: Clarifying, with guiding statements that draw out more detail
Reflecting, by repeating the account back almost word for word
Providing rationale, by saying up front why the detail is needed
Using silence, by waiting without interrupting until she stops
preguntas.explicacion: Clarifying is the listed technique for guiding a patient to make a statement clearer and to obtain additional information. Reflecting repeats what was said, sometimes word for word; providing rationale explains why the information or the recommendation is needed; and silence is about attentiveness and not interrupting. All four are techniques, but only one fits a confused account.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Testicular self-exam — What Abnormal Results Mean
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a
preguntas.pregunta: A man doing a testicular self-exam finds a small, hard lump the size of a pea. What is the advice?
opciones: Contact the provider right away, since a hard pea-sized lump is abnormal
Watch it for one full month, since normal blood vessels feel much the same
Ignore it if the other side matches, since the two are normally identical
Ignore it if it is painless, since only tender lumps need to be reported
preguntas.explicacion: A small hard lump, an enlarged testicle, or any change that does not seem normal is reported without waiting. Normal findings are different: each testicle feels firm but not rock hard, and one may sit lower or be a little larger than the other. Vessels and other structures can make the exam confusing, which is another reason to ask rather than wait.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Alcohol: Uses
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.B.5.b (2027 I.B.4.b) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why are alcohols not recommended for sterilizing surgical instruments?
opciones: They have no sporicidal action and cannot penetrate material rich in protein
They corrode stainless steel and dissolve the lubricant used on hinged joints
They lose all activity the moment they meet the salts left by tap-water rinsing
They need an exposure of several hours, which no outpatient office can arrange
preguntas.explicacion: Two failures rule them out: they do not kill spores, and they cannot get through protein-rich material. Fatal postoperative Clostridium wound infections have followed attempts to sterilize instruments with alcohol. They also evaporate fast, which makes a long exposure hard to hold unless the item is fully immersed, and they are flammable.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: health care proxy
preguntas.subtema: Health care proxy · CCMA k218 · CMA E.8.c / 2027 E.7.b · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: What is a health care proxy, in the strict sense of the term?
opciones: The agent a health care declaration names to decide for the principal
The written document itself, listing the treatments the person refuses
The relative the state's law puts first when nobody has been named
The clinician who signs the orders once the person becomes incapacitated
preguntas.explicacion: The proxy is whoever a health care declaration names as agent to take medical decisions for the person who signed it, once that person can no longer decide. The declaration is the written document setting out how they should be cared for. The proxy's authority usually runs to decisions the declaration never mentioned, to authorizing procedures and to accessing the records.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: What are the Types of Controls? (internal controls)
preguntas.subtema: Internal (procedural) controls · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.3 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.1.a.ii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: On a rapid pregnancy cassette, what does the built-in control line tell the operator?
opciones: That the device worked and enough sample migrated through the strip; not whether the result is right
That the whole process, from applying the sample through to interpreting it, was carried out correctly
That the result is positive, because a control line only develops in the presence of the analyte
That the kit lot has passed the manufacturer's quality control and is within its expiration date
preguntas.explicacion: Internal, procedural or built-in controls check that the test itself is functioning: the sample volume was adequate, the fluid moved through the strip, and any electronic functions worked. They do not prove the operator handled the whole process correctly; that is what an external control, run like a patient sample, is for. A missing control line means an invalid test, whatever the result window shows.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: On a normal ECG tracing, what does the P wave represent?
opciones: Depolarization of the atria
Depolarization of the ventricles
Repolarization of the ventricles
Repolarization of the atria
preguntas.explicacion: The ECG has three prominent features: the small P wave is atrial depolarization, and the atria start contracting about 25 ms after it begins; the large QRS complex is ventricular depolarization; and the T wave is ventricular repolarization. Atrial repolarization does occur during the QRS complex, which masks it, but that is not what the P wave shows.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings; Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Critical value vs STAT · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT IV.C · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement correctly distinguishes a critical value from a STAT test result?
opciones: A critical value is defined only by how far it lies outside the normal range; a STAT test is designated by the ordering clinician
A critical value is designated by the ordering clinician; a STAT result is any value that falls outside the reference range
A critical value is any result outside the reference range; a STAT result is one that was reported within an hour of collection
A critical value is a result the instrument flags as invalid; a STAT test is one that must be confirmed by a second method
preguntas.explicacion: A critical value sits so far outside the normal range that it flags possible pathology, and the definition rests on that distance alone, whatever state the patient is in. A STAT or urgent test is the other thing entirely: the ordering clinician designates it, usually already knowing how the patient is doing. Both are handled post-analytically, when findings go to the treatment team.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: misdemeanor
preguntas.subtema: Civil and criminal acts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4 · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What usually separates a misdemeanor from a felony?
opciones: A misdemeanor is typically punishable by less than 12 months in jail
A misdemeanor is typically punishable by a fine and never by any jail
A misdemeanor is tried in a civil court and a felony in a criminal one
A misdemeanor is charged by the state and a felony only by the federal government
preguntas.explicacion: Both are offenses that criminal law punishes. A misdemeanor typically carries less than 12 months in jail, with community service, probation and fines among the usual sentences; felonies, being more serious, carry stiffer penalties, jail beyond a year included. Many states grade both into lettered classes, while others sentence crime by crime.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Follow-up After an Exposure: HIV; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Testing and counselling
preguntas.subtema: HIV follow-up schedule · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: How long is an exposed worker followed with HIV antibody testing after an occupational exposure?
opciones: Baseline, then periodically for at least 6 months, for example at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
Baseline and one repeat at 7 days, when the 28-day PEP course is one quarter done
Baseline and one repeat at 1 to 2 months, the schedule used after the hepatitis B series
Baseline only, since a negative rapid test rules out infection from that exposure
preguntas.explicacion: HIV antibody is tested as soon as possible after exposure and periodically for at least 6 months, typically at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months; WHO's annex uses baseline, 6 to 12 weeks and 6 months. Workers on PEP also have blood counts and kidney and liver tests before and 2 weeks after starting. The 1-to-2-month test is the anti-HBs check after hepatitis B vaccination, and a baseline test only shows the worker's status at the time of exposure.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Triennial reminder from a plan · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: How often must a health plan remind the individuals it covers that its notice of privacy practices exists and how to obtain it?
opciones: At least once every three years, to the individuals then covered by the plan
At least once every year, to the individuals then covered by the plan
At least once every five years, to the individuals then covered by the plan
At least once every three years, and again whenever a claim is denied
preguntas.explicacion: Among the duties that fall on health plans rather than on providers, the plan must notify the individuals it then covers of the availability of the notice and of how to obtain it at least once every three years. A separate duty sends a revised notice within 60 days when the plan makes a material revision.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, PEP not indicated; CDC, Exposure to Blood (2003), Risk of Infection: HIV; CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP
preguntas.subtema: When PEP is not indicated · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: For which of these exposures do the CDC and WHO guidance say HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is NOT indicated?
opciones: A few drops of blood on intact skin
A splash of blood into the eye
A needlestick with a hollow-bore needle
Blood contact with a fresh abrasion on the hand
preguntas.explicacion: When a potentially infectious fluid meets skin that is intact, there is no indication for HIV or hepatitis B prophylaxis; the same holds for fluids not known to transmit HIV, such as feces, saliva, urine or sweat. The CDC adds that a few drops of blood landing on skin that is whole most likely carry no risk, and that no such transmission has ever been documented; its PEP guidance keeps mucous membranes, non-intact skin and perforated skin as the routes worth considering. An eye splash, a hollow-bore needlestick and an abrasion are all on that list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: R-Wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: On a normal tracing, how does the R wave change across the chest leads?
opciones: It grows from V1, the smallest, to V5, the largest
It shrinks from V1, the largest, to V5, the smallest
It stays the same height from V1 through to V6
It grows from V6, the smallest, to V1, the largest
preguntas.explicacion: The R wave gets taller as the leads move from the right side of the chest to the left, an orderly pattern called R-wave progression, with the smallest in V1 and the largest in V5. When that build-up is missing, one of the causes to rule out is an electrode placed in the wrong spot.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Power of Attorney", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Advance directives · CCMA k217, k218 · CMA E.8.b-c / 2027 E.7 · RMA I.C.1.f · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a living will and a health care power of attorney?
opciones: The living will states the choices; the power of attorney names who decides
The living will names who decides; the power of attorney states the choices
The living will works while the patient can still speak; the power does not
The living will is a medical order; the power of attorney is a legal document
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is a written statement of the person's own wishes, such as whether they want resuscitation or intubation, and it designates nobody. A health care power of attorney grants a named agent the power to make medical decisions on the person's behalf, and that agent may use the living will to guide those decisions. Both are legal documents; neither is a medical order.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Positions and Directions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order calls for an intramuscular injection, and the same note mentions an intercostal muscle. Which pair of meanings is right?
opciones: Intra- is within and inter- is between
Intra- is between and inter- is within
Intra- is within and inter- is beneath
Intra- is beyond and inter- is between
preguntas.explicacion: Intra- means within, so an intramuscular injection is placed inside the muscle. Inter- means between, so an intercostal muscle lies between the ribs. Two more from the same group are easy to confuse with them: infra- is beneath or below, and ex- and extra- carry the sense of beyond.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Technology screening · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which question belongs to the check on what technology a telehealth patient already has, rather than to another part of the preparation?
opciones: Whether she needs help opening an e-mail account, if the platform calls for one
Whether she has somewhere quiet and private in which to take the appointment
Whether she is able to raise the camera so that it sits at the level of her eyes
Whether she has the bottles of her current medicines within reach of the screen
preguntas.explicacion: Working out what technology a patient already has means asking whether her computer, tablet or mobile device carries a camera and microphone that suit the platform; whether her internet connection has the bandwidth video needs; whether she has somewhere with secure internet; and whether she needs help opening an e-mail account. Privacy, camera position and having the medicines ready sit on other lists.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Medicare telehealth coverage · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks whether she can have a telehealth visit from her own home. What is the current answer?
opciones: Yes, Medicare covers telehealth from anywhere in the country through December 31, 2027
Yes, but only if she travels to a clinic in a rural area that acts as the originating site
No, Medicare stopped covering telehealth when the public health emergency was declared over
Yes, but only for the brief virtual check-ins that last ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare covers telehealth services obtained from anywhere in the United States, the patient's own home included, through December 31, 2027. Telehealth there means care from a provider in another location over audio and video, or over audio alone in some cases, and it takes in office visits, psychotherapy and consultations. E-visits through a portal and short virtual check-ins are extra ways of communicating, not the only ones.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Topical and Transdermal Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(4) · RMA III.G.4.d(iii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wearing a fentanyl patch asks whether a heating pad may be placed over it for back pain. What is the answer?
opciones: No: heat over a patch speeds the release of the drug and has caused fatal overdoses
Yes: heat brings vasodilation, which is why it is applied over patches of every kind
Yes, as long as the previous patch is left in place while the new one is being applied
No: heat loosens the adhesive, so the patch has to be pressed down for ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Heat is sometimes used with an inunction rubbed into the skin, because vasodilation improves the blood flow and the absorption. Over a patch it is dangerous: heat increases the release of the drug, and with fentanyl or nitroglycerin patches that has caused overdose and death. Manufacturer guidance decides. Pressing for ten seconds and removing the old patch belong to how a new patch is applied.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2L k48 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · CMA F.1.c / 2027 F.1.d · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says 'I hate needles' and begins to tremble. What does WHO step 2 direct?
opciones: Reassure her, and ask what would help her feel more comfortable
Tell the patient firmly that it will not hurt at all this time
Proceed as quickly as possible before the anxiety builds further
Ask a colleague to hold the arm firmly while you perform the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says that where the patient is anxious or afraid, the health worker gives reassurance and asks what would help them feel more at ease. Promising that it will not hurt is the false reassurance listed among therapeutic communication pitfalls, rushing ignores the patient, and holding somebody down is a pediatric immobilization technique, not a response to an anxious adult.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.8 Checklist for Applying and Removing Sterile Gloves
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k60 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: The dominant hand is now gloved. How is the second sterile glove picked up?
opciones: Four fingers together reach under the folded cuff, thumb held out so it touches nothing sterile
Thumb and index finger pinch the inside of the cuff, exactly as the first glove was lifted
The gloved palm presses down on the glove and slides it to the edge of the inner wrapper
The bare hand steadies the glove at the fingertips while the gloved hand pulls the cuff open
preguntas.explicacion: The gloved hand keeps its four fingers together and reaches under the folded cuff, on the outer surface, with the thumb held outstretched so it never brushes the second glove. The bare nondominant hand only steadies the package flap. Its fingers are then held out straight with the thumb tucked into the palm while the glove is pulled on.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, VAERS (co-managed with FDA): About VAERS, Background
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k66 · CMA I.D.3.a(4)
preguntas.pregunta: Who may report an adverse event after a vaccination to VAERS?
opciones: Anyone; health professionals must report certain events and makers report all
Only the physician who ordered the vaccine, using the patient's medical record
Only the manufacturer, which collects reports from providers and forwards them
Only a state immunization program, which files on behalf of the practice
preguntas.explicacion: The Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, set up in 1990 and co-managed by the CDC and the FDA, takes reports from anyone. Certain adverse events must be reported by health professionals, and manufacturers must report every event that reaches them. Vaccine administration errors are among the things reported, and each report is coded and entered into the database.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for medication preparation
preguntas.subtema: Aseptic medication preparation · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague leaves a needle inserted in a medication vial's septum between doses. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: It opens a direct route for microorganisms into the vial and its contents
It counts as recapping, which the bloodborne pathogens standard prohibits
It exposes the drug to light and reduces its potency within minutes
It is acceptable in a clean medication area away from patient treatment
preguntas.explicacion: A needle is never parked in a vial septum between doses, because it leaves microorganisms an open road into the vial and into what it holds; any vial whose sterility is compromised or in doubt is discarded. The same section asks that medications be drawn up in a designated clean area away from sinks, as near to administration time as possible. Recapping is a sharps rule about the cap of a used needle, a different hazard, and none of this has to do with light.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Key Terms
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A payer asks the office to send its claims as an 837P, version 5010A1. What has it asked for?
opciones: The current electronic standard for professional claims
The paper claim form that a national committee designs
The electronic standard for institutional facility claims
The remittance standard the payer sends back afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: In that string the 837 is the standard format for sending claims electronically, the P marks the professional version used by health care professionals and suppliers, and 5010A1 is the current version of the electronic transaction standards. The paper alternative is the claim form the national uniform claim committee designs and maintains.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.C.3.b (2027 I.C.3.b) · RMA III.A.3.b(i) · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: With an antimicrobial scrub agent, how long is the surgical hand antisepsis, and what does going past ten minutes add?
opciones: About 2 to 6 minutes, and going past ten adds no benefit while irritating the skin
About 2 to 6 minutes, and going past ten adds residual activity that lasts the case
About 8 to 12 minutes, and going past ten adds no benefit while irritating the skin
About 30 to 60 seconds, and going past ten adds a measurable drop in resident flora
preguntas.explicacion: Surgical hand antisepsis with an antimicrobial agent runs roughly two to six minutes, using a sponge or brush that is sterile and used once, and following the manufacturer and the facility. Scrubbing ten minutes or more brings no extra benefit and raises the risk of skin irritation. Routine handwashing is a different exercise, at 15 to 20 seconds.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, SBAR
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2E k23 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant calls a provider about a patient whose catheter has stopped draining. In SBAR, which part says what the caller thinks is wrong?
opciones: The assessment, naming what the caller believes is wrong
The situation, naming what is going on with the patient
The background, giving the clinical context of the case
The recommendation, saying what should be done about it
preguntas.explicacion: SBAR carries critical information that needs attention and action right away. Situation says what is happening with the patient, background gives the clinical context, assessment states what the caller thinks the problem is, and recommendation or request says what should be done to correct it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A red top tube is sent to the laboratory for a prothrombin time. Why will it be rejected?
opciones: Coagulation tests need plasma; serum has lost its clotting factors
Coagulation tests need serum; the red tube gives plasma instead
The red tube clots too slowly, beyond the 60 minutes the test allows
The clot activator in the red tube binds the calcium the test measures
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation testing is done on plasma, never on serum, because the clotting factors are removed when serum forms. The correct specimen is a light blue tube with 3.2% sodium citrate, which chelates calcium and holds the sample in stasis until calcium chloride is added in the laboratory. The clot activator does not bind calcium; it does the opposite, it lets the blood clot.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Engineering Controls, Work Practice Controls; NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors, Hierarchy of Controls
preguntas.subtema: Engineering vs work practice controls · CPT D1 k12 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A self-sheathing needle is an example of which type of control under the standard?
opciones: An engineering control, which isolates or removes the hazard from the workplace
A work practice control, which changes the way a task is performed
Personal protective equipment, which is used when exposure remains after controls
An administrative control, such as the annual review of the Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) lists self-sheathing needles, sharps disposal containers and sharps with engineered injury protections as engineering controls: devices that wall off the bloodborne pathogen hazard or take it out of the workplace. A work practice control changes how the task is done, and the example the standard itself gives is the ban on two-handed recapping. PPE is specialized clothing or equipment the employee wears. NIOSH's hierarchy puts elimination and substitution first, then work practices and administrative controls, then engineering controls, with PPE last.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guidance for SARS-CoV-2 Rapid Testing in Point-of-Care Settings: CLIA Certificate Requirements; Reporting
preguntas.subtema: COVID point-of-care under a CoW · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA 2027 I.C.10.d.(7) COVID-19 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A pharmacy plans to offer rapid antigen SARS-CoV-2 testing and nothing else. Which CLIA certificate fits?
opciones: A Certificate of Waiver, appropriate when point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 testing is the only testing done
A Certificate of Compliance, because respiratory antigen testing is moderate complexity
A PPM certificate, because the pharmacist reads the result during the visit
No certificate, because negative rapid antigen results no longer have to be reported
preguntas.explicacion: Point-of-care testing cannot be done without a CLIA certificate, and where SARS-CoV-2 point-of-care testing is all a site does, a Certificate of Waiver is the right one. The site fills in Form CMS-116, sends it to the state agency, pays the fee, and has 30 days to report a change of director, of address, of name or of ownership. Dropping the required reporting of negative antigen results did not remove the certificate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pain Assessment", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k53 · CMA I.A.1.g · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old cannot use numbers to rate pain. Which tool fits?
opciones: The Wong-Baker FACES scale, built for children who are nonverbal in acute settings
The numeric rating scale, which most children can manage from the age of four
The McGill Pain Questionnaire, whose 78 descriptors cover sensory and affective terms
The Short Form Health Survey 36, which measures quality of life across many domains
preguntas.explicacion: The FACES scale was designed for children who cannot put pain into words in an acute setting, and it can be adapted for adults with communication difficulties. Numerical scales become usable around adolescence. The questionnaires with dozens of items are self-report instruments for older patients with chronic pain.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Consent exceptions · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A 16-year-old comes to the office alone and asks to be treated without her parents being told. What decides whether she can consent for herself?
opciones: Whether she is emancipated or her state lets minors consent to that service
Whether she is able to pay for the visit herself on the day of the appointment
Whether the clinician judges that she is mature enough during the encounter
Whether a parent can be reached by telephone before the visit starts
preguntas.explicacion: Minors under 18 usually cannot consent, and the parent gives permission instead. The openings are emancipation — marriage, active military duty, or living apart and managing one's own money — and the services a state lets minors seek alone, such as contraception, care for a sexually transmitted infection, or prenatal care. Paying for a visit does not emancipate anyone, and the mature minor doctrine exists in very few states.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Reservoirs and Carriers
preguntas.subtema: Asymptomatic carriers · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which pathogens are named as often being passed on by carriers who show no symptoms?
