The location is acceptable as one identifier, provided a second identifier such as the ordering physician's name is added
Two staff members must independently confirm the bed number before a specimen can be collected
preguntas.explicacion: The first international patient safety goal requires at least two ways of identifying the patient, for example name, identification number, birth date or a bar-coded wristband, and it excludes the room number or location outright. The wristband is one valid option, not the only one; the physician's name identifies the order, not the patient; and a second witness does not turn a location into an identifier.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which range is accepted as the normal body temperature of a resting adult?
opciones: 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F), around an average of 37.0 °C (98.6 °F)
36.0 to 37.0 °C (96.8 to 98.6 °F), around an average of 36.5 °C (97.7 °F)
37.0 to 38.0 °C (98.6 to 100.4 °F), around an average of 37.5 °C (99.5 °F)
35.5 to 36.5 °C (95.9 to 97.7 °F), around an average of 36.0 °C (96.8 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: The figure everyone quotes, 37.0 °C or 98.6 °F, is an average and not a fixed value: the accepted reference band runs from 36.5 to 37.5 °C (97.7 to 99.5 °F). The hypothalamus holds core temperature inside that narrow band. A single reading at either edge is normal, so it is compared with the patient's own baseline.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(c)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes to the collection agency asking it to stop contacting her about the account. What follows under the statute?
opciones: The collector must stop communicating about that debt, subject to narrow exceptions
The collector must stop only once the debt has been validated to her in writing
The collector may carry on for thirty days while the dispute is being investigated
The collector must hand the account back to the practice within five days of that
preguntas.explicacion: Once the consumer has told the debt collector, in writing, that she refuses to pay the debt or that she wants the communication to stop, the collector must not contact her about that debt again, apart from the narrow exceptions the section itself sets out. The thirty days and the five days belong to the validation provision instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: Scrub duration · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee scrubs for ten minutes before a sterile procedure, believing longer is safer. What is the effect?
opciones: No added benefit, and more risk of irritating the skin
A longer lasting effect on the resident skin flora
The same effect as a rub, which needs no drying time
A shorter effect, since the antiseptic is rinsed away
preguntas.explicacion: The usual scrub with an antimicrobial agent runs about two to six minutes, following the manufacturer and the institution. Scrub times of ten minutes or more add nothing and raise the risk of skin irritation, and irritated skin is harder to keep clean. Some institutions use shorter staged techniques or an alcohol-based formulation instead, applied as the manufacturer directs and left to dry completely before sterile gloves go on.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Generic Drug Facts: Generic medicines work the same as brand-name medicines
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.f · NCMA 1.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is switched from a brand-name tablet to its approved generic. What must the generic match?
opciones: The active ingredient, the strength, form and route, and it must be bioequivalent
The active and the inactive ingredients as well, color and shape of the tablet
The price the brand is sold at, because the FDA sets what a generic may charge
The clinical trials of the brand, which the generic maker has to run over again
preguntas.explicacion: An approved generic works the same way and carries the same benefits and risks as the brand. The applicant has to show that the active ingredient is the same, that strength, dosage form and route of administration match, that manufacturing meets the same standards, that the label is the same apart from certain exceptions, and that the product is bioequivalent. The FDA reviews before approval and inspects the plants.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What are the four parameters of steam sterilization that an autoclave has to control?
opciones: Steam, pressure, temperature and time
Steam, humidity, temperature and pressure
Steam, pressure, gas concentration and time
Steam, temperature, pH and exposure time
preguntas.explicacion: The principle is that every item meets steam directly, at the temperature and the pressure the cycle calls for, for as long as it calls for, which makes four parameters: steam, pressure, temperature and time. Pressure is only the means of reaching the temperature needed. Relative humidity and gas concentration matter for ethylene oxide, not for steam.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Holter monitor (24h)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(b) · RMA III.F.6.c.iii III.F.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being fitted with a Holter monitor. How long is it usually worn?
opciones: 24 to 48 hours, recording continuously during normal activity
2 to 4 hours, recording continuously during normal activity
7 to 10 days, recording continuously during normal activity
24 to 48 hours, recording only when the patient presses it
preguntas.explicacion: The monitor is a small recorder carried in a pouch or pocket, wired to electrodes on the chest, and it writes the rhythm without a break for 24 to 48 hours of ordinary life. The patient goes about the usual routine and returns the device afterwards for the provider to review.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime review · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An unexpected outage has kept the record system down for a day and a half. What does the guidance ask the organization to do afterwards?
opciones: Review it in depth with root-cause or failure modes analysis, as a group
Report it to the certifying body that tested the record system's software
Repeat the yearly downtime drill within the month that follows the outage
Rebuild the disaster recovery plan from scratch before the system restarts
preguntas.explicacion: Unexpected downtimes lasting more than 24 hours are treated as learning material. The organization convenes clinicians and technical staff together to look at the event and how it was handled, identify possible root causes with a structured method, and decide what would prevent or soften the next one.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is diagnosed with polycythemia. What is the main drawback of the condition?
opciones: Higher blood viscosity, so the heart circulates blood with more effort
Too little oxygen delivered directly to the tissues by the red cells
Loss of the plasma buffers that keep the pH between 7.35 and 7.45
A hematocrit that falls below the 36 percent lower limit
preguntas.explicacion: Polycythemia is an overproduction of red cells, and the trouble it causes is not poor oxygen delivery but thicker blood that the heart has to work harder to move. In polycythemia the hematocrit climbs, it does not fall, and the plasma buffers have nothing to do with it. Viscosity is the same property that makes honey pour more slowly than water.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 3: core elements; and MyPlate, USDA: Grains
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement matches what the Dietary Guidelines say about grains in a healthy pattern?
opciones: At least half of the grains eaten should be whole grains
At least a quarter of the grains eaten should be whole grains
Whole grains should replace refined grains completely
Grains are counted in cups, like fruits and vegetables
preguntas.explicacion: Among the core elements of a healthy pattern, grains carry the instruction that at least half of them be whole grain. Refined grains are not forbidden, so a complete swap overstates the rule. Grains are measured in ounce-equivalents; cups are the unit for fruits, vegetables and dairy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Types of PPE
preguntas.subtema: Gown barrier levels · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Two isolation gowns carry different fluid barrier levels. What do those levels come from?
opciones: A four-level standard for medical gowns, from the lowest barrier up
The number of layers of fabric the manufacturer sewed together
The quality level that also grades gloves for micro-perforation
The hazardous materials scale that runs from level A down to D
preguntas.explicacion: Medical gowns are graded against a published standard that sets four levels of fluid barrier protection, and a separate guidance document deals with gowns worn to handle hazardous drugs. Choosing well means matching the level to the setting: sterile gowns for surgery, non-sterile ones for contact exposure. The acceptable quality level is a glove measure, and levels A through D belong to the hazardous materials scale, where A is the most protective.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ear Irrigation", Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B9 k76 · CMA I.C.2.b · NCMA 2B.17
preguntas.pregunta: Why must the fluid used for ear irrigation be at body temperature?
opciones: Fluid that is too cold or too hot provokes dizziness through the semicircular canal
Fluid that is too cold or too hot hardens the cerumen and blocks the canal further
Fluid at body temperature dissolves keratin, which is what cerumen is made of
Fluid at body temperature keeps the tympanic membrane from becoming translucent
preguntas.explicacion: The lateral semicircular canal lies close to the ear canal, so water off body temperature sets off vertigo and nystagmus. Warm water drives nystagmus toward the same side and cold water toward the opposite side, remembered as cold-opposite, warm-same. Transient vertigo, hearing loss or tinnitus after irrigation usually trace back to the temperature.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k16 k49 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: About what share of older adults have hearing loss?
opciones: About one-third
About one-half
About one-quarter
About two-thirds
preguntas.explicacion: Age-related hearing loss is common, reaching about one-third of older adults, and the chance of it grows with age. That is why the guidance asks the clinician to be sure the patient can hear before going on: check that a hearing aid is working, look for a build-up of earwax, and keep the background noise in mind.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Verbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Communication cycle · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: What makes verbal communication effective, as the term is defined?
opciones: Words the receiver understands, conveying care and respect
Words the sender prefers, matched to the sender's training
Words taken from the record and repeated as documented
Words in plain language, but delivered only in writing
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal communication is more than talking: it is an exchange of information using words the receiver understands, in a way that carries professional caring and respect. Heavy jargon or slang raises a barrier the sender did not intend, so the receiver's preferred method is assessed and understanding is always verified.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Do Not Resuscitate", Function
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a-b / 2027 E.7.a · RMA I.C.7 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: A chart holds an advance directive that mentions CPR. Is that the same as a DNR order?
opciones: No: a directive is a legal document, and a DNR is a medical order
No: a directive covers intubation, while a DNR covers only medication
Yes: any written mention of CPR in the chart operates as a DNR order
Yes: once the directive is scanned in, the code status changes to DNR
preguntas.explicacion: Advance directives are legal documents, not medical orders, so a directive that mentions resuscitation is not equivalent to a do-not-resuscitate or do-not-intubate order. The team has to draw the patient's preference out specifically and turn it into an order signed by the provider. On a MOLST or POLST form those same wishes are already written as orders.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, Rationale and EP 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · NCMA 2C.1 · CMA III.H.2.a / 2027 III.H.2.a patient verification
preguntas.pregunta: Under NPSG.01.01.01, which of the following may never be used as a patient identifier?
opciones: The room number or bed location
The telephone number on file
An assigned identification number
Any other person-specific identifier
preguntas.explicacion: The rationale for the goal lists what counts: the person's name, an identification number assigned to them, a telephone number, or another identifier tied to that person. EP 1 adds the one exclusion examiners like to test: the room number, or where the patient physically is, does not identify anyone, because it belongs to the bed rather than to the person.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Reporting Critical Findings)
preguntas.subtema: Repeat critical values · CPT D5 5G k93 · PBT VI.A quality assurance · CCMA 3D3 k116 · CMA I.C.9.a · RMA III.C.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient's point-of-care potassium is critical again today, as it was at the last two visits and is documented in the chart. What does the reporting policy require?
opciones: Treat it as a reportable event and follow the critical value policy for this instance, even though earlier critical values are known
Skip the call, because a critical value that has already been reported for the same patient does not need to be reported again
Report it only if today's value differs from the previous critical result by more than 10 %, and otherwise just record it
Record it in the log and report all of the day's critical values together to the provider at the end of the clinic session
preguntas.explicacion: A critical value counts as a reportable event even where the patient has had critical values before and they are on record, and the reporting policy is followed the same way each time one appears. Stepping outside the policy is considered only in exceptional cases with evidence behind them, an obvious testing or pre-analytical error for instance. Both the result and whatever was done about it are documented every time.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(14) · RMA III.F.4.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which imaging method is ruled out for a patient with iron-containing metallic implants?
opciones: Magnetic resonance, whose powerful field can dislodge the metal implants
Computed tomography, whose rotating scanner cannot pass over the metal
Ultrasound, because metal reflects the sound waves back toward the probe
Plain x-ray, because the metal blocks the beam and hides the bone behind
preguntas.explicacion: Patients with iron-containing implants, internal sutures or some prosthetic devices cannot be scanned by magnetic resonance, because the field can move them. The same technique is otherwise attractive since it uses no radiation, but it is costly, noisy and encloses the patient in a tube for as long as half an hour.

preguntas.subtema: Tests waived by regulation · CPT D1 k29 · PBT IV.A.2 / IV.C · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.10.b.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.i
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these procedures is named in the CLIA regulation itself as a test a Certificate of Waiver site may perform?
opciones: Spun microhematocrit test
Automated sedimentation rate
Serum hCG color comparison
Benchtop hemoglobin A1c
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation's own list includes non-automated dipstick urinalysis, non-automated fecal occult blood, visual ovulation and urine pregnancy tests, non-automated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, copper sulfate hemoglobin, home-use glucose meters, spun microhematocrit and single-analyte hemoglobin instruments. The sedimentation rate is waived only when non-automated, and pregnancy tests only on urine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Allergy Testing", Specimen Collection: Serum Testing
preguntas.pregunta: Which allergy test can be ordered from the primary care office on a blood sample?
opciones: Serum IgE testing, which measures circulating allergen-specific antibodies
Skin prick testing, which measures the immediate mast cell response
Intradermal testing, which is read as a wheal at the injection site
Patch testing, which measures a delayed cell-mediated hypersensitivity
preguntas.explicacion: Allergen-specific IgE in serum is the one test that needs only a blood sample and is readily available outside a specialist office; each antibody has to be named on the request, and grouped panels get expensive fast. The older radioallergosorbent method is no longer used. The three skin-based tests are usually done by specialists.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Stool ova and parasites exam (003756), Why the Test is Performed; and MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Ova and Parasite Test, What happens during an ova and parasite test?; and StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests" (NBK570615)
preguntas.subtema: Three O&P specimens · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: Why are 3 separate stool specimens recommended for an ova and parasite examination?
opciones: Parasites are not shed in the stool every day, so several samples raise the chance of finding them
Each specimen is examined for a different infection: amebiasis, giardiasis or strongyloidiasis
The first specimen is used for culture, the second for the smear and the third for molecular testing
The specimens are pooled to reach the 8 to 10 mL that the microscope smear requires
preguntas.explicacion: Parasites and their eggs may be absent from the stool on a given day, so collecting several specimens over a few days makes the examination more sensitive; three different specimens are the usual recommendation. In the laboratory a small smear of each is placed on a slide and examined under the microscope, and molecular tests may be added. The 8 to 10 mL figure is the volume of each sputum specimen for tuberculosis.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles with safety mechanism
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which mechanism is described for winged steel needles that carry a safety feature?
opciones: A needle-locking mechanism that also prevents the set being reused
A blunting mechanism that dulls the tip once the last tube is filled
A color change in the tubing that shows the set has been used once
A hinged shield activated by pressing the wings against each other
preguntas.explicacion: Winged steel needles with a passive or an active safety feature use a needle-locking mechanism that cuts the risk of a stick and stops reuse, and they make the transfer of blood safer when a syringe is used. Joined to vacuum tubes, they still need the first tube to be additive-free or discarded.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with severe neurological impairment of the legs needs the steadiest crutch for the long term. Which one, and at what cost?
opciones: The platform crutch: more stability, but less maneuverability than the others
The forearm crutch: more stability, but it demands good upper body strength
The axilla crutch: more stability, but it cannot be used beyond a few weeks
The platform crutch: more maneuverability, but less stability than the others
preguntas.explicacion: Of the three kinds, the platform crutch is the one seen least often. The weight goes onto the forearms and the platform gives the user more stability than the axilla or forearm types, at the price of maneuvering less easily. They are meant for long-term use, and severe neurological impairment of the legs is the situation named for them.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives
preguntas.subtema: Preservative fill line · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient fills a preservative-containing urine tube only to one-third of the marked line. What is the problem?
opciones: Too little urine leaves the preservative too concentrated, which can inhibit bacterial growth in the culture
Too little urine leaves the preservative too dilute, so it cannot keep the bacteria from multiplying in transit
The tube should be filled to the line with sterile normal saline so the preservative ratio is restored
Too little urine is acceptable for culture, since only 15 to 30 mL is needed for an accurate analysis
preguntas.explicacion: The preservative-to-specimen ratio matters in both directions. Overfilling past the line dilutes the preservative and weakens its action; underfilling leaves an excess of preservative that can suppress the very bacteria the culture is looking for. Topping up with saline dilutes the specimen and the colony count, and the 15 to 30 mL figure applies to urinalysis in a plain cup, not to a preservative tube with a fill line.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Recapping in the numbers · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What share of needlestick injuries did older studies blame on recapping, and what does current hospital surveillance show?
opciones: Between 10% and 25% then; about 5% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 40% and 60% then; about 20% in the surveillance hospitals now
About 5% then; between 10% and 25% in the surveillance hospitals now
Between 10% and 25% then; none at all since the standard prohibited it
preguntas.explicacion: Older studies traced ten to twenty-five percent of needlestick injuries to recapping a used needle. Recapping by hand has been discouraged for years and is prohibited by the bloodborne pathogens standard unless no alternative exists, yet it still causes about five percent of the injuries counted in surveillance hospitals. The share fell; it did not disappear, and that is the point of the rule.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, staging
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Tests are ordered to learn how far a cancer has spread from where it started. What is that process called?
opciones: Staging, which is done to plan the best treatment
Screening, which is done to plan the best treatment
Remission, which is done to plan the best treatment
Grading, which is done to plan the best treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Staging means running the exams and the tests that show how far a cancer reaches in the body, above all whether it has left the place where it formed, and the stage drives the treatment plan. Screening is different: it looks for disease in someone with no symptoms at all, as with mammograms, colonoscopy and the Pap and HPV tests.

preguntas.subtema: PSDA · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.d / 2027 E.7.c · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says he has no advance directive and does not want one. What may the practice do about his care?
opciones: Nothing may change: care cannot be conditioned on having a directive
Care may be limited to what the state surrogate hierarchy authorizes
Care may go ahead once a relative signs a directive on his behalf
Care may be delayed until the community education material is given
preguntas.explicacion: A provider may not make the provision of care conditional on whether a person has executed an advance directive, nor discriminate on that basis in any other way. The state hierarchy of surrogates matters only when a patient can no longer decide, community education is an obligation the provider owes the public, and nobody else may execute a directive for a competent adult.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, Health Plans
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: How are the TRICARE health plans grouped?
opciones: Into plans in the United States, plans overseas, and premium-based plans
Into active-duty plans, retiree plans, and plans for surviving family members
Into inpatient plans, outpatient plans, and plans covering prescriptions only
Into regional plans: an eastern one, a western one, and one for overseas care
preguntas.explicacion: Several different health plans are offered by TRICARE, set out in three groups: plans inside the United States, plans overseas, and premium-based plans available worldwide. Which of them a person can take depends on who that person is and where they live, which is why the program keeps a plan finder and a side-by-side comparison tool for narrowing the choice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Patients with Impaired Decision-Making Capacity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 k49 · PBT II.D · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with early dementia clearly explains what the draw is for and why she agrees to it. Who consents?
opciones: She does; a diagnosis alone does not remove the right to give informed consent
Her daughter must, because a dementia diagnosis removes decision-making capacity
A psychiatrist must certify her competency before any venipuncture is done
No one needs to; consent is waived because the test is low risk
preguntas.explicacion: Cognitive impairment, mental illness or severe illness do not by themselves revoke the right to consent, so long as the person can understand, weigh and communicate a decision. A psychiatrist is called in only where the ability to decide is in doubt or hard to read, and the waiver exception applies where the patient waives voluntarily, not because the test is a small one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prostate Cancer Screening", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a digital rectal exam today and a PSA draw is also on the order. What should happen?
opciones: Hold the blood draw for three days, because the exam can raise the value
Draw the blood first, before the exam, or the sample will hemolyze in transit
Draw the blood immediately after the exam, while the prostate is stimulated
Hold the blood draw for eight weeks, the interval used to confirm a result
preguntas.explicacion: A rectal examination can push the value up for a while, so three days are allowed to pass before the specimen is collected. Eight weeks is a different interval: it is the gap between the two abnormal levels needed to confirm an elevation, since a quarter to 40% of men with one high result come back normal on the recheck.

preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430 (Nov. 6, 2000), secs. 2 and 3; OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens and Needlestick Prevention: Standards
preguntas.subtema: Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act of 2000 require?
opciones: Revising the OSHA standard to add safer devices, annual device review, employee input and a sharps injury log
Creating the bloodborne pathogens standard itself, with the hepatitis B vaccine offer and exposure control plans
Replacing the OSHA standard with the CDC's Standard Precautions for every healthcare employer
Requiring every employer to keep the OSHA 300 log, a form that had not existed before 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Public Law 106-430, signed on November 6, 2000, ordered changes to the 1991 bloodborne pathogens standard: bringing safer devices, meaning sharps that carry engineered injury protections and needleless systems, into the definition of engineering controls; requiring the review of the Exposure Control Plan to reflect new technology and to document that safer devices were considered each year; requiring input from non-managerial direct-care employees; and establishing the sharps injury log. OSHA revised the standard in 2001; Congress found the existing OSHA 200 log insufficient rather than creating it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Basic safe injection practices
preguntas.subtema: One needle, one syringe · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse changes the needle but reuses the syringe to give medication to a second patient. According to the CDC, this practice is which of these?
opciones: Unsafe: a syringe is contaminated after one use, even with a new needle
Safe, since the needle is the only part that touches the patient
Safe if the second dose is injected through IV tubing rather than into tissue
Unsafe only if the first patient has a known bloodborne infection
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's rule is One Needle, One Syringe, Only One Time. After a single use both syringe and needle count as contaminated and go into the sharps container; one syringe must never serve two patients, not even with a fresh needle fitted, and not even through a length of IV tubing. Reusing a syringe across patients is on the CDC's list of practices that have caused outbreaks of viral, bacterial and fungal infection, and the rule does not depend on what is known about the first patient.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 · CMA E.3.b (both outlines) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: After the explanation a patient nods and holds out his arm, then says 'Wait, I don't want this.' The needle has not touched him. Per WHO step 2?
opciones: Stop; the patient may refuse the test at any time before the blood is taken
Proceed, because verbal consent was already given when he offered the arm
Proceed if the ordering clinician confirms by telephone that the test is needed
Ask him to sign a refusal form first; until then the consent still stands
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 says to discuss the test, obtain verbal consent, and remember that the patient has the right to refuse at any time before the blood sampling, which is why the WHO insists that the patient understand the procedure. An earlier nod does not lock the patient in, a clinician's wish does not override the refusal, and no paperwork is a precondition for stopping.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1; and Section 3.1.1, Choice of gauge
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which needle gauge range does WHO Table 3.1 reserve for blood donation, and why does a larger gauge apply?
opciones: 16 to 18 G; collection for transfusion needs a larger gauge than blood drawing
21 to 22 G; the standard adult phlebotomy needles are used for donation as well
19 to 20 G; the intermediate sizes are set aside for donor collection only
23 G; a small needle protects the donor's vein during a long collection
preguntas.explicacion: Table 3.1 ticks 16 to 18 G for adults in the blood donation column, and Section 3.1.1 explains that collecting blood for transfusion calls for a wider gauge than drawing a sample does. The 21 and 22 G needles are the adult phlebotomy sizes, 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable, and 23 G is the small-vein and butterfly size.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Basic Communication Concepts
preguntas.subtema: Communication cycle · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2E k23 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Effective communication needs a sender, a clear message and a receiver. What completes the cycle?
opciones: A feedback message the receiver returns to the sender
A written note the sender files once the exchange ends
A second message the sender repeats until there is a reaction
A witness who confirms the receiver decoded the words
preguntas.explicacion: The exchange runs from a sender, through a clear and concise message, to a receiver who decodes and interprets it; the receiver then sends a feedback message back. Without that return leg the sender never learns how the message landed. Repeating the message or charting it is not feedback.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: HCG in urine (003619), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Urine pregnancy specimen · CPT D4 4G · PBT V.D.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.10.d.(4) · RMA III.C.4.b · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: Which urine specimen is best for a urine hCG pregnancy test, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because it is the most concentrated and holds enough hormone
The first void of the morning, because overnight urine is the most dilute of the whole day
A specimen taken 2 hours after a large drink, because dilution reduces false-positive results
A midstream clean-catch taken at any hour, because the hormone level does not vary at all
preguntas.explicacion: Human chorionic gonadotropin is produced during pregnancy and detected in urine. The first specimen of the day is usually best because it is the most concentrated and therefore carries enough hormone to be picked up. The patient voids into a sterile cup, or with a home kit dips the strip or passes it through the stream, following the package directions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Patient Abandonment, Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: No-show policy · CCMA 5 k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · CMAA 4F k60 · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has missed six scheduled appointments in a row. Before the practice ends the relationship, what does the ethical guidance expect?
opciones: Efforts to repair the relationship, all of them documented in the record
An immediate dismissal letter, since repeated no-shows end the relationship by themselves
A referral to the health plan, which decides whether the patient may be dismissed
A written waiver from the patient releasing the practice from any further duty of care
preguntas.explicacion: Ethically, dismissal comes only after the clinician has asked whether everything possible was tried to mend the relationship: talking through what the patient needs and expects, agreeing reasonable goals together, and working on expectations that are unrealistic. All of that belongs in the record. Repeated noncompliance with treatment and with follow-up appointments agreed beforehand is one of the grounds on which a patient may lawfully be dismissed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Unsecured Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Unsecured PHI · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A laptop holding the appointment schedule is stolen from a car. Notification is required only if the information was unsecured. What makes it secured?
opciones: Encryption or destruction as specified in the Secretary's guidance
A password on the operating system that the thief would have to guess
Storage on a device the practice had listed in its inventory of equipment
A remote lock the practice can apply to the device after it goes missing
preguntas.explicacion: Notice is owed only where the PHI involved was unsecured: information that was never made unusable, unreadable or otherwise indecipherable to people without authorization, by a technology or methodology the Secretary names in guidance. Encryption and destruction are what that guidance names. Secure the information the way it describes and the duty to notify after a breach of it falls away.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CCMA 6 k198 communication cycle · CMA II.F.3.a level of understanding
preguntas.pregunta: What does the chunk-and-check approach to teach-back mean in practice?
opciones: Break the information into small pieces and have the patient teach each piece back
Wait until the end of the visit and have the patient teach the whole plan back once
Hand over the printed sheet first and have the patient read the key lines out loud
Ask the patient to repeat each sentence using the same words that were used to say it
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back is not saved for the door. Information is broken into small segments, each one is taught back, and only then does the next segment start. Reading a handout aloud or parroting the words back does not show understanding, so patients may consult the handout but must answer in their own words.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is surprised that she owes nothing for a screening the office carried out. Why is that, under Part B?
opciones: Most preventive services cost nothing when the provider accepts assignment
Preventive services are paid for under Part A rather than under Part B
The yearly Part B deductible is waived for every service she is given
A Medigap policy pays for preventive services in full for every enrollee
preguntas.explicacion: Part B helps cover two kinds of service: those that are medically necessary, meaning they meet accepted standards of practice to diagnose or treat a condition, and preventive ones meant to stop illness or catch it early. The patient pays nothing for most preventive services when they come from a provider who accepts assignment.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Habilitation Services and Rehabilitation Services
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A toddler who is not yet walking or talking at the expected age is referred for therapy. Which benefit covers that?
opciones: Habilitation, which helps her gain skills she has not had
Rehabilitation, which helps her regain skills she has lost
Preventive care, which looks for a problem before symptoms
Skilled nursing care, performed or supervised by a nurse
preguntas.explicacion: Habilitation services help someone hold on to, learn or better the skills and the functioning that daily life asks for, and the therapy for a child who is not walking or talking on time is the example the federal glossary gives. Rehabilitation is for skills lost or impaired through illness, injury or disability. Both may be delivered by the same therapists.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Anaphylaxis", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 k82 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient having a severe allergic reaction is short of breath and hoarse. Which action is wrong?
opciones: Giving the patient an antihistamine tablet with a little water
Injecting the emergency epinephrine the patient carries in a bag
Calling the emergency number while another person stays with them
Laying the patient flat and raising the feet about 12 inches (30 cm)
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing goes into the mouth of someone who is having trouble breathing, so an oral tablet is out. A hoarse or whispered voice, or coarse sounds on breathing in, warns of dangerous throat swelling. Injectable or intranasal epinephrine is used at the start of the reaction, without waiting to see whether it worsens, and help is called.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, 3.2 Cultural Diversity and Cultural Humility
preguntas.subtema: Cultural competence · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2C k17 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What does cultural humility add to cultural competence?
opciones: A lifelong stance that challenges one's own biases
A checklist of the traits of each group being served
A single training session that certifies the worker
A rule that care always follows the patient's beliefs
preguntas.explicacion: Cultural competence is a lifelong business of applying evidence-based practice in agreement with a patient's values, beliefs, worldview and practices. Cultural humility is the attitude beside it: challenging your own biases, accepting that you cannot know everything about another culture, and keeping at it for life.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Acetaminophen: How should this medicine be used?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k18 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(vi) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether an extended-release tablet can be cut in half to make it easier to swallow. What is the answer?
opciones: No: an extended-release tablet is swallowed whole, never split, chewed or crushed
Yes: splitting is allowed as long as both halves are taken within the same hour
Yes: splitting is allowed because the coating on the tablet controls the release
No: but the tablet may be crushed and stirred into food if it is not chewed first
preguntas.explicacion: Extended-release tablets are swallowed whole; they are not split, chewed, crushed or dissolved, because the form is what spreads the release out over hours. A patient who cannot swallow a tablet may have other forms available instead. An orally disintegrating tablet is a different form altogether, made to dissolve quickly in the mouth, and a chewable tablet is meant to be chewed.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a colonoscopy and a barium enema. Which ending marks the study in which the colon is looked at directly?
opciones: -scopy, the ending that means examining
-graphy, the ending that means recording
-metry, the ending that means measuring
-centesis, the ending that means puncture
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic endings say how the information is obtained. The pair -scope and -scopy is for looking at a structure; -gram, -graph and -graphy are for recording an image or a tracing; -meter and -metry are for measuring; and -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid. Only the first involves a direct look.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.i · CMA I.A.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: Only one crutch has been prescribed. On which side is it carried, and what moves with it?
opciones: On the uninjured side, and it advances together with the injured leg
On the injured side, and it advances together with the injured leg
On the uninjured side, and it advances together with the sound leg
On the injured side, and it advances just before the sound leg moves
preguntas.explicacion: The single crutch is positioned on the side of the uninjured lower limb. The crutch and the injured leg go forward together, and then the uninjured leg follows while the crutch takes the user's weight. The crutch and the weak leg working as a pair is what keeps the load off the injury.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection steps 4 and 5
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen identification · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 · CCMA 3E k127 chain of custody · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: How is the donor identified at a federal drug test collection site?
opciones: With a photo identification, and the collector identifies themself on request
With a photo identification, which the collector photocopies for the file
With two spoken identifiers, name and date of birth, matched to the order
With the employer representative vouching for the donor at the door
preguntas.explicacion: The collector checks who the donor is against a photo ID and, if asked, has to show identification back, an employee badge or an entry on an employee list. Two spoken identifiers are the rule for a clinical draw such as a blood culture, not for this collection, and the procedure starts without delay even if the employer's representative has not turned up.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth staffing · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which staffing question does HHS tell a practice to settle before it starts offering telehealth?
opciones: Whether new roles are needed, such as a telehealth coordinator and an IT lead
Whether the clinicians will accept a reduced fee for every virtual encounter
Whether the practice will stop offering in-person visits once telehealth begins
Whether the vendor will take over the front desk duties during virtual visits
preguntas.explicacion: The factors to consider before offering telehealth include whether additional staff or new roles are needed, such as a telehealth coordinator and an IT lead; how existing roles change, front desk personnel and patient intake among them; whether staff are ready and committed; how the team will be prepared and trained; and whether the platform is easy to use and integrates with the electronic health record.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Right Ventricle; Heart Valve Structure and Function; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart, Pathway of Blood through the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Trace a drop of blood returning from the arm. From the right atrium it passes through which valve, and into which chamber?
opciones: The tricuspid valve, into the right ventricle
The mitral valve, into the left ventricle
The pulmonary valve, into the pulmonary trunk
The bicuspid valve, into the right ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: Systemic blood enters the right atrium from the venae cavae, passes the right atrioventricular (tricuspid) valve into the right ventricle, is pumped through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk to the lungs, returns to the left atrium, crosses the mitral (bicuspid) valve into the left ventricle and leaves through the aortic valve. The bicuspid valve is on the left side only.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Challenges of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to open access · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: The manager of a practice about to move to open access asks where the resistance usually comes from. What does the guide answer?
opciones: Mainly from belief: the model feels counter-intuitive and staff doubt the resources can meet demand
Mainly from logistics: few record systems support same-day booking without an expensive rebuild
Mainly from patients, who prefer appointments fixed weeks ahead so they can plan around them
Mainly from payers, who will not reimburse a visit that was booked on the day it took place
preguntas.explicacion: The barriers called primary are psychological rather than logistical. To clinicians and staff alike the approach seems unintuitive and runs against their own experience of scheduling, and it asks them to abandon the ingrained idea that routine care can wait. On top of that, clinical and administrative staff are typically sceptical that existing resources can meet the demand.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A syndrome documented in the record has no guidance for it in the alphabetic index. How is it coded?
opciones: By coding the manifestations the record documents
By coding the unspecified code of that category
By coding the symptom that brought the patient in
By coding the etiology alone, with no other code
preguntas.explicacion: Syndromes are coded by following the guidance of the alphabetic index. Where the index offers none, codes are assigned for the manifestations that are documented, and a manifestation that falls outside the disease process itself may take an additional code where the condition has no unique code of its own.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Head circumference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.c
preguntas.pregunta: How is an infant's head circumference measured?
opciones: A tape is passed over the brows and the ears and round behind the head
A tape is passed at the level of the eyebrows and under the ears to the chin
A tape is passed over the crown from ear to ear and the two halves are added
A tape is passed around the widest part of the forehead only, above the eyes
preguntas.explicacion: The measurement follows the largest circumference of the head: over the brows and the ears and round behind. A nonstretchable tape is pulled snug enough to compress the hair. The value is compared with the child's own earlier measurements and with the normal range for that sex and age.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Preparing for Testing; CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Preparing the Testing Area, Test Materials, and Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Reagents to room temperature · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.d · RMA III.C.3.f
preguntas.pregunta: Rapid test kits and their controls are taken straight from the refrigerator to run a patient sample. What does good practice call for first?
opciones: Allow the refrigerated reagents, kits and sample to reach room temperature before testing
Warm the reagents briefly in a water bath so the reaction is not slowed by the cold
Run the test at once, since reagents are most stable right out of the refrigerator
Discard the kit, because a refrigerated kit cannot be used at room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Test kits, patient samples and reagents kept in the refrigerator are given time to reach room temperature before testing where the insert says so. Extremes of temperature degrade reagents, alter reaction times and can bring on premature expiration, so the storage and operating ranges in the insert govern. Warming devices and shortcuts are not in the guidance; waiting is.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts; Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with untreated diabetes is passing very large amounts of urine, charted as polyuria. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning many or excessive plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning few or little plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
A prefix meaning many or excessive plus a root meaning kidney
preguntas.explicacion: Poly- means many or excessive and -uria means in the urine, so the term says there is a great deal of it. The opposites sit in the same lists: olig- and oligo- are few or little, and a- or an- is without, which is the part that turns the word into anuria. The kidney itself is nephr- or ren-, not part of this term.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Deep Nasal Swab
preguntas.subtema: Deep nasal swab · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: Which technique describes a deep nasal swab?
opciones: Insert less than one inch until resistance at the turbinates, rotate several times, repeat in the other nostril
Insert less than one inch until resistance at the turbinates, hold still 10 seconds, and use a new swab per nostril
Insert to the depth of the ear opening, rotate several times, then repeat in the other nostril
Insert less than one inch and withdraw at once, then place the swab tip into a dry sterile tube
preguntas.explicacion: With the head tilted back 70 degrees, the swab is gently rotated as it goes in, stopping under an inch when resistance is met at the turbinates. It is rotated several times against the nasal wall and the same swab is then used in the other nostril. The tip goes into a viral transport tube and the applicator stick is cut off. The ear-opening depth belongs to the nasopharyngeal swab.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Myocardial Infarction", Introduction and Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027 I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes retrosternal pressure spreading to the jaw and left arm, with sweating and nausea. Which findings confirm the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: Electrocardiographic changes together with a rise in cardiac troponin
Electrocardiographic changes together with a rise in blood urea nitrogen
A chest radiograph together with a rise in the white blood cell count
A rise in cardiac troponin together with a fall in the hemoglobin level
preguntas.explicacion: Myocardial infarction is death of heart muscle from a prolonged lack of oxygen, most often from plaque rupture with clot on top. The discomfort is diffuse pressure or tightness behind the sternum that can travel to shoulders, arms, neck, jaw or upper abdomen. History and examination alone may not settle it: the diagnosis combines the story with the ECG and a high-sensitivity troponin.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Hypothermia", Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Below which body temperature is a patient hypothermic?
opciones: Below 95 °F (35 °C), which is a dangerously low temperature
Below 97 °F (36.1 °C), the lower end of the normal band
Below 93 °F (33.9 °C), when shivering has already stopped
Below 90 °F (32.2 °C), when the pulse becomes hard to find at all
preguntas.explicacion: Hypothermia is a body temperature under 95 °F, or 35 °C. Cold injuries of the limbs are separate: frostbite is the commonest freezing injury, while trench foot and immersion foot come from cold wet conditions and chilblains from cold dry ones. Someone found motionless in the cold is never assumed to be dead.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: Nobody read the refrigerator thermometer over a long holiday weekend and the log has three empty rows. What should the person filling it in on Monday do?
opciones: Leave those rows blank, because there is no temperature data for them
Enter the Monday reading in the blank rows and initial each of them
Enter the average of the readings before and after the gap
Enter the acceptable range midpoint and note that the site was closed
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is blunt: if a reading was missed and no temperature data exist for that stretch, the entry stays blank, and nobody invents or guesses what the reading would have been. Where weekends or closures are foreseeable, the answer is a data logger that records minimum and maximum values, not a log filled in afterwards from memory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Drug Addiction Screening", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k45 · CMA I.A.5.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which four questions make up the CAGE screen?
opciones: Cutting down, being annoyed by criticism, guilt, and a morning eye-opener
Cutting down, craving, guilt, and drinking more than six on one occasion
How often, how many on a typical day, six or more at once, and guilt
Cutting down, tremor, nausea and vomiting, and a morning eye-opener
preguntas.explicacion: Each yes scores one point out of four. The screen loses sensitivity in milder cases, and when there is time for a longer interview the alcohol use disorders identification test is used instead: how often a drink was taken this past year, how many on a typical drinking day, and how often six or more went down on one occasion.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Amputation - traumatic", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a severed fingertip wrapped in a paper towel. How is the amputated part kept?
opciones: In a clean damp cloth, inside a sealed bag, set in a bath of ice water
In a clean damp cloth, packed directly in crushed ice inside a cup
In a sealed bag of sterile saline, with the bag resting on dry ice
In a dry sterile dressing, kept warm next to the patient's body
preguntas.explicacion: The severed part is rinsed gently if the cut end is dirty, wrapped in a clean damp cloth, put in a sealed plastic bag and set in ice water. It never goes straight into water or onto ice, and dry ice is not used because it freezes and injures the tissue. Cooling widens the window for reattachment, which without cooling is about 4 to 6 hours.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Warm-site activation · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An unplanned outage has lasted an hour and a half with no end in sight. What does the downtime policy ideally say about the backup site?
opciones: The warm-site process should be started before two hours of unavailability pass
The warm-site process should be started once eight hours of records pile up
The warm-site process waits until the vendor confirms the outage is unplanned
The warm-site process is reserved for outages announced ahead of time by IT
preguntas.explicacion: The policy is expected to say when the warm-site backup process gets activated, and the guidance puts that trigger ideally before two hours of unplanned unavailability have gone by. The eight hours elsewhere in the same guide belong to a different practice: the stock of paper forms each care area keeps.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Non-Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient meets her state's Medicaid income limit but has just moved in from another state. Which non-financial rule applies to her?
opciones: She must be a resident of the state whose Medicaid program is paying for her care
She must have lived in the state for a full year before an application is accepted
She must apply first in the state she came from and ask for the file to be moved
She must be enrolled in a Marketplace plan while the new application is decided
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside the financial rules, Medicaid applicants have to satisfy non-financial criteria: a beneficiary must generally live in the state whose program covers her, and must be a citizen of the United States or a qualified non-citizen of certain kinds, a lawful permanent resident for example. Some eligibility groups narrow further by age, or by pregnancy or parenting status.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Code Sets Overview
preguntas.subtema: Code sets · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which code sets did HIPAA adopt for use in standard health care transactions?
opciones: ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, dental procedure codes and national drug codes
ICD-10 and CPT only, since the other sets are used inside each practice
ICD-10, HCPCS and the place of service codes each contractor publishes
ICD-10, HCPCS and the adjustment reason codes payers use on remittances
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets named in the HIPAA regulations classify diagnoses, procedures, tests, treatments, equipment and supplies, and they are ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, the code on dental procedures, and the national drug codes. Place of service codes identify where care happened, and adjustment reason codes explain payment decisions; neither is a medical data code set.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Issues of Concern: Relevant Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Competency vs capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A coworker says a patient with dementia "is not competent to sign." What is accurate about that word?
opciones: Competence is a legal finding a judge makes; the bedside call is capacity
Competence is the bedside finding; capacity is what a court declares later
Competence and capacity are one finding, made by any licensed staff member
Competence is presumed lost once a dementia diagnosis appears in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: Competence is about being able to take part in legal proceedings. It is presumed, and disproving it takes a hearing with evidence before a judge; clinicians never make that call. What the clinical team assesses is capacity: whether this patient can make this decision, now, in this situation. A dementia diagnosis does not by itself remove capacity.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Vacuum-tube systems and Manually retractable evacuated tube systems
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k55 3D · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A vacuum-tube system is being used on a small child. What adjustment does the WHO device table call for, and why?
opciones: A smaller tube with reduced vacuum (1 to 5 ml), to reduce hemolysis
A larger tube with full vacuum, so the sample is collected before the vein collapses
A butterfly set with a discard tube, to remove the air from the tubing
A 16 to 18 G needle, so the tube fills before the tourniquet limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 says that with vacuum systems a smaller tube whose vacuum is lower is what a pediatric patient gets, and for retractable evacuated systems specifies a 1 to 5 ml tube with lower vacuum to reduce hemolysis. The discard tube is the butterfly rule for air in the tubing, and 16 to 18 G is the blood donation gauge in Table 3.1, far too large for a child.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Repetitive or Continuous Non-covered Care
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: The office realizes no advance written notice went out before the first sessions of a repeated non-covered treatment. What can it do now?
opciones: Issue one now, though the earlier sessions stay the provider's cost
Issue one now and date it back to the first session of the course
Issue one now and bill her for the whole course of that treatment
Skip the notice, since the chance to shift liability has gone
preguntas.explicacion: A notice may be issued at any point during a course of repetitive care that started without one. What it cannot do is reach backwards: it may not be dated back, and the care given before it was delivered stays the financial responsibility of the provider or supplier. From the delivery of the notice onward the liability can be transferred.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, BMI Frequently Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A 7-year-old girl's body mass index is at the 88th percentile for her age and sex. How is that read?
opciones: Overweight: the band runs from the 85th to below the 95th percentile
Obesity: the band starts once the 85th percentile has been reached
Healthy weight: the band runs from the 5th to below the 95th percentile
Overweight: the band runs from the 75th to below the 90th percentile
preguntas.explicacion: Children from 2 through 19 are compared with others of the same age and sex rather than with fixed adult numbers. A percentile of 88 means the value equals or exceeds that of 88% of the reference group, and the overweight band runs from the 85th to below the 95th. Obesity starts at the 95th percentile.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Evaluating a new device · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Before a hospital adopts a new safety needle across its draw stations, what must the product evaluation show?
opciones: That the feature works reliably, staff accept it, and patient care does not suffer
That the device costs no more than the one it replaces over a full year
That the manufacturer has registered and listed it with the federal agency
That the injury rate has already fallen in the department that will use it
preguntas.explicacion: Three points settle whether a device with a safety feature is adopted: does the feature work reliably and effectively, will the worker who has to use it accept it, and does patient care come to no harm. The recommended process adds training in the new device, clear written criteria, on-site follow-up for informal feedback, and monitoring after implementation. Registration and listing are what the manufacturer owes the device regulator, not what the evaluation measures.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.3 Gross Anatomy of the Kidney
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(7) (2027 I.C.6.f(7)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A frontal section of a kidney is described as having an outer and an inner region. What are they called?
opciones: The renal cortex on the outside and the medulla on the inside
The medulla on the outside and the renal cortex on the inside
The renal pelvis on the outside and the renal columns inside
The renal capsule on the outside and the renal calyces inside
preguntas.explicacion: Cut in a frontal plane, into front and back halves, the kidney shows an outer renal cortex and an inner medulla. Connective tissue renal columns run down from the cortex through the medulla and separate the renal pyramids, and the papillae at their tips are bundles of collecting ducts that deliver urine to the calyces. An adrenal gland sits on top of each kidney.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Rapid Influenza Diagnostic Tests: Information for Clinicians, Advantages and disadvantages of RIDTs; Accuracy of the test compared to a reference test
preguntas.subtema: RIDT sensitivity · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.d.(6) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: During a week of very high influenza activity, a febrile patient with cough and body aches has a negative rapid influenza diagnostic test (RIDT). How should the result be weighed?
opciones: A false negative is likely; RIDT sensitivity is only about 50 to 70 %, and misses are most common when flu activity is high
The negative is reliable; RIDT specificity is high, which means negatives are rarely wrong when flu is circulating widely
A false negative is unlikely, because false negatives occur mainly when influenza activity in the community is low
The test should be repeated with the same kit after 15 minutes, since RIDTs need two negative readings to be valid
preguntas.explicacion: Rapid influenza diagnostic tests give results in under 15 minutes but have low to moderate sensitivity, generally 50 to 70 % against RT-PCR, so false negatives are common, and especially so when influenza activity is high. Specificity is high, which protects positives; false positives occur mainly when activity is low. A negative RIDT in a symptomatic patient during peak season does not exclude influenza, and molecular testing may be used.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Types of health care providers: Specialty care
preguntas.subtema: Identifying medical specialties · CCMA 1A k7 · CMA II.F.4.d / 2027 II.F.2.d
preguntas.pregunta: A chart shows worsening kidney function and the provider wants a referral. Which specialty fits?
opciones: Nephrology, the specialty for disorders of the kidneys
Urology, the specialty for the urinary tract and male organs
Endocrinology, the specialty for hormonal and metabolic disorders
Hematology, the specialty for disorders of the blood
preguntas.explicacion: Nephrology treats kidney disorders. Urology covers disorders of the male reproductive system and of the urinary tract; endocrinology deals with disorders that are hormonal and metabolic, diabetes among them; hematology takes blood disorders. The primary care provider refers to these specialties when a problem goes past the common medical conditions handled in the office.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.1 Eligibility Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: Is a resting tracing recorded on a patient with cognitive impairment?
opciones: Yes: nobody is automatically excluded from the test
No: the patient cannot follow the instructions given
Yes, but only if a relative holds the arms still for it
No, unless a provider stays in the room during the run
preguntas.explicacion: The eligibility rules say plainly that there are no automatic exclusions and that patients with cognitive impairment should have the recording done. What is asked of every patient still applies: relax, breathe normally and stay still without talking.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia" (2025), sections Continuing Education Activity and Introduction; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is 155,000 per microliter. Below what count would this be called thrombocytopenia, and where is about a third of the body's platelets kept?
opciones: Below 150,000 per µL; about one third is stored in the spleen
Below 150,000 per µL; about one third is stored in the liver
Below 100,000 per µL; about one third is stored in the spleen
Below 50,000 per µL; about one third stays in the red marrow
preguntas.explicacion: In adults the line for thrombocytopenia is drawn at a count under 150,000 per microliter, so 155,000 sits just above it; mild cases run from 100,000 up to that line, moderate from 50,000 to 100,000, and severe below 50,000. Once platelets reach the circulation, roughly a third of them move to the spleen, which keeps them until a vessel tears. The liver and the red marrow are not that store.

preguntas.subtema: Compound authorizations · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants one signed form to release both a patient's psychotherapy notes and the rest of her chart. What does the compound authorization rule allow?
opciones: Nothing of the sort: notes of that kind travel only with an authorization of their own
One form, as long as the two kinds of record are listed under separate headings
One form, as long as the patient initials the psychotherapy section separately
One form, as long as neither release is a condition of her continuing treatment
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization may not be combined with another document to make a compound authorization except in the cases the rule sets out. One of them is narrow: an authorization for psychotherapy notes may be combined only with another authorization for psychotherapy notes. Research permissions are the other main exception.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Can I drink anything besides water, and What if I make a mistake
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a fasting glucose says he skipped breakfast but had a coffee with sugar an hour ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: He has broken the fast; tell the provider, since the test may need rescheduling
Coffee does not count as food, so the draw may proceed as a fasting sample
Proceed and mark the sample 'non-fasting' only if he also ate solid food
Wait one more hour so the sugar clears, then draw it as a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting means no food or drink except plain water; juice, coffee, soda and other beverages get into the bloodstream and affect results, and a patient who eats or drinks before the test should tell the provider because the test may have to be rescheduled. A fasting glucose needs at least 8 hours without caloric intake, not one more hour.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.D.2.f
preguntas.pregunta: A gloved assistant turns away from the sterile field to answer a question at the doorway, then turns back. What must be assumed?
opciones: The field is contaminated, because supplies not directly monitored count as unsterile
The field is intact, because the assistant did not touch the drape at any moment
The field is intact, because the door stayed shut and nobody entered the room
The field is contaminated only below waist level, where the assistant's back was turned
preguntas.explicacion: Any field or supplies the practitioner has not kept in direct view are counted as contaminated, whether the reason is turning away or leaving the room. The same reasoning makes an unattended field unusable: someone may have contaminated it without anyone seeing. That is why fields are established as close to the procedure time as possible.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote c
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A chemistry panel gives results the clinician cannot explain, and the tube was set down without being inverted. What does the table warn about?
opciones: Blood not thoroughly mixed with its additive can give erroneous results
Blood not mixed with its additive loses the vacuum it was drawn under
Blood left unmixed separates into serum before it reaches the laboratory
Blood left unmixed cools too quickly and the additive stops working at all
preguntas.explicacion: The footnote to the order-of-draw table asks for additive tubes to be inverted gently and warns that erroneous results may follow if blood and additive are not properly combined. The movement described elsewhere is a figure-of-8, and it is done as soon as the tube comes off the needle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Issues of Concern (recapping and disposal); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: The sharps container in a drawing station is full to the top, so a phlebotomist sets the used needle on the tray to dispose of it later. Which risks are being ignored?
opciones: Injuries happen when sharps containers are overfilled and when used needles are not placed in them immediately
The needle should have been recapped with two hands and left on the tray until a container was available
The needle should have gone into the regulated-waste bag, since bags are acceptable whenever containers are full
There is no added risk once the safety feature is activated, so the delay is acceptable
preguntas.explicacion: Used needles go straight into an approved sharps container kept close to the point of use; injuries also happen when a needle ends up in an ordinary waste bag, or when a container is filled past the line or handled badly. Recapping as a routine is no longer advised, because handling a used needle is what raises the risk of a puncture, and the WHO requires the container to be within arm's reach and clearly visible.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A child arrives with one leg in a cast and the parent asks for the usual growth measurements. What does the technique call for?
opciones: The numbers taken now may mislead, so they are not forced in this state
The numbers are taken anyway and the weight of the cast subtracted later
The numbers are contraindicated in any child with a limb deformity
The numbers are taken and plotted on a chart drawn for injured children
preguntas.explicacion: Body measurements are noninvasive and carry no true contraindication, but there are states in which the figure will not mean what it appears to mean: acute illness, a limb deformity, a cast. A height or a weight taken then can be falsely reassuring or falsely alarming, so the measurement is better postponed than plotted.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Collection methods · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Several tubes are needed from one venipuncture. Which system does the WHO's Step 7 say to use, and what if it is not available?
opciones: Vacuum tubes with a needle and a tube holder; failing that, a syringe or a winged set
A syringe, because it lets the phlebotomist control the pressure; otherwise evacuated tubes
