opciones: Water-soluble vitamins are not stored and leave in the urine
Water-soluble vitamins are stored in muscle and used up faster
Water-soluble vitamins are destroyed by stomach acid within hours
Water-soluble vitamins are absorbed only when dietary fat is present
preguntas.explicacion: The nine water-soluble vitamins, vitamin C and the whole B complex, are not kept in the body; whatever is left over leaves in the urine, so they have to be eaten regularly to avoid a shortage. Vitamin B12 is the exception that can be held in the liver for years. Fat is what helps the fat-soluble group get absorbed.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment, Tips for communicating with a patient who has cognitive impairment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 k49 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6) · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia looks unsure who you are as you set out the tray. What does the guidance advise?
opciones: Explain once more who you are and what the visit will involve
Ask the caregiver to introduce you, then begin without further delay
Begin the draw quickly, since explanations add to the confusion
Postpone the draw until a family member is able to attend in person
preguntas.explicacion: Among the tips for talking with someone whose cognition is impaired: address the patient directly, in simple wording, one idea at a time, and help orient them by saying again who you are and what is about to happen. The patient is also reassured that their answers are not being judged.

preguntas.subtema: Workstation use · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A policy states which programs may be run at the front desk computer, how they are to be used and how the desk is laid out. Which standard is that?
opciones: Workstation use, which sets the functions, the manner of use and the surroundings
Workstation security, the physical guard that limits a machine to authorized users
Access control, the technical limit on who may open which record in the system
Facility access controls, which limit physical entry to where the systems are kept
preguntas.explicacion: Two standards sit side by side. Workstation use calls for policies covering which functions are proper, the manner of carrying them out, and what the physical surroundings of a workstation, or of a class of workstations, should look like. Workstation security is the narrower one: the physical measures that keep an unauthorized person away from the machine.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Nasal Instillation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii)
preguntas.pregunta: How is a nasal spray administered?
opciones: The patient blows the nose, tilts the head back, and one nostril is held closed
The patient blows the nose, leans forward, and both nostrils are sprayed at once
The patient tilts the head back and the tip is pushed in until it meets the septum
The patient lies on one side and the spray goes into the upper nostril only
preguntas.explicacion: Nasal medication is used mostly for allergies, sinus infections and congestion, and clean technique is enough. Tissues are offered and the patient blows the nose, then sits or lies with the head tilted back, looking upward. The tip of the spray bottle or the dropper goes into one nostril while the other is occluded, and the spray is released as the patient breathes in. Gloves and the medication rights apply as always.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Skeletal System: Divisions of the Skeleton; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology: Appendicular Skeleton
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many bones are in the axial skeleton and how many in the appendicular skeleton?
opciones: 80 axial and 126 appendicular
126 axial and 80 appendicular
106 axial and 100 appendicular
60 axial and 146 appendicular
preguntas.explicacion: The skeleton splits in two. The axial part, with 80 bones, is the skull, hyoid, vertebral column and thoracic cage. The appendicular part, with 126, is the limbs plus the pectoral and pelvic girdles that anchor them. The two together give the adult total of 206.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 580: Medical record retention
preguntas.subtema: Safeguards through disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is shredding charts that state law no longer requires it to keep. Does the Privacy Rule have anything to say about that moment?
opciones: Yes, its safeguards run for as long as the information is held, disposal included
No, its safeguards end on the day the state retention period runs out for a chart
Yes, but only if the practice is destroying more than 500 records at one time
No, because destroying a record is a health care operation and needs no safeguard
preguntas.explicacion: HIPAA fixes no retention period for the clinical record itself; State law does. What the Privacy Rule demands is safeguards, administrative and technical and physical, for however long the covered entity holds the information, and it counts disposal as part of that stretch.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Respiratory System: Conducting Passages
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(5) (2027 I.C.6.f(5)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the upper respiratory tract and which the lower?
opciones: Nose, pharynx and larynx above; trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, pharynx and trachea above; larynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose and pharynx above; larynx, trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, larynx and trachea above; pharynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting passages split into an upper tract of nose, pharynx and larynx and a lower tract of trachea, bronchial tree and lungs. All of them communicate with the outside air and carry a mucous membrane lining, with hairs in some regions to filter the air and cilia in others to move mucus along.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), If an Exposure Occurs; NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors, Treatment; OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), p. 21
preguntas.subtema: Eye splash first aid · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Blood splashes into a phlebotomist's eye while she uncaps a tube. What is the first thing to do?
opciones: Irrigate the eye with clean water, saline or a sterile irrigant, then report the exposure
Apply an antiseptic eye drop, then complete the incident report before seeking care
Squeeze the eyelids shut and wait for the occupational health nurse to examine it
Flush with a dilute bleach solution, which inactivates bloodborne viruses on contact
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC and NIOSH give the same immediate steps, and they differ by site: soap and water for a needlestick or a cut, plain water for a splash that lands on the nose, the mouth or the skin, and clean water, saline or a sterile irrigant for the eye. Then the exposure is reported to whoever manages exposures, and medical care is sought at once. OSHA's laboratory guidance suggests irrigating eyes and mucous membranes for 15 minutes. The CDC adds that nothing shows antiseptics or squeezing the wound reduce transmission, and that caustic agents such as bleach are not recommended.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Patient Rights under HIPAA
preguntas.subtema: Asking for a correction · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads her record and says one entry is wrong. What right does she have?
opciones: To ask for a correction, which the provider may accept or deny
To have the entry deleted within thirty days of the request
To have the entry rewritten by the clinician who made it
To bill the provider for the time spent finding the mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the rights the privacy rule gives are the right to a notice of privacy practices, to ask that disclosures be restricted, to say how information should be handled and communicated, to inspect and review one's own information and request a change to anything that looks wrong, to obtain a copy, to receive an accounting of disclosures, and to complain to the Office for Civil Rights. The request for a change is a request: the provider may accept or deny it, and a documented diagnosis a patient dislikes is not erased for that reason.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: A newer machine shows muscle tremor that an older one never wrote. How is that read?
opciones: As an advantage: it also writes small P and Q waves
As a fault: the unit needs the biomedical engineer
As a fault: the standardization has drifted upward
As an advantage: it filters the tremor out by itself
preguntas.explicacion: Picking up the tremor is not a defect. A machine able to reproduce those small signals is also able to write the small P and Q waves that less accurate units have missed, so the answer is to settle the patient rather than to blame or replace the equipment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Heart Sounds", Related Testing
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a(1) · RMA III.F.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the mitral valve heard loudest during auscultation of the heart?
opciones: The 5th intercostal space on the left, at the midclavicular line
The 2nd right intercostal space beside the sternal border
The 2nd left intercostal space beside the sternal border
The 4th left intercostal space beside the sternal border
preguntas.explicacion: The four valve areas run in order: aortic in the 2nd right space, pulmonic in the 2nd left, tricuspid in the 4th left, and mitral in the 5th left at the midclavicular line. The first heart sound is the mitral and tricuspid valves closing in systole; the second is the aortic and pulmonic valves closing in diastole.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Burn Classification", Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which burn injuries are on the list of criteria for transfer to a burn center?
opciones: Burns of the face, hands, feet, genitalia or perineum, and any chemical burn
Burns of the trunk only, and any burn with blisters over a joint surface
Burns of the forearm and calf, and any burn that has not healed in 3 weeks
Burns of the scalp only, and any burn a patient cannot dress unaided
preguntas.explicacion: The burn association sets 10 transfer criteria, which take in burns of the face, hands, feet, genitalia and perineum, any full-thickness area, chemical and electrical burns, inhalation injury, and a total body surface area above 10 %. That surface can be figured with the rule of nines, the Lund-Browder chart or the rule of palms.

preguntas.subtema: RMA III.B.1.b · CMA I.C.5.b (2027 I.C.5.a)
preguntas.pregunta: A tracheal bistoury is listed among the ear, nose and throat instruments. What is it?
opciones: A long, narrow surgical knife
A hook that lifts the trachea
A dilator that widens the airway
A tube left after a laryngectomy
preguntas.explicacion: The bistoury of that list is a knife: long and narrow. The tracheal hook, the tracheal dilator and the laryngectomy tube are three separate entries in the same group, which also holds the adenoid curette, the metal tongue depressor, the mouth gag, the tonsil snare and the ear curette.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Coding & Billing Dates of Service
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A service begins one evening and ends the following morning. What does the billing rule say?
opciones: Bill it once it is complete, using the start day or the next one
Bill it twice, once on each of the two calendar dates it spans
Bill it on the day it started, before the service has finished
Bill it on the day the note about it is signed by the provider
preguntas.explicacion: For a service spanning two calendar dates, either the day it started or the day it concluded may be reported unless the instructions say otherwise, and the claim waits until the service is complete. Splitting it into two claims would report work that was done once as though it had been done twice.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene · CPT D3 3A · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist washes her hands between patients. How long should that last, and which parts are easy to miss?
opciones: At least thirty seconds, covering the wrists and between the fingers
At least ten seconds, covering the palms and the backs of the hands
At least two minutes, covering the forearms as far as the elbows
At least thirty seconds, covering the fingertips and the nails only
preguntas.explicacion: The infection control table asks for hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub, washing carefully for at least thirty seconds and including the wrists and the spaces between the fingers. The pairing instruction on the other side of the table is simply not to forget to clean the hands.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2, Infection prevention and control practices
preguntas.subtema: Exposure incidents and post-exposure follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist sustains a needlestick from a used needle. According to the WHO's infection prevention table, what is the time limit after which post-exposure prophylaxis is no longer effective?
opciones: 72 hours
24 hours
48 hours
7 days
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.2 of the WHO guideline pairs each practice with its opposite. On the Do side: report any needle or sharps injury at once, seek help, and start post-exposure prophylaxis as soon as possible following the local protocol. On the Do-not side: do not put off PEP after contact with potentially contaminated material, because past 72 hours it no longer works. The lesson for the exam is twofold: report at once, and the window is three days, not one day and not a week.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate"; Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Tube orientation in ESR · PBT IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.b.(3) · RMA III.C.4.b.iii
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR rack was bumped and the Westergren tube stood tilted about 3° off vertical during the hour. What effect does this have?
opciones: Tilting raises the ESR; an angle of 3° can increase the value by as much as 30 %
Tilting lowers the ESR, because the red cells slide along the glass and settle more slowly
Tilting has no measurable effect as long as the reading is taken at exactly 60 minutes
Tilting affects only the Wintrobe method, whose shorter tube is more sensitive to inclination
preguntas.explicacion: The Westergren ESR is the distance red cells settle in a vertical tube after one hour, reported in millimeters per hour. Tube tilt and vibration falsely elevate the result, and an inclination of 3° from vertical can raise the ESR by up to 30 %. Elevated room temperature and direct sunlight also increase it, and air bubbles from an underfilled tube add to the error. Delay in setting up the test has the opposite effect and lowers the value.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Testicular self-exam — How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: When is a testicular self-exam most easily performed?
opciones: Standing, during or just after a shower, when the scrotal skin is relaxed
Lying down, first thing in the morning, before the scrotal skin has warmed
Standing, before a shower, so that the skin stays dry and easier to grip
Sitting, at the end of the day, when the scrotum hangs at its lowest point
preguntas.explicacion: Warm, relaxed scrotal skin is what makes the testicle easy to feel, so during or after a shower, standing up, is the moment to teach. One hand steadies the testicle while the fingers and thumb of the other cover the whole surface firmly but gently, and then the other side is checked the same way.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), File Proper & Timely Claims
preguntas.subtema: Insurance fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k180
preguntas.pregunta: What can follow from repeatedly giving Medicare inaccurate information about a patient's other health coverage?
opciones: A fine, where the inaccurate information is given knowingly, willfully and repeatedly
A fine, wherever the inaccurate information leads Medicare to pay as the primary payer
Exclusion from the program, where the inaccurate information is given more than once
Recovery of the payment alone, since the responsibility rests with the primary payer
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law lets Medicare take back what it paid wrongly as the primary payer, and the provider has to give it up. On top of that, a provider who gives inaccurate information about a patient's other health insurance coverage knowingly, willfully and repeatedly can be fined. Recovery may also be pursued directly from a primary payer, from another entity or from a third payer.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antihistamines", Indications and Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.a · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: An older adult asks why the provider chose cetirizine instead of diphenhydramine for allergic rhinitis. What is the reason?
opciones: Second-generation agents barely enter the brain, so they sedate less and go first
First-generation agents barely enter the brain, so they suit a driver on therapy
Second-generation agents block H2 receptors, so they settle the stomach as well
First-generation agents are the guideline choice once drowsiness has worn off
preguntas.explicacion: First-generation H1 antagonists are lipophilic and cross into the brain, so they bring sedation, slowed reaction times and anticholinergic trouble: dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, blurred vision. Second-generation agents stay peripheral, and guidelines put them first for allergic rhinitis and urticaria. In older adults the risk of falls and of cognitive decline has narrowed the use of diphenhydramine.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(8), Workplace labeling
preguntas.subtema: Portable containers · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist pours a bleach solution from a labeled jug into a basin she will use and empty during her own shift. Must she label the basin?
opciones: No: a portable container for her own immediate use is exempt
No: containers under one liter are exempt from workplace labels
Yes: every container in the work area needs the full label
Yes: unless the jug's own label is carried alongside the basin
preguntas.explicacion: No label is required on a portable container filled from a labeled one when whoever did the pouring means to use it right away herself. The exemption is narrow, and it turns on that immediate personal use rather than on the size of the container: a bottle filled for the next shift, or for somebody else, falls straight back under the workplace labeling rule. Drugs a pharmacy dispenses for direct administration are exempt as well.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Lactose intolerance — Causes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 food intolerance · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(e) · RMA I.A.2 disorders
preguntas.pregunta: What causes the symptoms of lactose intolerance?
opciones: Too little of the enzyme lactase to digest the sugar in milk
An immune reaction to the protein in cow's milk and dairy foods
Too little stomach acid to break down the fat in dairy products
Damage to the small intestine caused by the gluten in malted milk
preguntas.explicacion: Lactose is the sugar of milk and dairy foods, and the enzyme lactase is what digests it. Infants make lactase for breast milk; production may fall off later, which is why the problem is common in adults. An illness or surgery involving the small intestine can also lower how much lactase is made.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi), (d)(3)(vii) and (d)(3)(viii), Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Removing PPE before leaving · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and heads to the cafeteria still wearing her gloves and lab coat. What does the standard require?
opciones: All PPE must be removed before leaving the work area and placed in a designated container
Gloves must be removed, but the lab coat may be worn out if it is not visibly soiled
PPE may be worn out if hands are washed first with soap and running water
PPE may be worn out if it is penetrated by blood, so long as it is changed within the shift
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(vii) has all personal protective equipment come off before the employee leaves the work area, and (d)(3)(viii) sends what comes off to a designated container or area, there to be stored, washed, decontaminated or discarded. Every item is covered, the coat included, and visible soiling has nothing to do with it. The handwashing after glove removal in (d)(2)(v) is an extra duty, not a permit to keep the gear on, and a garment that blood penetrates comes off at once under (d)(3)(vi).

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypothyroidism", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(9) (2027 I.C.6.g(9)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, fatigue and weight gain. Which laboratory pattern would confirm the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: A high TSH with a low free T4
A low TSH with a high free T4
A high TSH with a high free T4
A low TSH with a low free T4
preguntas.explicacion: Those complaints point to hypothyroidism, and the serum TSH is the first test. In primary hypothyroidism the gland cannot keep up, so free T4 falls and the pituitary pushes TSH up. When TSH is raised but free T4 is still normal, the picture is subclinical. Symptoms are mild and nonspecific often enough that the labs, not the story, settle it.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Mode of action column
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes in the order of draw share the same mode of action on calcium. Which are they?
opciones: The light blue citrate tube and the purple EDTA tube
The light blue citrate tube and the gray fluoride tube
The purple EDTA tube and the dark green heparin tube
The gray fluoride tube and the light green PST tube
preguntas.explicacion: Citrate at position 3 and EDTA at position 8 are both described as forming calcium salts to take calcium out of play, which is why both tubes stop the blood clotting. Heparin works instead by inactivating thrombin and thromboplastin, and the gray tube pairs oxalate with an antiglycolytic agent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dextrocardia", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.2 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: A tracing shows inverted complexes in lead I but a normal chest lead pattern. What does that point to?
opciones: Reversed arm electrodes rather than a heart on the right side
A heart on the right side rather than reversed arm electrodes
Reversed leg electrodes rather than reversed arm electrodes
A normal variant that calls for no check of the electrodes
preguntas.explicacion: Swapped arm wires produce findings that look like dextrocardia, but the two are told apart by the chest leads: with a simple limb reversal the precordial pattern stays normal. So the wiring is checked and the tracing repeated before anything else is considered.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 k9 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient has an IV catheter running in the right forearm. Why does the WHO say NOT to take blood from that existing peripheral access?
opciones: Results may be false: hemolysis, contamination and IV fluid or medication alter them
The catheter lumen is too narrow, so the tubes fill slowly and the sample clots inside
The nursing staff alone may access it, and only for blood cultures
The results are valid only if a non-additive tube is drawn first and discarded
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 says that in hospitalized patients blood should not be taken from a peripheral venous access already in place, because the results may be false, naming hemolysis, contamination and the intravenous fluid and medication present as the causes. The contraindication list likewise includes any venous access device, including an IV catheter, as a contraindication. The WHO mentions no discard-tube workaround.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Infection Control in Healthcare Personnel (2019), section 7, Recommendations 7.b.2 to 7.b.5 and Exposure management
preguntas.subtema: Non-punitive reporting · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k96 · CMA I.B.11.a / 2027 I.B.10.a · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC ask occupational health services to establish for reporting infectious exposures?
opciones: A timely, confidential, non-punitive mechanism available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
A written form reviewed by the supervisor and filed within 60 calendar days
A monthly review meeting where exposures of the previous month are discussed
A punitive policy, so that workers who fail to follow precautions are held accountable
preguntas.explicacion: Recommendation 7.b.2 asks for a mechanism that is timely, confidential and non-punitive, by which staff can report an exposure that might be infectious and reach exposure management services at any hour of any day, with expert clinicians and prompt laboratory testing available on the same footing. The background explains the need: exposures go significantly underreported because of time pressure, fear of reprimand, not knowing how the report is made, and worry about who pays. A punitive policy would deepen that very problem, and 60 days is a HIPAA breach figure.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k16 k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: While verifying a date of birth with a hard-of-hearing patient, which technique applies?
opciones: Say the digits one at a time, 'six, one', rather than 'sixty-one'
Say the year louder, because numbers are especially hard to lip-read
Show the date on the wristband and ask him to confirm it with a nod
Skip the date of birth and use the room number as the second identifier
preguntas.explicacion: Where certain letters and certain numbers are hard to tell apart by ear, give context: 'm as in Mary', or 'five, six' rather than 'fifty-six'. Shouting distorts the sounds of speech, the WHO wants the patient to state the identifiers rather than nod at them, and The Joint Commission excludes the room number as an identifier.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-scheduling · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.1 (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4E k56 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which task can some patient portals let a patient perform, beyond viewing information?
opciones: Scheduling a non-urgent appointment and requesting a prescription refill
Correcting a diagnosis in the chart directly, without asking the practice
Opening the records of a family member who uses the same practice
Canceling a claim the practice has already submitted to the health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Some portals do more than display: they let the patient send a secure message to the doctor, ask for a prescription refill, book appointments that are not urgent, look up benefits and coverage, change contact details, pay a bill, download forms and fill them in, and read educational material. ONC presents the portal as a way of saving time and keeping care going between visits.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: Does shifting the limb electrodes onto the upper arms and thighs change the reading?
opciones: No, the accuracy of the tracing is not affected
Yes, the limb leads then read the chest instead
Yes, the tracing has to be marked as non-standard
No, but the standardization has to be halved first
preguntas.explicacion: The move is offered precisely because it costs nothing: placing the limb electrodes higher up eliminates tremor from the arms and legs and in no way affects the accuracy of the electrocardiogram. It is a useful option in a patient who cannot keep the limbs still.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k9 k59 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is filling an evacuated tube from a syringe. In what position is the tube held, and with what pressure?
opciones: Upright, pierced from directly above, with slow and steady pressure
Upright, pierced from directly above, with one firm push on the plunger
Tilted, pierced through the side of the stopper, with steady pressure
Upright, with the stopper taken off first and the blood run down the wall
preguntas.explicacion: The needle goes through the stopper from directly above the tube, with slow, steady pressure, and the plunger is not pressed because the extra pressure raises the risk of hemolysis. The stopper is never removed either, since taking it off releases the vacuum inside.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Choking - infant under 1 year", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old infant is choking, cannot cry, and is turning blue. Which sequence is used?
opciones: Up to five back blows face down, then up to five chest thrusts face up
Up to five abdominal thrusts with the infant held along the forearm
Thirty chest compressions and two breaths, repeated in cycles of five
Five back blows alone, repeated until the object leaves the airway
preguntas.explicacion: The infant is laid face down along the forearm with the head lower than the body and given up to 5 blows between the shoulder blades with the palm; if the object stays, the infant is turned face up for up to 5 chest thrusts. Those cycles repeat until the object comes out or the infant stops responding, and then CPR begins.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Structure and Function: Fowler Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(2) · RMA III.F.2.a.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in mild respiratory distress is sat up in Fowler's position. What does that change?
opciones: Chest expansion is maximized and abdominal muscular tension drops, so oxygenation rises
Venous return to the head and to the heart increases, which is useful in severe hypotension
Abdominal contents shift up against the diaphragm, so higher airway pressures are needed
Ventilation is favored in the nondependent lung as the mediastinum shifts to one side
preguntas.explicacion: Sitting the patient up lets the chest expand, relieves the pull of the abdominal muscles and takes gravity off the chest wall, which is why it helps in mild to moderate respiratory distress. Raising venous return by tipping the head down is Trendelenburg, and shifting ventilation toward the upper lung is what the lateral decubitus position does.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: One chest electrode is left to place on a patient. Where does V6 go?
opciones: Mid-axillary line, at the fifth intercostal space
Mid-clavicular line, at the fifth intercostal space
Mid-axillary line, at the fourth intercostal space
Mid-axillary line, at the sixth intercostal space
preguntas.explicacion: V6 marks the left end of the chest row: fifth intercostal space, mid-axillary line. The mid-clavicular line at that same level belongs to V4, and the fourth space is where V1 and V2 sit, so the two coordinates have to be read together rather than one at a time.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: The P, QRS and T are almost invisible in one standard limb lead. What is the likely cause?
opciones: Two of the electrodes for that lead are on the legs
Two of the electrodes for that lead are on the arms
The chest electrodes were attached in reverse order
The gel on those electrodes had dried out completely
preguntas.explicacion: When all three main components go nearly flat in one of the standard limb leads, the probable reason is that both electrodes feeding that lead ended up on the two legs, so there is almost no voltage difference between them. The hook-up is checked before the tracing is repeated.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ECG T Wave" (NBK538264), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: What does the T wave represent?
opciones: Repolarization of the ventricles, after their contraction
Depolarization of the ventricles, before they contract
Repolarization of the atria, after their contraction
Depolarization of the septum, before the ventricles fire
preguntas.explicacion: The T wave is ventricular repolarization: the muscle cells returning to their resting charge before the next impulse arrives, which roughly matches ventricular diastole. Its shape is easily changed by hormones, electrolytes and drugs, so it is one of the most variable parts of the tracing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Defense Mechanisms", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Defense mechanisms · CCMA 1E k33 · CMA F.1.b / 2027 F.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What separates suppression from repression?
opciones: Suppression is a conscious choice to block the thought
Suppression is a subconscious block of the same thought
Suppression swaps the impulse for its exact opposite
Suppression channels the anxiety into a useful pursuit
preguntas.explicacion: Suppression is consciously choosing to block undesirable ideas or impulses, which is what sets it apart from repression, a subconscious process. Reaction formation replaces an initial impulse with the opposite one, and sublimation redirects the feeling into a pursuit that societal norms treat as useful.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 2: Compliance Leadership and Oversight
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the OIG guidance say the compliance officer should sit in an entity's reporting structure?
opciones: Reporting to the chief executive with independent access to the board, or to the board
Reporting to the billing manager, who sees every claim before it leaves the office
Reporting to the entity's outside counsel, who then directs any investigation there is
Reporting to the human resources director, who imposes the consequences on staff
preguntas.explicacion: Compliance leadership and oversight is the second element, and every entity should designate a compliance officer carrying the authority, the stature, the access and the resources the role needs. That officer should report either to the board itself or to the chief executive, in the latter case with access to the board that is direct and independent, and should stand as an equal among the other senior leaders.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Nerve injury · CPT D3 3F 3L k62 k68 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Along which vein does the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve travel, and at what level does it reach the surface?
opciones: With the basilic vein, about ten centimeters above the medial epicondyle
With the cephalic vein, about ten centimeters above the lateral epicondyle
With the median cubital vein, at the apex of the cubital fossa itself
With the basilic vein, about two centimeters below the medial epicondyle
preguntas.explicacion: This sensory nerve runs down the arm inside the brachial fascia together with the basilic vein and leaves that fascia roughly ten centimeters above the medial epicondyle, dividing into an anterior and a posterior branch. Its closeness to the basilic vein is what puts it at risk during a draw.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Faxes
preguntas.subtema: Fax safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which safeguard applies when faxing protected health information?
opciones: Keep the fax machine in a secure area and use a cover page saying what to do if misdirected
Place the fax machine at the reception desk so that staff can retrieve incoming pages quickly
Send faxes overnight so that they arrive before the office opens and are not seen
Confirm receipt by mailing a paper duplicate of every fax to the recipient on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: The machine lives somewhere secure, out of reach of the public, of patients and of most staff. The first page is a disclaimer telling whoever receives it what to do if the fax landed on the wrong number. Faxes go out during working hours except in an emergency, so that someone picks them up instead of leaving them in the tray, and the sender then contacts the other party to confirm the pages were collected. A machine at reception and overnight transmissions both leave PHI sitting in the open, and mailing a duplicate adds a second disclosure rather than a confirmation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Intestinal Stoma", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.4.d (solo outline vigente) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the site of a planned stoma marked beforehand by a trained nurse or clinician?
opciones: Because an ill-fitting stoma brings its own complications, which correct siting prevents
Because the mark tells the surgeon how long a segment of bowel will have to be resected
Because the mark records the length of mesentery available for a tension-free exteriorization
Because the mark is what the pathology request form uses to identify the specimen later
preguntas.explicacion: Choosing and marking the site in advance is described as critical, because it heads off the complications that come from a stoma that does not sit well; the apex of the infraumbilical fat fold is often considered ideal since it is easy to reach and to see. Teaching the patient and supporting them psychologically before surgery also improve the long-term result.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position and fasting)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient who has just hurried up three flights of stairs sits down in the drawing chair. According to the phlebotomy guidance on position, what should happen before the draw?
opciones: The patient stays seated for at least 15 minutes before the draw, and any unavoidable change of position is recorded
The patient lies down for 2 minutes and the draw proceeds, because lying down offsets the effect of the exertion
The draw proceeds at once, because position affects only patients who are drawn lying down in the hospital
The patient stands for 5 minutes to let the blood volume redistribute, then sits and is drawn immediately
preguntas.explicacion: Changing position produces statistically significant differences in several biochemistry parameters, so the position, lying or sitting, is maintained for at least 10 to 15 minutes before the procedure; in an office setting the patient should sit for at least 15 minutes beforehand, and when a change of position is unavoidable it is recorded so the results can be interpreted accordingly. Fasting status and the patient's diet, medicines, supplements and herbal preparations are checked at that same point.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9: Clean contaminated surfaces and complete patient procedure
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care · CPT D3 3Q 3R k74 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E9 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: The tubes are filled and the needle is discarded. Which closing steps does the WHO list before the patient leaves?
opciones: Check labels and forms, perform hand hygiene, ask how the patient feels and check the site for bleeding
Invert every tube 8 to 10 times, remove the gloves and send the patient out while the tubes clot in the rack
Apply ice to the site for 15 minutes, then recheck the labels once the patient has gone
Ask the patient to bend the arm over the gauze and hold it for five minutes before standing
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 runs through the closing routine: drop the sharp into the sharps container, check label and forms against each other, discard the other items in the right waste category, perform hand hygiene again, recheck the labels before dispatch, tell the patient the procedure is over, ask how they feel, verify the site is not bleeding, and say something reassuring. Bending the arm is what Step 6 forbids.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Permitted Uses and Disclosures: Limited Data Set
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CCMA 7E k220 conditions for release · CMA II.E.2.a authorization to release · RMA I.C.1.b disclosure laws
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory is asked for records with the direct identifiers of the patients and their households stripped out. What has it been asked for, and on what condition may it go out?
opciones: A limited data set, for research, public health or operations, once a data use agreement is signed
A limited data set, for any purpose and on no condition, since the direct identifiers are gone
De-identified information, for research, public health or operations, under a data use agreement
A limited data set, for research alone, and only once every patient in it has signed authorization
preguntas.explicacion: Taking out the direct identifiers of the person, and of relatives, household members and employers, does not make the information anonymous. What it makes is a limited data set, which is still protected health information and still carries conditions. It travels for three purposes only — research, public health and health care operations — and it travels under a data use agreement in which whoever receives it promises the safeguards attached to it. Genuine de-identification is the other road: once information is truly de-identified the rule stops reaching it, and no agreement is called for.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old has a pulse of 118 beats per minute at a well-child visit. What does that value represent?
opciones: A normal rate: children of 3 to 4 years rest between 80 and 120 beats per minute
Tachycardia: the 60 to 100 adult band is applied from the age of 3 years onward
A normal rate, but only for children under 2 years, whose band reaches 130 per minute
A rate that needs a recount, since a value above 100 in a child is not reported as such
preguntas.explicacion: Resting rates fall as children grow: 80 to 130 at 1 to 2 years, 80 to 120 at 3 to 4, 75 to 115 at 5 to 6, 70 to 110 at 7 to 9, and 60 to 100 from 10 years and through adulthood. A rate of 118 in a 4-year-old sits inside the band for that age, so the adult ceiling of 100 does not apply.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Sodium in Your Diet: Check the Package for Nutrient Claims
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient cutting sodium asks what the front-of-package claim "low sodium" guarantees. What does it mean?
opciones: One serving of the food holds 140 milligrams of sodium or less
One serving of the food holds 35 milligrams of sodium or less
The food carries at least 25% less sodium than the regular one
The food carries at least 50% less sodium than the regular one
preguntas.explicacion: Sodium claims are defined per serving: salt-free means under 5 mg, very low sodium means 35 mg or less, and low sodium means 140 mg or less. The comparison claims are different animals: reduced sodium is at least a quarter less than the regular product and light in sodium is at least half less.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Patient Identity and Patient Record Matching
preguntas.subtema: Duplicate records · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 4D k57 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Two records appear to belong to the same woman, one under her maiden name. Which process is meant to resolve that?
opciones: Patient matching, which links a person's data by comparing several demographic fields
Accounting of disclosures, which lists everyone the practice has sent her records to
An amendment request, which lets the patient ask that an incorrect entry be corrected
De-identification, which strips the identifiers so the two files can be compared safely
preguntas.explicacion: ONC defines patient matching as the work of identifying a single patient's data and linking it, inside a health system and across several. The minimum method is to link a handful of demographic fields, and the ones named are name, birth date, telephone number and address. ONC treats it as a cornerstone of interoperability and of the country's health IT infrastructure.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Electrocardiogram
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient told to avoid immediately before a resting tracing?
opciones: Exercise or cold water, since either can falsify the result
Eating or smoking for the three hours before the recording
Taking any regular medicine on the morning of the test
Speaking or moving for the ten minutes before the test
preguntas.explicacion: Exercising or drinking cold water just beforehand may produce false results. Medicines are not stopped on the patient's own decision; the provider is told what is being taken, because some drugs interfere with the reading. The fasting rules belong to the exercise test.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Background; Recommendations for Employers
preguntas.subtema: Under-reporting · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What do surveillance data say about how often needlestick injuries are actually reported?
opciones: About half go unreported, and a typical hospital sees some 30 per 100 beds a year
Nearly all are reported, since the sharps injury log is reviewed every month
About one in ten goes unreported, mostly among housekeeping employees
Half go unreported, and a typical hospital sees about 300 per 100 beds a year
preguntas.explicacion: Estimates put the United States at between 600,000 and 800,000 percutaneous injuries a year, needlesticks among them, and roughly half are never reported. Surveillance data suggest the average hospital sees about 30 needlestick injuries for every 100 beds in a year. Under-reporting costs twice: the worker misses post-exposure management, and the institution loses the record that would show where the hazard lives. That is why employers are told to set up procedures that encourage reporting.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP); and CMS, Medicaid.gov: CHIP
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.c / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: A family earns too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance for their children. Which program is meant for them?
opciones: CHIP, which covers children in that income range and is run by each state
COBRA, which continues children's coverage in that income range for a time
Medigap, which supplements children's coverage while the parents apply
Medicare Part C, which enrolls children whose parents lack job-based coverage
preguntas.explicacion: The Children's Health Insurance Program covers children in families that earn too much for Medicaid yet too little to buy private coverage; the states run it under federal requirements and share the funding with the federal government, and in some states it reaches pregnant women too. Applications are taken at any point in the year. COBRA continues employer coverage, Medigap supplements Original Medicare, and Medicare Advantage is Medicare coverage.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Electrolytes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(d) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(d) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a
preguntas.pregunta: An athlete who sweats heavily asks whether plain water replaces what he loses. What is accurate about electrolytes?
opciones: They are lost in sweat and plain water holds no meaningful amount of them
They are lost in sweat and plain water replaces them as fast as they are lost
They are lost only in urine, so sweating does not change the body's supply
They are lost in sweat, but only the sodium and the chloride are affected
preguntas.explicacion: Electrolytes are the charged minerals of blood and body fluid: chloride, calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, sodium and potassium. They govern body water, blood pH, and nerve and muscle function. Sweat carries them out, and since plain water holds almost none, they have to come back in fluids that contain them.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(e)(2)(i), (e)(2)(ii) and (e)(2)(iii), Multi-employer workplaces
preguntas.subtema: Multi-employer workplaces · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A contract cleaning crew works nights in a laboratory that stores hazardous chemicals. What must the laboratory's program provide for?
opciones: On-site access to the sheets, the precautions to take, and the labeling system
A copy of the crew's own written program, kept in the laboratory office
Training of the crew by the laboratory, repeated once every three years
A separate storage room for the chemicals while the crew is on site
preguntas.explicacion: Where an employer produces, uses or stores hazardous chemicals in a way that can expose another employer's workers, the written program has to add three things: how the other employer will be given on-site access to a safety data sheet for each chemical their people may meet, how they will be told what precautions are needed under normal operating conditions and in a foreseeable emergency, and how they will be told which labeling system the workplace uses. Each employer still trains its own staff.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.1 and 2.2.3, Step 5
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k9 k63 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Apart from raising the risk of contamination, what else follows from puncturing before the antiseptic has dried?
opciones: It appears on the list of factors that cause hemolysis
It appears on the list of factors that cause clotted tubes
It appears on the list of factors that cause nerve injury
It appears on the list of factors that cause a lost vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Failing to let the alcohol or disinfectant dry is named among the factors that increase the risk of hemolysis, as well as leaving the site poorly disinfected. That is why the swab is followed by thirty seconds of drying rather than an immediate puncture through a wet surface.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers: Insulin benefit
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses an insulin pump covered under the Part B equipment benefit. What is the most she pays for a month's supply of that insulin?
opciones: Thirty-five dollars, and the yearly Part B deductible is not applied to it
Thirty-five dollars, but only once she has met the yearly Part B deductible
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as for other equipment and supplies
One hundred and five dollars, the ceiling set for one month's covered supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where insulin is covered through the Part B durable medical equipment benefit for a pump, or through a Medicare Advantage Plan, the cost of a month's supply cannot exceed thirty-five dollars and the Part B deductible does not apply. A three-month supply is capped at thirty-five dollars for each month, so generally no more than a hundred and five dollars in all.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Precertification · CMA III.G.5.a(1) (2027 III.G.5.a(1)) · CMAA 4G · CCMA 5H k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: The surgeon changed the procedure on the day of surgery and the authorization still names the old one. What is the warning about fixing that afterwards?
opciones: Some payers will change an authorization only up to fourteen days after the service
Some payers will change an authorization only up to sixty days after the service
No payer will change an authorization once the service has already been provided
Every payer has to reopen the authorization when the record justifies the change
preguntas.explicacion: Where the procedure billed is not the procedure authorized, the advice is to put the information right before the claim goes out, or to justify the discrepancy with solid reasons. A changed code on a service that needed authorization has to be dealt with at once: some payers will not touch an authorization more than fourteen days past the date of service, and after that the denial is likely to be permanent.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what Part B is for in the broadest terms. Which two categories of service does it cover?
opciones: Medically necessary services and preventive services
Medically necessary services and long-term custodial care
Preventive services and inpatient hospital admissions
Preventive services and skilled nursing facility stays
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers two kinds of thing. Medically necessary services or supplies are those meeting accepted standards of medical practice for diagnosing or treating the patient's condition. Preventive services are the care meant to head off illness or catch it early, when treatment is likeliest to work, and most of them cost the patient nothing when the provider accepts assignment. Inpatient hospital and skilled nursing stays belong to Part A.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for same-day surgery and the surgeon calls it off that morning because of a contraindication. Which diagnosis is listed first?
opciones: The condition the surgery was meant to treat, which is the reason for the encounter
The contraindication that stopped the surgery, which is what the visit finally found
The postoperative diagnosis the surgeon expected, as the more definitive of the two
A code for the surgery that was called off, with the condition added as secondary
preguntas.explicacion: In the outpatient setting the first-listed diagnosis is the reason for the encounter, and for same-day surgery that is the condition the surgery was scheduled to treat. The guideline keeps it first even when the surgery is not carried out because of a contraindication. The postoperative diagnosis rule belongs to surgeries that actually take place.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Issues of Concern: Patient Abandonment
preguntas.subtema: Termination of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(2) · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a malpractice claim against the practice. May the practice drop him at once?
opciones: No: the suit does not release the clinician from giving due notice
No: the suit freezes the relationship until the case has been decided
Yes: filing suit is treated as the patient ending the relationship
Yes: a conflict of interest requires the practice to dismiss him now
preguntas.explicacion: A patient who sues does not thereby end the therapeutic relationship, and a court has expressly rejected the idea that suing absolves the clinician of the duty to give notice of withdrawal in due form and a fair chance to line up other care. Dropping such a patient without the usual process is precisely what exposes the clinician to an abandonment claim.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Closed-Loop Communication
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2E k23 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the assistant to send a pamphlet and book a follow-up; the assistant restates the task and the provider confirms. Which strategy is that?
opciones: A check-back, which closes the loop on the message
A call-out, which informs the whole team at once
A teach-back, which confirms a patient understood
A handoff, which transfers responsibility for care
preguntas.explicacion: A check-back is the closed-loop strategy for making sure what the sender conveyed is what the receiver understood: the receiver repeats it and the sender confirms. A call-out broadcasts to everyone at once, a teach-back checks a patient or family member, and a handoff moves responsibility between caregivers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Two R waves on a regular strip sit five large squares apart. What does that give?
opciones: 60 per minute, sitting at the lower edge of the normal band
75 per minute, sitting in the middle of the normal band
50 per minute, sitting just under the lower edge of normal
100 per minute, sitting at the upper edge of the normal band
preguntas.explicacion: With an even rhythm the rate is 300 divided by the large squares between two R waves, so five of them give 60 per minute. That is the bottom of the 60 to 100 band: one square more would put the tracing under 60, which is what bradycardia means.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Warfarin", Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on warfarin comes in for the scheduled blood test. Which result guides the dose of this drug?
opciones: The international normalized ratio, which standardizes the prothrombin time
The prothrombin time in seconds, preferred because it is not standardized
The hemoglobin and hematocrit, which are drawn every six months on therapy
The potassium and the creatinine, drawn before starting and then once a year
preguntas.explicacion: Warfarin is followed with the INR, which puts the prothrombin time on one scale whatever reagent the laboratory uses; someone not anticoagulated sits near 1.0. Hospitalized patients are checked daily and maintenance patients roughly every four weeks, plus whenever an interacting drug starts or stops. Hemoglobin and hematocrit are baseline and six-month checks, not the dosing guide.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: A and B Recommendations — Cervical Cancer: Screening
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C screening timelines · CMA I.A.5.a · 2027 I.A.5.a
preguntas.pregunta: A 25-year-old woman asks how often she needs cervical cancer screening. What is recommended for her age band?
opciones: Cytology alone every 3 years from 21 through 29
Cytology alone every 5 years from 21 through 29
Cytology with HPV cotesting every 3 years from 21 through 29
Cytology alone every year from 21 through 29
preguntas.explicacion: Screening for cervical cancer covers women from 21 through 65. Between 21 and 29 it is cervical cytology alone every three years. From 30 through 65 there are three acceptable strategies: cytology alone every three years, high-risk HPV testing alone every five, or the two together every five. The recommendation carries an A grade.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "2) College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation Program", items GEN.40490 and GEN.40491
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 3E12 k124 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A tube arrives labeled with the patient's full name and the room number only. Why does it fail the labeling checklist item used by CAP-accredited laboratories?
opciones: Primary specimen containers must carry at least two identifiers, and a room number is not an identifier
Primary specimen containers must carry the name plus a bar code; a handwritten room number is not machine-readable
Primary specimen containers must carry three identifiers when the specimen is collected on an inpatient unit
Primary specimen containers must carry the name and the collector's initials; the room number is merely optional
preguntas.explicacion: The CAP Laboratory General Checklist has the collector positively identify the patient before collection with at least two identifiers (GEN.40490), and asks that at least two identifiers appear on the primary specimen container itself (GEN.40491); the parallel Joint Commission International goal rules the room number or location out as an identifier altogether. A name plus a location therefore leaves the tube one identifier short.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction (Green)
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's stat chemistry goes into a green top tube. Which heparin salts may it hold, and what is tested?
opciones: Sodium, lithium or ammonium heparin; the sample tested is plasma
Sodium or potassium heparin; the sample tested is serum after a spin
Lithium heparin only; the sample tested is serum after a longer spin
Sodium or lithium citrate; the sample tested is plasma after a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: Green tubes hold heparin in the form of the sodium, lithium or ammonium salt, and the heparin stops thrombin from forming. Because the blood does not clot, what the laboratory tests is plasma, not serum; these tubes are often chosen when chemistry results are wanted immediately.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical History", Definition/Introduction; and "SOAP Notes", Function: Objective
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k44 · CMA I.A.4 · RMA III.F.1.a · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of elements makes up a comprehensive history intake at a wellness visit?
opciones: Past medical and surgical history, allergies and medications, plus family and social history
Vital signs, height and weight, and all of the findings of the head-to-toe physical examination
The chief concern alone, expanded with the onset, location and severity of the symptom
Laboratory results, imaging reports and the discharge summaries of earlier admissions
preguntas.explicacion: A full intake gathers what the patient has lived through: conditions already diagnosed, operations already done, illnesses that run in the family, the social picture, allergies with the reaction each one caused, and every current medication. Vital signs, examination findings, laboratory values and imaging are objective data and are recorded apart.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.c · 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the extinguisher nozzle aimed when the letters of PASS are followed?
opciones: At the base of the fire, sweeping the nozzle from side to side
At the top of the flames, sweeping the nozzle from side to side
At the ceiling above the fire, so the agent falls onto the flames
At the middle of the flames, holding the nozzle in one position
preguntas.explicacion: Four steps: pull the safety pin, aim low at the fire's base, squeeze the handle, and sweep the nozzle side to side. Whether staff fight a small fire at all is a decision the employer makes in the plan: choosing to evacuate instead is what most surely keeps employees from fire-related injuries.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient needs a full coagulation work-up. Summarized in four groups, the order runs sterile tubes, coagulation tubes, and then which two?
opciones: Plain or gel tubes, and last the tubes holding additives
Tubes holding additives, and last the plain or gel tubes
Capillary microtubes, and last the tubes holding additives
Plain or gel tubes, and last a second sterile culture bottle
preguntas.explicacion: Set out as four groups, the sequence runs blood culture or sterile tubes first, then the coagulation tubes, then plain and gel tubes, and finally the tubes that hold additives. That grouping matches the numbered table, where the citrate tube precedes the clot activator, separator and EDTA tubes.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(c)(3)(ii), Time and manner of access
preguntas.subtema: Sending records to a third party · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a(5) · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that a copy of her records be sent directly to another physician. What does HIPAA require of that request?
opciones: That it be written, signed, and clearly name the recipient and where to send it
That the receiving physician sign a business associate agreement before records are sent
That the patient collect the records in person and deliver them herself
That the request be approved by the privacy official within 15 days
preguntas.explicacion: Under 164.524(c)(3)(ii), where the individual directs that the copy go to somebody else, the entity must send it to that person; the individual has to put the request in writing and sign it, naming who is to receive it and saying where the copy should be sent. The 30-day clock runs as it does for any access request. A business associate agreement covers entities working on the covered entity's behalf, not a physician the patient has chosen to receive her own records.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 6 and 7
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient needs a serum lithium level and an ammonia level. Which heparin tube is required for each?
opciones: Sodium heparin for the lithium level; either heparin salt for the ammonia level
Lithium heparin for the lithium level; sodium heparin only for the ammonia level
Either heparin salt for the lithium level; sodium heparin only for the ammonia
Sodium heparin for both, because lithium heparin is limited to chemistry panels
preguntas.explicacion: The dark green heparin tube may carry sodium heparin or lithium heparin. For a lithium level the sodium salt is the one specified, while an ammonia level accepts either salt. The light green PST is the tube that carries lithium heparin with a gel separator, and its listed use is chemistries.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries; Examples of Safety Device Designs
preguntas.subtema: Assemblies taken apart after use · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Why has a needle and vacuum tube assembly been singled out as carrying a higher injury risk?
opciones: It has to be taken apart or handled after use, which has raised injury rates
It holds a larger volume of blood than a syringe of the very same gauge
Its needle is longer, so it reaches deeper into the vein of the patient
It cannot be fitted with a shield, so no safer version of it is made
preguntas.explicacion: A device that has to be taken apart or handled once the draw is finished stands out as a hazard, and the injury rates bear it out: prefilled cartridge syringes, and phlebotomy needles with their vacuum tube assemblies, are the examples named. Safer versions do exist, among them hinged or sliding shields for phlebotomy and winged-steel needles, sliding shields on the tube holder, and needles that retract into the holder. Length and blood volume are not what the injury data point to.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality checks · CPT D3 3B k9 k58 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory traces odd results back to the drawing room itself. Besides the tubes, which conditions should be controlled?
opciones: Room temperature, humidity and how much light the specimen receives
Room temperature only, since humidity and light reach sealed tubes
Barometric pressure and the height of the chair the patient sits in
The color of the tray and how far the rack sits from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Environmental conditions are listed among the things to keep in check when a specimen is collected: the temperature and humidity of the room and possible exposure to light. Expiry dates belong on the same list, since an out-of-date tube aspirates poorly and its additive may have degraded.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Advance Care Planning: Advance Directives for Health Care (advance directives)
preguntas.subtema: Advance directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a / 2027 E.7 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: How often should a person revisit an advance directive already on file?
opciones: At least once a year, and after a major life event
Only when the named agent asks for it to be changed
Only when a new diagnosis is added to the problem list
Every five years, which is when the form legally lapses
preguntas.explicacion: Advance directives are meant to be living documents: reviewed at least once each year and updated after a major life event such as retirement, a move to another state or a significant change in health. When a form is replaced, the older version is kept and dated. No annual or five-year expiry makes the document lapse on its own.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse Pressure; Mean Arterial Pressure
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: For a blood pressure of 120/80, what are the pulse pressure and the approximate mean arterial pressure (MAP)?
opciones: Pulse pressure 40 mm Hg; MAP about 93 mm Hg
Pulse pressure 40 mm Hg; MAP about 100 mm Hg
Pulse pressure 200 mm Hg; MAP about 100 mm Hg
Pulse pressure 30 mm Hg; MAP about 80 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic, here 120 minus 80, which gives 40 mm Hg; as a rule it should not fall under a quarter of the systolic figure. MAP is estimated by adding a third of the pulse pressure to the diastolic: 80 plus 40/3, about 93 mm Hg, inside the usual 70 to 110. Held under 60 mm Hg for long, the tissues stop getting enough flow.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ocular Burns", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B9 k76 · CMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 2B.17
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a chemical splash in one eye. How long does irrigation continue?
opciones: At least 30 minutes, and until the surface pH reads 7.0 to 7.4 on litmus
At least 5 minutes, and until the patient reports the pain has settled down
At least 30 minutes, and until the visual acuity returns to its usual level
Until the ophthalmologist arrives, since irrigation may wash away the evidence
preguntas.explicacion: Copious irrigation is the single most important step and it often matters more to the final vision than which chemical was involved. It runs for a minimum of half an hour, longer in severe injuries, until the ocular surface reads neutral on litmus paper. Alkali burns need more volume and more time, because they keep penetrating after the exposure ends.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", sections Etiology and Pathophysiology; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope vs seizure · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who fainted during a draw remains unresponsive for more than five minutes, with jerking movements and loss of bladder control. What does this episode indicate?
opciones: It is not simple syncope but more likely a seizure, which needs urgent evaluation
It is a prolonged vasovagal episode; keep the legs raised and wait calmly for recovery
It is typical syncope, since jerking and incontinence are common during a faint
It is near syncope, because the patient never fully lost postural tone
preguntas.explicacion: An episode that runs beyond a few minutes is not syncope at all but more likely an acute neurologic event, a seizure for instance, and, unlike seizure patients, people with syncope keep sphincter control, rarely show tonic-clonic activity and are not confused on waking. Emergency services are called if the person does not become alert within a couple of minutes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J II.I · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A light blue tube reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. Which collection faults are recognized causes?
opciones: A traumatic venipuncture, clotting inside the device, or poor mixing with the additive
A tourniquet released too early, a needle angle below fifteen degrees, or a warm room
An expired needle, a second puncture in the same arm, or a bandage applied too tightly
A tube filled from a syringe, a tube stored upright, or a label written after the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting in a citrate specimen is traced to a rough venipuncture, to coagulation set off inside the collection device, or the anticoagulant not being properly mixed with the blood. A clot consumes clotting factors, so the testing that follows is unreliable and the specimen is repeated.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old has an axillary temperature of 37.3 °C. Does this meet the definition of fever in a child?
opciones: Yes: an axillary reading of 37.2 °C (99 °F) or above is a fever in a child
No: an axillary reading only counts as fever from 38 °C (100.4 °F) upward
No: fever in a child is defined from the oral threshold of 37.5 °C (99.5 °F)
Yes, but only if the same value is confirmed rectally within the next hour
preguntas.explicacion: Each route carries its own cut-off in children: 38 °C (100.4 °F) rectally, 37.5 °C (99.5 °F) orally and 37.2 °C (99 °F) in the armpit. The armpit reads lowest, so its threshold is the lowest of the three. A value of 37.3 °C there is above the cut-off and is documented as a fever with the route beside it.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Advance Care Planning: Advance Directives for Health Care (other advance care planning documents); and StatPearls, "Do Not Resuscitate" (NBK470163)
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.b / 2027 E.7.a · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: What does a do-not-intubate order tell the staff of a hospital or nursing facility?
opciones: That the person does not want to be placed on a ventilator
That the person does not want to be sent to a hospital at all
That the person does not want chest compressions attempted
That the person does not want artificial feeding through a tube
preguntas.explicacion: A do-not-intubate order tells staff the person does not want to be put on a ventilator. Not wanting CPR is the do-not-resuscitate order, and not wanting to be sent to a hospital from long-term care is the do-not-hospitalize order. Feeding tubes and artificial nutrition are preferences a living will can address rather than a separate order of that kind.

preguntas.fuente: SAMHSA, Urine Specimen Collection Handbook for Federal Agency Workplace Drug Testing Programs (2024), Chapter 7 collection steps 13 and 16
preguntas.subtema: Drug screen volume · CPT D4 4J k86 · PBT V.C.5 chain-of-custody · CCMA 3E k127 · RMA III.C.4.a.i urine drug screen · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: What minimum volume of urine must a donor provide in a federal workplace drug test collection?
opciones: 45 mL
30 mL
15 mL
60 mL
preguntas.explicacion: The donor is directed to provide at least 45 mL, and the collector checks the volume before going on. That figure exists because the specimen is split afterwards, 30 mL or more into bottle A and 15 mL or more into bottle B. A container holding less than 45 mL is discarded and a second collection begins at once, with a new container and the same chain of custody form.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(c)(2) and (c)(4), Provision of access; Fees
preguntas.subtema: Fees for copies · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
