Serum separator tube, then light blue citrate, then purple EDTA
Light blue citrate, then purple EDTA, then the serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 numbers the tubes from 1 to 10. The coagulation tube is number 3, the serum separator tube (red-gray tiger or gold) is number 5, and EDTA is number 8, so citrate comes first, the SST second and EDTA last among these three. Step 8 gives the reason for a fixed sequence: it prevents the additive of one tube from contaminating the next.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: Where do prevention and de-escalation sit in managing a patient who may turn violent?
opciones: First, with restraints held back as a last resort
Last, once a security team has already come in
First, but only after a supervisor authorizes it
Last, and only after chemical restraint is given
preguntas.explicacion: Management centers on prevention and de-escalation, with the fight-or-flight reaction as the last resort. Triage is early enough for de-escalation to begin, staff should be trained in it, and physical restraints used alongside chemical ones are likewise a last resort rather than a first move.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Permissive Exclusions; and OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A provider's license was revoked over her professional competence. What kind of exclusion may follow?
opciones: A permissive one, which OIG may impose and whose length varies
A mandatory one, which runs for a minimum of five years
A mandatory one, which lasts as long as the license is gone
None at all, since no criminal conviction has been entered
preguntas.explicacion: Losing a health care license for reasons of professional competence, performance or financial integrity is one of the grounds on which OIG may exclude, and permissive exclusions vary in length. The mandatory exclusions, with their floor of five years, follow convictions such as program fraud or patient abuse.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Anatomy and Physiology: Enteral Route
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(v)
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement compares the buccal route with the sublingual route correctly?
opciones: Buccal tissue is less permeable, so absorption there is slower than under the tongue
Buccal tissue is more permeable, so absorption there is faster than under the tongue
Buccal drugs pass through the liver first, while sublingual drugs go straight to the heart
Buccal drugs drain into the rectal venous plexus, so half the dose still meets the liver
preguntas.explicacion: Both are enteral routes that skip first-pass metabolism, because the venous blood of the mouth drains into the superior vena cava instead of the hepatic portal vein. The difference is the tissue itself: the mucosa under the tongue is highly permeable and reaches the capillaries beneath it quickly, while the cheek is less permeable and takes the drug up more slowly. The half that meets the liver belongs to the rectal route.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Maintenance of Homeostasis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · PBT I.B.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is exercising on a hot day. How does the blood help keep the core temperature from rising?
opciones: More blood is routed to the skin, where heat is lost to the surroundings
Blood is diverted away from the skin so the core keeps its heat
Plasma proteins act as buffers that hold the blood pH near 7.4
The kidneys release erythropoietin so more red cells carry the heat
preguntas.explicacion: Temperature control works as a negative-feedback loop: when the core warms up, more blood is sent to the cooler periphery, heat escapes through the skin vessels and the returning blood is cooler. On a cold day the opposite happens and blood is kept away from the skin to keep the core warm. Buffering pH is a separate homeostatic role of blood, and erythropoietin responds to low oxygen, not to heat.

preguntas.subtema: QC after maintenance or reagent change · CPT D1 1E / k27 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D k115 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: A benchtop chemistry analyzer just had its lamp and pump, both critical parts, replaced by the service technician. What does CLIA require before patient testing resumes?
opciones: Control material testing, as after a complete reagent change or major maintenance
A calibration verification alone, with patient testing resumed before any control is run
Enrollment of the affected analytes in a new proficiency testing event
Written approval from the state agency, since a critical part changed the test system
preguntas.explicacion: Before patient testing resumes, control materials have to be tested whenever the reagents are changed completely, whenever major preventive maintenance has been done, or whenever a critical part that could affect performance has been replaced. Calibration verification is a separate requirement triggered by the same events, but it never stands in for the controls: what opens the gate to patient testing again is an acceptable, documented control run.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: How do medical asepsis and surgical asepsis differ in what they set out to do?
opciones: Medical asepsis reduces pathogens as a barrier; surgical asepsis attacks every microorganism
Medical asepsis attacks every microorganism; surgical asepsis reduces pathogens as a barrier
Medical asepsis applies in the operating room; surgical asepsis applies at the bedside only
Medical asepsis covers hand hygiene alone; surgical asepsis covers every use of any glove
preguntas.explicacion: Aseptic technique, or medical asepsis, is the deliberate reduction of pathogens so they are not carried from one person or object to another, a protective barrier. Sterile technique, or surgical asepsis, goes further and aims to eliminate every microorganism in and around the field. It is the standard for surgery, for the care of a central line, and for wound management that goes below the skin.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(a), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5D · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A new clinic laboratory is writing the manual for everything that happens before testing. Which item needs a written policy under the specimen submission and handling standard?
opciones: Specimen acceptability and rejection criteria
Calibration verification of the analyser
Competency assessment of the testing staff
Enrollment in an approved proficiency testing program
preguntas.explicacion: That standard sets out eight written policies, where each applies: preparing the patient, collecting the specimen, labeling it, storing and preserving it, the conditions of transport, processing, acceptability and rejection, and referral. Calibration verification belongs to the analytic systems, competency assessment to the general laboratory systems, and proficiency testing to a subpart of its own.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sweat Testing", Specimen Collection and Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Iontophoresis technique · PBT V.C.4 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a
preguntas.pregunta: How is sweat obtained for a sweat chloride test?
opciones: Pilocarpine is driven into the skin by iontophoresis for 5 minutes, then sweat is collected for no more than 30 minutes
Pilocarpine is driven into the skin by iontophoresis for 30 minutes, and sweat is then collected for no more than 5 minutes
The arm is wrapped in occlusive plastic for 30 minutes and the sweat that forms is blotted onto filter paper
The patient exercises until sweating begins and gauze is then held against the skin for up to 30 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: In the Gibson-Cooke method two electrodes go on the arm or leg, one carrying gauze soaked in pilocarpine and the other deionized water, and a small painless current runs for 5 minutes to make the glands sweat. Collection onto gauze, filter paper or a macroduct coil follows and must not exceed 30 minutes. A trained technician does it at an accredited cystic fibrosis center.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Colon Cancer Screening", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k45 · CMA I.A.5.a · RMA III.F.4.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's father was diagnosed with colon cancer at 52. When should this patient start screening?
opciones: At 42, which is ten years before the age at which the relative was diagnosed
At 45, the same age recommended for everyone who is at an average risk
At 52, matching the age at which the relative received the diagnosis
At 62, which is ten years after the age at which the relative was diagnosed
preguntas.explicacion: A positive family history moves the start date forward: screening begins ten years before the age at which the relative was diagnosed. With a genetic cancer syndrome, testing can begin as early as the teenage years and repeat at short intervals. Risk assessment is what sorts patients into high, average and low risk before any test is chosen.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section What types of blood tests require fasting; MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, section What are the different types of blood tests
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition lists a complete blood count, a lipid panel, a coagulation panel and a troponin. For which of these tests is fasting usually required?
opciones: The lipid panel
The blood count
The clotting panel
The troponin test
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting is usually required for a blood glucose, for cholesterol or lipid panels and for the basic metabolic panel, with liver function tests and the renal function panel sometimes added; triglycerides and calcitonin also appear among the tests that need it. A CBC, coagulation tests and cardiac enzymes such as troponin are not on that list, and no special preparation at all is needed for most blood tests.

preguntas.subtema: Reusable sharps · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How must contaminated reusable sharps be stored while they wait for reprocessing?
opciones: So that no employee has to reach into the container by hand to retrieve them
Immersed in a 1:10 bleach dilution for at least 10 minutes in an open pan
In a red bag closed before removal, like other regulated waste
In a labeled container that is emptied by hand only when three-quarters full
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(E) forbids storing or processing contaminated reusable sharps in any manner that would oblige an employee to put a hand inside the container holding them, and (d)(2)(viii) wants that container puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom, and labeled or color-coded. Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(4) adds that reusable containers are never opened, emptied or cleaned by hand. A red bag is for soft regulated waste, and the 1:10 hypochlorite dilution is WHO's spill disinfectant, not a way of storing sharps.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Stroke", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.k · 2027 I.B.8.k · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room suddenly has a drooping face on one side, a weak right arm and slurred speech. What is done?
opciones: Call the emergency number at once and note the time symptoms began
Give aspirin and water and drive the patient to the clinic next door
Lay the patient flat with the feet raised and recheck in 15 minutes
Take a full set of vital signs first and then call the provider in
preguntas.explicacion: A stroke is a medical emergency and the single most important action is to call for emergency help right away, at the first signs. Muscle weakness of face, arm or leg on one side, numbness on one side, and trouble speaking or understanding speech are typical and they usually start suddenly and without warning.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What is the role of the placeholder character X in ICD-10-CM?
opciones: It fills an empty position so the code keeps room for future expansion or a later character
It marks a code the coder could not verify against the medical record documentation
It replaces a character the provider left out of the documentation for the encounter
It flags a code as unspecified when the record gives no further detail about the case
preguntas.explicacion: The X is a placeholder, sitting at certain codes so that future expansion is possible, notably in the categories for poisoning, adverse effect and underdosing, and it also fills empty positions so an applicable seventh character lands in the seventh place. Where a placeholder exists it has to be used or the code is not valid. It says nothing about missing documentation or about unspecified conditions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Variability of Vital Signs in Older Adults
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How is the patient positioned and timed for orthostatic blood pressures?
opciones: Supine for about 5 minutes, then measured again within 1 to 3 minutes of standing
Seated for about 5 minutes, then measured again 10 minutes after standing up
Supine for about 1 minute, then measured again immediately on standing up
Standing for about 5 minutes, then measured again after lying down for 3 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The patient lies down for roughly five minutes and the pressure is taken again within one to three minutes of standing. The measurement is called for in older adults being evaluated for dizziness, fainting, falls or suspected loss of fluid volume, where the reflexes that defend pressure on standing are often impaired.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Atrioventricular Node
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: A healthy young patient's rate climbs stage after stage on the treadmill. What sets the usual ceiling on it?
opciones: The atrioventricular node passes at most about 220 impulses a minute
The sinoatrial node fires at most about 220 impulses a minute
The Purkinje fibers pass at most about 220 impulses a minute
The bundle branches pass at most about 220 impulses a minute
preguntas.explicacion: Under extreme stimulation from the sinus node above it, the atrioventricular node can still transmit only around 220 impulses a minute, and that is what fixes the typical maximum rate. Damaged or drug-driven hearts can beat faster, but then they pump poorly.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Limited English Proficiency (LEP), Your Right to Language Assistance Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Under which two federal laws does HHS OCR say HHS-funded programs must provide language access services free of charge?
opciones: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the ACA
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act together with the ADA
HIPAA and the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act (ADAAA)
EMTALA and Title X of the Public Health Service Act (family planning)
preguntas.explicacion: Two federal laws require language access services at no charge in programs receiving HHS funds: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, each with implementing regulations. Title VII and the ADA are anti-discrimination laws cited elsewhere; EMTALA and Title X govern emergencies and minors.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Professionals Required To Report; and Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect - State Statutes
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Are health care workers mandatory reporters of suspected child maltreatment?
opciones: Yes, in every state except the four that instead require everyone to report
Yes, but only in the states that also require training for those reporters
No, unless the child is a patient of that clinician's own practice already
No, the duty falls on the head of the facility, who files on their behalf
preguntas.explicacion: Physicians, nurses and other health care workers are named as mandated reporters in 46 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories. The four missing ones, Wyoming, North Carolina, New Jersey and Indiana, do not list professions at all, because they require every person to report. Training requirements exist in some states and change nothing about who must report.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin B12 — Consumer
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(e) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet asks which vitamin she is most likely to fall short on. Which one, and why?
opciones: Vitamin B12, because only animal foods carry it naturally
Vitamin B12, because plant foods block its absorption in the gut
Folate, because only animal foods carry it naturally
Vitamin C, because cooked plant foods lose almost all of it
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin B12 sits in a wide range of animal foods; plant foods hold none unless they have been fortified, so people who eat little or no animal food may fall short, and so may their infants when they are pregnant or breastfeeding. The adult recommended amount is 2.4 micrograms a day.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erikson's Stages of Psychosocial Development", Table
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · CMA F.1.c(7) / 2027 F.1.d(7) · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which conflict belongs to adolescence in Erikson's stages, and which strength comes from it?
opciones: Identity versus identity confusion, yielding fidelity
Intimacy versus isolation, yielding love as its virtue
Industry versus inferiority, yielding competence
Autonomy versus shame and doubt, yielding will
preguntas.explicacion: Each period pairs two opposing tendencies with the virtue gained from navigating them. Adolescence is the fifth stage, identity against identity confusion, and its virtue is fidelity, with repudiation as the malignancy. Intimacy against isolation belongs to young adulthood, industry against inferiority to school age.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Open Payments Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which program makes drug and device manufacturers report publicly what they pay physicians and teaching hospitals?
opciones: Open Payments, whose data goes up by the end of June each year
The exclusion list, which OIG refreshes at the start of a month
The compliance guidance, which the industry follows voluntarily
The designated health services code list, kept for the Stark law
preguntas.explicacion: The Open Payments program requires manufacturers of drugs, devices and biologics to report nearly every payment or transfer of value made to physicians, to certain practitioners who are not physicians and to teaching hospitals, together with ownership interests, and CMS posts the data by 30 June each year. Covered recipients are encouraged, not required, to review their entries.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(7), Workplace labeling
preguntas.subtema: Signs instead of labels · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: May an employer use a sign or a placard instead of putting a label on a fixed process container?
opciones: Yes, if it names the containers it covers and is available each shift
Yes, if the container is emptied and refilled at least once a week
No, every container of a hazardous chemical must carry its own label
No, unless the safety data sheet is posted beside the container
preguntas.explicacion: For an individual stationary process container the employer may post a sign or a placard, or lean on batch tickets, process sheets, operating procedures and similar written material, rather than affixing a label. Two conditions ride along: the alternative has to say which containers it applies to and carry the same information a workplace label would, and that written material has to stay within the employees' reach in their work area throughout every shift.

preguntas.subtema: Research consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Under the federal rule on research consent, what must a subject be told about withdrawing?
opciones: That leaving at any point costs no benefit they were entitled to
That leaving is allowed once the study's enrollment period has closed
That leaving requires the review board to approve the request first
That leaving forfeits any compensation paid for visits already made
preguntas.explicacion: Among the basic elements of research consent is a statement that taking part is voluntary, that refusing carries no penalty or loss of benefits the subject was otherwise entitled to, and that they may stop at any time on the same terms. Nothing in the rule makes withdrawal wait for board approval or tie it to the enrollment calendar.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Appointment lengths · CMAA 4A k51 k52 · CCMA 5B k173 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice simplifying its appointment book asks how many different appointment lengths it should keep. What does the improvement guide suggest?
opciones: Two, short and long, with a long appointment worth roughly two short ones
Three, short, standard and long, one for each of the three appointment types
One, since the guide asks that every appointment be made exactly the same length
Four, one for each appointment type plus a longer slot reserved for new patients
preguntas.explicacion: The advice is to cut the number of appointment types down to three — personal, team and unestablished — so as to minimize complexity, and to make them all roughly the same length. Length itself is then reduced to two options, short and long, where a long appointment is about the equivalent of two short ones.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: An entry in the alphabetic index ends with a dash. What is the coder being told?
opciones: More characters are needed, and only the tabular list has them
The entry is a manifestation code that has to be sequenced second
The code is invalid and another main term has to be looked up
The entry carries an excludes note over in the tabular list
preguntas.explicacion: The index does not always give the full code. A dash at the end of an index entry says that more characters are required, and laterality or an applicable seventh character can only be picked up in the tabular list. Even where no dash appears, the tabular list still has to be checked to see whether a seventh character is required.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cryotherapy in Dermatology", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: A patient treated with liquid nitrogen asks what the treated spot will do over the next days. What is expected?
opciones: Redness, blistering and crusting, with healing over several weeks
Redness and swelling only, with healing complete within about two days
Immediate blanching that fades in an hour, with no visible change afterward
A firm painless nodule that grows for a week and then resolves on its own
preguntas.explicacion: Erythema, blistering and crusting are the expected responses after cryotherapy, and healing usually takes several weeks by secondary intention. The complications worth counseling about are loss of pigment, scarring, nerve injury and recurrence, which is why undertreating a benign lesion is preferred: what persists can be treated at another visit.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(ix) and (d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Work practice controls at the bench · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist keeps a water bottle at the draw station and applies lip balm between patients. Which rule applies?
opciones: Eating, drinking and applying lip balm are all prohibited where exposure is reasonably likely
Drinking is allowed from a closed container, but cosmetics and lip balm are prohibited
Both are allowed if the counter is decontaminated with disinfectant at the end of the shift
Both are allowed as long as the water is not stored in a refrigerator with specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(ix) bans eating and drinking, smoking, handling contact lenses, and applying cosmetics or lip balm, anywhere occupational exposure can reasonably be expected. A closed bottle is not an exception the standard grants. The end-of-shift decontamination in (d)(4)(ii)(A) is a housekeeping duty and licenses nothing at the bench, and (d)(2)(x), which keeps food and drink out of refrigerators and off countertops where blood is kept, is a second and separate prohibition.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Preparation and Technique or Treatment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time · CPT D3 3E k60 k67 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: Ninety seconds have passed with the tourniquet on and the phlebotomist still cannot find a vein. What should happen next?
opciones: Release the band before two minutes and look again with a vein illuminator
Keep the band on until a vein appears, then draw all the tubes without pause
Tighten the band further until the radial pulse disappears at the wrist
Release the band and draw from the peripheral access line already in place
preguntas.explicacion: One guideline asks for the band to come off within a minute of placement and another sets the ceiling at two minutes, so at ninety seconds it is released. Illumination devices are recommended in place of a long application for veins that are hard to see, especially when two or more tubes are due.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Consent versus authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3 · RMA I.C.1.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice asks new patients to sign a consent for use of their information in treatment, payment and operations. What is the status of that form?
opciones: Voluntary, and it does not substitute for an authorization where one is required
Mandatory, since the rule requires written consent before any treatment begins
Mandatory, and it doubles as the acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices
Voluntary, but once signed it permits every disclosure the practice may wish to make
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may choose to obtain consent for treatment, for payment and for health care operations, but nothing obliges it to, and one that does has complete discretion over how the process runs. A consent document is not valid permission where the rule demands an authorization instead, nor where the rule attaches other conditions to the use or disclosure.

preguntas.subtema: Record completion · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Within what period after discharge must the hospital medical record be completed with a final diagnosis?
opciones: Thirty days following discharge
Twenty-four hours following discharge
Ninety days following discharge
Five years following discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The content standard closes with the final diagnosis and completion of the medical record within 30 days following discharge. The 24 hour figure belongs to the history and physical, which must be in the record within a day of admission and before anesthesia; five years is the minimum retention period for the record once it is complete.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Ethical Duties Relevant to Termination of the Therapeutic Relationship
preguntas.subtema: Mediation before dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: Attempts to repair the relationship with a patient who keeps missing appointments have come to nothing. Which step does the guidance place before termination?
opciones: Formal mediation by an ombudsperson, a professional mediator or a hospital ethics committee
Formal review by the state medical board, which rules on whether a dismissal is justified
A written warning setting out how many further missed visits will end the relationship
Notice to the insurer, which decides whether the patient may be dropped from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: Conflict resolution is expected to start by exploring the reasons underneath the disagreement and setting reasonable, clear expectations for the relationship going forward. Where those efforts fail, the step to consider is formal mediation by an ombudsperson, a professional mediator or a hospital ethics committee. Only where the conflict proves intractable does the standard notification procedure begin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2N · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the armrests of the patient's chair adjusted before an outpatient draw?
opciones: So the worker can act quickly if the patient has a vasovagal reaction
So the tourniquet can be anchored on the rest instead of the arm
So the tray of tubes can be balanced within the patient's reach
So the arm stays below heart level throughout the whole procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The chair is expected to be comfortable for both people, with the armrests set to a convenient position that also allows appropriate action if the patient has a vasovagal episode. Preparedness of that kind matters most in the patients who admit to fainting during earlier tests.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access scheduling · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A caller with a routine problem is told the next opening is six weeks away, and the practice is considering open access. What does that model do?
opciones: It offers every caller a slot on the day of the call, almost always with her own physician
It sorts callers by how urgent the problem sounds and books routine ones into a later week
It reserves about half of each day for the follow-up visits clinicians asked for in advance
It lets plan members go straight to a specialist, since the gatekeeper has been removed
preguntas.explicacion: Open access, also called advanced access or same-day scheduling, gives patients a slot the day they call, usually with their own clinician. Roughly half the day is left open; the rest holds clinically necessary follow-ups and the patients who preferred another day, normally no more than a quarter. The same words also name the removal of HMO gatekeepers, which is a different idea.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, row 10
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A glucose specimen will not reach the laboratory for two days. What does the additive in the gray top tube provide?
opciones: It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to five days
It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to twelve hours
It activates clotting so the glucose stays with the separated serum
It inactivates thrombin so the glucose stays with the plasma fraction
preguntas.explicacion: The light gray tube holds sodium fluoride with potassium oxalate. The oxalate binds calcium and stops clotting, and the fluoride is the antiglycolytic agent credited with preserving glucose for as much as five days. Clot activation belongs to the red tube and thrombin inactivation to the heparin tubes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A strip is regular at 48 per minute with a P wave ahead of every QRS. What does that fit?
opciones: Sinus bradycardia, since the pace still starts at the sinus node
Sinus arrhythmia, since the pace still starts at the sinus node
A first-degree block, since a P wave precedes every QRS
Atrial fibrillation, since the ventricular rate is slow
preguntas.explicacion: Every feature of sinus rhythm is present except the rate, which sits below 60, and that is what sinus bradycardia means. A first-degree block is defined by a PR interval past 200 ms rather than by the rate, and atrial fibrillation has no identifiable P waves at all.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Prepare the skin
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3G 3O k71 antiseptic for dermal puncture · PBT II.F technique · CCMA k130 cleansing · NCMA 2C.8 site preparation · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse hands you povidone iodine to prepare a 2-year-old's finger for a capillary puncture. What is the correct action?
opciones: Do not use povidone iodine for capillary punctures in children; apply alcohol and let it air dry
Use povidone iodine, since alcohol is not effective against skin flora on a child's finger
Use povidone iodine only on the heel; on the finger either antiseptic is acceptable
Use chlorhexidine instead, which the WHO prefers over alcohol for children under 2 months
preguntas.explicacion: Povidone iodine has no place in a dermal puncture on a child or a newborn; the skin is cleaned with alcohol and left to dry, exactly as in an adult. Chlorhexidine is the antiseptic ruled out under 2 months of age, and that rule belongs to venepuncture rather than to the lancet.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Treadmill Stress Testing", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F5 k154 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(c) · RMA III.F.6.c.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Which finding is an absolute reason to stop a treadmill test?
opciones: Moderate to severe angina during the exercise stages
Mild leg tiredness with no change seen on the tracing
A rise in systolic pressure with each stage of exercise
A heart rate that reaches 85% of the target for the age
preguntas.explicacion: The absolute list includes moderate to severe angina, a fall in systolic pressure over 10 mm Hg with other evidence of ischemia, growing neurologic symptoms, signs of poor perfusion such as pallor, trouble monitoring the tracing, the patient asking to stop, and sustained ventricular tachycardia.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Muscular System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient shivers when the room is cold. Which function of muscle contraction does that use?
opciones: Heat production, which accounts for most of the heat made in the body
Posture, which accounts for most of the heat made in the body
Joint stability, which accounts for most of the heat made in the body
Contractility, which accounts for none of the heat made in the body
preguntas.explicacion: Besides producing movement, muscle contraction holds posture, stabilizes joints through the tendons that cross them, and makes heat. Heat production is not a side issue: muscle contraction supplies nearly 85 percent of the body's heat, which is what shivering exploits.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(i); OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens and Needlestick Prevention: Evaluating and Controlling Exposure
preguntas.subtema: Order of controls · CPT D1 k31 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: According to paragraph (d)(2)(i) of the standard, when is personal protective equipment required?
opciones: When occupational exposure remains after engineering and work practice controls are in place
Instead of engineering controls, when the employer documents that safer devices cost more
Only when an exposure incident has already occurred and follow-up is under way
Before engineering controls are considered, as the first line of protection
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(i) sets the order: engineering and work practice controls come first, to remove exposure or cut it down, and PPE is added where exposure survives them. OSHA's page on evaluating and controlling exposure reads that to mean the employer has to look at an effective control fit for the clinical setting, a safety-engineered sharp for instance, and put it in place; the text grants no exemption for cost. PPE is preventive, not something that begins after an incident.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Supraventricular Tachycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which features describe a supraventricular tachycardia?
opciones: A narrow QRS under 120 ms with a rate above 100 a minute
A wide QRS over 120 ms with a rate above 100 a minute
A narrow QRS under 120 ms with a rate below 60 a minute
A narrow QRS under 120 ms arising below the His bundle
preguntas.explicacion: The term covers the fast rhythms that start at or above the atrioventricular node. The narrow complex is the giveaway: it means the ventricles were activated through the normal pathway from above the His bundle. Rates in adults run over 100 and often between 150 and 220.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Compensating for visual deficits
preguntas.subtema: Vision impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.a · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: An office is reprinting its handouts for a geriatric clinic. What is the minimum type size recommended for older patients?
opciones: 14-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
10-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
12-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
18-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
preguntas.explicacion: Printed handouts and questionnaires for older patients should use at least 14-point type in an easy-to-read typeface, with enough space between items to answer. Where low vision makes reading hard, offer something else: instructions in audio, diagrams enlarged, or pillboxes with raised markings.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Downtime drills · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Staff have never worked a shift on paper. Which training practice does the contingency guidance recommend to fix that?
opciones: Unannounced downtime drills held at least once a year for the whole staff
A yearly written test on the downtime policy graded by the security official
A refresher whenever the record system is upgraded by its own developer
A briefing given to every new hire during the first week of employment
preguntas.explicacion: At any moment an organization is likely to have staff who have never worked in a paper-based environment. The guidance answers that with training requirements, paper-based ordering and charting practice, and downtime drills held without warning at least once a year, so people meet the situation before it is real.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Hyperventilation", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.q · 2027 I.B.8.q · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is breathing fast and deep and complains of tingling around the mouth and spasm in both hands. What should be considered first?
opciones: That rapid breathing may signal a medical emergency and needs assessment
That the spasm is a side effect of the patient's own inhaler being overused
That the tingling is a sign the oxygen level in the blood has fallen too low
That the patient has a bleeding disorder, since the hands are involved too
preguntas.explicacion: Overbreathing drops the carbon dioxide level and produces lightheadedness, a feeling of not catching the breath, chest pain or pounding heartbeat, dry mouth, muscle spasms of hands and feet, and numbness or tingling in the arms or around the mouth. The cause may be emotional, as in a panic attack, or medical, such as bleeding or infection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulmonary Function Tests", Lung Volume
preguntas.pregunta: Which measurement is the standard for diagnosing a restrictive ventilatory defect?
opciones: Total lung capacity, with a value below 80% of predicted
The ratio of the one-second volume to the vital capacity
The diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide, when it is low
The peak expiratory flow, taken as a share of personal best
preguntas.explicacion: Total lung capacity is the volume in the lungs at the end of a maximal breath in, and it is the standard for restriction: under 80% of predicted is diagnostic. Lung volumes are measured by body plethysmography, the standard method, or by gas dilution with nitrogen or helium. Diffusing capacity is interpreted alongside spirometry and volumes, not alone.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1252(b); CDC, MMWR RR-54(13) (2005), Physical Requirements for Testing
preguntas.subtema: Environmental conditions · CPT D5 k90 · PBT VI.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.d · RMA III.C.3.e
preguntas.pregunta: Which environmental conditions does CLIA say a laboratory must monitor and document when they affect reagent storage or test performance?
opciones: Temperature, humidity, water quality and protection from electrical fluctuations
Temperature, lighting, noise level and the number of operators per shift
Humidity, barometric pressure, altitude and the color of the work surfaces
Water quality, air exchanges per hour, and the distance to the nearest sink
preguntas.explicacion: The laboratory sets out the conditions essential for storing reagents and specimens and for running and reporting reliably, in line with what the manufacturer's instructions say, then monitors and documents them. The four named, where they apply, are water quality, temperature, humidity, and keeping instruments safe from current that fluctuates or cuts out. Extremes of humidity can degrade reagents and blur test endpoints.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Indications: Sublingual and Buccal Routes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(v) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Nitroglycerin for angina is placed under the tongue instead of being swallowed. What is the reason?
opciones: More than 90% of a swallowed dose is cleared in a single pass through the liver
A swallowed tablet would irritate the lining of the stomach and the small intestine
Sublingual tissue absorbs slowly, which stretches out the effect of every dose
Swallowed nitroglycerin is destroyed by acid before it reaches the small intestine
preguntas.explicacion: Sublingual and buccal drugs diffuse into the venous blood of the mouth, which drains into the superior vena cava rather than the hepatic portal vein, so the first-pass effect is avoided. Nitroglycerin is the standard example: more than 90% of it is cleared in one pass through the liver, so a swallowed tablet would leave almost nothing. The permeable mucosa also makes the onset fast, and the tablet can be removed if needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Counting between two R waves on a regular strip gives four large squares. What rate does that work out to?
opciones: 75 per minute, from 300 divided by the large squares
60 per minute, from 300 divided by the large squares
80 per minute, from 400 divided by the large squares
100 per minute, from 400 divided by the large squares
preguntas.explicacion: On a regular rhythm the rate is 300 divided by the number of large squares between two R waves, so four large squares give 75 beats per minute. That value sits inside the normal band of 60 to 100, so it is neither bradycardia nor tachycardia.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Cardiac Axis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k151 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.a.iii
preguntas.pregunta: How is a normal cardiac axis picked out quickly?
opciones: The QRS complex points upward in both lead I and lead aVF
The QRS complex points downward in both lead I and lead aVF
The QRS complex points upward in lead I and downward in aVF
The QRS complex points downward in lead I and upward in aVF
preguntas.explicacion: The axis is the direction the wave of depolarization takes in the frontal plane, normally between -30 and +90 degrees. The shortcut is to read leads I and aVF: positive in both is normal, negative in I with positive in aVF is the right axis deviation seen in dextrocardia.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): Do I need to notify anyone if I make any changes?
preguntas.subtema: Changes reported within 30 days · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.v
preguntas.pregunta: A waived testing site moves to a new suite across town and hires a new laboratory director. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Notify the state agency of both changes within 30 days of the change
Notify the state agency of both changes within 90 days of the change
Apply for a new certificate, since a certificate cannot move with the site
Notify CMS only of the new director; the address is updated at renewal
preguntas.explicacion: For every certificate type, changes in ownership, name, location or laboratory director must be reported to the state agency within 30 days. Accredited laboratories also tell their accreditation organization, and high complexity COC laboratories report a change of technical supervisor on the same timeline. A move does not require a brand-new application; adding nonwaived tests does.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ventricular Fibrillation", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i
preguntas.pregunta: What does ventricular fibrillation write on the monitor?
opciones: Fibrillatory waves, with no QRS complexes that can be made out
Wide complexes, marching regularly at a rate faster than 100
A flat line, with no P waves, QRS complexes or T waves at all
Narrow complexes, with a sawtooth line running between them
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing is chaotic and disorganized: coarse or fine fibrillatory waves with no discernible complexes, matched by a patient who has collapsed with no pulse. The flat line belongs to asystole, the sawtooth to flutter and the wide regular run to tachycardia.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antihistamines", Indications and Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.a · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which condition is treated with an H2 receptor antagonist rather than with an H1 antagonist?
opciones: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
Allergic rhinitis with sneezing
Chronic urticaria with hives
Pruritus from histamine release
preguntas.explicacion: The two receptor subtypes are treated by two different groups of drugs. H1 antagonists cover allergic disease, whether IgE mediated or not: allergic rhinitis, chronic urticaria, and the itching, vasodilation and swelling that histamine produces. H2 antagonists cut gastric acid secretion, which is why they are used in reflux and in functional dyspepsia, and why they are combined with a proton pump inhibitor for tighter control.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Devices Associated with Needlestick Injuries and Figure 1
preguntas.subtema: Devices behind the injuries · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices account for most of the percutaneous injuries hospitals report to national surveillance?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles, above all hypodermic and winged-steel needles
Suture needles, followed by the scalpel blades used in minor surgery
Glass items, above all broken capillary tubes and specimen slides
Retractable lancets used for the finger and heel sticks of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Surveillance over four years collected close to 5,000 percutaneous injuries, and hollow-bore needles were involved in 62 percent of them: hypodermic needles on disposable syringes took 29 percent and winged-steel needles 13 percent. Glass followed at 17 percent and suture needles at 15 percent, with phlebotomy needles themselves at 4 percent. Hollow-bore needles weigh most because they carry a measurable volume of blood, which is why devices that enter a vein or an artery get the highest priority for replacement with safer ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Violations of HIPAA; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Civil and Criminal Violations
preguntas.subtema: Penalty tiers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: Among the HIPAA civil penalty tiers, which category carries the highest penalty per violation?
opciones: Willful neglect that is not corrected
Willful neglect corrected within the period
Reasonable cause, not willful neglect
A violation the person did not know about
preguntas.explicacion: The four civil tiers climb with culpability: not knowing of the violation, reasonable cause short of willful neglect, willful neglect put right inside the required period, and willful neglect left uncorrected, which tops the scale at $50,000 per violation. Criminal liability is a separate ladder, starting with knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable information, rising when it is done under false pretenses, and rising again when it is done for commercial advantage, for personal gain, or to do malicious harm. The civil side is enforced by the Office for Civil Rights.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient holds beliefs about her plan of care that the assistant does not share. How should the information be given?
opciones: In a nonjudgmental way, even though the beliefs are not the same
By agreeing with the belief so that she stays in the conversation
After moving her to a quieter area where the beliefs can be argued
Through a family member who already shares the same viewpoint
preguntas.explicacion: Differences in perception and viewpoint are a listed barrier: patients who feel their beliefs are not valued tend to disengage from the conversation and from the plan of care, so information is given without judgment even when the views differ. Agreeing is named as a pitfall, and routing the message through a relative is what the interpreter guidance warns against.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who kept working past sixty-five retires in March. How long does she then have to sign up for Part B?
opciones: Eight months from the day she or her spouse stops working, COBRA notwithstanding
Eight months from the day the job-based coverage itself ends, COBRA included
Seven months around her sixty-fifth birthday, a period that has already passed
Sixty-three days, the gap allowed before a drug coverage penalty begins to run
preguntas.explicacion: The eight-month Special Enrollment Period for Part B starts when the person or the spouse stops working, even if COBRA or some other non-Medicare coverage is taken up in the meantime. Someone who loses job-based coverage before that date has eight months from then. Missing the period means a wait, a gap and a monthly penalty for as long as Part B is held.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Managed Care, Summary
preguntas.subtema: Managed care · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which three plan designs are usually grouped together as managed care?
opciones: Health maintenance, preferred provider and point of service plans
Health maintenance, preferred provider and prescription drug plans
Health savings, flexible spending and high deductible health plans
Hospital insurance, medical insurance and supplemental policies
preguntas.explicacion: Managed care plans contract with providers and facilities to care for members at reduced cost, and the three types described are the health maintenance organization, the preferred provider organization and the point of service plan, which lets the patient choose between the two approaches at each visit. Savings and spending accounts are ways to pay costs, not plan designs, and hospital plus medical insurance describes the two parts of Original Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Surgical Fire Safety", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k80 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.j
preguntas.pregunta: A fire starts on the patient during a procedure. What is the first sequence of actions?
opciones: Stop the supplemental gas, remove the burning material, then put the fire out
Put the fire out, then stop the supplemental gas, then remove the burning material
Remove the burning material, then assess the patient, then stop the supplemental gas
Isolate the room, then stop the supplemental gas, then remove the burning material
preguntas.explicacion: For a fire on or in the patient the steps run in order: stop administering supplemental gas, take away the material that is burning and extinguish the fire. Only then is the patient assessed and cared for. Notifying the right people and isolating the room come last, and the room is isolated when the fire cannot be controlled or contained.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.2 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which move is suggested to quiet muscle tremor coming from the limbs?
opciones: Move the limb electrodes up to the arms and the thighs
Move the chest electrodes down one intercostal space
Move the limb electrodes down to the wrists and ankles
Move the patient from the table to a seated position
preguntas.explicacion: After reassuring the patient, the limb electrodes may be shifted onto the upper arms and the thighs to get away from the muscles that are generating the signal. Other steps in the same list are moving or removing the pillow, tucking the hands under the buttocks and raising the knees on a pillow.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.3 Wound Assessment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l
preguntas.pregunta: How are the length and width of a wound measured, and how is a tunnel located?
opciones: Length on the head-to-toe axis and width side to side, with tunnels placed by clock face
Length side to side and width on the head-to-toe axis, with tunnels placed by clock face
Length on the head-to-toe axis and width side to side, with tunnels placed by compass point
Length along the longest visible edge and width across it, with tunnels placed by quadrant
preguntas.explicacion: Wounds are recorded as length by width in centimeters, with length taken on the head-to-toe axis and width laterally from side to side, and the same method is used by everyone so the records compare. Depth is probed with a sterile cotton-tipped applicator, and the site of a tunnel is described using a clock face with 12:00 toward the patient's head.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Upper Limbs; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins" (2023), section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which veins join to form the brachial vein, and is the brachial vein superficial or deep?
opciones: The radial and ulnar veins; it is a deep vein
The cephalic and basilic veins; it is superficial
The median cubital and cephalic veins; it is superficial
The axillary and subclavian veins; it is a deep vein
preguntas.explicacion: The radial and the ulnar veins run alongside the bones of the forearm and come together to form the brachial vein, a deep vessel that carries on into the axillary vein; in the forearm those deep veins travel in pairs beside the arteries as venae comitantes and merge at the cubital fossa. Cephalic and basilic are the superficial pair, and the axillary and subclavian lie further along.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Semi-Fowler's Position; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning" (NBK513320)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(2) · RMA III.F.2.a.i · NCMA 2B.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which angle of the head of the bed defines the semi-Fowler position?
opciones: 30 to 45 degrees, and it is better tolerated over long stretches of time
45 to 90 degrees, which is the range of the Fowler position itself
60 to 90 degrees, the range used while a nasogastric tube is placed
0 to 15 degrees, with the head raised only slightly off the flat bed
preguntas.explicacion: Semi-Fowler keeps the head of the bed between 30 and 45 degrees, with the hips flexed or not, and it serves the same purposes as Fowler while being easier to hold for hours. Fowler itself runs from 45 degrees upward, and the high or full variant, at 60 to 90 degrees, is what lowers the risk of aspiration while an orogastric or nasogastric tube goes down.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In a spun hematocrit tube, what makes up the thin pale layer between the packed red cells and the plasma?
opciones: Leukocytes and platelets, normally under 1 percent of the sample
Reticulocytes, normally 1 to 2 percent of the red cell count
Plasma proteins, roughly 7 percent of the plasma volume
Fibrin strands with trapped platelets from a forming clot
preguntas.explicacion: That pale band is the buffy coat. It holds the formed elements that are not red cells, the white cells and the platelets, and normally amounts to less than 1 percent of the sample. Reticulocytes are immature red cells, not a separate layer; the plasma proteins are dissolved in the plasma above; and fibrin only appears if the sample has been allowed to clot, which an anticoagulated hematocrit tube has not.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Lung Exam", Function: Palpation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.1.a(4) · RMA III.F.3.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: The examiner places both hands on the patient's back and asks him to say ninety-nine. Which method is that?
opciones: Palpation, assessing tactile fremitus over the chest wall
Percussion, comparing resonance from the apices to the bases
Auscultation, comparing the sound over each of the lung zones
Inspection, judging the symmetry of movement of the chest wall
preguntas.explicacion: Tactile fremitus is felt, not heard, so it belongs to palpation. Increased fremitus points to denser lung tissue, while decreased fremitus points to something separating pleura from parenchyma, such as an effusion or a pneumothorax. On the chest the order is to look, then feel, then percuss, then listen, remembered with position as PIPPA.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the fist placed to give abdominal thrusts to a standing adult?
opciones: Thumb side in, just above the navel, gripped tightly with the other hand
Thumb side in, on the middle of the breastbone, level with the nipples
Flat over the lowest ribs on the left, with both hands pressing inward
Just below the navel, with the thrusts aimed straight backward and down
preguntas.explicacion: The rescuer stands behind the patient, reaches around the waist, and sets the fist thumb side in just above the navel; the other hand grasps that fist and the thrusts go quickly upward and inward. The fist on the middle of the breastbone belongs to the pregnant or obese patient, whose thrusts go backward against the chest.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Cost sharing
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does cost sharing in Medicaid and CHIP differ from cost sharing in a commercial plan?
opciones: In those programs the premium counts as cost sharing too
In those programs the deductible is never counted into it
In those programs only the copayment is counted into it
In those programs the balance billed amount is counted in
preguntas.explicacion: Cost sharing is the member's own share of the cost of covered services, and it generally covers deductibles, coinsurance and copayments while leaving out premiums, balance-billed amounts and non-covered care. In Medicaid and CHIP the federal glossary counts premiums within cost sharing as well, which is the exception worth remembering.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: An employer and a health plan exchange the payment of the plan premium electronically. Is that one of the transactions HIPAA standardized?
opciones: Yes, premium payment is on the list of adopted transactions
No, only claims and remittances are on that adopted list
No, only exchanges between a plan and a provider are on it
Yes, but only where a clearinghouse handles it for the two
preguntas.explicacion: The adopted transactions run wider than the claim. On the list sit payment and remittance advice; the status of a claim; eligibility; how benefits are coordinated; claims and encounter data; enrollment and disenrolment; referrals and authorizations; and the payment of the premium. Several of them, that last one included, never involve a provider at all.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5
preguntas.pregunta: When is RhoGAM (Rh immune globulin) normally given to an Rh negative pregnant patient?
opciones: In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 3 hours after the birth
In weeks 12 to 14 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
Only within 72 hours after the birth of a second Rh positive baby
preguntas.explicacion: RhoGAM temporarily prevents the Rh negative parent from forming anti-Rh antibodies by destroying any fetal Rh positive cells that cross the placenta, and it is normally given during weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours of birth. Since its introduction in 1968 the incidence of hemolytic disease of the newborn in such pregnancies fell from about 13 to 14 percent to about 0.1 percent.

preguntas.subtema: Consent in the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which item does the medical record condition of participation expect to find in the chart before a procedure the medical staff has designated?
opciones: An informed consent form, properly executed, for that procedure or treatment
A copy of the notice of privacy practices signed by the patient at check-in
An advance beneficiary notice explaining what the health plan may not pay for
A statement from the patient describing why the procedure is being requested
preguntas.explicacion: The record must document, as appropriate, informed consent forms properly executed for whichever procedures and treatments the medical staff, or Federal or State law, has specified as needing written consent. The same list runs to consultative evaluations, complications and infections acquired in hospital, every practitioner order and the nursing notes, records of treatment and of medication, reports from radiology and from the laboratory, and the vital signs.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements, Sites of Hemopoiesis
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In an adult, where does most hemopoiesis take place?
opciones: Red marrow of the skull, pelvis, vertebrae, sternum and upper femur
Red marrow in the medullary cavity of the long bones, as in children
The liver and spleen, which take over from the marrow after birth
The yolk sac, then the fetal liver, spleen and lymphatic tissue
preguntas.explicacion: After birth the red marrow does nearly all of it, and in an adult the work is limited to the bones of the skull and pelvis, the vertebrae, the breastbone and the near ends of the femur and humerus. A child also makes blood in the marrow cavity of the long bones. Liver and spleen keep the ability, called extramedullary hemopoiesis, but step in only when the marrow fails.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label: Serving Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient points at the serving size on a package and asks whether that is how much he is supposed to eat. What is the correct explanation?
opciones: It reflects how much people usually eat, not how much he should eat
It reflects how much he should eat to stay within his calorie needs
It is set by each manufacturer to match its own package sizes
It is the amount that supplies 100% of the Daily Value for the day
preguntas.explicacion: The serving size is standardized so similar products can be compared, and it is drawn from the amount people typically consume. It is a reference point, not a target. Every number on the panel, calories included, is tied to it, so eating two servings doubles the calories, the nutrient grams and the percentages.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 16: Discuss and resolve patients' concerns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A patient quietly stopped a medicine because of a side effect. What does the toolkit tell the practice to do?
opciones: Ask what makes the medicine hard to take, and act on side effect reports
Restate the importance of the medicine and schedule an earlier follow-up
Switch to a combination product, which removes most side effect problems
Note the nonadherence in the chart and let the prescriber address it later
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are asked directly whether anything makes their medicines difficult or impossible to take, and reports of side effects are taken seriously, because otherwise people stop without saying so. What comes next depends on the obstacle: cost goes to the tool on paying less, and physical or cognitive trouble can be met with presorted packets from the pharmacy.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Susceptible staff and airborne pathogens · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist who has never had chickenpox or the vaccine is assigned to a patient with varicella on Airborne Precautions. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Restrict her from the room if immune personnel are available to do the draw
Let her draw with an N95, since the respirator makes immunity irrelevant
Let her draw with a surgical mask, since varicella spreads by droplets
Restrict her permanently from all patients on Transmission-Based Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's airborne recommendations keep susceptible staff out of the room of a patient who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox, measles, smallpox or disseminated zoster, provided immune colleagues are on hand to do the work, and they ask that susceptible people be immunized as soon as possible after an unprotected contact with a vaccine-preventable infection. Whoever does go in wears the respirator, but that does not cancel the preference for immune staff. Varicella belongs on the airborne list, not the droplet one, and the restriction attaches to this patient rather than to every isolation room.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · D2 k47 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A serology test is ordered. Which two tubes list immunology and serology among their uses?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the gold serum separator tube
The red clot activator tube and the purple top EDTA tube
The gold serum separator tube and the light green PST tube
The pale yellow ACD tube and the gold serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Immunology and serology appear against two rows of the table: the red clot activator tube at position 4 and the separator tube at position 5, both of which give serum. EDTA is assigned to hematology and cross-match, the PST to chemistries, and the ACD tube to tissue typing and DNA work.

preguntas.fuente: DEA Diversion Control Division, Definition of Controlled Substance Schedules: Schedule I
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k15 · CMA 2027 I.D.1 · RMA III.G.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does placement in Schedule I mean for a substance?
opciones: No medical use accepted anywhere in the country, plus a high potential for abuse
An accepted medical use, and abuse that may lead to severe physical dependence
An accepted medical use, and an abuse potential lower than that of Schedule II
An accepted medical use, and abuse that leads only to limited physical dependence
preguntas.explicacion: Three conditions define Schedule I at once: the drug has no medical use accepted anywhere in the country, it cannot be considered safe even under a clinician's supervision, and its abuse potential is high. Heroin, LSD, marijuana, peyote, methaqualone and MDMA are the listed examples. From Schedule II down, every drug does have an accepted medical use, and the schedules rank abuse potential and dependence from there.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Personal protection and hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Between procedures · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How often should hand hygiene be performed when two different samples are collected from the same patient?
opciones: Before and after the contact, and also between the procedures
Once before the first procedure and once after the last one
Only after the second procedure, when the gloves come off
Only if the gloves tore or blood reached the skin underneath
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table sets hand hygiene before and after each patient contact and also between procedures on the same patient, because the point is to reduce cross-contamination, which can happen within one encounter as well as between two patients. The gloves follow the same logic, one clean pair per patient or per procedure. Waiting for a torn glove or visible blood is a different rule, the one that forces washing after contact with blood.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 12: Assess patients' learning style and readiness to learn
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has just been given a new diagnosis and looks overwhelmed. What should guide how much teaching happens now?
opciones: Check readiness to learn and ask how she prefers to receive information
Give the full teaching now, because the diagnosis makes it most relevant
Postpone all teaching until the next visit as a matter of routine
Give only written material now, since spoken words will not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: Before material is handed over, the patient is asked how she likes to learn, whether by reading, diagrams, listening, video or an interactive program, and whether she is ready to take information in. Right after a new diagnosis a patient may not be ready for much, which is why the question is asked rather than assumed.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Needle Shield
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After activating the shield on a safety needle, the phlebotomist notices the tip is still visible at the end of the shield. Against which FDA design recommendation does this fall short?
opciones: The shield must fully enclose the needle and block finger access
The sharp should end up drawn right back inside the body of the device
The housing of a fixed recessed needle should extend beyond the sharp
Color should be used for a clear, specific purpose
preguntas.explicacion: FDA Table 1 gives one recommendation per feature type: a needle shield should enclose the needle completely and keep fingers away once activated; a retractable sharp should end up drawn right back inside the housing; and a fixed recessed needle should have a housing that extends beyond and fully covers the sharp. A shield that leaves the tip exposed fails the first of these; the retraction rule applies to a different design.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1, Recommended needle gauge, length and device; and CDC, NIOSH Alert: Preventing Needlestick Injuries in Health Care Settings, DHHS (NIOSH) Publication No. 2000-108 (Nov. 1999), PDF de CDC Stacks
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes and lengths · CPT D3 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture on an adult with ordinary veins, which needle does WHO Table 3.1 list with a length of 1 to 1.5 inches?
preguntas.explicacion: Table 3.1 gives the adult 21 G needle a length of 1 to 1.5 inch (2.54 cm), and the adult 22 G needle 1 inch. The 23 G appears for adults at 1 to 1.5 inch as a straight needle, but for children and neonates only as a 0.5 inch winged set. Sixteen to eighteen gauge is reserved for blood donation, and 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable for every age group.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Biopsy", Equipment and Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: An excised skin lesion is going to pathology. What is the usual fixative, and when is something else needed?
opciones: Formalin usually; direct immunofluorescence or tissue culture needs another medium
Sterile saline usually; direct immunofluorescence or tissue culture needs formalin instead
Formalin usually; a pigmented lesion needs the specimen sent in a dry sterile container
Michel's solution usually; a routine histology specimen needs it diluted with saline first
preguntas.explicacion: Most biopsy specimens go into formalin, but some studies do not tolerate it: a tissue culture, or direct immunofluorescence, needs another medium such as Michel's solution or sterile saline. Blistering conditions may need lesional and perilesional samples in different media, so the pathologist is consulted beforehand to be sure the right container is on the tray.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Both pedal pulses are easily felt in a patient being screened for peripheral arterial disease. What does that finding allow?
opciones: Leaving the ankle-brachial index aside, since disease is unlikely at that point
Leaving the ankle-brachial index aside only if the patient has no diabetes
Calling the screen negative once the femoral pulses are found to match them
Repeating the palpation in a month in place of ordering any other test
preguntas.explicacion: Palpating the pulses of both feet is a cheap screen. When they are present on both sides the chance of peripheral arterial disease falls below 3.5%, low enough to skip the ankle-brachial index, which compares ankle with arm systolic pressure and costs time, equipment and training. No extra condition is attached to that finding.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Explanation of benefits · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.3.b(2) · RMA II.A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls upset about the explanation of benefits she received, saying she cannot pay that bill today. What should she be told?
opciones: It explains how the claim was handled and what she may owe; it is not the bill itself
It is the bill from her health plan, and payment goes to the plan rather than the office
It is the plan's request for more information before it decides whether to pay
It is the written order her primary care doctor sent so the plan would pay
preguntas.explicacion: The notice a patient gets after adjudication reports the services billed, what the plan paid, and the most the patient may owe the provider. In Original Medicare the equivalent document is the Medicare Summary Notice, which states plainly that it is not a bill.
