A request for more information and a referral from the primary care doctor are entirely different documents.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2, Selecting the length of lancet
preguntas.subtema: Lancets · CPT D3 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: When choosing a lancet for an adult finger-prick, why does the WHO advise one slightly shorter than the depth that seems necessary?
opciones: Pressure compresses the skin, so the puncture ends up slightly deeper than the lancet length
Shorter lancets give more blood, because the capillary bed lies in the upper dermis
The finger-prick must never exceed 1.5 mm, and most lancets are longer than that
Thinner and shorter lancets are the only ones that retract to prevent needle-sticks
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.2 explains that the lancet picked is a little shorter than the depth estimated because the pressure applied compresses the skin, making the actual puncture a little deeper than the lancet length; pain rises with penetration depth, though blood volume rises with it too. Lengths run from 0.85 mm to 2.2 mm, and an adult finger-prick should not exceed 2.4 mm, not 1.5 mm.

preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(2) and 3(3); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b)
preguntas.subtema: Definitions added by the Act · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which two terms did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act add to the definitions in the bloodborne pathogens standard?
opciones: Sharps with engineered protections, and needleless systems
Universal Precautions, and the definition of an exposure incident
Regulated waste, and the definition of a contaminated sharp
Occupational exposure, and the definition of regulated waste
preguntas.explicacion: The Act put two definitions into 29 CFR 1910.1030(b). One covers sharps that carry engineered sharps injury protections: a needle or non-needle sharp used to draw fluids, reach a vein or artery, or give medication, built with a feature that lowers the risk of exposure. The other covers needleless systems, devices that take fluids out once access is established, deliver medication, or handle other tasks carrying percutaneous risk, all without a needle. Universal Precautions, exposure incident, occupational exposure, regulated waste and contaminated sharps were already defined in the 1991 standard.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: What to ask before booking · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to book her first video visit says she has no health insurance and is worried about the bill. What does the patient guidance tell her to do?
opciones: Ask beforehand what the visit will cost, since her provider may know of local resources
Book the visit anyway, since a visit taken by video is free of charge to the patient
Ask her plan for a preauthorization, which will fix in advance what she is going to owe
Wait for an in-person appointment instead, since a price is quoted only for those visits
preguntas.explicacion: Before a telehealth visit the patient is told to know the costs and to ask what the visit will come to. If she cannot afford it or has no health insurance, her provider may have local resources. The same list asks her to say if she needs help such as a screen reader or closed captioning, to check the details in the reminder she is sent, to find a quiet spot with good internet, and to test her device beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 3D k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A syringe draw is planned for a small child. Which adjustment does the device table call for?
opciones: A smaller syringe together with a pediatric laboratory tube
A larger syringe together with a standard adult laboratory tube
A smaller syringe together with a standard adult laboratory tube
A larger syringe together with two pediatric laboratory tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where a needle and syringe is used on a pediatric patient, the table asks for a smaller syringe and a pediatric laboratory tube. The parallel adjustment for the evacuated system is a smaller tube with a reduced vacuum, which is there to keep the specimen from haemolysing.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse practitioner on the exclusion list writes an order that the practice then acts on. What does exclusion mean for payment?
opciones: No federal program pays for anything she furnishes, orders or prescribes
No federal program pays her directly, though her employer may still bill for it
No federal program pays her until the exclusion period ends and lapses by itself
No federal program pays for what she furnishes, but her written orders are payable
preguntas.explicacion: An excluded person can be paid nothing by federal health care programs for any item or service she furnishes, orders or prescribes, and that bites on every program whose health benefits the United States funds, directly or indirectly, with the Federal Employees Health Benefits Plan as the one carve-out. The order itself is caught, not only the hands-on service.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: General Provisions
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A man holds a limited health care power of attorney covering only his mother's life support decisions. What may he access?
opciones: Only the protected health information relevant to the decision his authority actually covers
The complete designated record set, because any power of attorney makes him her representative
No information, since a power of attorney is not a document the Privacy Rule recognizes
Only the billing records, because clinical information stays with the patient in every case
preguntas.explicacion: A personal representative must generally be treated as the individual, but the scope of that authority comes from the underlying law. Where it is broad, as with a parent of a minor or the guardian of an incompetent adult, the representative is treated as the individual for all purposes; where it is limited to particular decisions, the representative is treated as the individual only for information relevant to that representation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Green and Red
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: The emergency department wants immediate chemistry results. Which tube is commonly used for stat chemistry, and what type of sample does it produce?
opciones: A green heparin tube, which yields plasma rather than serum
A red tube with no additive, which yields serum after clotting
A lavender EDTA tube, which yields plasma for hematology
A gray oxalate tube, which yields plasma for glucose and lactate
preguntas.explicacion: Green heparin tubes are often used when stat or immediate chemistry results are requested for emergency cases, and unlike red tubes the sample they give is plasma, not serum. The red tube has to clot first, typically 10 to 15 minutes, before centrifugation. The lavender tube is for hematologic assays and the gray tube for glucose and lactic acid.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Contact Transmission and Vehicle Transmission
preguntas.subtema: Fomites and indirect contact · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A doorknob contaminated by an infected person's hands is an example of which element of disease transmission?
opciones: A fomite, in indirect contact transmission
A vehicle, like contaminated food or water
A mechanical vector, like a fly carrying bacteria
A droplet nucleus, the residue of an evaporated droplet
preguntas.explicacion: Indirect contact transmission works through fomites, inanimate objects that pick up pathogens from an infected person or reservoir and pass them to a new host who touches them and then a portal of entry; doorknobs, towels and tablecloths are the everyday examples, and improperly sterilized syringes, needles and catheters are the clinical ones behind many healthcare-associated infections. Vehicle transmission is through water, food or air; a mechanical vector is an animal carrying the pathogen on its body; and a droplet nucleus is what remains when a droplet desiccates in the air.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(c), Content of notification
preguntas.subtema: Breach notice content · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a breach notification letter to an individual include?
opciones: Steps the individual can take to protect against potential harm
The name of the workforce member who caused the breach
A copy of the covered entity's complete privacy policies and procedures
The civil penalty amount the covered entity expects to pay to HHS
preguntas.explicacion: In plain language, and as far as it can, the letter describes what happened, with the date of the breach and the date it was discovered; which types of unsecured PHI were involved, such as a name, a Social Security number, a date of birth or a diagnosis; what individuals should do to protect themselves; what the entity is doing to investigate, to limit the harm and to stop it happening again; and how to make contact, by toll-free number, e-mail, website or postal address. Naming the employee, attaching the policies and estimating penalties are no part of the required content.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Common Pitfalls), Negative body language
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k15 · CCMA 6 k197 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Standing over a seated patient with arms crossed while asking about allergies illustrates which communication pitfall?
opciones: Negative body language
Value judgments
Approving or disapproving
Agreeing or disagreeing
preguntas.explicacion: The table pictures negative body language as arms folded, an air of distraction, or looming over the seated patient. The recommended posture is the reverse: eye contact, an interested expression, leaning forward, sitting close. Value judgments and approving or disapproving responses are verbal pitfalls about the provider's opinions, not matters of posture.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hematocrit", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Centrifuge handling · PBT IV.A.2 / IV.B.1 · CCMA 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.b · RMA III.C.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: To save time between patients, an assistant lifts the microhematocrit centrifuge lid as soon as the rotor starts slowing and pulls the tubes out. What is the problem?
opciones: Interrupting the spin makes an inaccurate result more likely; the lid stays closed until the rotor has stopped
It is acceptable provided the tubes were sealed with clay, since the packed cells cannot move once the rotor begins to slow
The tubes must be re-spun for one extra minute, because otherwise the plasma column is read too high
Only the buffy coat is disturbed, so the packed cell column may still be read as long as it is done immediately
preguntas.explicacion: Whether the macro- or microhematocrit method is used, the centrifuge must not be opened during the run: interrupting centrifugation increases the likelihood of an inaccurate result, and the operator should wait until the machine has completely stopped before lifting the lid. Sealing the tube securely prevents leakage but does not make an interrupted spin acceptable, and no extra one-minute spin is described as a fix.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Packaging
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.D.2.n
preguntas.pregunta: Which material must not be used to wrap items for an ethylene oxide cycle?
opciones: Aluminum foil and polyvinylchloride kitchen-type transparent wrap
Nonwoven sterilization wrap and heat-sealed paper-plastic peel pouches
Woven sterilization wrap and paper-plastic roll stock cut to length
Rigid containers with a paper filter and a plastic external lock
preguntas.explicacion: Packaging has to let the sterilant through, keep microbes out and survive handling. Foil, polyvinylchloride and the transparent kitchen wraps are listed as unacceptable for ethylene oxide, and linens and paper are unacceptable for hydrogen peroxide gas plasma. Wraps, peel pouches, roll stock and rigid containers are the accepted options.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she is scared her results will be bad. The assistant answers, "You are scared about the results." Which technique is that?
opciones: Reflecting, repeating back what the patient said
Summarizing, restating the visit in the staff member's words
Clarifying, guiding the patient to give more detail
Providing rationale, explaining why the test was ordered
preguntas.explicacion: Reflecting repeats back what the patient said, at times word for word, to show that they are being listened to. Summarizing gathers several points in the interviewer's own words and often closes an interview; clarifying is a guiding statement that draws out more; providing rationale explains why the information is needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Ten minutes after a faint the patient is awake but still noticeably pale. What does that persisting pallor suggest?
opciones: Symptomatic anemia, which calls for a fuller evaluation
A normal recovery, since pallor lingers after every faint
A seizure rather than a faint, as the tongue was not bitten
Hemoconcentration from the tourniquet used during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: After a simple vasovagal event the examination should be entirely normal. Pallor that carries on suggests symptomatic anemia and, like a bitten tongue or an atypical story, prompts a search for another cause rather than a comfortable label.

preguntas.subtema: Security official · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which Security Rule standard does a practice meet by naming one person to develop and run its security policies?
opciones: Assigned security responsibility, which asks for an identified security official
Security management process, which is met by writing out the policies themselves
Workforce security, which settles which staff members may reach the information
Evaluation, which reviews whether the safeguards still fit how the practice works
preguntas.explicacion: Assigned security responsibility is a standard in its own right: name the security official who will develop the policies the subpart requires and put them into effect. It is the security counterpart of the privacy official the Privacy Rule asks for, and one person may hold both roles.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: De-Identified Health Information
preguntas.subtema: De-identification · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k35 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee wants a data file with no restrictions on its later use. Which step achieves that under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Stripping the listed identifiers of the patient, relatives, employers and household members
Removing only the names and leaving birth dates, addresses and account numbers in place
Replacing each patient name with the medical record number used inside the practice
Having the privacy official sign a statement that the file is for internal use only
preguntas.explicacion: De-identified information carries no restrictions on use or disclosure, and two routes lead to it. One is a qualified statistician making a formal determination; the other is stripping out the identifiers specified for the individual herself and for her relatives, household members and employers, which counts only where the entity has no actual knowledge that what remains could still identify somebody. Medical record numbers, account numbers and full-face photographs are on the safe harbor list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Suture Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: Where is a suture cut during removal, and why there?
opciones: Immediately under the knot, so the least contaminated surface is dragged through the tissue
Immediately above the knot, so the whole knot lifts out without pulling on the wound edges
At both ends of the knot, so the strand comes free without any tension on the skin at all
At the midpoint between two stitches, so each half slides out on the side where it entered
preguntas.explicacion: The cut goes immediately under the knot, as close to the skin as possible at the far end of the knot, so that the portion which has been lying on the skin surface is not pulled down through the tissue. Both ends of the knot must never be snipped, because then nothing is left to grasp and the strand below the surface cannot be retrieved.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a wheelchair cannot stand for a height measurement. Which alternatives are described?
opciones: Estimates from arm span, lower leg, foot length or recumbent length are used
The last recorded standing height is carried forward until the patient can stand
Height is left blank, because no measurement is valid unless the patient stands
Height is estimated from the seated shoulder width, which tracks stature closely
preguntas.explicacion: Where standing height cannot be obtained, regression equations based on arm span, the lower leg, foot length, shoeprint length or recumbent length are used as indicators of stature, and imaging of long bones has also been used. Where cerebral palsy is severe, measuring the child directly while supine is the most reliable way.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b)(1) and (b)(2), Standard: Minimum necessary
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary exceptions · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: To which disclosure does the HIPAA minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A disclosure to a health care provider for treatment
A disclosure to a health plan for payment
A disclosure to a business associate for operations
A disclosure to a researcher under a privacy board waiver
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity using, disclosing or requesting PHI must make reasonable efforts to keep it to the minimum necessary for the purpose. Section 164.502(b)(2) sets out where that does not apply: a provider disclosing for treatment or asking for what treatment needs; uses and disclosures to the individual; anything done under an authorization; disclosures to the Secretary for compliance; and uses required by law or by the rule itself. Payment, operations and research disclosures all stay under the minimum necessary limit.

preguntas.subtema: Business associate agreements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: An outside company will digitize the clinic's paper charts. What does HIPAA require before it receives the PHI?
opciones: Satisfactory assurances in a written business associate contract that it will safeguard the PHI
A signed authorization from every patient whose chart will be digitized by the company
Only the notice of privacy practices, since scanning counts as a health care operation
A certificate of accreditation for the company from a CMS-approved organization, renewed yearly
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(e) lets a covered entity disclose PHI to a business associate, and let it create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on its behalf, if it first secures satisfactory assurances that the associate will safeguard the information, documented in a written contract or arrangement meeting 164.504(e); the associate may then use the PHI only as its contract or the law permits, and must secure the same assurances from any subcontractor. Patient authorizations are not needed for this kind of operational service, and accreditation is a CLIA concept.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Body Mass Index (BMI)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is obesity defined in children and teenagers?
opciones: A body mass index at or above the 95th percentile for that sex and age
A body mass index at or above the 85th percentile for that sex and age
A body mass index of 30.0 or more, the same threshold as in adults
A body mass index at or above the 90th percentile for that sex and age
preguntas.explicacion: For children and teenagers of 2 through 19 the threshold is the 95th percentile of the index for sex and age. Fixed adult categories do not apply, because children are still growing. Severe obesity in that group is defined at 120% of the 95th percentile or an index of 35 or more.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: Before the Visit, Screen for Contraindications and Precautions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient screened for contraindications before every dose of a vaccine, not just the first one?
opciones: Health status and the recommendations may have changed since the last dose
The vaccine lot changes between doses and each lot has its own precautions
The screening replaces the vaccination history that was taken the first time
A second dose is contraindicated whenever the first one caused any soreness
preguntas.explicacion: Screening prevents adverse reactions such as anaphylaxis, and it is repeated before every dose because things move: the health of the patient may have changed since the last one, and so may the recommendations on contraindications and precautions. A standardized screening tool keeps the practice correct and consistent, and checklists exist for children, teenagers and adults.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Coordinating with the patient's provider · CCMA 4E · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: Once hospice starts, may a patient keep seeing the doctor who has treated her for years?
opciones: Yes, if she named that doctor or nurse practitioner as the attending professional
Yes, but only for health problems that are unrelated to the terminal illness
No, because every clinician involved must be employed by the hospice agency itself
No, unless the hospice medical director signs a new election statement first
preguntas.explicacion: All care for the terminal illness has to be given or arranged by the hospice the patient chose, and care from a hospice the team did not set up is not covered. One opening remains: the patient may keep her own doctor or nurse practitioner if she named that person the attending professional who helps supervise hospice care. The election statement records that choice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k41 · CMA I.C.6.h(6) (2027 I.C.6.g(6)) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of factors raises the risk of gastroesophageal reflux disease?
opciones: Hiatus hernia, age over 50, obesity, smoking and alcohol use
Hiatus hernia, age under 30, low body weight and heavy exercise
Iodine deficiency, age over 50, obesity and a family history of goiter
Multiple sex partners, age under 25 and inconsistent barrier use
preguntas.explicacion: The listed risk factors are a hiatus hernia, being over 50, a body mass index above 30, smoking and alcohol, fatty, spicy or acidic foods, and low physical activity. Drugs that lower the pressure of the lower esophageal sphincter, such as nitrates, calcium channel blockers and anticholinergics, add to the problem.

preguntas.subtema: Amendment of the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her chart lists an allergy she does not have and asks the office to fix it. How long does the practice have to act?
opciones: Sixty days, with one thirty day extension if the patient is told the reason in writing
Thirty days, the same period the rule gives for responding to a request for access
Ten working days, after which the entry must be deleted from the electronic record
Six years, the period the rule sets for keeping its privacy policies and procedures
preguntas.explicacion: The amendment right lets an individual ask a covered entity to correct PHI in the designated record set that is inaccurate or incomplete. The regulation gives 60 days to act on the request, with a single 30 day extension. If the amendment is accepted, the entity must make reasonable efforts to pass it on to those the individual names and to those it knows may rely on the old information to her detriment.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, About TRICARE; and VA, CHAMPVA benefits; and DOL, Office of Workers' Compensation Programs
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which agency manages TRICARE?
opciones: The Defense Health Agency, under the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs
The Department of Veterans Affairs, through the Veterans Health Administration
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, through its own regional offices
The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs, through the Department of Labor
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE is the health care program serving members of the uniformed services, retirees and their families, wherever in the world they are, and it is run by the Defense Health Agency, which answers to the Defense Department's Assistant Secretary for Health Affairs. Veterans' benefits and CHAMPVA belong to the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the federal injury compensation programs to the Labor Department.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorization to release · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A life insurance company asks the office for a patient's records to decide on a policy. What does the office need?
opciones: The patient's written authorization, since this purpose is outside treatment, payment or operations
No document at all, since disclosures to insurers count as payment activities of a plan
A note in the accounting of disclosures, which by itself makes the release permissible
The good faith acknowledgment the patient signed for the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: Written authorization is required for any use or disclosure that falls outside treatment, outside payment and outside health care operations, and that is not otherwise permitted or required. The examples OCR gives are a disclosure to a life insurer weighing coverage, a pre- employment physical result going to an employer, and information going to a drug company for its own marketing. The payment definition reaches the patient's health plan, not a life insurer.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMA III.G.1.d (2027 III.G.1.d) · CMAA 5 k69 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: CMS receives a complete request for a national coverage determination that needs no outside technology assessment and no advisory committee review. How long may the decision take?
opciones: No more than six months after the completed request is received
No more than nine months after the completed request is received
No more than sixty days after the completed request is received
No more than one year after the completed request is received
preguntas.explicacion: Coverage of an item or service is limited to what is reasonable and necessary, and national determinations are reached through an evidence-based process with fixed deadlines. A request that needs no external assessment and no advisory committee is decided within six months of the completed request; one that needs either of them, within nine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Loop Diuretics", Mechanism of Action and Indications; and StatPearls, "Antihypertensive Medications" (NBK554579)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: Furosemide is ordered for a patient admitted with fluid overload from heart failure. Where does this class act?
opciones: On the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter of the loop of Henle's thick ascending limb
On the sodium-chloride channel of the distal convoluted tubule of the nephron
On the beta-1 receptors that make the juxtaglomerular cells release their renin
On the enzyme that converts angiotensin I into the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II
preguntas.explicacion: A loop diuretic competes with chloride for the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter of the thick ascending limb and blocks it, so sodium and chloride are not reabsorbed, the interstitium loses its tonicity and free water leaves in the urine. The distal convoluted tubule is where thiazides work; renin release and the angiotensin-converting enzyme belong to beta blockers and ACE inhibitors.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which services does Medicare Part A help cover?
opciones: Inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care, hospice and home health
Inpatient hospital stays, doctors' services in the office and durable equipment
Outpatient care, preventive screenings and yearly wellness visits with a doctor
Prescription drugs bought at the pharmacy and many recommended vaccines
preguntas.explicacion: Part A is the hospital insurance half of Original Medicare: inpatient hospital care, care in a skilled nursing facility, hospice, and some home health care. Doctors' services, outpatient care, durable medical equipment and preventive services sit under Part B, and drugs bought at the pharmacy come through Part D, either as a standalone plan or built into a Medicare Advantage plan.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Allergy Testing", Procedures: Skin Prick Testing
preguntas.pregunta: How far apart are the allergens placed during skin prick testing, and when is the result read?
opciones: At least 2 cm apart, with the allergen sites read after 15 to 20 minutes
At least 2 cm apart, with the allergen sites read after 48 to 72 hours
At least 5 mm apart, with the allergen sites read after 15 to 20 minutes
At least 2 cm apart, with the allergen sites read after 3 to 5 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Solutions go on the skin at least two centimeters from one another, along with a positive control of histamine and a negative control of glycerinated saline; a device then punctures the skin beneath them. Controls are checked at ten minutes and the allergen sites at 15 to 20, when a sensitized patient shows a wheal at the site.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Fainting", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.l · 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient faints in the hallway and comes round within seconds. What is the immediate care?
opciones: Check breathing, loosen the collar and raise the feet above heart level
Sit the patient in a chair and offer a sweet drink and a cold compress
Roll the patient face down with the head turned so the airway drains
Stand the patient up slowly with support to restore normal circulation
preguntas.explicacion: Airway and breathing are checked first, tight clothing at the neck is loosened, and the feet are raised above the level of the heart, about 12 inches (30 cm). If the patient vomited, they are turned onto one side. They stay lying down 10 to 15 minutes in a cool quiet place; if that is impossible, they sit forward with the head between the knees.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A family moving out of state asks whether their new state's Medicaid has to cover the child's dental care. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: Dental care is optional, so a state adds it only through the state plan process
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way family planning services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way nurse midwife services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, as federally qualified health center services are
preguntas.explicacion: The federal list separates the benefits every state has to provide from those a state may add through the state plan process. Family planning, nurse midwife services and federally qualified health center services are mandatory; dental services, clinic services, physical therapy, private duty nursing and other licensed practitioner services are optional.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Torts and consent · CCMA 7B k216, k221 · CMA E.4.a(5)-(6) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient in the emergency department refuses an IV. Staff place it before any capacity assessment is made. What has occurred?
opciones: Battery, since contact was made with no consent and no documented assessment
False imprisonment, since the patient was held in a bounded area unwillingly
Implied consent, because the emergency exception covers a refused procedure
Negligence, because the standard of care for agitation was not followed first
preguntas.explicacion: Until a capacity assessment has been done and documented, treating a refusing patient is the tort of battery: harmful or offensive contact without consent. Putting the same patient on a hold would add false imprisonment, and restraining or sedating would be both. The way out is the assessment: once lack of capacity is documented, sedation, restraint, venipuncture and testing may go ahead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Availability of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Besides handing the notice of privacy practices to new patients, where must a treatment provider keep it available?
opciones: Posted at the facility, with copies to take away, and on a website describing its services
Posted at the facility, with copies to take away, and filed with the state licensing board
Posted in the staff area, with copies to take away, and sent to each health plan it bills
Posted at the facility, with copies on request, and read aloud before the first appointment
preguntas.explicacion: The latest version, the one reflecting any change in privacy policies, has to be available at the office for people to ask for and take with them, and posted where it can be seen clearly. Any website the entity keeps that describes its customer services or benefits must carry the notice prominently, and anyone who asks for a copy gets one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Evaluation of Visual Acuity", Methods of Assessing Visual Acuity
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(10)(b) · RMA III.F.5.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does BCVA mean when it appears beside a recorded visual acuity?
opciones: Best-corrected visual acuity, the sharpest reached once refraction is applied
Binocular corrected visual acuity, measured with both of the eyes open
Basic central visual acuity, measured only in the middle of the visual field
Baseline corrected visual acuity, taken at the very first visit on record
preguntas.explicacion: Distance acuity is written either as uncorrected or as best-corrected, the latter being the best result obtained with refraction. Distance is measured before near, and by convention the right eye is recorded first, then the left, then both together. Near vision is marked separately.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction; and "Syncope", section Etiology
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which form of syncope is the most common, and which of its triggers matter in a phlebotomy setting?
opciones: Vasovagal syncope, triggered among other things by pain or emotional upset, with bradycardia and hypotension
Carotid sinus syncope, triggered by pressure on the neck, with tachycardia and high blood pressure
Situational syncope, triggered by coughing or urination, with normal heart rate and pressure
Cardiac syncope, triggered by exertion, with ventricular tachycardia and pallor
preguntas.explicacion: The vasovagal episode is the most common form of reflex syncope and can be set off by pain or by emotional upset, though often no trigger is found; it accounts for nearly half of all cases, with severe pain and stress among its situations, leading to vasodilation and bradycardia. During the event the patient is typically slow of pulse, hypotensive, pale and sweating.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3.1 Recording the ECG
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 3F7 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: The first tracing prints and its quality is poor. What is done before any extra copies are made?
opciones: Stop the machine, fix the problem and run a new tracing
Ask for the extra copies and mark the poor quality on them
Stop the machine and send the poor tracing to the provider
Ask for the extra copies and repeat it only if requested
preguntas.explicacion: The routine has the technician read the first printed tracing for errors before anything else. If the quality is not good, the run is stopped, the problem is resolved and a fresh recording is taken; the number of extra copies is only entered once the strip is good.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and tube labeling)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A tube arrives in the laboratory bearing only the patient's full name. Which element is missing that is normally required on a labeled specimen?
opciones: The date and time of collection and the identity of the person who collected it
The diagnosis code and the name of the insurance carrier that covers the requested test
The room number and the bed number where the specimen was collected
The color of the stopper and the lot number of the evacuated tube used
preguntas.explicacion: A complete label carries, beside the patient's names and date of birth, the exact date and time of collection and the collector's identification, according to each center's policy; the requesting provider and the specimen's own identifying details may also be included. Diagnosis codes belong on the requisition, not the tube; room or bed numbers cannot serve as identifiers; stopper color and lot are not label content.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Strategies for Communicating with Patients with Impaired Hearing and Vision
preguntas.subtema: Vision impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant walks into the room of a patient with very low vision. What comes first?
opciones: Identifying themselves as they enter the patient's space
Handing over the large-print copy of the instructions
Turning the overhead lighting off to cut down the glare
Taking the patient by the arm to guide them to the chair
preguntas.explicacion: For impaired vision the opening step is to identify yourself on entering the patient's space. After that, check that glasses are present, clean and current, provide enough room lighting while minimizing glare, and supply material in large print or read the pertinent parts aloud.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Contaminated, Contaminated Sharps, Regulated Waste
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated sharps definition · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which item meets the standard's definition of a contaminated sharp?
opciones: A broken capillary tube with dried blood on it
A sealed tube of blood in a transport rack
A dressing soaked with liquid blood that would drip if squeezed
An unused lancet still in its sterile package
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) calls a contaminated sharp any contaminated object capable of penetrating the skin, and its examples run from needles and scalpels to broken glass, broken capillary tubes and the exposed ends of dental wires. Two conditions have to hold at once: the object can pierce skin, and blood or OPIM is on it or is reasonably anticipated to be. A sealed tube pierces nothing; a gauze pad that would drip is regulated waste of the liquid kind rather than a sharp; and an unused lancet can pierce but carries nothing, so it is not a contaminated sharp yet.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Function
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic communication · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What is the goal of therapeutic communication as it is generally defined?
opciones: Helping the patient get past some form of emotional or mental distress
Gathering the history in the shortest time the appointment allows
Making sure the record holds everything the provider will need later
Keeping the rest of the team informed of changes in the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The definition in general use describes an exchange between patient and provider using verbal and nonverbal methods, whose ultimate goal is to help the patient overcome emotional or psychological distress. Speed, documentation and reports to other team members are real duties, but they are not what this term names.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Exposure Incident; and (f)(3), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Exposure incidents and post-exposure follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these events meets OSHA's definition of an "exposure incident"?
opciones: Blood splashes into a technician's eye while a tube is being uncapped
A drop of blood lands on the intact skin of a gloved hand
A technician is assigned to a job where contact with blood is reasonably anticipated
A contaminated needle is found in a regulated waste bag, without any parenteral contact
preguntas.explicacion: The definition names the routes that count: the eye, the mouth or another mucous membrane, skin that is not intact, or a parenteral route such as a needlestick, with the contact coming from the employee's duties. A splash to the eye is mucous-membrane contact and qualifies. Intact gloved skin is not a listed route. A job where contact is reasonably anticipated is Occupational Exposure, the neighbouring definition, not an incident. A contaminated needle in a waste bag is regulated waste in the wrong container, but without parenteral contact there is no exposure incident. The label matters because reporting an exposure incident is what obliges the employer to make the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up available at once.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care and bandaging · CPT D3 3Q k73 k74 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E9 k137 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.13
preguntas.pregunta: How is pressure maintained on the site after the needle is removed?
opciones: Gauze pressed over the site as the needle comes out, then taped in place, or a bandaid applied over it
The patient bends the elbow over the gauze, which keeps pressure on the vein without tape
An ice pack wrapped in a towel is held on the site for 15 minutes to prevent a hematoma
The tourniquet is reapplied loosely over the gauze for one minute to compress the vein
preguntas.explicacion: Once the draw is done, clean gauze is used to apply pressure as the needle is swiftly removed, pressure is continued, and the gauze is taped in place to provide continuous pressure against a hematoma; alternatively a bandaid goes over the gauze. Bending the arm is what the WHO forbids, and ice is first aid for a bruise that has already formed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Religious Competence in Clinical Practice", sections Religion and Healthcare, and Islam (Clinical Significance)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A Muslim woman asks for a female phlebotomist. What is the culturally competent response?
opciones: Find a same-sex practitioner unless the situation is an acute emergency
Explain that staff assignments cannot be changed for religious reasons alone
Proceed with the male phlebotomist if her husband gives his agreement
Ask her to sign a waiver acknowledging the delay before rescheduling
preguntas.explicacion: Religion can shape a patient's preference for the gender of their health provider, along with diet, medicines from animal products and modesty, and the clinical note for Islam reads: find a same-sex practitioner if it is not an acute emergency. Health professionals are asked to accommodate such needs rather than refuse them or route the decision through a relative.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 17, Stages of Grief
preguntas.subtema: Stages of grief · CCMA 1E k34 · CMA F.1.c(1) / 2027 F.1.d(2)
preguntas.pregunta: Which mnemonic gathers the five stages of grief, in the order they were described?
opciones: DABDA: denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance
DABDA: denial, anxiety, bargaining, despair, adaptation
SBARD: shock, blame, anger, resolution, denial
ADAPT: anger, denial, acceptance, protest, testing
preguntas.explicacion: The five responses set out in the 1969 book On Death and Dying are denial, then anger, bargaining, depression and finally acceptance, remembered as DABDA. They apply not only to a death but also to divorce, a lost job or a new terminal diagnosis, and there is no single correct way to move through them.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Why do I need to fast, and What if I make a mistake; StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Diagnostic Tests in Diabetes Mellitus
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: During check-in a patient admits to having eaten a pastry two hours before a fasting glucose. What is the correct action?
opciones: Report it to the provider; the test may need to be rescheduled for a day when the patient can fast
Draw the sample anyway and write the time of the pastry on the tube so the laboratory can adjust the result
Have the patient wait in the lobby for six more hours and then draw, since 8 hours will have passed by then
Draw the sample and order a random glucose instead, since the two tests share the same normal value
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient eats or drinks anything other than water during the fast, the instruction is to tell the provider, who may reschedule the test for another time when the patient can fast, because nutrients absorbed from food change the levels of substances in the blood and an inaccurate result gives an inaccurate picture of health. Fasting and random glucose have different normal values, and no note on the tube converts one into the other.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Angle of insertion · CPT D3 3I k65 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: At what angle to the surface of the arm is the phlebotomy needle inserted?
opciones: Between 15 and 30 degrees
Between 30 and 45 degrees
Less than 45 degrees
Between 5 and 10 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The needle goes in slowly at an angle of 15 to 30 degrees to the surface of the arm, after the skin has been pulled taut with the thumb. The WHO gives 30 degrees or less, which is consistent. The 'less than 45 degrees until a flash of blood appears' figure belongs to the peripheral line placement chapter and describes an IV cannula, not a phlebotomy needle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has had a mastectomy on the left side. Which arm is used for the cuff?
opciones: The right: a mastectomy on that side is an absolute reason to avoid the left arm
Either arm, provided the cuff is inflated more slowly on the operated side
The left, because the readings on the two sides have to be kept comparable
The right, but only during the first year after the operation was carried out
preguntas.explicacion: A history of mastectomy on that side is listed among the absolute reasons not to put a cuff on that limb, along with a dialysis fistula or shunt and recent surgical wounds. Lymphedema, paralysis or weakness of the limb, and indwelling lines are relative reasons. In each case the other limb or another site is used.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.12 Checklist for Wound Cleansing, Irrigation, and Packing
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.k · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A wound healing by secondary intention is being irrigated. How is it done?
opciones: A 35-mL syringe with a needleless cannula, held an inch above, flushing until the return runs clear
A 35-mL syringe with a needleless cannula, held against the bed, flushing for a fixed thirty seconds
A 10-mL syringe with a fine needle attached, held an inch above, flushing until the return runs clear
A bulb syringe with warmed tap water, held an inch above, flushing until the periwound skin is wet
preguntas.explicacion: Irrigation uses a 35-mL syringe of sterile saline with a needleless cannula, held about an inch above the wound and flushed gently with continuous pressure until the fluid coming back is clear. The runoff drains into a basin, since it is a medium for bacterial growth. The edges are then dried with sterile gauze so the surrounding tissue does not macerate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Generalized Anxiety Disorder", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Mental health conditions · CCMA 1E k30 · CMA F.1.a / 2027 F.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: How long must the worry last before generalized anxiety disorder is diagnosed?
opciones: At least 6 months of excessive, hard-to-control worry
At least 1 month of excessive, hard-to-control worry
At least 2 weeks of excessive, hard-to-control worry
At least 12 months of excessive, hard-to-control worry
preguntas.explicacion: The criteria call for excessive anxiety and worry over at least 6 months, worry the person has trouble controlling, and three or more accompanying symptoms across that same span: restlessness, tiring easily, trouble concentrating or a mind going blank, irritability, and muscle tension.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Coinsurance and Out-of-network Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.b, III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76, 4 k61 · CCMA 5K k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A plan allows $150 for a visit, the patient has met her deductible, and her out-of-network coinsurance is 40%. What is her coinsurance for that visit?
opciones: Sixty dollars, which is forty percent of the amount the plan allows
Thirty dollars, which is twenty percent of the amount the plan allows
Ninety dollars, which is the share the plan itself pays on that visit
A hundred and fifty dollars, since out-of-network care sits outside the plan
preguntas.explicacion: Coinsurance is the patient's share of a covered service, worked out as a percentage of the allowed amount and paid on top of any deductible owed. Out-of-network coinsurance is the share owed to providers who have no contract with the plan, and it usually costs more than the in-network share, with forty percent against twenty percent given as the illustration.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Equipment: Automated Office Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic installs a device that takes several blood pressure readings on its own while the patient waits alone in the room. Which problem is that meant to solve?
opciones: Readings pushed up or down by the presence of the person measuring
Cuffs of the wrong width that squeeze a large arm far too tightly
Readings started before the patient has sat quietly for five minutes
Monitors that drift out of calibration between one service and the next
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure moves when a clinician is in the room: it climbs in white-coat hypertension and hides in masked hypertension. Automated office monitoring records several readings over a few minutes with nobody present, and the values land closer to awake ambulatory pressure. Cuff size, resting time and calibration are separate matters, handled by technique.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Cataract surgery was done on the right eye last month and the left eye is treated today, with the right one now resolved. Which code fits today's visit?
opciones: The unilateral code for the eye that still has the condition
The bilateral code, since both eyes had the condition this year
The unspecified side code, because only one side is treated now
Two codes, one for each of the eyes that have been treated so far
preguntas.explicacion: The bilateral code is assigned while the condition exists on both sides, including at the encounter that treats the first side. At the second encounter, once treatment has resolved the condition on the side already done, the appropriate unilateral code is used for the side that still has it. If the first treatment did not resolve it, the bilateral code still fits.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dialysis Fistula", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient has an arteriovenous fistula in the left forearm. What should be avoided on that side?
opciones: Peripheral venous access, blood draws and blood pressure measurements
Blood draws only; blood pressure cuffs are safe if inflated briefly
Blood pressure measurements only; draws are permitted below the fistula
Only the puncture of the fistula itself; draws above it are permitted
preguntas.explicacion: Nurses help save the veins by keeping peripheral lines, blood draws and pressure cuffs OFF the side of the fistula or of planned fistula creation, and they should know how to assess the thrill and recognize its loss. Checking the thrill is part of monitoring the access, not a clearance to puncture that arm.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Physician Self-Referral Law
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A group bills for a designated health service, unaware that the referral behind it broke the self-referral law. What is the position?
opciones: Filing the claim is prohibited anyway, since intent is not needed
Filing the claim is allowed, because the group did not know of it
Filing is allowed if the referral is put right after the payment
Filing is prohibited only where the referral was made on purpose
preguntas.explicacion: The self-referral law stops the entity from billing at all for a designated health service that came from an improper referral, and it does so whether or not the entity knew of the problem or meant to claim for it. If Medicare pays such a claim the entity holds an overpayment, which has to be reported and returned within 60 days of being identified.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Access barriers · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient books her first video visit and says she has no internet at home. Which option does HHS suggest the office raise with her?
opciones: A public library, which usually offers high-speed internet and often a private room
A relative's telephone, which she can borrow for the length of the appointment
The clinic waiting room, where she can join the call on the practice's own tablet
A paper questionnaire she can post back instead of attending the appointment
preguntas.explicacion: Having no internet service with the bandwidth for video is named as one of the biggest barriers keeping patients away from telehealth. The suggestions offered are that the patient might be eligible for federal help under the Lifeline program, that plenty of fast food restaurants throw free Wi-Fi as far as the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often a private room.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Colored Feature or Component
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: When a sharps safety device uses color on a component, what is expected of that color?
opciones: It should serve a purpose and follow conventions users know already
It should be red, so the used device is visible in the sharps bin
It should differ between hospitals, so devices are not mixed up
It should change once the safety feature has been activated once
preguntas.explicacion: Color is expected to achieve a specific purpose, such as distinguishing models or sizes, and to fit conventions the user already recognizes, the example given being the orange hubs and needle covers of insulin syringes. Whether the feature has fired is judged by design, not by a color change.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, About TRICARE; and HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Grandfathered health plan
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: How do most TRICARE health plans stand against the Affordable Care Act's coverage requirement?
opciones: They satisfy the law's standard for minimum essential coverage
They are exempt from that law, being run by the Department of Defense
They meet the requirement for active-duty members but not for families
They count as grandfathered plans, so the requirement never reaches them
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is the standard the Affordable Care Act sets, and most of the program's health plans meet it. What TRICARE gives its beneficiaries is comprehensive: dental plans, prescriptions, special programs and health plans. A grandfathered plan is a different thing altogether, an individual or job-based plan that already existed when the law was signed and has not changed much since.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, classes of fire and extinguisher types; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(d)
preguntas.subtema: Classes of fire · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which fuels define a Class B fire?
opciones: Flammable liquids and gases, such as organic solvents
Ordinary combustibles that leave ash, such as paper
Combustible metal powders, flakes or shavings
Energized electrical equipment such as a centrifuge motor
preguntas.explicacion: Class A fires involve ordinary combustibles, fuels that burn and leave ash, and Class B flammable liquids and gases; many organic solvents and compressed gases in a laboratory are Class B hazards. Combustible metals are Class D, handled with a specialized dry powder extinguisher, and 29 CFR 1910.157 treats electrical equipment as Class C, distributing those units by the pattern of the A or B hazards present. The most common laboratory extinguishers are dry chemical BC or ABC and carbon dioxide.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth check-in · CCMA 5R · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit is about to begin. Which step belongs to the start of the encounter?
opciones: Confirming who the patient is and why she has come to the visit
Submitting the claim with the telehealth modifier already attached
Collecting the patient's feedback on how the technology performed
Sending the appointment reminder with the link to the platform
preguntas.explicacion: The workflow lists the steps in order. Ahead of the visit come the reminder, guidance on using the technology, the online paperwork, a walk-through of the equipment, troubleshooting information, consent and a request that the patient find somewhere quiet and private. The visit itself opens with confirmation, establishing who the patient is and what has brought her, and intake follows. Billing and evaluation come afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: What are the two essential components of manual instrument cleaning?
opciones: Friction, meaning scrubbing the soiled area, and fluidics, meaning fluid under pressure
Cavitation, meaning imploding bubbles, and sonication, meaning waves of acoustic energy
Agitation, meaning steam passing through the bath, and a short terminal steam cycle
Circulation, meaning water driven by spray arms, and a heat step held near ninety degrees
preguntas.explicacion: Cleaning by hand rests on friction and fluidics. Friction is the old dependable one, a brush rubbed over the soiled area; fluidics is fluid under pressure, used to flush internal channels after brushing or where no brush will pass. Cavitation belongs to the ultrasonic cleaner, and the steam bath and spray arms to washer-sterilizers and washer-disinfectors.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Minimum Value Standard
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.a (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An employee is told her job-based plan meets the minimum value standard. What does that mean about the plan?
opciones: It pays at least sixty percent of the total allowed costs of benefits
It pays at least eighty percent of the total allowed costs of benefits
It covers at least sixty percent of the essential health benefits
It caps her own share of the allowed costs at sixty percent a year
preguntas.explicacion: The minimum value standard measures the percentage of permitted costs a plan covers. An employer plan that pays for at least sixty percent of the total allowed costs of benefits offers minimum value, and the employee offered it may then not qualify for premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions on the Marketplace.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.d (2027 I.C.6.c) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity?
opciones: The diaphragm, a dome-shaped muscle used in breathing
The mediastinum, the space that holds the heart
The peritoneum, the membrane around the abdominal organs
The pleura, the membrane that wraps around each lung
preguntas.explicacion: The ventral cavity is split in two by the diaphragm, the dome-shaped respiratory muscle that forms the floor of the chest. Above it lie the heart and lungs, below it the digestive organs, kidneys and adrenal glands. The mediastinum, peritoneum and pleura are structures inside those cavities, not the wall between them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Specimen Collection (Immunological methods) and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: FIT versus gFOBT · PBT V.B.2 / V.E · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How does the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) differ from the guaiac test in patient preparation?
opciones: FIT needs no dietary restrictions, because its antibodies detect human globin rather than peroxidase activity
FIT needs a stricter diet, because it detects heme from any animal source as well as human blood
FIT needs the same 3-day diet, but vitamin C may be continued because it targets porphyrins
FIT needs no dietary restrictions, because it detects heme-derived porphyrins by spectrofluorimetry
preguntas.explicacion: Immunochemical kits use antibodies against the globin chain of human hemoglobin, so animal heme and plant peroxidases do not react and no diet is required, which improves adherence; they mainly pick up lower gastrointestinal bleeding and are more specific than guaiac. Guaiac relies on the pseudoperoxidase activity of heme, and the heme-porphyrin method is a separate laboratory assay using spectrofluorimetry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: In a capacity assessment, what must the patient demonstrate?
opciones: Grasp of the facts, weighing of options, a clear choice and steady logic
Correct orientation to person, place and time throughout the interview
Agreement with the plan the clinician has recommended for the problem
A mental status exam with no hallucinations, agitation or pressured speech
preguntas.explicacion: Capacity is shown when the patient understands what is relevant to this decision, can weigh the risks, benefits and alternatives, can tell the team what they have decided, and keeps that reasoning consistent through the encounter. Hallucinations, agitation and disorganized speech are triggers to look harder, not the test itself, and capacity never means agreeing with the clinician's recommendation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrosurgery", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.5.c (2027 I.C.5.a) · RMA III.D.2.j
preguntas.pregunta: What protection is used against the smoke plume generated during electrosection?
opciones: A smoke evacuator held within about two inches of the site, plus eye protection and masks
A smoke evacuator held about a foot from the site, plus a gown and a face shield for the patient
An open window and a room fan, plus eye protection and masks for the operator and assistants
A wet sponge held near the site, plus eye protection and masks for the operator and assistants
preguntas.explicacion: The plume has been shown to be mutagenic, so a smoke evacuator is essential and is held within about two inches of the surgical site to catch the airborne contaminants; the recommended units carry a filter for high-efficiency particulate air and pull at roughly 100 to 150 feet per minute. Eye protection, gloves and masks are worn by the operator and the assistants.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: Once the four limb wires are attached, what is double-checked?
opciones: That the right-side wires are on the right and the left ones on the left
That the chest wires are hanging clear of the patient's arms
That the four electrodes are all at the same height on the limbs
That the tabs of the electrodes all point down toward the feet
preguntas.explicacion: Before moving on to the chest, the right arm and right leg wires are confirmed on the patient's right and the left arm and left leg wires on the left, each on its matching limb. That single check is what prevents the reversal that turns every complex in lead I upside down.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Minimum Requirements [29 CFR 1910.38(b)]
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan has to be in writing. What is the answer?
opciones: No: with 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
No: any employer may keep the plan oral if the staff are trained yearly
Yes: the plan is written whenever the workplace has any employees at all
Yes: only a plan of 25 or fewer employees may be communicated orally
preguntas.explicacion: The plan is normally written down and held at the workplace where employees can consult it; the exception is an employer of 10 employees or fewer, who may pass it on by word of mouth. That is the only exception in the rule; the six minimum elements still have to be covered, and everyone still has to know how to respond.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87 centrifuging) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A whole-blood sample is spun in a centrifuge. Which component settles at the very bottom of the tube?
opciones: The erythrocytes, the heaviest formed elements
The buffy coat of leukocytes and platelets
The straw-colored plasma, over half the sample
The serum, once the clotting factors are gone
preguntas.explicacion: In a spun sample the heaviest formed elements, the red cells, pack at the bottom; above them sits a thin pale layer of white cells and platelets, the buffy coat; and the plasma, a pale straw-colored liquid, floats on top as the lightest component and makes up more than half of the sample. Serum is not a layer of whole blood: it is plasma minus its clotting factors, obtained only after the blood has clotted.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.7 Medical Imaging, Ultrasonography
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k40 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.A.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which imaging technique is chosen most freely during pregnancy, and what is its main weakness?
opciones: Ultrasonography, whose image quality depends heavily on the operator
Computed tomography, whose image quality depends heavily on the operator
Magnetic resonance imaging, whose cost depends heavily on the operator
Positron emission tomography, whose tracer depends heavily on the operator
preguntas.explicacion: Ultrasonography sends high-frequency sound into the body and turns the echo into a real-time image, with no electromagnetic radiation, so it is the least invasive of the techniques and the one used in sensitive situations such as pregnancy. Its weak points are that the picture depends on who is holding the probe and that it cannot penetrate bone or gas.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Chain of Custody", section Chain of Custody in Legal Drug Testing
preguntas.subtema: Chain of custody · CPT D5 5C k91 · PBT III.A.4 special sample types · CCMA 3E k127 witness · RMA III.C.4.a.i · CMA I.C.7.a(2)(f)
preguntas.pregunta: An unconscious patient arrives after a crash and a legally defensible urine specimen is needed. Who identifies the specimen?
opciones: The nurse who collects it identifies it in the patient's place
The police officer who brought the patient in identifies it
The laboratory identifies it on arrival from the requisition
No one: the collection waits until the patient can identify it
preguntas.explicacion: In legal drug testing the donor normally identifies the sample and seals the cup, preferably in person, and signs the custody form ahead of the collector. Where the patient is insentient in the emergency room, whoever draws the urine or blood, the nurse, identifies it in the patient's place. Everyone who takes charge of it afterwards signs the form in sequence and may be called to testify.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs on the organized collection tray prepared before a venous draw?
opciones: A stirrer for tubes and waterproof transport bags
A centrifuge rotor and a rack of reagent cartridges
A capillary microtube warmer and a slide staining kit
A pair of sterile scissors and a suture removal blade
preguntas.explicacion: The tray is set out with a utility cart, gloves, a collection apparatus with safety measures, a complete series of unexpired tubes in various volumes, a tourniquet, antiseptic, dressings and gauze pads, a waste bin, a stirrer for tubes and waterproof transport bags.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cognitive Assessment", Cognitive Assessment Screens
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k46 · CMA I.A.5.h / 2027 I.A.5.f
preguntas.pregunta: How is the mini-mental state examination described?
opciones: A 30-point questionnaire that usually takes under ten minutes to give
A 27-point questionnaire that usually takes under ten minutes to give
A three-item recall paired with a clock-drawing task, done in minutes
A 21-item scale filled in by the clinician rather than by the patient
preguntas.explicacion: It is a 30-point questionnaire, generally finished in under ten minutes, and it has been studied since 1975. Its use is falling off because of copyright and cost. The three-item recall with a clock drawing is the Mini-Cog, and a clinician-administered scale of 21 items describes a depression rating instrument, not a cognitive screen.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, prognosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the doctor meant by prognosis. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: The likely course of the disease and the chance of recovery or recurrence
The name given to the disease after the exam and the tests are reviewed
The extent of the disease within the body at the moment it is discovered
The cause or origin of the disease that brought the patient to the visit
preguntas.explicacion: A prognosis is what the disease is expected to do: how it will probably run, and what chance there is of recovery or of a return. The distractors are the terms that sit next to it: diagnosis is identifying the disease from its signs and symptoms, staging measures how far it has spread, and etiology is its cause or origin.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Marketing
preguntas.subtema: Marketing and PHI · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to pay the practice for its patient list so it can promote a product. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An authorization from each patient, and it must reveal the payment involved
A business associate agreement, after which no authorization is needed
A notice in the accounting of disclosures listing the names that were sold
Removal of the diagnoses from the list, after which it may be sold freely
preguntas.explicacion: Marketing means any communication that talks up a product or a service so as to encourage buying or using it, and it also reaches an arrangement where a covered entity discloses PHI for payment, direct or indirect, so that another entity can push its own products. Authorization is required, save for face-to-face marketing between the entity and the individual and for promotional gifts of nominal value; where a third party is paying, the authorization has to say so.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Hypothermia", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient with hypothermia warmed while help is on the way?
opciones: With warm compresses on neck, chest wall and groin, out of the cold
With a heating pad on the arms and the legs, set to its lowest level
With a hot water bottle on the feet, wrapped in a towel first
With a heat lamp aimed at the chest from a safe distance away
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is moved out of the cold and warmed gently, with warm compresses on the neck, chest wall and groin and the rescuer's own body heat if needed; warm sweetened nonalcoholic fluids can be given if the patient is alert and swallows easily. Heat applied directly is not used, whether from a heat lamp, a heating pad or hot water, and no alcohol.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Skin or nail culture (003762), How the Test is Performed and Normal Results
preguntas.subtema: Skin and nail culture · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(b)
preguntas.pregunta: A nail sample was sent for culture. What should the patient be told about the result?
opciones: It can take up to 3 weeks, and organisms that normally live on skin are not a sign of infection
It can take up to 3 days, and any organism at all that grows in the dish is a sign of infection
It can take up to 3 weeks, and any organism at all that grows in the dish is a sign of infection
It comes back the same day, and organisms that normally live on skin are not a sign of infection
preguntas.explicacion: A nail culture can take as long as three weeks to report. Some organisms live on skin normally, and finding them is considered a normal result rather than an infection. The sample itself is taken with a swab or a blade from an open rash or sore, by scraping or clipping the affected nail, or by a skin biopsy taken after a numbing injection.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ventricular Tachycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: How is ventricular tachycardia defined on the tracing?
opciones: Three or more consecutive wide beats faster than 100 a minute
Three or more consecutive narrow beats faster than 100 a minute
Two or more consecutive wide beats slower than 100 a minute
